The previous Striatum repository is the bootstrap compiler — prior art and bootstrap machinery, never architecture to preserve by default. If a legacy concept conflicts with the compiler model, the compiler model wins.\\n\\n**Epoch 1 and the Epoch 2 Runtime Foundation are complete.** The language, compiler architecture, IRs, passes, and artifact lifecycle are fixed by RFCs 0001–0005 (decisions D0001–D0005); the runtime — provenance ledger and artifact store, driver control surface, execution backends, scheduler and capacity policy, work-graph execution — is fixed by RFCs 0006–0010 (decisions D0006–D0010). Do not relitigate accepted decisions casually; amend the owning RFC and regenerate its decision record.\\n\\n## Core Thesis\\n\\nStriatum does not orchestrate agents. Striatum compiles intent.\\n\\nThe purpose of Striatum is not to orchestrate intelligent systems. It is to compile the outputs of arbitrary nondeterministic capability providers into a deterministic, provenance-preserving artifact graph.\\n\\nA human issues a compilation request:\\n\\n```text\\nAdvance RFC 0028 to Verified.\\n```\\n\\nThe system determines the current artifact-graph state, the target-state delta, the required passes, scheduling, gates, invalidation, provenance, and escalation. The human requests a desired state; Striatum computes and executes the path. Verified is a predicate the graph satisfies — never a status anyone declares.\\n\\n## Start Here\\n\\nFor cold start, read in order:\\n\\n1. `README.md`\\n2. `docs/explanation/striatum-as-compiler-for-engineering-intent.md`\\n3. `docs/concepts/language-specification.md`\\n4. `decisions/index.md` — the accepted semantic state (what the architecture IS)\\n5. `docs/explanation/decision-layer.md`\\n6. `docs/explanation/driver.md`\\n7. `docs/explanation/lanes-and-execution-backends.md`\\n8. `docs/explanation/capacity-aware-engineering-compute.md`\\n9. `rfcs/INDEX.md` — the design conversations (why)\\n10. `docs/explanation/discoveries.md` — non-normative: the discoveries that changed the compiler's direction, mapped to where each was absorbed\\n11. The active RFC or work packet named by the task\\n\\n## Compiler Ontology (compact; canonical form in RFC 0001)\\n\\n- **Intent / Intent Statement** — a human goal; its verbatim L0 capture (the root IR).\\n- **Artifact** — durable, versioned, provenance-bearing; exactly one role: IR, Decision Record, Evidence, or Product Artifact.\\n- **IR ladder** — Intent Statement (L0) → Proposal (L1) → Design (L2) → Implementation Plan (L3) → Work Graph (L4) → Change Set (L5); Product (L6) is a designation, not an IR.\\n- **Decision Record** — the compiler's canonical architectural memory: the generated, binding interface of an RFC identity. RFCs are the conversation; decisions are the accepted semantic state.\\n- **Evidence** — immutable attestations (Review Ledger, Receipt, Verification Report, Exogenous Change Record); never invalidated, force decays.\\n- **Compiler Pass** — a versioned transformation contract (transform or analysis class); pass runs are its provenance-recorded executions under sealed run manifests.\\n- **Pipeline** — a catalog-resident composition template (passes + gate wiring + re-run bounds); no new semantics.\\n- **Quality Gate** — exactly one class: Check (mechanical), Review (independent judgment, closed verdicts), Acceptance (authority).\\n- **Claim** — a falsifiable statement with a computed level: `Verified \\u003e Asserted \\u003e Designed`; promotion needs binding closure and independence; decay is arithmetic.\\n- **Driver** — the compiler driver: a deterministic program that plans, gates, admits, invalidates, escalates. Produces no artifacts. (Retired alias: Meta-Operator.)\\n- **Principal** — the human authority: intent source, escalation resolution, acceptance.\\n- **Scheduler / Capacity** — the policy engine deciding where work runs; capacity (incl. vendor quota) is its resource, never semantics.\\n- **Lane / Lane Requirement / Lane Binding** — execution context instance / contract declaration / dispatch record. A lane is not a backend.\\n- **Execution Backend / Agent Runtime** — crash-only adapter behind the submit/admit seam / the harness inside a lane (named only in `backends/`).\\n- **Provenance Ledger** — append-only memory (pass runs, gate results, staleness events, plans, escalations); records are not artifacts and are never consulted for authority.\\n- **Target State** — a named, versioned predicate over the artifact graph.\\n\\n\\\"Workflow\\\" and \\\"Operator\\\" are retired terms. Do not use them. Full glossary, conventions N1–N11, invariants P1–P11, and the retired-terms table: RFC 0001.\\n\\n## Architectural Rules\\n\\n- The artifact graph + provenance ledger are the system of record; every runtime store is derived and rebuildable (Derived-State Doctrine, D0002.C2).\\n- Passes produce; gates permit; the Driver transitions; the scheduler places (P4).\\n- Backends submit; the Driver admits. Nothing is true until admitted through gates.\\n- Every artifact version has exactly one producing pass run; hand-authored artifacts are refused (P1). World-authored change enters via the `observation` pass.\\n- One invalidation algebra: content-hash pins; eager transitive marking; lazy demand-driven regeneration; revalidation before regeneration; no gate passes over a stale input.\\n- Claims are computed from evidence bindings, never stored as truth.\\n- Every durable concept is exactly one of: artifact (in one role), compiler pass, pipeline, scheduler policy, execution backend capability, quality gate, provenance record type (P2).\\n- Prefer strengthening existing ontology over introducing new ontology. Before adding a term, concept, or abstraction, check whether an accepted one already has the home and strengthen that instead; a genuinely new durable concept enters only via an RFC amendment (N8) and must never shadow an existing home (P2).\\n- A capability is fully admitted only when implemented, justified, and explained — Product Artifacts, the accepted Decision Record, and canonical Diátaxis documentation are complementary projections of one admitted change, each through the existing gates (P11); implementation never silently outruns explanation. Documentation is part of the artifact graph, not commentary.\\n\\n## The Decision Layer\\n\\nThe RFC is the design conversation. The accepted semantic state lives in `decisions/`: one record per RFC identity, generated by the `decision-generation` pass on every accepted-stage transition, never hand-written, with element structure for element-grain linking. Downstream work links against decisions, not RFC prose. Stale records degrade gracefully (last-accepted + recorded deviation); revoked records fail closed. Acceptance of decision records is Principal authority; delegating it requires an RFC.\\n\\n## Boundaries\\n\\n**Driver** owns artifact-state inspection, target planning, pass selection, scheduling invocation, gate enforcement, invalidation, provenance linkage, escalation. It never performs engineering work, produces artifacts, or overrides gates. Do not make the Driver intelligent; if it seems to need judgment, a declaration is underspecified.\\n\\n**Scheduler** decides where work runs (pass requirements, backend capabilities, quality, latency, context, independence, capacity, reset horizons, cost, history, repository policy). It never redefines semantics. Model choice is scheduler policy. Backend facts enter semantics only as declared capability facts (e.g. aliasing class) read by declared rules (e.g. independence).\\n\\n**Execution backends** are crash-only and replaceable: sealed work in; results + evidence submitted, or nothing. All supervision mechanics stay inside the adapter. Vendor harnesses never define the artifact model, pass semantics, provenance model, or lifecycle.\\n\\n**Capacity policy** maximizes useful engineering work, converting expiring capacity into durable evidence via cataloged `review`/`verification` posture parameterizations (adversarial review, second-opinion verification, doc freshness, test-gap analysis, dependency audit, stale-artifact scan, plan critique, coherence scan). No fake work. Capacity pressure never touches check/review gates or claim minting.\\n\\n## Product Boundary\\n\\nStriatum-next is a local-first engineering-intent compiler. No hosted services, cloud persistence, external telemetry, or vendor lock-in without an explicit RFC. Artifacts and provenance are durable; backends are replaceable.\\n\\n## Documentation Discipline\\n\\nDiátaxis. `docs/explanation/` explains why; `docs/concepts/` defines what (one page per term); `docs/tutorials/` teaches; `docs/how-to/` shows procedures; `docs/reference/` points at contracts and never restates them. Contracts live once: in `catalog/` and `schema/`.\\n\\n## RFC Discipline\\n\\nOne RFC identity per architectural decision:\\n\\n```text\\nrfcs/000N-topic/\\n    proposal.md        # intent\\n    design.md          # what should exist and why\\n    implementation.md  # how it is built / encoded\\ndecisions/D000N-topic.md   # generated: the accepted semantic state\\n```\\n\\nDo not allocate a new RFC number for implementation planning unless it introduces a genuinely new architectural decision. Terms used in RFCs must exist in RFC 0001 or arrive via an explicit Language Amendment section (N8).\\n\\n## Change Discipline\\n\\n- Architecture changes amend RFCs and regenerate decision records.\\n- Artifact shapes change → update `schema/`. IRs, passes, gates, target states change → update `catalog/`.\\n- Scheduling behavior changes → update `policy/`. Backend assumptions change → update `backends/`.\\n- Keep examples current. Do not leave stale documentation behind architecture changes.\\n\\n## Forbidden Patterns\\n\\n- No hidden lifecycle state; no state in terminal output, branch names, marker files, or chat transcripts (P10).\\n- No stored pipeline status; positions and target states are computed predicates.\\n- No artifacts without provenance; no hand-written decision records.\\n- No duplicated canonical definitions.\\n- No coupling of passes to backends; no model names outside `backends/`.\\n- No scheduler policy redefining compiler semantics; no capacity pressure on gates or claims.\\n- No second invalidation mechanism; no second recovery verb.\\n- No preserved legacy abstractions without translation into the compiler ontology.\\n\\n## Development\\n\\nGo project, Go-native layout:\\n\\n```text\\ncmd/\\ninternal/\\ndocs/\\nrfcs/\\ndecisions/\\ncatalog/\\nschema/\\npolicy/\\nbackends/\\nexamples/\\ntestdata/\\ntools/\\n```\\n\\nNo Python runtime scaffolding. Those changes may be proposed by humans, LLMs, shell scripts, Terraform, Kubernetes, Ansible, or any other capability provider. Capability providers do not define truth. They propose changes. The compiler decides what becomes true.\\n\\nThe purpose of Striatum is to transform arbitrary nondeterministic capability into deterministic engineering. Capability providers may retry, improve, drift, fail, or be replaced without changing the semantics of the compilation. Correctness moves out of the capability providers and into the compilation process.\\n\\nThe compiler does not orchestrate intelligent systems. It compiles the outputs of arbitrary nondeterministic capability providers into a deterministic, provenance-preserving artifact graph.\\n\\nCapabilities belong to the backends, never the compiler. Desired state belongs to the subject, never the capability. A compilation request names a subject and a target state. What the available capabilities can do shapes only the path, never the destination.\\n\\nThis repository contains the compiler product. The history of building the compiler belongs to the compiler instance, not the compiler product, and lives in the companion striatum-instance repository (Discovery 0019).\\n\\n## Current Capability\\n\\nThe compiler is self-hosting. It compiles and verifies its own architectural evolution, compiles independent repositories through the same artifact model, and supports a fleet of repositories with deterministic graph evolution. The architecture is fixed by fifteen accepted RFCs, in force through generated decision records. (RFC 0015, Fleet Knowledge, is in flight; its number is reserved.)\\n\\n| RFC | Decision | Owns |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| [0001](rfcs/0001-language-specification/design.md) | [D0004](decisions/D0004-compiler-passes.md) | the eleven-pass catalog, contract schema, replay doctrine |\\n| [0005](rfcs/0005-artifact-lifecycle-and-state-machine/design.md) | SCF-1 ledger, object store, admission funnel, locks, anchors |\\n| [0010](rfcs/0010-work-graph-execution/design.md) | [D0010](decisions/D0010-work-graph-execution.md) | lease-free execution, verifier uid isolation |\\n| [0013](rfcs/0013-adapter-supervision/design.md) | [D0013](decisions/D0013-adapter-supervision.md) | forked per-dispatch supervision, fate-bound runtime trees, detached lanes |\\n| [0014](rfcs/0014-cross-repository-compilation/design.md) | [D0014](decisions/D0014-cross-repository-compilation.md) | the fleet: repo-qualified pins resolved through Foreign Head Attestations |\\n| [0016](rfcs/0016-graduated-acceptance/design.md) | [D0016](decisions/D0016-graduated-acceptance.md) | graduated acceptance: the three IR acceptance gates close under deterministic policy on unanimous clean review; authority never delegated past the constitution |\\n\\nThe compiler has progressed through the conceptual foundation, runtime foundation, self-hosting, and fleet architecture. Those milestones are historical properties of the bootstrap instance, not the compiler product. Forward work is represented only as desired states in `catalog/target-states/`. The Principal names the next one.\\n\\n## The Architecture in Five Sentences\\n\\nArtifacts are the system of record. They are content-addressed, provenance-bearing, and exist in four roles: Intermediate Representation, Decision Record, Evidence, and Product Artifact.\\n\\nTransform passes lower intent through explicit intermediate representations while analysis passes attach evidence. Gates (check, review, and acceptance) determine every accepted-head movement. Claims (`Verified \\u003e Asserted \\u003e Designed`) are computed from evidence bindings and decay automatically when their supporting evidence changes.\\n\\nThe Driver is a deterministic program that plans toward target-state predicates and admits what crash-only execution backends submit. The scheduler determines placement under capacity policy and never changes meaning.\\n\\nThe decision layer is the compiler's canonical architectural memory. RFCs are the design conversation. Generated decision records are the accepted semantic state.\\n\\n## Reading Path\\n\\n1. `docs/explanation/striatum-as-compiler-for-engineering-intent.md` — why\\n2. `docs/concepts/language-specification.md` — the language\\n3. `decisions/index.md` — what is in force\\n4. `rfcs/INDEX.md` — the conversations behind it\\n5. `AGENTS.md` — working rules for humans and agents in this repository\\n\\n## Build\\n\\n```sh\\nmake build\\nmake check\\n```\\n\\n`make build` produces the `striatum` CLI together with the backend and tooling binaries under `bin/`.\\n\\nThe runtime is fully operational. Every durable compiler concept has exactly one machine-read entry here — the driver parses these files as its world model. (There is no whole-catalog schema validator; the record-type registry is the one governed sub-catalog, and `lint-rfcs` enforces the retired-term / model-name / N-P self-law over it.) Documentation links to catalog entries; it never restates them.\\n\\n## Contents\\n\\n- `artifact-kinds/` — the twelve artifact kinds, classified by role: IR, decision, evidence, product. A thirteenth requires an RFC. (RFC 0003)\\n- `irs/` — the six-level lowering ladder, L0–L5; thin pointers into `artifact-kinds/`. (RFC 0003)\\n- `passes/` — the eleven compiler pass contracts. A twelfth requires an RFC; scheduling is not a pass. (RFC 0004)\\n- `gates/` — the quality gates, each exactly one class: check, review, or acceptance. (RFCs 0003, 0005)\\n- `target-states/` — named, versioned predicates over the artifact graph. Gate results pin the predicate version they were evaluated under. (RFC 0005)\\n- `pipelines/` — catalog-resident composition of passes, gate wiring, and re-run bounds; populated in Epoch 2. the hint both postdates kill-domain readiness and precedes exit 0, so acceptance is never abort-visible without a *usable* kill handle on disk. The four-verb contract, bundle schemas, rename-only commit, typed refusal set, and A1–A8 are unchanged; the Epoch 3 synchronous bound is closed (its trigger, lane concurrency mattering, has arrived and is retired with it). Acceptance stays durable: after exit 0, a submission eventually commits or the run is closed from above; the backend owes no recovery. Process mechanics (setsid with a child-ready handshake, parent-established process groups, double-fork, groups, namespaces) are adapter-internal and non-normative provided the readiness property holds; the supervision entry point is not a fifth verb.\\n- **D0013.C2 — The Lane Supervisor owns the dispatch lifecycle.** For exactly one dispatch: runtime invocation from the sealed bundle, confined to the supervisor's session and process group and fate-bound per C10; the bounded internal-relaunch loop with pristine workspace reset (A2, `internal_retry.max`, recorded as `internal_relaunches`) — this names what supervises internal relaunches; pre-submission validation and shape repair; sealed submission assembly, fsync, and the rename commit (A4); the post-commit wake with bounded exit-4 retry; wall-clock enforcement as mechanics; self-termination and residue cleanup. The supervisor never writes the Supervisor Hint — that is the verb's act. A5/A6/A7 hold for the supervisor verbatim; everything it needs rides the sealed bundle.\\n- **D0013.C3 — Nothing supervises the supervisor.** A dead supervisor is a lapsed dispatch, recovered above the seam solely by the existing chain — dispatch horizon → `dispatch_lapse` → provisional abandonment → closure-then-new-run re-dispatch → winner rule. No watchdog, relauncher, pidfile poller, or resident recovery machinery may exist **as contract, as a recovery authority for the Lane Supervisor, or as anything readable above the seam**; adapter-internal process mechanics that neither relaunch nor recover a dead supervisor and create no registry readable above the seam remain lawful where the S-rules pass. Kernel-mediated fate-sharing (C10) is launch plumbing, not a supervision rung: it watches nothing and recovers nothing. Kill -9 at any instant is a legal conformance test and leaves committed-or-nothing.\\n- **D0013.C4 — Wall-clock ownership order.** (a) The adapter's invocation limit bounds one runtime invocation; expiry feeds the relaunch loop as a `runtime_crash` diagnostic. (b) The manifest's advisory `abort_after_s` (else an adapter-block default) is the supervisor's whole-dispatch budget, enforced as mechanics; on expiry the supervisor kills the runtime and best-effort commits a `failed` submission carrying diagnostics, usage hints, and full attribution — never owed, since a killed supervisor lawfully leaves nothing. (c) The Driver's dispatch horizon is affirmed as the only wall-clock with semantics above the seam, and those semantics remain observation-then-provisional-adjudication. (d) Enforcer death is not an enforcement gap: by C10 a dead supervisor implies a dead runtime tree, so no supervisor clock ever needs a survivor to enforce it; the horizon is the only clock that outlives the supervisor, which is precisely its role. The budget is likewise what bounds any lane `abort` cannot stop (C5). No supervisor clock is ever a semantic deadline; the diagnostics vocabulary does not grow.\\n- **D0013.C5 — Abort reaches detached work through the Supervisor Hint; the hint is never published before its kill domain is signalable; and the hint's loss or failure is priced, not papered over.** The dispatch verb writes `advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/supervisor.json` (pid, process group, start token guarding pid reuse) after fork, **after the named process group exists and is verified signalable**, and before exit 0; the supervisor never writes or rewrites it. `abort` verifies the token and signals the group (TERM, bounded grace, KILL) — reaching the runtime, which C10 confines to that group — then reclaims workspace and advisory residue. A **verifying token whose named kill domain cannot be signaled** is a failed abort over a live lane: `abort` reclaims nothing, deletes nothing, reports incompleteness, and stays idempotent — never cleanup, never a completeness claim; a conforming adapter cannot produce this state (S1), but abort's behavior in it is defined against defect and hostility alike. A **present but unverifiable** hint yields residue cleanup that is complete by C10: the supervisor it names is dead and its runtime tree died with it. An **absent** hint yields residue cleanup that is complete when the dispatch was never accepted or has already concluded, and **partial when the hint was deleted out from under a live lane**: that lane continues unreached — lawfully, because `abort` is advisory and nothing above the seam depends on it succeeding, and boundedly, by the lane's dispatch budget (C4b) below the seam and the horizon, abandonment, and winner rule above it. The verb stays advisory, idempotent, unknown-id-safe, and never touches a committed submission. The hint is an Advisory Signal: non-authoritative, deletable at will, janitor-reclaimable, never read above the seam, never enumerable as a registry — and deleting it costs `abort` its reach over that lane's remaining budget window, never correctness.\\n- **D0013.C6 — In-flight accounting and concurrency enforcement stay above the seam.** The scheduler learns what is running from `lane_binding` versus submission/closure records, never from process liveness; `concurrency.max_lanes` binds in the scheduler's hard-constraint filter and is now load-bearing. Adapters never count their own processes and gain no concurrency refusal code; over-dispatch is a promptness bug, never a correctness hazard.\\n- **D0013.C7 — The wake convention is exercised unchanged.** The supervisor fires the non-authoritative wake after rename, retries boundedly on exit 4, and may abandon safely; the standing timer and the post-quiescence spool re-scan remain the liveness floor. Drive sessions dispatch and quiesce promptly; the drive lease is held for verbs, never for lane execution.\\n- **D0013.C8 — Supervision conformance rules S1–S7** extend the per-adapter suite: S1 detachment with kill-domain readiness and hint ordering (exit 0 follows the hint write, which follows a verified-signalable kill domain; an abort issued immediately after acceptance kills), S2 kill-at-any-instant two-states **split by who dies** (supervisor death leaves no surviving lane-tree process, per S7; runtime-only death lawfully feeds the relaunch loop within `internal_retry.max`, with no extinction assertion while the supervisor lives), S3 limit-kill failed-or-nothing, S4 abort quaternity — kill on a verified hint with signalable domain, tested to the earliest accepted instant; cleanup asserted complete on a stale hint; cleanup asserted honestly partial on a hint deleted over a live lane; failure asserted, with nothing reclaimed, on a verifying token whose domain cannot be signaled — with committed submissions untouched on every branch, S5 duplicate-dispatch idempotence with single rename winner, S6 hint non-semantics (semantic invariance under advisory deletion, with abort degradation acknowledged as S4's third branch), S7 fate-sharing (supervisor death kills the runtime tree, descendant-spawning fake included, within harness grace; daemonizing runtimes are non-conforming). A1–A8 remain D0007's and are unmodified.\\n- **D0013.C9 — No new records; hardening unforeclosed.** This design demonstrates no owned-record gap: D0007.C10's four record types stand, and no new ledger record, verb, lease, heartbeat, session table, or recovery verb is introduced. Detachment changes process ancestry, not credentials: rung-2 uid isolation lands on this shape as credential and ownership changes only, per D0012.C4.\\n- **D0013.C10 — The runtime shares the supervisor's fate, as a tree property.** No runtime process outlives its Lane Supervisor beyond kernel teardown (a mechanics grace measured in seconds, never horizon-scale) — grandchildren and helpers included. The supervisor confines every runtime invocation to its own session and process group and binds its whole tree kernel-mediated to its own life. Reference mechanics are tiered and non-normative provided S7 passes: parent-death signaling on the direct child suffices only for genuinely single-process runtimes; whenever the runtime may spawn descendants — the default assumption — tree-capable containment is required, with the reference composition a private PID namespace whose init carries the parent-death signal (namespace teardown kills every descendant with no surviving actor needed); cgroup kill is lawful where an actor exists at teardown. Fate-sharing is a property of how work is started, not a resident watcher: it introduces no supervision rung, no registry, and no reader above the seam. Adapters must invoke runtimes as one-shot, headless, non-daemonizing CLIs; a runtime that detaches from the supervisor's confinement is an S7 conformance defect — and even then a resource-consumption problem only, never a semantic hazard: it has no path to an admissible commit, and committed-or-nothing holds above the seam in every case.\\n\\n## Consequences\\n\\nDeclared concurrency becomes real: divergent topologies execute their lanes simultaneously, and the scheduler's slot and write-scope arithmetic binds against work that is actually in flight. Drive sessions return to quiescence in seconds — the Driver is again an invoked program, with promptness carried by wakes and the standing timer rather than by a lease held hostage to vendor wall-clock. Lane lifetime decouples from Driver lifetime: a session crash orphans nothing and kills nothing. `abort` stops work instead of only sweeping residue — its kill handle is on disk *and signalable* before acceptance is even visible, its cleanup-only path is complete wherever a hint survives to be verified, the one branch where the kill itself can fail (a verifying hint aiming at nothing — producible only by defect or hostility) is a reported failure with residue retained rather than a silent false success, and the one branch where it cannot stop work (a hint deleted out from under a live lane) is named and priced — bounded by the lane's own dispatch budget and the horizon — rather than silently claimed complete. Limit-kills convert what were silent lapses into `failed` submissions with diagnostics and usage facts, closing runs a drain earlier and feeding the capacity estimator. No process outlives the lane that justified it: a SIGKILLed supervisor takes its entire runtime tree with it, descendants included, leaving no ghost burning vendor budget while the horizon lapses and re-dispatches around it — while a crashed runtime under a living supervisor feeds the relaunch loop exactly as designed, and the conformance suite now distinguishes the two instead of outlawing the second. The wake convention, the horizon sweep, provisional abandonment, and the winner rule — all previously idle or degenerate under synchronous dispatch — are now exercised on every LLM lane, which means the conformance suite finally tests the architecture that was designed rather than a serialization of it. The costs: one new adapter-internal moving part (the detached supervisor), one synchronization on the dispatch path (kill-domain readiness confirmed before the hint write — a pipe read or a `setpgid`, milliseconds against a lane's hours), one new advisory file shape written by the verb, one runtime-shape obligation (one-shot, non-daemonizing CLIs, kernel-fate-bound as a tree), and one honestly-priced degradation (advisory deletion downgrades abort's kill to cleanup) — all crash-only, all reclaimable, all bounded, none visible to the core.\\n\\n## Constrains\\n\\nAll LLM adapter implementations and their four-verb process surfaces (`internal/backend/llm`, the three `cmd/striatum-backend-*` surfaces, and any fifth backend joining under RFC 0007's evolution walkthrough), including each adapter's choice and configuration of runtime CLI, which must satisfy the one-shot non-daemonizing shape and the tree-wide fate-sharing property (D0013.C10), and each adapter's dispatch verb, which must establish and verify the supervisor's signalable kill domain and write the Supervisor Hint after fork and before exit 0, in that order (D0013.C1/C5); each adapter's `abort` verb, which must treat a verifying token whose kill domain cannot be signaled as a failed abort over a live lane — residue retained, nothing reclaimed (D0013.C5); the conformance suite under `tools/` (S1–S7 join the per-adapter obligations, with S1 asserting kill-domain readiness at exit 0, S2 split by who dies, S4 exercising all four abort branches, and S7's harness exercising descendant-spawning fakes); the Driver's dispatch step (must treat exit 0 as durable acceptance and must not block on execution) and its abort issuance under the winner rule (which remains courtesy ordering, aware that a deleted hint lawfully degrades the kill to cleanup and that a reported abort failure over a live lane is bounded by that lane's budget and horizon, not retried into a guarantee); the scheduler's treatment of `concurrency.max_lanes` as a live binding constraint; the `advisory/` subtree's contents (the Supervisor Hint joins the pulse as the only sanctioned shapes; the hint is verb-written, the pulse supervisor-written); and the RFC 0012 rung-2 enforcement work, which must land on this shape as credentials-only changes and must not break kernel fate-delivery (no setuid runtime binaries on the lane path).\\n\",\n    \"decisions/D0014-cross-repository-compilation.md\": \"# D0014 — Cross-Repository Compilation\\n\\n- **Status:** Accepted\\n- **Owning RFC:** [RFC 0014 — Cross-Repository Compilation](../rfcs/0014-cross-repository-compilation/design.md)\\n- **Decided:** 2026-07-03 (Multi-Repository Compilation Pass)\\n- **Generated by:** `decision-generation` (Principal-accepted)\\n- **Pins:** proposal `0d1d16b0008cccaa` · design `8fcef24439c921e1` · implementation `1483d8fd8f48c855`\\n\\n## Decision (clauses)\\n\\n- **D0014.C1 — The cross-repository pin is D0009's repo-qualified pin; nothing new is minted.** A compilation whose intent originates in repository A may require or produce artifacts bound to repository B by a **cross-repository pin** — the repo-qualified pin D0009 already fixed (`artifact_pin := {repo_id?, identity, version_seq?, content_hash}`; `repo_id` absent ⇒ the local graph). RFC 0014 adds no pin kind, no artifact role, and no invalidation algebra (P2/N11; P holds). A cross-repository compilation is **linked per-repository compilations exchanging repo-qualified pins** (D0009 design): each compilation admits into its own repository's graph, each is governed by its own repository's policy (D0002.C8), and the single graph-of-record per repository stands (D0009.C1) — there is no cross-repository graph and no shared mutable store. `store.Pin` gains the one optional `repo_id` field the grammar already specifies; every existing record is byte-identical under absent-⇒-omitted encoding, so the golden corpus does not drift (D0009.C5).\\n- **D0014.C2 — Cross-graph freshness resolves on the gate path against a Foreign Head Attestation, never a live read (refines D0009.C8; extends D0010.C11 across graphs).** A **Foreign Head Attestation** is the Exogenous Change Record evidence kind (D0001) with a typed body capturing one foreign accepted head — `{ repo_id, identity, content_hash, foreign_ledger_seq, seal_domain, as_of }` — admitted into the *local* graph by the observation pass with an `evidences` edge to the head it attests. The live cross-graph read that produces an attestation happens exclusively at **planning**, off the gate path, demand-driven for the pins a plan touches (the laziness D0009.C8 names). The **gate and admission** path reads only the locally-admitted attestation — content-addressed, execution-free, no foreign read — so D0010.C11 holds across graphs by construction. D0009.C8's \\\"lazy at plan/gate time\\\" stands: the attestation is how it is lazy at gate time; only D0009 design's \\\"gate evaluation\\\" as a *live-read* site is struck, superseded by this clause.\\n- **D0014.C3 — Cross-repository pin freshness rides the one invalidation algebra (P).** A cross-repository pin `{repo_id: B, identity: X, content_hash: H}` is fresh iff the latest Foreign Head Attestation admitted locally for `(B, X)` reports content hash `H` — the existing `PinFresh` algebra resolving the local attestation-stream head over one indirection, never a cross-graph read. A moved foreign head is admitted at planning as a fresh attestation reporting `H' ≠ H`; its admission fires a staleness wave with `cause.kind: exogenous` (D0009), decaying every local claim bound to the stale cross-repository pin exactly as any head movement does. No second invalidation mechanism, no cross-graph event routing (marking stays graph-local; D0009.C8); revalidation-before-regeneration and \\\"no gate over a stale input\\\" apply unchanged.\\n- **D0014.C4 — A change under an intent concerning A integrates into B's product lineage under the guard, held across graphs (extends D0010.C8/C11).** Integration is D0010.C8's deterministic topological linking, unchanged, executed against **repository B's** Graph Store: E2 realized at admission in B (lanes only stage), B's product ref moved under B's gate-passing transition with `tree_moved` compare-and-set. The producing intent (A) and the integrating admission (B) are bound by the cross-repository pin (C1) and the Foreign Head Attestation that resolves it (C2). The **execution-independence guard (D0010.C11) is held across graphs**: the trusted core stays execution-free for cross-graph resolution (hash comparison, no foreign read, no exec); an adversarial or nondeterministic lane can never admit an invalid cross-repository pin (a forged or stale attestation resolves to *stale*, never a spurious accept); and the admitted cross-repository result is invariant to execution noise. The standing guard gains cross-graph fences.\\n- **D0014.C5 — The cross-repository trust boundary trusts B's seal domain exactly as far as B warrants; the v1 domain is not widened (affirms D0012).** A Foreign Head Attestation captures B's seal domain; the local graph trusts it under the v1 keyed-seal discipline (D0012.C2). Within one workstation's data-home every registered graph shares the single-OS-user trust domain (D0009.C10, D0012.C5), so a same-workstation cross-repository pin is crash-evidence, exactly as a local pin, and adds no trust surface — the v1 reach is a fleet under one workstation's trust domain. A cross-**workstation** attestation (a foreign graph under a different OS-user or host trust domain) is refused in v1 and named as a rung-3 external-anchoring deferral (D0012.C1); the single-OS-user trust statement is not silently widened. Rung-2 uid isolation lands on this shape as credentials-only changes (D0012.C4).\\n- **D0014.C6 — No new record types, verbs, or leases; scheduling is unamended; the corpus ratchet holds.** The Foreign Head Attestation is the existing exogenous-change-record kind produced by the existing observation pass — no new artifact kind, ledger record type, verb, or lease (D0009.C5's registry unchanged; the golden corpus does not drift). The one governed addition is the attestation's evidence-body schema under `schema/` (a versioned artifact-body kind, not a ledger record type) and the optional `repo_id` pin field D0009 already spec'd. Repository-scoped placement needs no amendment: D0008.C3 folds capacity over all graphs and D0008.C6 makes repository policy a placement input; the scheduler stays D0008.C1's pure function with a run's target repository as one more content-addressed input. Constitutional decisions remain read from the compiler repository's graph, failing closed only on revocation or absence (D0009.C8).\\n\\n## Consequences\\n\\nThe compiler's reach becomes a fleet under one workstation's trust domain: a change worked under an intent in one repository is verified and integrated into another's product lineage under that repository's closed gates and Principal acceptance, with provenance bound across the two by content. Every guarantee that made single-repository compilation sound holds across graphs unchanged — execution-free admission (the gate path never reads a foreign graph), one invalidation algebra (cross-graph freshness is the existing algebra over a local attestation), the single graph-of-record per repository (linked compilations exchange pins; neither writes the other's truth), and honest trust bounds (same-workstation crash-evidence; cross-workstation refused and named). The costs are minimal and all strengthenings: one optional pin field (already in the grammar), one evidence-body schema (an existing evidence kind, typed), one plan-time observation that admits attestations, and cross-graph cases added to the standing guard. No new ledger record type, no new verb, no second invalidation mechanism, no scheduler, and no widening of the trust domain enter the system.\\n\\n## Constrains\\n\\nThe pin type and its admission/fold encoding (`internal/store/admission.go` `Pin`, `internal/driver/fold.go` `pinsOf`), which surface the optional `repo_id` without drifting the golden corpus; the fold's freshness algebra (`PinFresh`/`FreshnessPins`), which resolves a cross-repository pin against the local Foreign Head Attestation stream and never reads a foreign graph on the gate path; the observation pass and the Driver's planner, which perform the sole lawful live cross-graph read at planning and admit attestations off the gate path; the Foreign Head Attestation evidence-body schema under `schema/`; cross-repository integration against a foreign Graph Store (D0010.C8 mechanics, B-owned product ref, `tree_moved` CAS); the standing execution-independence guard (`internal/driver/soundness_guard_test.go`), which gains cross-graph adversarial and metamorphic fences; the workstation registry as the sole cross-graph resolver (`internal/store/registry.go`); and the trust-claim prose discipline for every cross-repository document (same-workstation crash-evidence; cross-workstation refused until rung 3).\\n\",\n    \"decisions/D0016-graduated-acceptance.md\": \"# D0016 — Graduated Acceptance\\n\\n- **Status:** Accepted\\n- **Owning RFC:** [RFC 0016 — Graduated Acceptance](../rfcs/0016-graduated-acceptance/design.md)\\n- **Decided:** 2026-07-07 (Graduated-Acceptance Pass)\\n- **Generated by:** `decision-generation` (Principal-accepted)\\n- **Pins:** proposal `929574e033316dc7` · design `dfa6bffdbb3a0ffb` · implementation `fe94278098676308`\\n\\n## Decision (clauses)\\n\\n- **C1 — The grant.** Graduated acceptance is a delegation class over exactly `proposal-acceptance`, `design-acceptance`, and `implementation-plan-acceptance`. A decision record is the accepted semantic state of the system. When a pass, a lane, or an operator needs to know what the architecture **is**, it reads decisions. When it needs to know **why**, it reads the owning RFC.\\n\\nEach record captures one architectural decision in force and points to the RFC identity that produced it.\\n\\n## Decision Records Are Generated Artifacts\\n\\nA decision record is the output of the `decision-generation` compiler pass. It is never hand-written.\\n\\n```text\\nRFC Proposal\\n    ↓\\nRFC Design\\n    ↓\\nRFC Implementation\\n    ↓\\nDecision Generator Pass\\n    ↓\\nDecision Record\\n```\\n\\n- The pass consumes an RFC identity's accepted stages and derives the record mechanically, regenerating on every accepted-stage transition; the record pins the exact stage hashes it was generated from.\\n- Records carry element structure (clauses `D000N.CX`) so downstream work links at element grain.\\n- Hand-editing a decision record is refused at admission: a version with no producing pass run violates provenance totality (RFC 0005, W4).\\n- When an owning RFC changes, its record goes stale and is regenerated; consumers may continue against the last-accepted version under a recorded deviation — only **revoked** records fail closed.\\n- Acceptance of a decision record is a human (Principal) authority in Epoch 1; delegating it requires an RFC, never a policy edit.\\n\\nThe generating pass is cataloged at [`catalog/passes/decision-generation.yaml`](../catalog/passes/decision-generation.yaml). Decision-record acceptance, rejection, escalation resolution, override, and agent-principal acceptance authority are never in scope; attribution is honest (`delegation_ref` + condition-pinning `authority_proof`); the retrospective queue, RFC-free kill switch, mandatory expiry, and D0016 decision pin guard the grant. Zero new nouns: an instance of RFC 0006's delegation model. (RFC 0015, Fleet Knowledge, remains in flight — record numbering keeps the RFC correspondence, so D0015 arrives when it is accepted.)\\n\\n## Conventions\\n\\n- One record per RFC identity, numbered to match (`D000N` ↔ `rfcs/000N-topic/`).\\n- Records state the decision and its consequences; rationale and alternatives live in the owning RFC's `design.md`.\\n- Records are outputs of the `decision-generation` pass and are replaced, not edited, when regenerated.\\n\",\n    \"docs/concepts/agent-principal.md\": \"# Agent Principal\\n\\nPurpose: define the Agent Principal.\\n\\nAn agent runtime exercising a recorded, bounded delegation of Principal-issuable acts — request issuance and cancellation, and named escalation-resolution classes. Each lowering level removes a named class of ambiguity.\\n\\nThe six IRs: Intent Statement (L0), Proposal (L1), Design (L2), Implementation Plan (L3), Work Graph (L4), Change Set (L5). Product (L6) is a designation over product artifacts, not an IR. This rendering never diverges from it. Terms not defined there and not in its Retired Terms appendix do not exist. Accepted semantic state: [D0001](../../decisions/D0001-language-specification.md). One page per major term lives beside this file; see the [concepts index](index.md).\\n\\n## The Layered Ontology\\n\\nEvery term belongs to exactly one layer.\\n\\n| Layer | Concern | Terms |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| SUBJECT | what compilation is about | Artifact (supertype) and its four roles: IR · Decision Record · Evidence · Product Artifact |\\n| TRANSFORM | what changes subjects | Compiler Pass · Pass Run · Run Manifest · Pipeline |\\n| JUDGMENT | what permits state transitions | Quality Gate (Check · Review · Acceptance) · Verdict · Claim · Claim Level |\\n| AGENCY | who or what does the work | Principal · Driver · Scheduler · Lane · Execution Backend · Agent Runtime |\\n| MEMORY | what remembers everything | Provenance Ledger · Provenance Record · Attribution |\\n\\nTwo load-bearing structural decisions: the SUBJECT layer has one supertype (Artifact) with four disjoint roles; and the MEMORY layer is not part of the SUBJECT layer — provenance records are not artifacts, and the ledger is never a pass input for lowering.\\n\\n## Glossary\\n\\nDefinitions are compressed to their leading sentences; RFC 0001 is complete and controlling.\\n\\n### Subject layer\\n\\n- **Artifact** — a durable, versioned, provenance-bearing unit of record in the artifact graph, produced by exactly one pass run and immutable at each version. Every artifact plays exactly one role.\\n- **Artifact Graph** — the directed graph of artifact versions and their typed edges; with the provenance ledger, the system of record. One graph per target repository.\\n- **Artifact Version** — one immutable revision of an artifact identity, linked to its predecessor by supersession.\\n- **Element Anchor** — a stable, schema-defined address of one element inside an artifact; pins and evidence bindings may bind at element grain.\\n- **Intermediate Representation (IR)** — an artifact role: an artifact class whose purpose is consumption by a downstream pass. Each lowering level removes a named class of ambiguity.\\n- **Intent** — a human goal before formal engineering begins. Informal; not an artifact.\\n- **Intent Statement** — the L0 source IR: the first durable, verbatim capture of an intent. Never edited, only superseded.\\n- **Proposal** — the L1 IR: problem, motivation, candidate direction. Removes problem-framing ambiguity.\\n- **Design** — the L2 IR: what should exist, why, invariants, interfaces, semantics, tradeoffs. Removes architectural ambiguity.\\n- **Implementation Plan** — the L3 IR: phases, milestones, packet decomposition, verification strategy. Removes execution-strategy ambiguity; never relitigates the design.\\n- **Work Graph** — the L4 IR: the machine-oriented dependency graph of work packets derived from an accepted implementation plan. Removes schedulability ambiguity.\\n- **Work Packet** — a node of the Work Graph: the smallest unit of engineering work executable by a single pass run without interactive clarification.\\n- **Change Set** — the L5 IR: one work packet's bounded output — a diff plus advisory lane-local evidence. The object file of this compiler; integration is the linker.\\n- **Product** — the target repository tree at the accepted versions of its product artifacts. A designation over artifacts, not an artifact.\\n- **Product Artifact** — an artifact role: a shipped result anchored by content hash into the target repository.\\n- **RFC Identity** — the namespace `rfcs/000N-topic/` grouping one intent's Proposal, Design, and Implementation Plan, plus its generated Decision Record. An identity, not an artifact.\\n- **Decision Record** — an artifact role: the binding, accepted semantic state distilled from an RFC identity by the decision-generation pass; never hand-written. The compiler's canonical architectural memory.\\n- **Evidence** — an artifact role: an immutable attestation of fact about another artifact or about the observed world. Never invalidated; its force decays when bound hashes change.\\n- **Review Ledger** — evidence: structured findings from one review pass run plus a summary Verdict. Gates evaluate predicates over ledgers, never prose.\\n- **Receipt** — the atomic evidence kind: a sealed, content-addressed record of one mechanical check execution, minted by a verifier lane and validated — never executed — by the trusted core.\\n- **Verification Report** — evidence aggregating the receipts and check outcomes for one artifact version against its pinned check identities.\\n- **Exogenous Change Record** — evidence recording world-authored change to a watched target, produced by the observation pass. The admission path for the world's writes.\\n- **Lifecycle State** — the stored position of one artifact version: `candidate → accepted → superseded | retired`. Everything else commonly called a \\\"state\\\" is a computed predicate.\\n- **Target State** — a named, versioned predicate over the artifact graph, defined in the catalog. You cannot declare a target state satisfied.\\n- **Compilation Request** — the Principal's command: (subject, target state, constraints).\\n- **Staleness** — the computed predicate: stale iff some pinned input's accepted head moved or the producing contract version changed invalidatingly. Stale is not wrong; it is unproven against the present.\\n- **Invalidation** — the propagation of staleness along derivation and environment edges. Marking is eager and transitive; regeneration is lazy and demand-driven.\\n- **Revalidation** — the early-cutoff analysis asking whether a stale artifact still satisfies its gates against the new upstream.\\n- **Re-stamp** — the driver-mechanical creation of a body-identical artifact version with moved pins, licensed by an accepting revalidation verdict; the single gate-exempt accepted-head movement.\\n- **Supersession** — replacement of an artifact version by a successor. Superseded versions were valid; stale ones are unproven.\\n\\n### Transform layer\\n\\n- **Compiler Pass** — a named, versioned transformation contract. Passes produce artifacts; they never move lifecycle states. Two classes: transform and analysis; scheduling is not a pass.\\n- **Pass Run** — one provenance-recorded execution of a pass against pinned input versions under a sealed run manifest.\\n- **Run Manifest** — the immutable record sealed at pass-run start: input pins, environment pins, contract version, lane requirements, prompt asset hashes.\\n- **Pipeline** — a catalog-resident template composing passes, gate wiring, and re-run bounds. No new semantics: a pipeline compiles to pass runs.\\n- **Lowering** — the direction of compilation: each transform pass consumes a higher-ambiguity representation and produces a lower-ambiguity one.\\n- **Revision** — a re-run of the producing pass with a Review Ledger as declared diagnostic input. There are no fix-passes.\\n- **Contract Version / Impl Version** — the two version fields of a pass. Contract bumps invalidate outputs; impl changes are recorded and invalidate nothing retroactively.\\n- **Determinism Class** — D0 (bit-replayable) · D1 (bit-replayable from transcript) · D2 (stochastic; provenance replay and contract replay only).\\n- **Effect Class** — E0 (graph-only) · E1 (isolated workspace) · E2 (target-repository integration; `integration` only) · E3 (external; forbidden without RFC).\\n\\n### Judgment layer\\n\\n- **Quality Gate** — a declared condition an artifact version must satisfy before an accepted-head movement. Every gate is exactly one class: check, review, or acceptance.\\n- **Check Gate** — verification-class: machine-decidable, deterministic, replayable evaluation of a declared contract against evidence. No judgment.\\n- **Review Gate** — validation-class: a predicate over a Review Ledger produced by an independent review pass run. Independence requirements attach here.\\n- **Acceptance Gate** — authority-class: the decision by the Principal, or explicitly delegated policy, that a version becomes the accepted head.\\n- **Verification / Validation / Acceptance** — the mechanical, judgment, and authority strata. Acceptance may require validation; validation may require verification; never sideways or backwards.\\n- **Verdict** — the closed review vocabulary: `accept`, `accept_with_findings` (accepting); `needs_revision`, `reject` (non-accepting).\\n- **Claim** — a falsifiable statement about an artifact version, carrying a claim level computed from evidence bindings.\\n- **Claim Level** — the lattice `Verified \\u003e Asserted \\u003e Designed`. Claims are computed views over evidence bindings, never stored truth.\\n- **Binding Closure** — the promotion rule: promoting evidence must bind the subject's hash and the accepted-head (or element) hashes of every governing IR.\\n- **Independence** — the anti-aliasing condition on Verified: the minting execution shares no provenance ancestry with the producing execution. Co-blindness is aliasing.\\n- **Posture** — a cataloged, versioned parameterization of the review pass, each owning its Review Ledger section schema.\\n\\n### Agency layer\\n\\n- **Principal** — the human authority: source of intent, resolution authority for escalations, default holder of acceptance authority. Not an execution role.\\n- **Driver** — the compiler driver: a deterministic program that inspects graph state, evaluates target predicates, plans, requests scheduling, evaluates gates, admits, propagates staleness, and escalates. Produces no artifacts; all outputs are ledger records.\\n- **Scheduler** — the policy engine deciding where work runs: binds lanes to execution backends under versioned policy. Its outputs are never semantic.\\n- **Capacity** — a scheduler resource dimension: any bounded, possibly-resetting supply of execution. Quota is the vendor-subscription kind; the word belongs to policy documents.\\n- **Lane** — an isolated execution context instantiated inside a pass run, with role, write scope, and independence constraints. Specification: Lane Requirement; placement: Lane Binding.\\n- **Execution Backend** — the crash-only adapter that launches agent runtimes into lanes: sealed work in; results submitted out, or nothing. Declares capabilities and an aliasing class.\\n- **Agent Runtime** — the concrete executable environment inside a lane. Named only inside backend definitions; a model name outside `backends/` is a lint error.\\n\\n### Memory layer\\n\\n- **Provenance** — the guaranteed property that every artifact's complete lineage is recorded and inspectable. Never consulted for authority.\\n- **Provenance Ledger** — the append-only substrate of provenance records, segmented into sealed, hash-anchored segments. Every record carries a `schema_version`.\\n- **Provenance Record** — one immutable ledger fact: pass-run record, gate result, staleness event, plan record, lane binding mirror, escalation, deviation warning, resolution event, segment manifest.\\n- **Escalation** — a ledger record signaling that compilation cannot proceed without the Principal, carrying a closed reason code. Unresolved, it blocks its subgraph.\\n- **Attribution** — the provenance fields identifying production: backend, agent runtime, lane role, prompt hashes, contract versions. Derived from recorded truth, never self-asserted.\\n- **Byline** — the rendered, privacy-safe projection of attribution embedded in a human-readable artifact.\\n\\n## Naming Conventions\\n\\n- **N1** — Target states and lifecycle predicates are past participles; stored lifecycle uses the closed set, `candidate` excepted.\\n- **N2** — Passes are kebab-case nominalized transformations; never named by actor, backend, or model.\\n- **N3** — IR classes are `\\u003cNoun\\u003e` with level; instances are named by identity.\\n- **N4** — Gates are `\\u003csubject\\u003e-\\u003cclass\\u003e`; the class is readable from the name.\\n- **N5** — Type/instance discipline: pass → pass run; decision → decision record; lane requirement → lane. No word names both.\\n- **N6** — Closed vocabularies stay closed; extension requires amending RFC 0001.\\n- **N7** — Banned morphology: no `meta-` prefixes; no manager-style agent nouns; no vendor or model names outside `backends/`; no humor in load-bearing names.\\n- **N8** — Definition before use: a term used in any RFC must exist in RFC 0001, or the RFC carries a Language Amendment section.\\n- **N9** — Retirement is explicit: terms leave only via the Retired Terms appendix, with disposition and replacement.\\n\\n## Conceptual Invariants\\n\\n- **P1 — Provenance totality.** Every artifact version has exactly one producing pass run; no artifact appears by hand; the Driver produces no artifacts.\\n- **P2 — Category exclusivity.** Every durable concept is exactly one of: artifact (in one role), compiler pass, pipeline, scheduler policy, execution backend capability, quality gate, provenance record type.\\n- **P3 — Provenance is memory, not subject.** The ledger is append-only; records are never versioned or invalidated; provenance records are not artifacts.\\n- **P4 — Passes produce; gates permit; the Driver transitions; the scheduler places.** No role crosses into another's verb.\\n- **P5 — Ambiguity monotonicity.** Each lowering pass leaves the compilation no more ambiguous about the subject intent and introduces no decision belonging to a higher level.\\n- **P6 — Claim soundness.** Levels are computed from evidence bindings; only minting gates with complete closure raise them; anything may lower them; Verified decays on bound-hash movement.\\n- **P7 — Gate trichotomy purity.** Every gate is exactly one of check/review/acceptance; no output type crosses classes.\\n- **P8 — Decisions are the link target.** Downstream work links against decision records, never RFC prose; only revoked records fail closed.\\n- **P9 — Backend independence.** No pass contract, IR schema, or gate names an execution backend or model.\\n- **P10 — No state outside the graph and ledger.** Terminal output, branch names, marker files, and chat transcripts are never state.\\n\\n## Epoch 2 Amendments (Runtime Foundation Pass)\\n\\nAccepted via the N8 mechanism as part of RFCs 0006–0010; [RFC 0001's Epoch 2 Amendments section](../../rfcs/0001-language-specification/design.md) is controlling. Full definitions live in the owning RFC's design; leading sentences here.\\n\\n### Escalation vocabulary (N6 extension)\\n\\nThe closed escalation reason set is fixed at eight codes: `ambiguous_goal`, `missing_authority`, `contradicting_decisions`, `committee_stalemate`, `override_required`, `bounds_exhausted`, `binding_unsatisfiable`, `independence_unsatisfiable`. The three new codes: `bounds_exhausted` — automation must stop retrying; the record's closed `budget_kind` field (`revision | redispatch | attempt_total | integration_conflict | withdrawal`) names the exhausted budget. `binding_unsatisfiable` — no capable backend exists for a lane requirement. `independence_unsatisfiable` — capable backends exist but anti-aliasing cannot be satisfied; a distinct resolution path (procure a different-family backend, not merely any backend).\\n\\n### New terms — Agency\\n\\n- **Agent Principal** — an agent runtime exercising a recorded, bounded delegation of Principal-issuable acts (request issuance and cancellation, named escalation-resolution classes). Never acceptance authority over decision-role artifacts without an RFC.\\n- **Drive Session** — one invocation-to-quiescence execution of the Driver loop, serialized per repository graph by the Graph Store's drive lease and recorded in the ledger.\\n- **Wake** — a non-authoritative trigger that invokes the Driver (timer, adapter, repository hook, human). A missed wake delays; it never corrupts.\\n- **Acceptance Queue** — the derived projection of open acceptance gates awaiting authority; a named derived store, never stored truth.\\n- **Dispatch** — the delivery of one lane of one pass run, at one attempt, to an execution backend as a sealed, content-addressed bundle.\\n- **Submission** — a backend's committed offer of results for one dispatch; nothing in it is true until admitted.\\n- **Spool** (owner RFC 0007) — the non-authoritative exchange area for dispatches and submissions; losing it is equivalent to abandonment.\\n- **Workspace** — the per-dispatch scratch execution tree (E1: an isolated worktree); never state.\\n- **Attempt** — the Driver-incremented dispatch ordinal for one lane, carried in the lane binding; a new attempt is always a new pass run.\\n- **Aliasing Registry / Kinship** — the declared model-family classes and their relatedness edges; independence's kinship conjuncts are evaluated against the registry current at claim-read time, under a governed staging protocol.\\n\\n### New terms — Scheduling\\n\\n- **Capacity Pool** — a named, bounded, possibly-resetting account of one capacity kind, declared in capacity policy; the unit of capacity accounting.\\n- **Capacity Snapshot** — a content-addressed view of the capacity-state derived store at an instant; the sealed capacity input to a scheduling evaluation.\\n- **Capacity Harvest** — the conversion of capacity that would otherwise expire into durable evidence via cataloged analysis-pass posture parameterizations.\\n- **Dispatch Horizon** — the policy-derived observed-active duration after which a lane binding without a submission may be superseded by re-dispatch. An interpretation rule, not a liveness claim.\\n- **Scheduling Decision** — the record of one scheduler evaluation: bindings, deferrals, refusals, harvest budgets, next horizon.\\n\\n### New terms — Memory and store\\n\\n- **Graph Store** — the per-repository durable directory holding a graph's ledger segments, object store, derived stores, and concurrency primitives; located outside the target repository's working tree.\\n- **Object Store** — the content-addressed body storage inside a Graph Store; the primary home of every artifact body.\\n- **Body Placement** — the per-kind routing of artifact bodies: `stored` (object store only) or `integrated` (also anchored into the target repository by the `integration` pass). Ledger records are never a body placement.\\n- **Canonical Form (SCF)** — the versioned, length-prefixed, language-independent serialization whose bytes are both the stored and the hashed representation of a ledger record.\\n- **Anchor Map** — the (anchor → element hash) table extracted from an artifact version at admission; the index basis of element-grain staleness.\\n- **Anchor Continuity** — the gate-checked postcondition that a regenerating pass preserves or explicitly retires every prior element anchor.\\n- **Graph Genesis** — the first ledger record of a graph, binding repository identity.\\n- **Repository Identity** — the durable identifier (`repo_id`) binding a target repository to its graph across paths and clones.\\n- **Constitutional Decision** — a decision record owned by the compiler repository's graph, constraining all graphs; contrasted with a repository-local decision.\\n\\n### New terms — Judgment and execution\\n\\n- **Check** — one mechanical predicate execution: pinned argv, pinned binary, sealed environment, no network.\\n- **Check Identity** — the content-addressed identity of a check, hashed over its full specification; \\\"what ran\\\" is a hash, not a convention.\\n- **Check Registry** — the repository's policy-maintained allowlist of check identities that may mint receipts; defense in depth beneath the acceptance authority carried by pinned check identities.\\n- **Attempt Budget** — the per-packet, per-failure-mode planning bound whose exhaustion trips quarantine and a `bounds_exhausted` escalation.\\n- **Residual Run** — a new pass run of the same contract pinning admitted partial outputs as declared inputs, completing a partial submission.\\n- **Partial-Admission Closure Rule** — an output of a partial submission is individually admissible iff its declared intra-run derivation closure is admitted.\\n- **Dual-Signal Rule** — the v1 `verified` predicate's requirement of two execution-independent verification runs, both independent of build.\\n\\n### Operational conventions (by reference)\\n\\nExhaust, Advisory Signal/Pulse, Session Nonce, Quiescence, Harvest Window, Composed Base, Integration Frontier, Linked Tree, Intra-Run Derivation Map, Open-Run Invariant — operational conventions defined in their owning RFCs (0006, 0007, 0008, 0010), listed in the glossary by reference only; never glossary-admitted terms.\\n\\n- **N10** — Record-type names and operational conventions never enter the core term list; bulk term admissions require per-term layer assignment and duplicate-merge adjudication.\\n\\n## Epoch 3 Amendment (Adapter Supervision)\\n\\nAccepted via the N8 mechanism as part of RFC 0013; [RFC 0001's Epoch 3 Amendment section](../../rfcs/0001-language-specification/design.md) is controlling.\\n\\n- **Lane Supervisor** (Agency) — the detached per-dispatch process, forked by an LLM backend's `dispatch` verb, that owns runtime invocation, the bounded internal-relaunch loop, pre-submission validation, the rename commit, and the post-commit wake for exactly one dispatch. Nothing supervises it; its death is a lapsed dispatch — and, by fate-sharing, the death of every runtime process it started. Operational conventions by reference: Supervisor Hint, Kill Domain, Fate-Sharing (RFC 0013).\\n\\n## Ontology-Discipline Amendment\\n\\n- **N11** — Prefer strengthening existing ontology over introducing new ontology. Before a new term, concept, or abstraction is admitted, establish that no accepted concept already holds its role and strengthen that one instead; a genuinely new durable concept enters only via the N8 amendment mechanism and never shadows an existing home (P2).\\n\\n## Admission-Completeness Amendment\\n\\n- **P11 — Admission completeness.** A capability of the compiled system is fully admitted only when the artifact graph simultaneously holds its implementation (Product Artifacts), its justification (the owning RFC identity's accepted, fresh Decision Record), and its explanation (canonical Diátaxis documentation — itself a Product Artifact, never commentary), each admitted through the existing gate classes. These are complementary projections of one admitted change, never independent checklists; implementation never silently outruns explanation. Computed form: the target state `capability-admission-complete`.\\n\\n## Retired Terms\\n\\nTwo banned literals are hyphenated in this rendering so the repository lint for them stays clean; RFC 0001 spells them out.\\n\\n| Term | Disposition | Replacement |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Meta-Operator | renamed | Driver |\\n| Operator | retired (three-way overload) | Principal / lane role / Driver, by sense |\\n| Worker, Clank-er | killed | Agent Runtime (occupying a lane) |\\n| Work-flow (and its shape/snapshot compounds) | banned / translated | pipeline, pass contract, run manifest |\\n| Job, run (bare) | translated | pass run |\\n| Human checkpoint | killed as noun | open Acceptance Gate |\\n| Blocker | translated | escalation (ledger record) |\\n| Verification IR, Product IR | reclassified | evidence kinds; product designation |\\n| Diagnostic (as artifact kind) | reclassified | Review Ledger findings; escalation records |\\n| Pass Schedule (as artifact) | reclassified | plan record (ledger) |\\n| Quota (core term) | demoted | Capacity (core); quota in policy docs |\\n| Lease, ack, heartbeat, queue message, session, supervisor, terminal mechanics | excluded | backend-internal mechanics; never ontology |\\n| Adapter, harness profile, tool family | collapsed | Execution Backend / Agent Runtime internals |\\n| Marker, branch confirmation, coordinator surrogates, publish-on-behalf | killed | — |\\n\",\n    \"docs/concepts/pipeline.md\": \"# Pipeline\\n\\nPurpose: define the Pipeline.\\n\\nA catalog-resident template composing passes, gate wiring, and re-run bounds.
