That reading was adequate while every subject was a document the compiler itself had linked: the first change-set's files were the whole tree, and every later base was a product the store already held. It becomes a fiction the moment a compilation edits a repository that already has content. The repository's tree is real state — packages, tools, vendored dependencies — and an empty base pin makes verification materialize the overlay alone, so the checks attest a tree nobody ships: exactly the vacuity [Verification With Teeth](verification-teeth.md) exists to prevent, reintroduced through the base pin.\\n\\nThe placement question was not open. [D0009.C2](../../decisions/D0009-provenance-ledger-and-artifact-store.md) had already decided that the object store is the primary body home and *git anchors secondary*; this capability is that clause delivered, not a re-decision. The tradeoff it banks is anchor versus ingest. Ingesting — copying the repository into an inline JSON product body — would buy the same pin arithmetic at the cost of a body as large as the repository in every stored version and every dispatch bundle that carries it. A git tree is already content-addressed immutable state; pinning it by commit and tree hash preserves the admission force of a content pin — the same refuse-on-drift comparison — without copying the repository into inline bodies.\\n\\n## The anchored body {#el:anchored-body}\\n\\nAn **anchored product body** carries an anchor of `{kind: \\\"git-tree\\\", commit, tree}` plus a `files` overlay; where the overlay and the anchored tree carry the same path, the overlay wins. Its content identity is its own canonical body hash, exactly like every other body — never the raw git hash. That keeps one identity scheme rather than two: the pin path compares canonical body hashes and never touches git, so an anchored body is small, deterministic, and indistinguishable to admission from any other body. The anchor is expanded into real files only where trees are materialized, never on the pin path. The canonical forms live in [`internal/changeset`](../../internal/changeset/changeset.go) (the body and the apply arithmetic) and [`internal/gitanchor`](../../internal/gitanchor/gitanchor.go) (anchor creation and expansion); this document argues the shape and does not restate them.\\n\\n## Expansion lives on the planning side {#el:planning-side-expansion}\\n\\nThree sites expand anchors, and all of them are planning-side: dispatch assembly, base composition, and the receipt-checks derivation. When a subject's product lineage has no head yet, [base composition](../../internal/driver/session.go) anchors the composed base at the repository's git HEAD — a planning-side world read, like observation. At dispatch, an anchored base travels as two hash-verified bundle inputs: the small anchored pin body at `inputs/00-base-pin` — the hash change-sets pin — and the expanded tree at `inputs/01-base` — what lanes materialize. Lanes stay **world-blind**: they receive expanded trees as pinned inputs and never read git. And the receipt-checks derivation, which recomputes a change-set's result tree by pure arithmetic at admission, expands the same anchor through the same content-addressed local git read the dispatch expansion performs — so the derived hash equals the tree hash the verifier's materialization computed — rather than acquiring an independent view of the world.\\n\\nThe trust argument is short: reading local git objects is a content-addressed read of immutable state pinned by hash — the same trust shape as an object-store read. It is not execution, and it is not observation of a mutable world; a pure-Go object reader is a named later strengthening that narrows the surface further while changing nothing about the shape.\\n\\nThis invariant is written down because it is load-bearing and easy to erode. Keeping every world read on the planning side is the division of knowledge that keeps lanes fungible — any lane, any backend, same bundle — and keeps admission execution-free. The erosion path is one convenient shortcut: a lane that \\\"just runs git\\\" once, because the repository happens to be right there. Nothing would fail loudly; the lane contract would simply have grown an undeclared read. A future change that wants expansion inside lanes must argue against this section, not drift past it.\\n\\n## The lineage is born at first integration {#el:lineage-birth}\\n\\nThe first integration over an anchored base links the pin body's anchor with the merged overlay — an **anchor-plus-overlay composite** — and stages it as the product candidate; the product ref then moves under the gate-passing transition with `tree_moved` compare-and-set, exactly as [D0010.C8](../../decisions/D0010-work-graph-execution.md) already specifies. This capability changes nothing about integration's discipline: the linker's arithmetic is the same [typed, no-judgment application](../../internal/backend/local/integrate.go) it always was, and E2 is still realized at admission, never in a lane. From that first admission forward the subject has a product lineage whose every head is anchored to the same immutable git tree it grew from — the anchor records where the lineage came from, the overlay records what the funnel has admitted since.\\n\\n## The v1 bounds {#el:v1-bounds}\\n\\nFour bounds, each a refusal by design with its reason — none of them a defect, and none of them roadmap:\\n\\n- **Binary content is excluded from expansion.** Files whose contents are not valid UTF-8 are skipped by the expansion gate. The expanded tree serves build, vet, format, and self-law checks, which never read binary fixtures — and inline product bodies are JSON, which cannot carry them.\\n- **Change-set deletes over an anchored base are refused.** A delete of an anchored file is not representable in an overlay, so the apply arithmetic refuses with a typed `apply_failure` rather than mislink a tree that silently still carries the file. The implementation calls deletes over an anchored base \\\"a named later version\\\" — a version boundary honestly stated, not a delivery promise.\\n- **Batch integration over an anchored base is refused**, under the same named-later-version boundary: the batch linker's union arithmetic has no anchored composite form at this version, and refusing is cheaper than linking a wrong one.\\n- **Lineages are subject-scoped.** An anchored lineage belongs to the subject whose funnel produced it; there is no single repo-level product ref at this version. Each subject's first compilation anchors at the HEAD it observed, and the base pin every change-set carries makes that choice auditable.\\n\\n## What this is not {#el:what-this-is-not}\\n\\nNot new architecture: this is D0009.C2 delivered through the existing funnel — no accepted clause was amended, and D0010.C8's integration discipline is untouched. Not a how-to: nothing here tells an author how to produce a repo-editing compilation. Not reference: the canonical body hash, the anchored body schema, and the dispatch stage formats live in their canonical homes, linked above and never restated here. The deferred work is named rather than folded in: change-set deletes over an anchored base, batch integration over anchored bases, binary handling under the expansion gate, and the pure-Go git object reader. Each is a version boundary this document records, so that relaxing one is a visible edit to this page rather than a silent drift.\\n\\n\",\n    \"docs/explanation/satisfaction-earns-its-force.md\": \"# Satisfaction Earns Its Force\\n\\nPurpose: explain why a target-state satisfaction now carries a claim level, so a green `[satisfied]` can no longer hide the fact that the compiler verified nothing.\\n\\n## The weakness\\n\\nOnboarding a repository to striatum is just registration — it establishes no verification substrate. So a fresh repo's target states default to the pass-bracket floor: `accepted_head:intent-statement` + `evidence_admitted:exogenous-change-record`. That floor is satisfied by capturing an intent and admitting a single, self-authored Exogenous Change Record — a world-authored *attestation* that says \\\"here is what I did.\\\" The compiler runs no lanes, no checks, no verification; it records that an ECR exists.\\n\\nUntil now, satisfaction was **binary**: the request read `[satisfied]`, identically whether it rested on that one asserted ECR or on independent dual-signal verification. So a newly-onboarded repo could mint a verified-*looking* product state on nothing the compiler checked. This is not hypothetical — a fleet repository (praxis) shows a whole `reminder-bot-product` state `[satisfied]` on three local pass runs, zero receipts, zero checks, one self-authored ECR. The underlying work happened to be real, but a fabricated ECR would have produced the same green mark. The checkmark carried more force than the evidence earned.\\n\\n## The fix: compute the level, don't declare it\\n\\nD0005.C5 already fixes the doctrine for artifact claims: *claims are computed; Designed/Asserted/Verified are backed by acceptance/validation/verification; **Verified is a predicate, never a declaration**.* The satisfaction surface simply never honored it. This change applies it there.\\n\\nEvery `satisfaction_record` now carries a `claim_level` computed from the kinds of conjunct that satisfied it — a pure function of the recorded evidence, minted like any other claim, never declared:\\n\\n- a `verified_dual_signal` / `integrated_head` / `integrated_batch` conjunct is backed by independent dual-signal verification receipts (which the record already pins) → **Verified**;\\n- an admitted attestation (`evidence_admitted`, e.g. an ECR) or a bare `built` conjunct asserts without verifying → **Asserted**;\\n- gated-but-unattested heads alone → **Designed**;\\n- the strongest conjunct present wins.\\n\\n`status` surfaces it: `… -\\u003e reminder-bot-product [satisfied: Asserted]`. A floor-only satisfaction is now visibly, computably weaker than a verification-backed one. Nobody — human or agent — can mistake an assertion for a compiler guarantee.\\n\\n## Why this is honest, not cosmetic\\n\\nThe level is not a label bolted on; it is the D0005.C5 lattice reaching the last surface that ignored it. D0010.C11 already names the stakes: compiler soundness is honest only *\\\"relative to the completeness of the checks a gate enforces — garbage that satisfies weak checks is still admitted.\\\"* The pass-bracket floor is a weak check. Levelling satisfaction does not make the floor stronger; it makes the floor's weakness **visible** rather than hidden behind a green mark. The trusted core still executes nothing — the level is computed from recorded conjunct evidence.\\n\\nFittingly, this pass's own close rests on the floor, so it reads `[satisfied: Asserted]` — the compiler telling the truth about its own evidence.\\n\\n## What this is not, and what's next\\n\\nNot new architecture: it delivers an accepted clause (D0005.C5) to a surface that violated it (P2/N11) — no RFC amended, no decision regenerated. It does not, by itself, give any repo teeth. The companion move is **onboarding that establishes a repo-appropriate check substrate** so a repo's satisfactions *can* reach Verified — for praxis, real Python checks (`ruff`, `pytest`, the surface `403`-on-loopback probe) so `reminder-bot-product` re-reads honestly once verified. That existence proof, and levelling by the ECR's lane-attribution independence (not only conjunct kind), are named later strengthenings. The point stands now: a repo can no longer present asserted-on-an-ECR as if it were verified.\\n\",\n    \"docs/explanation/striatum-as-compiler-for-engineering-intent.md\": \"# Striatum as a Compiler for Engineering Intent\\n\\nPurpose: state the thesis everything else in this repository serves.\\n\\n## Striatum compiles intent\\n\\nStriatum does not orchestrate agents. It compiles intent.\\n\\nStated in full: **the purpose of Striatum is not to orchestrate intelligent systems. It is to compile the outputs of arbitrary nondeterministic capability providers into a deterministic, provenance-preserving artifact graph.**\\n\\nA Principal says:\\n\\n```text\\nAdvance RFC 0028 to Verified.\\n```\\n\\nThat is a compilation request: a subject and a target state. The system determines the current graph state, the unmet conjuncts of the target predicate, the passes whose outputs satisfy them, the gates each output must pass, and the placement of the work. The human requests a desired state; Striatum computes and executes the path.\\n\\nThe frontier models are not the product. They are capacity — execution resources spent performing compiler passes.\\n\\n## The determinism boundary\\n\\nThe thesis draws one line, and it is the submit/admit seam (D0002). Upstream of the seam, everything may be nondeterministic: an execution backend and the agent runtime inside its lane may retry, drift, crash, or improve without notice — vendor behavior is data, never semantics (P9). Downstream of the seam, everything is deterministic: sealed work goes out, submissions come back or nothing does (crash-only, D0007), and nothing becomes true until the Driver — a deterministic program, not a judgment (D0006) — admits it through gates. The trusted core is execution-free, and the admitted result is invariant to execution noise (D0010.C11).\\n\\n\\\"Capability provider\\\" is deliberately broader than any accepted term. Today the providers are LLM lanes behind the file seam, but the compiler's semantics name only execution backends and their declared capability facts — never what intelligence, if any, sits inside (P9). *Arbitrary* means replaceable; *nondeterministic* means the compiler assumes nothing about their reliability.\\n\\nThis is why orchestration is the wrong frame, not merely a retired word. An orchestrator's product is a coordinated process, so its correctness inherits the reliability of whatever it coordinates. A compiler's product is the artifact graph, and the graph's integrity is independent of provider reliability by construction: every version records the pass run that produced it (P1), claims are computed from evidence bindings (P6), and graph plus ledger rebuild every derived store (D0002.C2). The providers may be arbitrarily unreliable. Admission is not.\\n\\n## The artifact is the primitive\\n\\nThe primitive is not the process; it is the **artifact** — durable, versioned, provenance-bearing. Processes come and go; the artifact graph plus the provenance ledger is the system of record. Every durable concept is exactly one of: artifact, compiler pass, pipeline, scheduler policy, backend capability, quality gate, provenance record type (P2). Fitting none or two is a design error.\\n\\nThis is why the orchestration framing was retired. When the process is the primitive, state hides in transcripts, branch names, and marker files, and nobody can say what is true. When the artifact is the primitive, truth is the graph, and everything else is computed from it (P10).\\n\\n## Two planes, plus the environment plane\\n\\nCompilation state is two-dimensional:\\n\\n- The **lowering plane** removes ambiguity: Intent Statement (L0) → Proposal → Design → Implementation Plan → Work Graph → Change Set → Product (L6, a designation). Each level removes a named ambiguity class and may introduce no decision belonging to a higher one (P5).\\n- The **evidence plane** raises justified confidence in artifacts that already exist: review ledgers, sealed receipts, verification reports — and the claims computed from their bindings. Verification is not an IR; it is evidence about IRs.\\n\\nThe **environment plane** is the [decision layer](decision-layer.md): generated Decision Records that passes link against. Underneath all three sits provenance — the append-only memory of how they moved.\\n\\n## You cannot declare Verified\\n\\nTarget states are versioned predicates over the graph, not statuses anyone sets. `verified(N)` holds when every packet's claims stand at Verified with unexpired evidence — and stops holding, arithmetically, when a bound hash moves. Nothing is true because someone said so in prose. Heads move only through gates: checks verify, reviews validate, acceptance authorizes, and never in any other order.\\n\\n## Models are capacity\\n\\nExecution backends and agent runtimes are replaceable capacity, never architecture. No pass contract, IR schema, or gate names one (P9); model choice is scheduler policy; capacity pressure never touches gates or claims. The compiler's semantics would be unchanged if every backend were swapped tomorrow — that is the point.\\n\\nCompressed to an epigram: **capabilities belong to the backends, never the compiler; desired state belongs to the subject, never the capability.** A compilation request names a subject and a target state; what the backends can do shapes only the path, never the destination.\\n\\nCanonical definitions: [the language specification](../concepts/language-specification.md). Architecture: [RFC 0002](../../rfcs/0002-compiler-architecture/design.md). The ladder: [RFC 0003](../../rfcs/0003-intermediate-representations/design.md). Judgment: [RFC 0005](../../rfcs/0005-artifact-lifecycle-and-state-machine/design.md).\\n\",\n    \"docs/explanation/truth-surface-hardening.md\": \"# Truth-Surface Hardening\\n\\nPurpose: explain why the compiler turns its own thesis — *nothing is true until admitted through gates* — on its own self-description, and why the fix is a documentation sweep plus one delivered linter, not new architecture.\\n\\n## The truth surface\\n\\nThe **truth surface** is every place the system describes itself: the README's State section, the CLI and control-surface reference, the CHANGELOG, the operator notes (AGENTS.md), the backend `runtime.md` files, and — most dangerously — the prose that asserts the compiler enforces its own law. A reader (a new human, the maintainer in six months, or the next agent session primed by AGENTS.md) takes these surfaces as fact. When they drift behind the shipped system, the front door lies.\\n\\nFor most projects that is ordinary staleness. For this one it is a category error, because the whole thesis is that a claim is not true until it is *admitted through a gate*. A repository built by an agent fleet in twenty hours minted ceremony faster than enforcement: it wrote \\\"every catalog entry is machine-validated,\\\" \\\"policy is schema-validated,\\\" \\\"retired terms and model names outside `backends/` are lint errors,\\\" \\\"quota constraints are lint-checked\\\" — and then shipped a `tools/lint-rfcs` and a `tools/validate-schema` that were each a four-line `func main() {}`. This is the **enforcement mirage**: the gates guarding the compiler's own law were painted on. In a system whose entire point is that nothing is true until gated, asserted-but-absent enforcement is the one lie that trains every future agent to treat the pattern as normal.\\n\\n## What hardening means\\n\\nHardening the truth surface is two conjoined moves.\\n\\n**Currency** — make the descriptions true. The README says Epoch 3, self-hosting in force, fourteen RFCs; the CLI reference documents the ten verbs the binary actually exposes, and names the RFC-0006-designed-but-unshipped verbs as exactly that rather than implying they run; the CHANGELOG carries every satisfied pass; the `runtime.md` files describe the detached forked-supervision mechanic that shipped, not the retired synchronous one; the pre-RFC incubation essays, written in retired vocabulary, leave the live Diátaxis tree for the bootstrap RFC's archive.\\n\\n**Enforcement, not mirage** — make the self-law executable. `tools/lint-rfcs` now enforces the grep-shaped law RFC 0001 already specified and D0001 already asserted: retired terms and model names must not appear on the compiler surface, and the N/P convention range must stay consistent with RFC 0001. It is wired into `make check`, so a violation fails the build. Every prior plan-log \\\"lint-rfcs exit 0\\\" — vacuously true when the main was empty — now means something. Where the enforcement genuinely does not exist yet (whole-catalog schema validation, telemetry-derived-quota checks), the prose was corrected to say so rather than claim a checker that isn't there.\\n\\n## The discipline, and its inverse\\n\\nThe mirage was made by asserting a capability and never building it. The correction is the exact inverse: **enforcement precedes the claim.** The linter was delivered and made green *before* the prose that cites it was allowed to read as true. The cardinal risk of the fix is minting a second mirage — a broad, flaky linter that false-positives on the retired-terms tables and historical prose and gets quietly neutered back to vacuity. So `lint-rfcs` enforces exactly what it can enforce deterministically and green, and its own package doc names the checks it delivers *and* the ones it defers (closed-vocabulary drift, gate-purity, the decision-clause↔design cross-check). Honesty about the boundary is part of the deliverable.\\n\\n## What this is not\\n\\nThis is not new architecture. Documentation currency is the standing P11 obligation; delivering the linter realizes an accepted D0001 clause (P2/N11 delivery of a designed capability, not a re-decision). No accepted clause was amended and no decision record was regenerated — RFC 0001's own N/P range statements were already current, so only the downstream echo was brought to currency. Adjacent gaps are named honestly rather than folded in: giving *Verified* teeth over code (a different axis — attesting external truth, not self-description), the deletion of dead scaffolding, and the retrofit of `## Decision (clauses)` sections into the older RFCs (so the \\\"lint-enforced\\\" clauses in generated records like D0004/D0008 can be corrected without hand-editing a record) are each candidate next desired states.\\n\",\n    \"docs/explanation/verification-teeth.md\": \"# Verification With Teeth\\n\\nPurpose: explain why \\\"Verified\\\" now attests that code compiles rather than that a file is non-empty, and why giving it teeth was delivering RFC 0010's own design, not adding to it.\\n\\n## The vacuity\\n\\nStriatum's central promise is that *Verified is a predicate the graph satisfies, never a status anyone declares* — a claim minted only from admitted, sealed, dual-signal evidence. The machinery around that promise is unusually well built: content-addressed check identities, sealed receipts, two sandbox profiles for execution independence, a flake veto. And until this pass it attested almost nothing. The repository check registry held two checks — `test -s body` and `grep -q '{#el:' body` — so a change-set passed Verified by being *non-empty* and *carrying an element anchor*. The first real code-producing packet would pass Verified while broken: the ceremony was deep, the bite was zero.\\n\\nThe cause was a v1 implementation cutline that quietly contradicted its own RFC. RFC 0010 §5.2 designs verification to \\\"materialize a fresh workspace purely from pins: composed base + Change Set diff = subject tree,\\\" and §5.1/§7.2 name the checks that run against it as \\\"full build, full test suite, repository lints.\\\" But the verifier lane materialized the subject as a single file literally named `body` and ran the checks against *that* — never a buildable tree. The design said \\\"compile the tree\\\"; the code wrote one file to disk.\\n\\n## What teeth means\\n\\nA code-bearing subject is a Change Set: a diff (`files` overlay + `deletes`) against a pinned base product. Verification now does what §5.2 always specified — it applies that diff onto the composed base it was built against (recomposed from pins when the base is a frontier packet's tree that equals no stored object), writing the result to a real filesystem tree, and hash-verifying that the composed tree equals the change-set's declared result tree before anything runs. Then it runs real mechanical checks against that tree in a hermetic verifier lane: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and the self-law `go run ./tools/lint-rfcs`. A change-set that does not compile produces a non-zero exit, which flips the verification report to reject, which denies the receipt — so it never reaches Verified. The teeth are demonstrated as a standing guard beside the soundness guard: a buildable change-set accepts, a non-compiling one rejects.\\n\\nThe lane is hermetic on purpose. The result tree carries the repository's vendored dependencies, and the toolchain runs under `-mod=vendor -buildvcs=false`, `GOPROXY=off`, and a workspace-relative build cache and home — so a verification build touches neither the network nor any ambient module cache. It builds exactly what the materialized tree carries and nothing else, which is what makes the receipt mean something.\\n\\n## Why this keeps soundness\\n\\nThe trusted core still executes nothing on the gate path. Builds and checks run below the submit/admit seam in a disposable lane; the core validates sealed receipts by pure content arithmetic. The one predicate that changed — the receipt-checks gate — moved from \\\"the materialized tree hash equals the subject's body hash\\\" to \\\"for a change-set, the materialized tree hash equals the change-set's *declared result tree hash*.\\\" That is sound by construction: the lane Apply-verifies that composed base + diff yields exactly that declared hash before running a single check, so a change-set that lies about its output fails at materialization, and the gate binds the receipt to the same declared tree. A change-set cannot obtain a Verified receipt for a tree other than the one it claims to produce. The compiler-soundness reduction (D0010.C11) is unchanged; its honest bound — \\\"the completeness of the checks a gate enforces\\\" — is exactly what this pass strengthened.\\n\\n## What this is not\\n\\nNot new architecture. RFC 0010 already designed tree materialization (§5.2), routed buildability to verification's `acceptance_checks` (§114), and anticipated code checks in the registry (§5.1); this pass aligned the code to the design (P2/N11 delivery), amending no accepted clause and regenerating no record. The teeth activate exactly when the repository registers a code check set — until then, and in any test with only the body set, verification is byte-identical to before.\\n\\nThe `@2` strengthening extends this the same way. Two of the checks named as deferred in v1 are now delivered: a **gofmt gate** (`go run ./tools/gofmtcheck` — a self-contained `go/format` wrapper, the exit-code wrapper v1 lacked, so a mis-formatted change-set fails Verified), and the **integration build check** (RFC 0010 §7.2), which puts the same teeth at the link point: the deterministic linker materializes the linked tree and — exactly as it refuses to stage an apply-conflict — refuses to stage a link that does not build, emitting a `link_check_failure` conflict and producing no product, so a batch of individually-Verified change-sets whose *combination* does not build never becomes the product head. The integration-checks gate stays execution-free; the checks run below the seam in the disposable linker lane; both are gated on the registered code set.\\n\\nStill deferred, named not folded in: `go test` as a gate (its suite's cgroup-dependent supervision tests would fail verification on correct code); the receipt-based §7.2 shape (link checks minting sealed link receipts the integration-checks gate requires, rather than the linker fail-closed refusing to stage); and real sandbox hardening (enforced network isolation and resource limits — the RFC 0012 rung-2 boundary, still declared-not-enforced in the single-user trust domain). Each is a versioned strengthening, invalidating nothing.\\n\",\n    \"docs/how-to/add-a-pass.md\": \"# Add a Pass\\n\\nPurpose: add a compiler pass to the catalog.\\n\\nThe catalog holds eleven passes; a twelfth requires an RFC (RFC 0004).\\n\\n## First: is it a pass?\\n\\nA pass consumes artifact versions and produces artifacts (transform) or evidence (analysis). Nothing to roll back. |\\n| `partial` | a partial result set was submitted | Admission is per-output under the Partial-Admission Closure Rule; the Driver plans a residual run pinning the admitted outputs. Finished lanes' work is never discarded. |\\n| `escalation` | the Principal is required | The subgraph halts. Resolve the escalation (below). |\\n| `abandonment` | no submission arrived within the dispatch horizon (crash-only backends) | The run closes `abandoned` — a **provisional adjudication**, not a death certificate. Re-dispatch is closure-then-new-run at attempt+1; a late submission is still admitted (recorded `submitted_late`); the first admitted valid result wins across attempts. |\\n\\n## Revision is a re-run\\n\\nThere are no fix-passes. Revision re-runs the producing pass with the Review Ledger as declared diagnostic input, producing the next candidate version. Re-run bounds before escalation are driver policy; exhaustion escalates `bounds_exhausted` with its `budget_kind`, never a silent retry loop.\\n\\n## Reconcile\\n\\nIf runtime state is suspect, run the one recovery verb: `striatum reconcile [--deep] [--migrate]`. It verifies sealed segments, anchors, and gate closure; rebuilds every derived store and reports divergence as self-healed notices; and quarantines orphan spool bundles. `--deep` re-hashes sealed bodies; `--migrate` is the explicit offline refold after a fold-version bump. It parks — never crash-loops — on `body_missing` and on records newer than the reader, each park naming its discharge. It may never author artifacts, move heads, mint evidence, or \\\"repair\\\" truth; damage to truth is reported and fenced, and restoring it is a Principal-level act from backups (objects first, ledger second). There is no second recovery verb. Semantics: [RFC 0006, `reconcile`](../../rfcs/0006-driver-control-surface/design.md).\\n\\n## Resolve an escalation\\n\\nAn escalation is a ledger record with a closed reason code — eight codes: `ambiguous_goal`, `missing_authority`, `contradicting_decisions`, `committee_stalemate`, `override_required`, `bounds_exhausted` (carrying `budget_kind`), `binding_unsatisfiable`, `independence_unsatisfiable`. It blocks its subgraph until the Principal appends a resolution via `striatum resolve \\u003cid\\u003e --disposition \\u003cd\\u003e` — an authority event. The runtime foundation is accepted (RFCs 0006–0010); implementation proceeds on the v0 spine, whose target predicates stop short of `verified` until the dual-signal predicate registers.\\n\\n## The request\\n\\n```text\\nstriatum request rfcs/0028 --target verified\\n```\\n\\n`verified(0028)` (RFC 0005) holds iff every packet in 0028's accepted Work Graph has claims at Verified with unexpired evidence and all gates passed. You cannot declare it; the graph either satisfies it or does not.\\n\\n## Descending the ladder\\n\\nSuppose 0028 stands at design-accepted. The Driver plans the residual lowering:\\n\\n1. `implementation-planning` — Design → Implementation Plan (L3). Gates: implementation-plan-review, implementation-plan-acceptance. Every packet boundary cites the design elements it implements; no L2 decision is introduced or reversed.\\n2. `packetization` — Plan → Work Graph (L4). Gate: work-graph-legality (check) — acyclic, every packet anchored to a plan element, parallel packets with disjoint write scopes.\\n3. `build`, fanned out per packet — Work Packet → Change Set (L5). Each runs in isolated lanes inside its declared write scope. Lane-local evidence is advisory: build never self-certifies.\\n\\n## The evidence plane\\n\\n4. `verification` — for each Change Set, disposable verifier lanes execute the pinned check identities and mint sealed receipts; the trusted core validates seals and never executes. The Verification Report carries binding closure: the subject's hash plus the accepted-head or element hashes of every governing IR.\\n5. Claims are computed, not granted. The v1 `verified` predicate is dual-signal: two accepting, execution-independent verification runs, both independent of build. With valid receipts, complete closure, and independence — the minting executions share no provenance ancestry with the producing one, aliasing classes checked — each packet's claim stands at Verified; until the second signal lands, it rests at Asserted.\\n\\n## Satisfaction — and decay\\n\\nWhen the last conjunct holds, `verified(0028)` is true for anyone who evaluates it. It stays true exactly as long as the evidence binds: if a governing design element moves, the bound claims fall to Asserted arithmetically — no meeting, no status edit; a ledger event records the implied transition. Implementation proceeds on the v0 spine — the named cutline of what is built first.\\n\\n## 1. An intent becomes a compilation request\\n\\nYou have an idea. You utter it. The Driver plans\\n\\nThe Driver reads the graph and evaluates the target predicate: `design-accepted(0031)` requires an accepted, fresh Design bound to an accepted Proposal. Neither exists, so the predicate has unmet conjuncts. Planning is graph reachability over the pass catalog — `proposal-generation`, then `design-convergence`, each with its gate set. The plan is appended to the ledger as a plan record; the Driver produces no artifacts.\\n\\n## 3. runtime\\n// invocations (D0013.C10): StartConfined starts a runtime whose entire\\n// process tree — descendants included — dies with the caller. Nothing above\\n// the seam imports this package; it is adapter launch plumbing, not a\\n// supervision rung (D0013.C3).\\n//\\n// # Chosen mechanics (W0 platform validation, host proximal, 2026-07-02)\\n//\\n// The design's reference composition — a private PID namespace whose init\\n// carries PR_SET_PDEATHSIG — is unavailable unprivileged on this deployment:\\n// Ubuntu 24.04 ships kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, and\\n// unprivileged CLONE_NEWPID requires a user namespace first. Rather than\\n// mutate host security posture, this package ships the design's sanctioned\\n// composed fallback (D0013.C10 \\\"cgroup kill is lawful where an actor exists\\n// at teardown\\\"):\\n//\\n//   - StartConfined creates a fresh cgroup2 leaf under the caller's current\\n//     cgroup (the systemd-delegated user subtree on this host) and starts a\\n//     small init helper directly inside it via clone3 CLONE_INTO_CGROUP\\n//     (SysProcAttr.CgroupFD), so no migration race exists.\\n//   - The init helper carries PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGTERM) and re-checks its\\n//     parent pid on startup to close the fork/death race. It forks the\\n//     runtime as its only child; runtime descendants cannot leave the\\n//     cgroup, whatever sessions or process groups they create.\\n//   - On parent death, SIGTERM, or runtime exit, the init helper TERMs the\\n//     remaining cgroup members, waits a bounded grace, migrates itself out,\\n//     writes cgroup.kill (kernel-atomic SIGKILL of every member), and\\n//     removes the cgroup directory. The init helper is the actor that\\n//     exists at teardown.\\n//\\n// The init helper stays in the caller's session and process group\\n// (D0013.C10: abort's single group signal reaches supervisor and runtime\\n// alike); only the cgroup is fresh. PR_SET_PDEATHSIG is delivered when the\\n// spawning thread dies, not only the process — in a Go caller a runtime\\n// thread's death could fire it early; the init helper treats any SIGTERM as\\n// teardown, which the relaunch loop above absorbs as runtime_crash, so the\\n// race costs one relaunch, never correctness.\\n//\\n// Known bounds, stated honestly: the composition needs a writable cgroup2\\n// parent (true anywhere inside a systemd-delegated user subtree; StartConfined\\n// fails loudly elsewhere), and an init helper SIGKILLed in the same instant\\n// as its caller leaves cgroup residue and any escaped descendants running —\\n// a resource-consumption problem only, never a semantic hazard (D0013.C10):\\n// such a tree has no path to an admissible commit. Verified is a predicate, never a declaration\\\") applied\\n// to the satisfaction surface. A verified/integrated conjunct is backed by\\n// independent dual-signal verification receipts (Verified, by the dual-signal\\n// rule's construction); an admitted attestation (evidence_admitted, e.g. an\\n// Exogenous Change Record) or a bare built conjunct asserts without verifying\\n// (Asserted); a satisfaction resting only on gated-but-unattested heads is\\n// Designed. This document records how the Epoch 1 Foundation Compilation Pass was executed by Striatum-0 acting as bootstrap compiler, and what it decided.\\n\\n## Execution Record\\n\\n- **Source language:** the six incubation documents, the repository scaffold, and an operational-experience survey of Striatum-0 (`~/git/striatum`).\\n- **Divergent lanes:** three independent proposals — Lane A (industrial systems architecture), Lane B (production compiler construction), Lane C (programming-language design).\\n- **Synthesis:** the smallest coherent architecture incorporating the strongest ideas; no voting, no averaging.\\n- **Red team:** a 2031-perspective attack produced 25 findings (6 critical); all were adjudicated. The critical findings were contradictions between the synthesis's strongest claims at their pairwise seams; every acceptance either closed a contradiction, named something structural in one paragraph, or simplified.\\n- **Output:** RFCs 0001–0005 accepted as a single architectural unit; decision records D0001–D0005 generated with stage pins and element structure; repository normalized.\\n\\n## Architectural Changes (deliverable 11)\\n\\n1. **Two-plane compilation model.** Lowering plane (L0–L6) × evidence plane + computed staleness; Verification and Product removed from the IR ladder; Change Set (L5) added as the load-bearing object-file level.\\n2. **Four artifact roles** under one supertype: IR, Decision Record, Evidence, Product Artifact. Provenance records are not artifacts.\\n3. **The decision layer formalized:** decision records are the compiler's canonical architectural memory — generated interfaces of RFC identities, element-structured, regenerated on every accepted-stage transition, linked-against at element grain, gracefully stale (last-accepted + recorded deviation), fail-closed only on revocation.\\n4. **Minimal stored lifecycle** (`candidate → accepted → superseded | retired`); staleness, claims, pipeline positions, and target states are computed predicates. The incubation twelve-state ladder survives only as a human projection.\\n5. **One invalidation algebra:** content-hash pins (element grain permitted), eager transitive marking, lazy demand-driven regeneration, revalidation-before-regeneration with a verdict-licensed gate-exempt re-stamp.\\n6. **Judgment layer fixed:** gate trichotomy (check/review/acceptance), closed verdict vocabulary, claims computed from evidence bindings with binding closure and anti-aliasing independence (lane attribution + backend aliasing classes), arithmetic decay with event-visible transitions.\\n7. **Driver replaces Meta-Operator** and is a deterministic program producing no artifacts; Operator retired; lane split into requirement/instance/binding; \\\"workflow\\\" banned in favor of Pipelines; quota demoted to Capacity.\\n8. **Five components** with a submit/admit seam, crash-only backends, one recovery verb (`reconcile`), Derived-State Doctrine with committed ledger versioning (schema_version, upcast-on-read, refuse-newer, sealed segments), exogenous change admission via `observation`, per-repository graph scope, and a named status-projection boundary.\\n9. **Eleven-pass catalog** (8 transform + 3 analysis), pass contract schema with determinism (D0–D2) and effect (E0–E3) classes, contract/impl version split with a lint-enforced adjudication test, `partial` failure mode (finished lanes' work never discarded), revision-as-re-run, and the recorded rejection of scheduling-as-a-pass.\\n10. **Repository normalized:** `prompts/` and `skills/` retired (pass prompt assets become content-addressed catalog references); backend policy folded into `policy/`; `catalog/artifact-kinds/` and `catalog/pipelines/` added; docs pointer-ized; `internal/metaoperator` → `internal/driver`.\\n\\n## Rejected Alternatives (deliverable 12)\\n\\n1. **Stored pipeline state machine** — hidden lifecycle state; migration-prone; invites declared-not-true status.\\n2. **Scheduling as a compiler pass** — category error; assignments are dispatch records mirrored into provenance (recorded in D0004 so it cannot silently return).\\n3. **Verification and Product as IRs** — evidence plane and target designation respectively.\\n4. **Operator as an ontology role** — three-way overload; the pass-executor sense named a role Striatum-0 proved vestigial.\\n5. **\\\"Meta-Operator\\\" as the canonical name** — prefix rot, operator collision, org-chart naming; **Driver** adopted; deprecated alias retained during bootstrap.\\n6. **A sixth RFC (Evidence \\u0026 Judgment)** — judgment is inseparable from lifecycle transitions; one home in RFC 0005 with 0003/0004 strictly referential; hub risk defused by element-grain decisions, not document splitting. Revisit if 0005 proves unwieldy.\\n7. **Per-item opportunistic passes** — the harvest backlog references `review`/`verification` posture parameterizations; the catalog stays closed while postures are governed (versioned catalog entries with owned ledger sections).\\n8. **Decision records as another IR stage** — nothing lowers them; they are the environment plane everything links against.\\n9. **Provenance records as artifacts** — infinite regress; Striatum-0's D273 drag relocated. The ledger is memory, not subject.\\n10. **Bit-replayability as a universal guarantee** — dishonest for LLM passes; contract replay adopted (no consumer may depend on bit replay of a D2 pass).\\n11. **Eager regeneration on upstream change** — capacity bankruptcy; eager marking + lazy regeneration + revalidation cutoff instead.\\n12. **Global fail-closed on stale decision records** — one amendment would make the Principal the fleet's mutex; graceful degradation with recorded deviations adopted; revocation retains fail-closed.\\n13. **Pass Schedule and Diagnostic as artifact kinds** — moved to ledger record types; the Driver produces no artifacts, keeping provenance totality exception-free.\\n14. **Liveness/lease/session vocabulary in the ontology** — backend-internal mechanics under the crash-only doctrine.\\n15. **A global artifact graph** — per-repository graphs with repository-qualified pins.\\n16. **Decision generation only after implementation acceptance** (the literal pipeline sketch) — refined to every-accepted-stage regeneration; the final state is the special case.\\n\\n## Remaining Open Questions (deliverable 13)\\n\\n1. **Element-anchor stability under D2 regeneration** — anchors must survive body regeneration for element-grain bindings to hold; anchor discipline per IR schema is Epoch 2 work and may prove hard for prose-heavy IRs.\\n2. **Revalidation calibration** — how often revalidation clears vs regenerates in practice determines the real economics; no data until the runtime exists.\\n3. **Decision-record scope boundaries** — when many repositories each carry graphs, which decisions are compiler-constitutional (this repo) vs repository-local remains to be exercised.\\n4. **Acceptance-fatigue trajectory** — mandatory human acceptance on decision generation is correct for Epoch 1; the RFC-gated delegation path exists, but the ergonomics of Principal attention at scale are unproven.\\n5. **Verifier independence supply** — anti-aliasing requires genuinely independent backends; under model-market consolidation, satisfying two-signal independence may become materially hard.\\n6. **The `partial` admission boundary** — per-output gating of partial result sets needs careful Epoch 2 semantics for cross-lane consistency (a synthesis lane without its divergent inputs is not a partial result).\\n7. **Pipeline template semantics** — named but deliberately not designed; the boundary between pipeline (composition) and driver policy (re-run bounds) will need one sharp RFC.\\n\\n## Recommended Epoch 2 RFC Ordering (deliverable 14)\\n\\n1. **RFC 0009 — Provenance Ledger \\u0026 Artifact Store** (format: schema_version/upcast/refuse-newer, sealed segments, blob exhaust, admission enforcement of W1–W10). Everything else stands on it.\\n2. **RFC 0006 — Driver Control Surface** (compilation requests, plan records, status projection with warnings/notices triage, `reconcile`).\\n3. **RFC 0007 — Execution Backends \\u0026 Agent Runtimes** (the submit/admit seam concrete; crash-only adapter contract; aliasing classes; lane attribution).\\n4. **RFC 0008 — Scheduler \\u0026 Capacity Policy** (policy engine, harvest scheduling over postures, telemetry-driven evolution).\\n5. **RFC 0010 — Work-Graph Execution \\u0026 Verification Runtime** (packet dispatch, verifier lanes, receipts at runtime, partial admission mechanics).\\n6. **RFC 0011 — Self-Hosting Bootstrap** (Striatum-next compiles Striatum-next; the epoch this architecture was built for).\\n\\n## Foundation Readiness Assessment (deliverable 15)\\n\\n**Ready.** The language is fixed (RFC 0001; closed vocabularies; retirement discipline). The compiler architecture is fixed (RFC 0002; components, seams, doctrines stated as invariants binding on Epoch 2). The IRs are fixed (RFC 0003; twelve kinds; forbidden-information rules). The passes are fixed (RFC 0004; closed catalog; honest replay doctrine). The lifecycle is fixed (RFC 0005; one invalidation algebra; judgment in one home). Terminology is internally consistent across RFCs, decisions, catalogs, docs, and AGENTS.md; the six incubation documents are absorbed (retained read-only as history). The known weakest points are recorded honestly as open questions above rather than hidden: anchor stability, revalidation economics, and independence supply are the three most likely to force an Epoch 2 amendment.\\n\\nResidual known debt: `rfcs/0006-meta-operator-control-surface/` retains its directory name (retired alias) until that RFC activates and can be renamed with its content; `examples/quota-harvest-review/` keeps the quota name pending Epoch 2 example refresh; `docs/incubation/` is retained as immutable history rather than deleted (relocated to `rfcs/0000-bootstrapping-striatum-next/incubation/` by the truth-surface-hardening pass, out of the live Diátaxis tree; relocated again to the instance repository `halbritt/striatum-instance` by the product-instance division, per Discovery 0019).\\n\\n## Critique of the Compilation Prompt (deliverable 16)\\n\\nFor the next compilation pass, amend the prompt as follows:\\n\\n1. **The five-RFC decomposition was nearly right but under-specified invalidation's home.** The charge scattered \\\"invalidation rules\\\" across RFCs 0003, 0004, and 0005 — the direct path to three staleness systems. Future prompts should assign each cross-cutting semantic (invalidation, judgment, provenance identity) exactly one owning RFC up front.\\n2. **\\\"Do not define provenance model\\\" (out-of-scope list) was impossible to honor literally.** Provenance identity, totality, and binding semantics are load-bearing for lifecycle and decisions; only the ledger *format* was genuinely deferrable. The prompt should distinguish semantics (foundation) from formats (runtime) in its scope fences.\\n3. **The prompt omitted exogenous change entirely.** Nothing in the mission, lanes, or RFC charges asked how the graph represents the world writing to the repository — the red team's most severe finding. Compilation prompts should always include \\\"what happens when reality moves without you\\\" as a standing question.\\n4. **No scale directive.** The lanes designed at 2026 scale; only the red team was instructed to assume 2031. Divergent lanes should also receive the success-scenario scale so eager/lazy and fan-out choices are stress-designed, not just stress-tested.\\n5. **The Red Team → Reconciliation structure worked and should be kept**, with one amendment: require the red team to attack the synthesis's claims *pairwise* (the critical findings all lived at seams between individually-sound claims), not just individually.\\n6. **The standing decision-layer commitment arrived mid-pass and was integrable** — but the prompt should carry standing commitments in the mission section so lanes design with them rather than around them.\\n7. **Multi-repository scope should be a mission-level question**, not something a red team has to discover missing.\\n8. **The prompt's ordering (language → architecture → IRs → passes → lifecycle) is correct** and should be kept; every lane independently endorsed it with boundary moves only.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# The Epoch 2 Runtime Foundation Report\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nComplete (2026-07-02, same day — the bootstrap compiler ran both passes). Target predicate `runtime-foundation-ready` ≔ decisions D0006–D0010 accepted and fresh: **satisfied**.\\n\\n## Execution Record\\n\\nFive parallel design lanes (one per runtime RFC identity, each given the 2031 scale directive at design time per the Epoch 1 prompt critique) → seam synthesis (rulings R1–R12: one record registry with one owner per type, three escalation codes, re-stamp attribution, dual-signal Verified, no-daemon confirmed) → a pairwise-seam red team (22 findings: 4 critical, 11 serious, 7 minor; 16-item held list) → reconciliation (19 binding adjudications) → authoring → decision generation. The Epoch 1 amendments this pass required (RFC 0001 Epoch 2 Amendments; RFC 0005 re-stamp attribution) regenerated D0001 and D0005 — the decision layer exercising its own semantics for the first time.\\n\\n## Architectural Changes\\n\\n1. **No daemon.** The Driver is an invoked program over Graph Store files; single-writer admission is the store's append lock + drive lease (lock-first invariant); promptness is non-authoritative wakes. Striatum-0's daemon is a recorded rejected alternative.\\n2. **Graph-in-Ledger.** The artifact graph has no durable encoding except ledger records + content-addressed bodies; heads, staleness, claims, and status are folds; `reconcile` = refold; sealed segments are never rewritten — there are no ledger migrations by construction.\\n3. **The file seam.** Dispatch/submission are content-addressed trees; `rename(2)` is the sole commit point; dispatch identity is deterministic; adapters are ledger-illiterate; leases/heartbeats/sessions do not exist.\\n4. **Deterministic placement.** The scheduler is a pure function over content-addressed snapshots with mandatory decision traces; capacity pools include Principal attention (workstation-global folds); harvest is a governed two-party protocol; the semantics boundary is enforced by signatures and schemas.\\n5. **Lease-free execution.** At-most-one-active-dispatch is an economy invariant; provisional abandonment means finished work is never discarded; dual-signal Verified is predicate v1; E2 is realized at admission; quarantine is a computed predicate.\\n6. **Governed extension surfaces:** 33 ledger record types (one owner each, versioned, upcast-on-read, golden-corpus ratchet); the aliasing registry with staged, impact-diffed changes; the check registry as defense-in-depth under plan-pinned authority.\\n\\n## Rejected Alternatives (this pass)\\n\\n1. A resident daemon (dissolved reasons; recorded in RFC 0006).\\n2. Same-run attempt re-entry for re-dispatch (closure-then-new-run is the sole mechanism).\\n3. Working-tree locks (split-brain by construction; all primitives in the Graph Store).\\n4. Read-time declaration-freshness for independence (one missed review would silently un-verify every graph; mint-time-only).\\n5. Implied tamper-evidence (v1 states crash-evidence honestly; hardening is an Epoch 3 boundary).\\n6. `attempt_budget_exhausted` as a fourth escalation code (absorbed into `bounds_exhausted` + closed `budget_kind` field).\\n7. Anchor-lexicographic patch ordering and content-bearing sibling references (explicit Work Graph index; anchor-id-only references).\\n8. Janitor-reads-ledger (version-skew reclaim hazard; live set passed as verb input).\\n9. A dispatch archive (bundles regenerate deterministically from the ledger).\\n10. Unbounded anchor retirement (retirement budget + `anchor_reminted` refusal).\\n\\n## Remaining Open Questions\\n\\n1. **Trust hardening (the one deliberate debt):** per-lane uid isolation, keyed seals, external chain anchor — Epoch 3; until then the single-user downgrade stands recorded.\\n2. **Principal throughput:** the v1 shape (acceptance bounds intent throughput) is stated; the graduated-acceptance/delegation RFC is Epoch 3's most important human-side design.\\n3. **Calibration debts:** revalidation priors, deadline classes, capacity pool sizes — all need an epoch of ledger data; record shapes are fixed so policy can iterate without schema churn.\\n4. **Second-signal supply** on one workstation is thin (two sandbox profiles); when verifier backends diversify, `verified` may bump to require distinct aliasing classes for verifiers.\\n5. **Cross-repo group planning** is linked per-repo planning with no global optimizer; revisit if practice shows heavy coupling.\\n\\n## Recommended Next Pass\\n\\n**Build the v0 spine** (the cutline in each runtime RFC's implementation.md): SCF-1 + ledger + object store + admission funnel stages 0–6 + `local` backend + minimal drive loop + status projection. This is deliberately a small-effort, high-verification slice: every piece is deterministic, golden-corpus-testable, and LLM-free. Then RFC 0011 (Self-Hosting Bootstrap) — the first LLM lane dispatched by the real runtime should be a `review` posture over this repository itself.\\n\\n## Critique of the Compilation Prompt (this pass)\\n\\n1. The Epoch 1 critique's amendments worked: scale-at-design-time produced workstation-global capacity folds and chunked marking *in the designs*; pairwise-seam red-teaming found all four criticals at seams. Keep both.\\n2. One-line target-state requests (\\\"advance X to Y\\\") are sufficient input when the decision layer is rich — this pass needed no divergent ontology lanes because Epoch 1's decisions constrained the space. Divergence budget should follow ontological novelty, not pass size.\\n3. The seam-declaration discipline (every lane declares record types and interfaces for the synthesizer) should be a standing template section, not a per-charge instruction.\\n4. What was still missed until the red team: lock topology (two lanes each \\\"owned\\\" concurrency), abandonment semantics (four documents, three answers), and the trust sentence (asserted by 0010, enforced by nobody). Next prompt: assign *concurrency*, *failure-path semantics*, and *trust enforcement* each to exactly one named owner up front, the way invalidation was assigned after Epoch 1.\\n\\n## Terminology
