Specification\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nAccepted (Epoch 1 Foundation Compilation Pass, 2026-07-02).\\n\\nThis document is the canonical language of Striatum-next. Terms not defined here and not in the Retired Terms appendix do not exist. `docs/concepts/language-specification.md` renders this vocabulary; it never diverges from it.\\n\\n## The Layered Ontology\\n\\nEvery term belongs to exactly one layer.\\n\\n```text\\nSUBJECT layer     what compilation is ABOUT\\n                  Artifact (supertype) and its four roles:\\n                  IR · Decision Record · Evidence · Product Artifact\\n\\nTRANSFORM layer   what CHANGES subjects\\n                  Compiler Pass (contract) · Pass Run (instance) · Run Manifest · Pipeline\\n\\nJUDGMENT layer    what PERMITS state transitions\\n                  Quality Gate in three classes: Check · Review · Acceptance\\n                  Verdict · Claim · Claim Level lattice\\n\\nAGENCY layer      who/what DOES the work\\n                  Principal · Driver · Scheduler · Lane · Execution Backend · Agent Runtime\\n\\nMEMORY layer      what REMEMBERS everything\\n                  Provenance Ledger · Provenance Record · Ledger Record types · Attribution\\n```\\n\\nTwo load-bearing structural decisions:\\n\\n1. The SUBJECT layer has one supertype (Artifact) with four disjoint roles. The roles have different invalidation semantics, mutability, and consumers; one undifferentiated word for all four is a type error.\\n2. The MEMORY layer is not part of the SUBJECT layer. Provenance records are not artifacts. Artifacts are the subjects of compilation; the ledger is its memory — append-only, never versioned, never invalidated, never a pass input for lowering.\\n\\n## Glossary\\n\\n### Subject layer\\n\\n- **Artifact** — a durable, versioned, provenance-bearing unit of record in the artifact graph, produced by exactly one pass run and immutable at each version. Every artifact plays exactly one role: IR, Decision Record, Evidence, or Product Artifact.\\n- **Artifact Graph** — the directed graph of artifact versions and their typed edges; together with the provenance ledger, the system of record. One artifact graph exists per target repository; the compiler's own repository is itself a target repository. Cross-graph references are ordinary pins qualified by repository identity.\\n- **Artifact Version** — one immutable revision of an artifact identity; a new version is a new node linked to its predecessor by supersession.\\n- **Element Anchor** — a stable, schema-defined address of one element inside an artifact (a design element, a plan element, a decision clause). Pins and evidence bindings may bind at element grain: (identity, element anchor, element hash).\\n- **Intermediate Representation (IR)** — an artifact role: an artifact class whose purpose is consumption by a downstream pass, with declared producer, consumers, schema, gates, and staleness sensitivities. Each lowering level removes a named class of ambiguity.\\n- **Intent** — a human goal before formal engineering begins. Informal; not an artifact. It becomes compilable only when captured as an Intent Statement.\\n- **Intent Statement** — the L0 source IR: the first durable, verbatim capture of an intent, produced by the intent-capture pass. Never edited, only superseded; the provenance anchor of everything downstream.\\n- **Proposal** — the L1 IR: problem, motivation, candidate direction. Removes problem-framing ambiguity.\\n- **Design** — the L2 IR: what should exist, why, invariants, interfaces, semantics, tradeoffs. Removes architectural ambiguity.\\n- **Implementation Plan** — the L3 IR: phases, dependency rationale, milestones, packet decomposition, verification strategy, migration, rollout. Removes execution-strategy ambiguity. Never relitigates the design.\\n- **Work Graph** — the L4 IR: the machine-oriented dependency graph of work packets derived from an accepted implementation plan, optimized for scheduling rather than human reading. Removes schedulability ambiguity.\\n- **Work Packet** — a node of the Work Graph: the smallest unit of engineering work executable by a single pass run without interactive clarification, declaring purpose, inputs, outputs, dependencies, write scope, and acceptance checks. Anchored to the plan element it derives from.\\n- **Change Set** — the L5 IR: one work packet's bounded output — a diff plus advisory lane-local evidence. The object file of this compiler; integration is the linker. Removes implementation ambiguity.\\n- **Product** — the target repository tree at the accepted versions of its product artifacts. A designation over artifacts, not an artifact. A **Verified Product** is a product whose acceptance-required claims all stand at level Verified with unexpired evidence.\\n- **Product Artifact** — an artifact role: a shipped result — source change, documentation, release — anchored by content hash into the target repository rather than stored in the compiler's own tree.\\n- **RFC Identity** — the namespace `rfcs/000N-topic/` grouping one intent's Proposal, Design, and Implementation Plan IRs, plus its generated Decision Record. An identity, not an artifact. The design conversation lives here.\\n- **Decision Record** — an artifact role: the binding, accepted semantic state distilled from an RFC identity by the decision-generation pass. Generated with element structure; never hand-written; invalidated and regenerated when its owning RFC identity's accepted heads move. The compiler's canonical architectural memory — the compiled interface downstream work links against.\\n- **Evidence** — an artifact role: an immutable attestation of fact about another artifact or about the observed world. Evidence is never invalidated; its **force** decays when the hashes it binds change. Kinds: Review Ledger, Receipt, Verification Report, Exogenous Change Record.\\n- **Review Ledger** — evidence: structured findings from one review pass run — finding id, severity, element anchor, rationale, proposed disposition, a dissent/minority section — plus a summary Verdict. Gates evaluate predicates over ledgers, never prose.\\n- **Receipt** — the atomic evidence kind: a sealed, content-addressed record of one mechanical check execution (command, resolved binary hash, exit code, output digests, tree hash, seal digest), minted by a verifier lane and validated — never executed — by the trusted core.\\n- **Verification Report** — evidence aggregating the receipts and check outcomes for one artifact version against its pinned check identities.\\n- **Exogenous Change Record** — evidence recording world-authored change to a watched target (a human commit, an upstream merge) with attribution, produced by the observation pass. The admission path for the world's writes; claims bound to moved hashes decay automatically.\\n- **Lifecycle State** — the stored position of one artifact version: `candidate → accepted → superseded | retired`. Everything else commonly called a \\\"state\\\" is a computed predicate.\\n- **Target State** — a named, versioned predicate over the artifact graph, defined in the catalog. You cannot declare a target state satisfied; the graph either satisfies it or does not. Gate results pin the predicate version they were evaluated under.\\n- **Compilation Request** — the Principal's command: (subject, target state, constraints). \\\"Advance RFC 0028 to Verified\\\" is a compilation request.\\n- **Staleness** — the computed predicate: an artifact version is stale iff some pinned input's accepted head moved or its producing contract version changed invalidatingly. Stale is not wrong; it is unproven against the present.\\n- **Invalidation** — the propagation of staleness along derivation and environment edges. Marking is eager and transitive; regeneration is lazy and demand-driven.\\n- **Revalidation** — the early-cutoff analysis (a review posture) asking whether a stale artifact still satisfies its gates against the new upstream. An accepting verdict licenses a re-stamp.\\n- **Re-stamp** — the creation of a body-identical artifact version with moved pins, produced by the licensing revalidation `review` run (`production_mode: re_stamp`) and mechanically appended by the Driver; the single gate-exempt accepted-head movement, always provenance-recorded.\\n- **Supersession** — replacement of an artifact version by a successor. Distinct from invalidation: superseded versions were valid; stale ones are unproven.\\n\\n### Transform layer\\n\\n- **Compiler Pass** — a named, versioned transformation contract: class, consumed and produced artifact kinds, environment reads, invariants, gates, determinism class, replay guarantee, effect class, failure modes. Passes produce artifacts; they never move lifecycle states. Three classes: **transform** (lowering plane), **analysis** (evidence plane), and no third — scheduling is not a pass.\\n- **Pass Run** — one provenance-recorded execution of a compiler pass against pinned input artifact versions under a sealed run manifest. The unit of execution history, replay, and attribution.\\n- **Run Manifest** — the immutable record sealed at pass-run start: input pins, environment pins, pass contract version, lane requirements, prompt asset hashes. What \\\"replaying a pass run\\\" means.\\n- **Pipeline** — a catalog-resident template composing passes, gate wiring, and re-run bounds. No new semantics: a pipeline compiles to pass runs. The compiler-native home of reusable composition (falsification treatments, adjudicated panels).\\n- **Lowering** — the direction of compilation: each transform pass consumes a higher-ambiguity representation and produces a lower-ambiguity one, from Intent Statement toward Product.\\n- **Revision** — a re-run of the producing pass with a Review Ledger as declared diagnostic input, producing the next candidate version. There are no fix-passes.\\n- **Contract Version / Impl Version** — the two version fields of a pass. A change is contractual iff it alters consumed/produced schemas, invariants, or gate predicates; contract bumps invalidate outputs. Impl changes (prompts, harness) are recorded and invalidate nothing retroactively.\\n- **Determinism Class** — D0 (bit-replayable), D1 (bit-replayable from transcript), D2 (stochastic; guarantees provenance replay and contract replay only). No consumer may depend on bit replay of a D2 pass.\\n- **Effect Class** — E0 (graph-only), E1 (isolated workspace), E2 (target-repository integration; `integration` only), E3 (external; forbidden without RFC).\\n\\n### Judgment layer\\n\\n- **Quality Gate** — a declared condition an artifact version must satisfy before an accepted-head movement. Every gate is exactly one class: check, review, or acceptance. Gate evaluation is driver mechanics — deterministic predicates over structured data, never delegated to a lane.\\n- **Check Gate** — verification-class: machine-decidable, deterministic, replayable evaluation of a declared contract against evidence (receipts, schema validity, presence, hashes). No judgment.\\n- **Review Gate** — validation-class: a predicate over a Review Ledger produced by an independent review pass run (e.g. \\\"no unresolved findings at severity major or above\\\"). Independence requirements attach here.\\n- **Acceptance Gate** — authority-class: the decision by the Principal, or by policy the Principal has explicitly delegated, that an artifact version becomes the accepted head. Delegation of acceptance over decision-role artifacts requires an RFC, never a policy edit.\\n- **Verification / Validation / Acceptance** — the mechanical, judgment, and authority strata. Acceptance may require validation; validation may require verification; never sideways or backwards. No output type crosses classes.\\n- **Verdict** — the closed summary vocabulary of review: `accept`, `accept_with_findings` (accepting); `needs_revision`, `reject` (non-accepting). Extension requires a language amendment.\\n- **Claim** — a falsifiable statement about an artifact version, carrying a claim level computed from evidence bindings.\\n- **Claim Level** — the lattice `Verified \\u003e Asserted \\u003e Designed`. **Claims are computed views over evidence bindings, never stored truth**: claim(A@v) is the maximum level with valid evidence whose bindings match A@v's pins and current accepted heads. Anything may lower a level; only the minting gate raises one; Verified decays when bound hashes move. The claim cache is a named derived store; head-movement ledger events record implied claim transitions.\\n- **Binding Closure** — the promotion rule: evidence promoting a claim must bind the subject's hash and the accepted-head (or element) hashes of every governing IR. Promotion gates refuse incomplete closure.\\n- **Independence** — the anti-aliasing condition on Verified: the minting execution must share no provenance ancestry (lane, backend session, synthesis lineage) with the producing execution, evaluated over recorded lane attribution and backend aliasing classes (model family). Co-blindness is aliasing.\\n- **Posture** — a cataloged, versioned parameterization of the review pass (adversarial, falsification, second-opinion, plan-critique, test-gap, doc-freshness, dependency-audit, stale-scan, coherence, revalidation), each owning its Review Ledger section schema. Posture versions participate in the pin algebra.\\n\\n### Agency layer\\n\\n- **Principal** — the human authority: source of intent, resolution authority for escalations, default holder of acceptance authority. Not an execution role.\\n- **Driver** — the compiler driver: a deterministic program that inspects graph state, evaluates target predicates, plans pass sequences, requests scheduling, evaluates gates, admits results, propagates staleness, and escalates. It performs no engineering work and **produces no artifacts**; all its outputs are ledger records. Planning may read provenance as data (retry counts, failure records); gates and acceptance never read provenance for authority. (Formerly \\\"Meta-Operator\\\"; retired alias.)\\n- **Scheduler** — the policy engine deciding where work runs: binds lanes to execution backends under versioned scheduler policy. Its outputs are dispatch records mirrored into provenance; they are never semantic. Rescheduling invalidates nothing; any semantic change flushes schedules free.\\n- **Capacity** — a scheduler resource dimension: any bounded, possibly-resetting supply of execution. **Quota** is the capacity kind imposed by vendor subscriptions; the word belongs to policy documents, not the core ontology.\\n- **Lane** — an isolated execution context instantiated inside a pass run, with role, write scope, and independence constraints. An instance; its specification is a **Lane Requirement** (declared by the pass contract); its placement is a **Lane Binding** (the scheduler's dispatch record). Lane topology is pass-internal and never leaks into IR shapes; lane attribution is always recorded in provenance.\\n- **Execution Backend** — the crash-only adapter that launches agent runtimes into lanes: sealed work in; results and evidence submitted out, or nothing. Declares capabilities, constraints, capacity behavior, context and latency profiles, supported and forbidden pass types, provenance fields, and an **aliasing class**. All supervision mechanics are internal. Backends submit; the Driver admits.\\n- **Agent Runtime** — the concrete executable environment inside a lane — a vendor coding harness, a local deterministic tool. Named only inside backend definitions; a model name outside `backends/` is a lint error.\\n\\n### Memory layer\\n\\n- **Provenance** — the guaranteed property that every artifact's complete lineage — producing pass run, pins, run manifest, lane bindings, gate outcomes — is recorded and inspectable. Provenance is never consulted for authority.\\n- **Provenance Ledger** — the append-only substrate of provenance records, segmented into sealed, hash-anchored **segments** whose manifests make reconciliation incremental and archival derivability-preserving. Every record carries a `schema_version`; readers upcast on read and refuse records newer than themselves.\\n- **Provenance Record** — one immutable ledger fact. Named record types: pass-run record, gate result, staleness event (with implied claim transitions), plan record, lane binding mirror, escalation, deviation warning, resolution event, segment manifest.\\n- **Escalation** — a ledger record signaling that compilation cannot proceed without the Principal, carrying a closed reason code (`ambiguous_goal`, `missing_authority`, `contradicting_decisions`, `committee_stalemate`, `override_required`). An unresolved escalation blocks its subgraph; resolution is an appended authority event.\\n- **Attribution** — the provenance fields identifying production: backend, agent runtime, lane role, prompt hashes, contract versions. Derived from recorded truth, never self-asserted.\\n- **Byline** — the rendered, privacy-safe projection of attribution embedded in a human-readable artifact (`author: reviewer-claude-2`).\\n\\n## Naming Conventions (normative)\\n\\n- **N1** — Target states and lifecycle predicates are past participles (`Accepted`, `Verified`, `Integrated`). Stored lifecycle uses the closed set above; `candidate` is the compiler-standard exception.\\n- **N2** — Passes are kebab-case nominalized transformations (`intent-capture`, `design-convergence`, `packetization`). Never named by actor, backend, or model.\\n- **N3** — IR classes are `\\u003cNoun\\u003e` with level (`Design`, L2); instances are named by identity (`rfcs/0028/design.md` is a Design).\\n- **N4** — Gates are `\\u003csubject\\u003e-\\u003cclass\\u003e` (`design-review`, `packet-checks`, `design-acceptance`); the class is readable from the name.\\n- **N5** — Type/instance discipline: pass → pass run; decision → decision record; lane requirement → lane. No word names both.\\n- **N6** — Closed vocabularies (verdicts, claim levels, escalation reasons, determinism/effect classes) stay closed; extension requires amending this RFC.\\n- **N7** — Banned morphology: no `meta-` prefixes; no `-manager`/`-orchestrator`/`-coordinator` agent nouns; no vendor or model names outside `backends/`; no humor in load-bearing names.\\n- **N8** — Definition before use: a term used in any RFC must exist here, or the RFC carries an explicit Language Amendment section.\\n- **N9** — Retirement is explicit: terms leave only via the Retired Terms appendix, with disposition and replacement.\\n\\n## Conceptual Invariants (every future RFC preserves these)\\n\\n- **P1 — Provenance totality.** Every artifact version has exactly one producing pass run. No artifact appears by hand — decision records especially. The Driver produces no artifacts.\\n- **P2 — Category exclusivity.** Every durable concept is exactly one of: artifact (in one role), compiler pass, pipeline, scheduler policy, execution backend capability, quality gate, provenance record type. Fitting none or two is a design error.\\n- **P3 — Provenance is memory, not subject.** The ledger is append-only; records are never versioned or invalidated; provenance records are not artifacts.\\n- **P4 — Passes produce; gates permit; the Driver transitions; the scheduler places.** A pass never moves lifecycle state; a gate never produces artifacts; the Driver never performs engineering work; the scheduler never touches meaning.\\n- **P5 — Ambiguity monotonicity.** Each lowering pass leaves the compilation no more ambiguous about the subject intent than its input, and introduces no decision belonging to a higher level.\\n- **P6 — Claim soundness.** Levels are computed from evidence bindings; only minting gates with complete binding closure raise them; anything may lower them; Verified decays on bound-hash movement.\\n- **P7 — Gate trichotomy purity.** Every gate is exactly one of check/review/acceptance; no output type crosses classes.\\n- **P8 — Decisions are the link target.** Downstream work links against decision records, never RFC prose; staleness propagates along environment edges at element grain; only revoked records fail closed.\\n- **P9 — Backend independence.** No pass contract, IR schema, or gate names an execution backend or model. Backend facts enter semantics only as declared capability facts (e.g. aliasing class) read by declared rules (e.g. independence).\\n- **P10 — No state outside the graph and ledger.** Terminal output, branch names, marker files, and chat transcripts are never state.\\n\\n## Epoch 2 Amendments (Runtime Foundation Pass, 2026-07-02)\\n\\nAccepted via the N8 mechanism as part of RFCs 0006–0010.\\n\\n**Escalation vocabulary (N6 extension).** The closed reason set gains three codes: `bounds_exhausted` (automation must stop retrying; the escalation record's closed `budget_kind` field — `revision | redispatch | attempt_total | integration_conflict | withdrawal` — names the exhausted budget), `binding_unsatisfiable` (no capable backend exists for a lane requirement), and `independence_unsatisfiable` (capable backends exist but anti-aliasing cannot be satisfied). Final set (8): `ambiguous_goal`, `missing_authority`, `contradicting_decisions`, `committee_stalemate`, `override_required`, `bounds_exhausted`, `binding_unsatisfiable`, `independence_unsatisfiable`.\\n\\n**New terms by layer** (full definitions in the owning RFC's design):\\n\\n- *Agency:* **Agent Principal** (an agent runtime exercising a recorded, bounded delegation of Principal-issuable acts; never acceptance authority over decision-role artifacts without an RFC), **Drive Session**, **Wake** (a non-authoritative Driver trigger; a missed wake delays, never corrupts), **Acceptance Queue** (named derived store), **Dispatch**, **Submission**, **Spool** (owner RFC 0007), **Workspace**, **Attempt**, **Aliasing Registry** / **Kinship**.\\n- *Scheduling:* **Capacity Pool**, **Capacity Snapshot**, **Capacity Harvest**, **Dispatch Horizon** (an interpretation rule, not a liveness claim), **Scheduling Decision**.\\n- *Memory/store:* **Graph Store**, **Object Store**, **Body Placement**, **Canonical Form (SCF)**, **Anchor Map**, **Anchor Continuity**, **Graph Genesis**, **Repository Identity**, **Constitutional Decision**.\\n- *Judgment/execution:* **Check** / **Check Identity** / **Check Registry**, **Attempt Budget**, **Residual Run**, **Partial-Admission Closure Rule**, **Dual-Signal Rule**.\\n\\n**Operational conventions (by reference; not glossary terms):** Exhaust, Advisory Signal/Pulse, Session Nonce, Quiescence, Harvest Window, Composed Base, Integration Frontier, Linked Tree, Intra-Run Derivation Map, Open-Run Invariant — defined in their owning RFCs.\\n\\n- **N10** — Record-type names and operational conventions never enter the core term list; bulk term admissions require per-term layer assignment and duplicate-merge adjudication.\\n\\n## Epoch 3 Amendment (Adapter Supervision, 2026-07-02)\\n\\nAccepted via the N8 mechanism as part of RFC 0013 (its design's Language Amendments section is the owning text; this section mirrors it).\\n\\n**New term by layer:**\\n\\n- *Agency:* **Lane Supervisor** — the detached per-dispatch process, forked by an LLM backend's `dispatch` verb, that owns runtime invocation, the bounded internal-relaunch loop, pre-submission validation, the rename commit, and the post-commit wake for exactly one dispatch. Nothing supervises it; its death is a lapsed dispatch — and, by fate-sharing, the death of every runtime process it started, descendants included. Realizes RFC 0007's \\\"per-dispatch supervisor child.\\\"\\n\\n**Operational conventions (by reference; not glossary terms):** Supervisor Hint, Kill Domain, Fate-Sharing — defined in RFC 0013's design and bound by D0013.\\n\\n## Ontology-Discipline Amendment (2026-07-02)\\n\\nAccepted via the N8 mechanism as a self-amendment of this RFC — the constituting language specification is extended by its own amendment mechanism, with no separate owning RFC.\\n\\n- **N11** — Prefer strengthening existing ontology over introducing new ontology. Before a new term, concept, or abstraction is admitted, establish that no accepted concept already holds its role and strengthen that one instead; a genuinely new durable concept enters only via the N8 amendment mechanism and never shadows an existing home (P2).\\n\\nThis amendment also retrofits this RFC to the mechanical decision-generation contract: the authored Decision (clauses), Consequences, and Constrains sections below make `decisions/D0001-language-specification.md` a projection of this design — generated by the `decision-generation` pass, never hand-authored (P1) — retiring the Epoch 1 bootstrap exception under which D0001 was previously curated by hand.\\n\\n## Admission-Completeness Amendment (2026-07-02)\\n\\nAccepted via the N8 mechanism as a self-amendment of this RFC. Applying N11, it admits no new term: every concept it binds already has an accepted home. Implementation lives in the Product Artifact role; justification lives in the owning RFC identity's Decision Record (P8); explanation lives in documentation, which the Product Artifact role has named as a shipped result since Epoch 1 — documentation is an artifact in the graph, never commentary outside it. What was missing was not a concept but a binding: nothing constitutional said the three must hold together.\\n\\n- **P11 — Admission completeness.** A capability of the compiled system is fully admitted only when the artifact graph simultaneously holds its three projections, each admitted through the existing gate classes (P7): **implementation** — the Product Artifacts realizing it; **justification** — the owning RFC identity's accepted, fresh Decision Record; **explanation** — canonical documentation in the target repository's Diátaxis home, itself a Product Artifact under the same admission semantics as any other. These are complementary projections of one admitted change, never independent checklists. Implementation never silently outruns explanation: architecture that moves without its documentation leaves the graph unsatisfied against this invariant — the gap is a computed fact, not an informal \\\"docs pending.\\\"\\n\\nThe word \\\"capability\\\" in this amendment is ordinary language, not a Subject-layer admission: the constitutional unit remains the RFC identity distilled into its Decision Record, realized by Product Artifacts. The only ontological sense of \\\"capability\\\" remains the execution-backend capability fact (P2, P9). The computed form of this invariant is the registered target state `capability-admission-complete` (catalog-resident, versioned; its v1 evaluation bound is stated honestly in the entry). The conceptual invariants now range P1–P11.\\n\\n## Decision (clauses)\\n\\n- **D0001.C1 — Layered ontology.** Five layers: Subject, Transform, Judgment, Agency, Memory. Every term belongs to exactly one.\\n- **D0001.C2 — Four artifact roles.** Artifact is a supertype with disjoint roles IR, Decision Record, Evidence, Product Artifact, each with distinct invalidation semantics. Provenance records are not artifacts.\\n- **D0001.C3 — Driver.** The compiler driver is named Driver; Meta-Operator is a retired alias. Operator is retired entirely (Principal / lane role / Driver by sense).\\n- **D0001.C4 — Lane split.** Lane (instance) / Lane Requirement (contract) / Lane Binding (dispatch record). A lane is not an execution backend.\\n- **D0001.C5 — Workflow ban.** \\\"Workflow\\\" is banned from the ontology; Pipeline, pass contract, pass run, and run manifest replace its senses.\\n- **D0001.C6 — Closed vocabularies.** Verdicts (`accept`, `accept_with_findings`, `needs_revision`, `reject`), claim levels (`Verified \\u003e Asserted \\u003e Designed`), escalation reason codes, determinism classes (D0–D2), and effect classes (E0–E3) are closed; extension amends RFC 0001.\\n- **D0001.C7 — Capacity.** The core scheduler resource term is Capacity; quota is policy vocabulary.\\n- **D0001.C8 — Conventions and invariants.** Naming conventions N1–N9 and conceptual invariants P1–P10 are normative for all future RFCs.\\n- **D0001.C9 — Retirement discipline.** Terms leave the language only via the Retired Terms appendix with disposition and replacement.\\n- **D0001.C10 — Epoch 2 amendments.** The escalation vocabulary is eight codes (adds `bounds_exhausted` with closed `budget_kind`, `binding_unsatisfiable`, `independence_unsatisfiable`); the runtime term set (Agent Principal, Wake, Dispatch/Submission/Spool, Capacity Pool/Snapshot/Harvest, Graph Store, Object Store, SCF, Anchor Map/Continuity, Check Registry, Residual Run, Partial-Admission Closure Rule, Dual-Signal Rule, and peers) is admitted per RFC 0001 §Epoch 2 Amendments; operational conventions stay in their owning RFCs; N10 governs future admissions.\\n- **D0001.C11 — Epoch 3 amendment (adapter supervision).** The Agency-layer term Lane Supervisor is admitted per RFC 0001 §Epoch 3 Amendment (owning text: RFC 0013's Language Amendments, bound by D0013): the detached per-dispatch process that owns runtime invocation, the bounded relaunch loop, pre-submission validation, the rename commit, and the post-commit wake for exactly one dispatch, nothing supervising it. Its operational conventions — Supervisor Hint, Kill Domain, Fate-Sharing — stay in RFC 0013 by reference.\\n- **D0001.C12 — Ontology-strengthening discipline.** Naming convention N11 is admitted: prefer strengthening existing ontology over introducing new ontology. A new term, concept, or abstraction is admitted only after it is shown that no accepted concept already holds its role — strengthen that one instead; a genuinely new durable concept enters via the N8 amendment mechanism alone and never shadows an existing home (P2). The naming conventions now range N1–N11; this clause serves invariant P2.\\n- **D0001.C13 — Admission completeness.** Conceptual invariant P11 is admitted per RFC 0001 §Admission-Completeness Amendment: a capability of the compiled system is fully admitted only when implementation (Product Artifacts), justification (the owning RFC identity's accepted, fresh Decision Record), and explanation (canonical Diátaxis documentation — itself a Product Artifact, never commentary outside the graph) hold simultaneously in the artifact graph, each admitted through the existing gate classes; implementation never silently outruns explanation. No new term is minted: \\\"capability\\\" stays ordinary language, and the ontological sense remains the execution-backend capability fact (P2, P9). The computed form is the registered target state `capability-admission-complete`. The conceptual invariants now range P1–P11.\\n\\n## Consequences\\n\\nAll catalogs, schemas, docs, and future RFCs use this vocabulary exclusively; undefined-but-used and retired-but-used terms are lint errors. Terms like \\\"workflow\\\" import the old primitive's thinking into the new primitive's architecture.\\n\\nNames outlive implementations. Every future RFC either inherits a precise vocabulary or re-fights these ambiguities.\\n\\n## Target State\\n\\nOne canonical language: a layered ontology, a closed glossary, naming conventions, conceptual invariants, and an explicit retired-terms appendix. All subsequent RFCs reference these definitions; none redefine them.\\n\\n## Non-Goals\\n\\n- Runtime vocabulary (daemon, RPC, CLI verbs) — Epoch 2.\\n- Scheduler policy vocabulary beyond what the foundation names.\\n- Preserving Striatum-0 terms out of familiarity.\\n\\n## Source Material\\n\\n- `incubation/04-phase0-language-specification.md` (instance evidence, archived in the instance repository `halbritt/striatum-instance` under `striatum-next/rfcs/0000-bootstrapping-striatum-next/incubation/`)\\n- Striatum-0 `docs/reference/ubiquitous-language.md` (operational experience)\\n- Epoch 1 divergent lanes A/B/C and red-team reconciliation\\n\\n## Affected Canonical Documents\\n\\n`docs/concepts/language-specification.md` (the rendered glossary), `AGENTS.md` (ontology section), all catalog entries, `decisions/D0001-language-specification.md` (generated).\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0002-compiler-architecture/design.md\": \"# RFC 0002 Design: Compiler Architecture\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nAccepted (Epoch 1 Foundation Compilation Pass, 2026-07-02). Vocabulary: RFC 0001.\\n\\n## The Compilation Model\\n\\nThe compilation state of an intent is two-dimensional, plus a computed staleness predicate:\\n\\n- **The lowering plane** removes ambiguity classes: Intent Statement (L0) → Proposal (L1) → Design (L2) → Implementation Plan (L3) → Work Graph (L4) → Change Set (L5) → Product (L6, a designation over product artifacts). Defined in RFC 0003.\\n- **The evidence plane** raises justified confidence in artifacts that already exist: Review Ledgers, Receipts, Verification Reports, Exogenous Change Records — and the claims computed from their bindings. Verification is not an IR; Product is not an IR.\\n- **The environment plane** is the decision layer: generated Decision Records that passes link against. The RFC is the design conversation; the decision record is the accepted semantic state.\\n\\nProvenance is the third substrate: the append-only memory of how all planes moved. All stored state is minimal; pipeline positions, target states, staleness, and claims are computed predicates over the graph and ledger. You cannot declare Verified; you can only be Verified.\\n\\n## The Derived-State Doctrine (invariant, binding on Epoch 2)\\n\\nThe system of record is the artifact graph — content-addressed artifact versions anchored in git plus the append-only provenance ledger. Every runtime store (index, queue, cache, database, claim cache, status projection) is derived and rebuildable from graph + ledger; destroying one is never data loss. Schema evolution of derived stores is `rm \\u0026\\u0026 rebuild`, never a migration.\\n\\nThe ledger itself carries the only durable format commitment: every provenance record has a `schema_version`; readers upcast on read; a reader older than a record refuses to interpret it (park, don't crash-loop). The ledger is segmented into sealed, hash-anchored segments; segment manifests make reconciliation incremental and define derivability-preserving archival — evidence and superseded versions move to cold segments verifiable by manifest without loading. This is the structural cure for the bootstrap compiler's migration treadmill; it must not be renegotiated silently in Epoch 2.\\n\\n## Components\\n\\nFive components. Each has one owner-sentence and explicit prohibitions.\\n\\n### Artifact Store\\n*Owns durable truth.* Content-addressed artifact versions and metadata (kind, role, level, lifecycle, pins), git anchoring for source-like artifacts, blob storage for bulky evidence from day one, and the provenance ledger as its write-ahead surface. Provides put/get by hash, staleness evaluation, graph queries. Prohibited: interpreting artifact semantics, executing anything, granting authority.\\n\\n### Compiler Core\\n*Owns semantics.* A deterministic library that loads catalogs and schemas and answers semantic questions: pass contracts, IR well-formedness, gate predicates, staleness and claim computation, target-predicate evaluation, receipt-seal validation. Prohibited: choosing backends, launching work, owning processes or wall-clock.\\n\\n### Driver\\n*Owns advancement.* The loop: read graph → evaluate target predicate → plan (emitting a plan record to the ledger) → request scheduling → evaluate gates on submitted results → admit → append provenance → repeat or escalate. The Driver is a deterministic program, not an agent: planning is graph reachability over declared catalog data. If the Driver \\\"needs judgment,\\\" a gate or declaration is underspecified — fix the declaration. The Driver produces no artifacts; all its outputs are ledger records. Planning may read provenance as data (retry counts, failure history) to break livelock; gates and acceptance never read provenance for authority. Escalation is its only interruptive act, via ledger records with the closed reason vocabulary. Prohibited: performing engineering work, editing artifacts, overriding gates, talking to backends directly.\\n\\n### Scheduler\\n*Owns placement.* A pure function: (ready pass runs, backend capability declarations, capacity state, versioned policy) → lane bindings. Bindings are dispatch records mirrored into provenance; the dispatch channel is the authority, the ledger entry is the record. Scheduler outputs are never semantic: rescheduling invalidates nothing; any semantic change flushes schedules free. Capacity-harvest behavior and telemetry-driven learning are policy versions of this one component. Prohibited: redefining pass contracts, mutating artifacts, blocking gates, touching claim minting.\\n\\n### Execution Backends\\n*Own execution.* Crash-only adapters: a sealed work packet and pass prompt assets go in; a result set with evidence is submitted out, or nothing is. All supervision, liveness, and process mechanics are internal and invisible above the seam — a dead backend is indistinguishable from a slow one, and both are handled by re-dispatch (pass purity makes this safe). Backends declare capabilities, constraints, capacity behavior, context/latency profiles, supported and forbidden pass types, provenance fields, and an aliasing class (model family) as a capability fact. Prohibited: writing to the artifact store directly, defining pass semantics, holding state the core depends on.\\n\\nThe human Principal is not a component: the human appears exactly twice — as the source of intent and as the authority behind acceptance gates not explicitly delegated.\\n\\n## The Submit/Admit Seam\\n\\nBackends submit; the Driver admits through gates. Nothing a backend does is true until admitted into the artifact store. The single-writer property lives at the admission boundary; execution is arbitrarily parallel and untrusted. Partial admission exists: a pass run may submit a partial result set (failure mode `partial`); the Driver gates admission per-output and re-dispatches the residual — finished lanes' work is never discarded.\\n\\n## Exogenous Change\\n\\nThe world writes to target repositories — human commits, upstream merges, hotfixes. The `observation` pass records world-authored change to watched targets as Exogenous Change Records with attribution. Claims whose binding closure includes moved hashes decay automatically; integration consumes observed product state. A mixed human/compiler repository is the normal case, not an error.\\n\\n## Graph Scope\\n\\nOne artifact graph per target repository. The compiler's own repository is itself a target repository (self-hosting). Cross-graph references are ordinary pins qualified by repository identity; cross-repository intents compile as linked per-repository compilations; the executing repository's policy governs its passes.\\n\\n## Recovery and Legibility\\n\\n- **One recovery verb:** `reconcile` — re-derive all runtime state from graph + ledger (incremental via segment manifests) and report artifacts whose bindings no longer verify. A second recovery verb is evidence that hidden state has crept back in.\\n- **Status projection (Epoch 2 boundary, named now):** a read-only derived store answering the operator's questions — what is running, what is wedged, what waits on the Principal — with actionable-vs-advisory triage (warnings vs notices) as a stated requirement, inherited from the bootstrap compiler's doctor legibility lessons.\\n\\n## Boundary Decision Procedure\\n\\nFor any proposed behavior, in order:\\n\\n1. Does it change what an artifact means, which artifacts exist, or when one is valid? → **Compiler semantics.** Lives in `catalog/` + `schema/`; changes require an RFC and regenerate a decision record.\\n2. Vocabulary: RFC 0001. A lowering pass may refine and serialize; it may never introduce a decision belonging to a higher level (P5).\\n\\n| Level | IR | Removes ambiguity of | Producer | Consumers |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| L0 | Intent Statement | — (captures it all) | `intent-capture` | `proposal-generation` |\\n| L1 | Proposal | problem framing | `proposal-generation` | `design-convergence` |\\n| L2 | Design | architecture | `design-convergence` | `implementation-planning` |\\n| L3 | Implementation Plan | execution strategy | `implementation-planning` | `packetization` |\\n| L4 | Work Graph | schedulability | `packetization` | scheduler, `build` |\\n| L5 | Change Set | implementation | `build` | `verification`, `integration` |\\n\\nL6, the **Product**, is a designation over accepted Product Artifacts anchored in the target repository — the linked output, not an IR.\\n\\n### Intent Statement (L0)\\n- **Purpose:** verbatim durable capture of a Principal's intent; the provenance anchor of the compilation.\\n- **Required:** verbatim intent text, principal attribution, capture context.\\n- **Forbidden:** interpretation, scoping, solutioning — capture must not editorialize.\\n- **Invariants:** never edited, only superseded.\\n- **Gates:** capture-checks (check: non-empty, attributed).\\n\\n### Proposal (L1)\\n- **Required:** problem, motivation, candidate direction, explicit non-goals.\\n- **Forbidden:** architectural commitments, interface definitions, implementation sequencing.\\n- **Gates:** proposal-review (review), proposal-acceptance (acceptance).\\n\\n### Design (L2)\\n- **Required:** what should exist, why, invariants, interfaces, semantics, tradeoffs, rejected alternatives; stable **element anchors** per design element.\\n- **Forbidden:** execution sequencing, packet decomposition, backend or model references (P9).\\n- **Gates:** design-review (review), design-acceptance (acceptance).\\n\\n### Implementation Plan (L3)\\n- **Required:** phases, dependency rationale, milestones, packet boundaries (each citing the design elements it implements), verification strategy per boundary, migration and rollout, risk register; element anchors per plan element.\\n- **Forbidden:** relitigating L2 decisions (gate-checked); prose that belongs in the work graph.\\n- **Gates:** implementation-plan-review (review), implementation-plan-acceptance (acceptance).\\n\\n### Work Graph (L4)\\n- **Required:** work packets (purpose, inputs, outputs, dependencies, write scope, acceptance checks, `derived_from` plan-element anchor), edges, parallelism constraints (disjoint write scopes).\\n- **Forbidden:** prose rationale (it lives at L3); any packet not derivable from a plan element — if packetization must invent structure, that is a finding against the plan, not license to improvise.\\n- **Invariants:** acyclic; every packet anchored; disjoint write scopes for parallel packets.\\n- **Gates:** work-graph-legality (check).\\n\\n### Change Set (L5)\\n- **Required:** bounded diff (isolated-workspace commits), the packet pin it implements, advisory lane-local evidence, attribution.\\n- **Forbidden:** self-certification — advisory evidence never promotes claims (RFC 0005); Downstream passes link against decisions, never RFC prose.\\n- **Producer:** `decision-generation`, on every accepted-stage transition of the owning RFC identity. A design-only decision is in force, and says so, while implementation is pending.\\n- **Required:** the decision in force, its consequences, scope of constraint, pins of the exact accepted stage hashes generated from, **element structure** (decision clauses with anchors) from day one.\\n- **Forbidden:** rationale and alternatives (they live in the owning RFC); hand-edits (provenance totality, P1 — a version with no producing pass run is refused at admission).\\n- **Gates:** decision-acceptance (acceptance; mandatory human authority in Epoch 1; delegation requires an RFC).\\n- **Staleness:** owning RFC accepted-head movement stales the record (element grain where determinable). future Intent Statements.\\n- **Invariants:** never regenerated, only superseded by later product versions.\\n\\n## Ledger Record Types Are Not Kinds\\n\\nPlan records, gate results, staleness events, lane binding mirrors, escalations, deviation warnings, resolution events, and segment manifests are provenance-ledger record types (RFC 0001, Memory layer) — not artifacts, and not listed here.\\n\\n## Staleness Sensitivities (per kind; algebra in RFC 0005)\\n\\n- Each IR is stale when its upstream IR's accepted head (or bound elements) move, when a linked decision record regenerates (element grain), or when its producing pass's contract version bumps.\\n- Change Set bodies do not rot when designs move; their **claims** decay (binding closure). Work graphs stale on plan movement; unbuilt packets stale with their graph.\\n- Decision records stale on owning-RFC movement. Evidence never stales; its force decays. Vocabulary: RFC 0001. Gate, claim, and invalidation semantics: RFC 0005 (referenced, never redefined).\\n\\n## Pass Classes\\n\\n- **Transform passes** (lowering plane): consume artifact versions, produce new artifact versions at the same or lower level. They bear invalidation: outputs go stale when inputs move.\\n- **Analysis passes** (evidence plane): consume artifact versions, produce evidence. They never transform. Results are cached by input pins; cache invalidation is exactly claim decay.\\n\\nThere is no third class. **Scheduling is not a pass** — it transforms no artifact and produces no engineering product; assignments are dispatch records mirrored into provenance. This rejection is recorded in D0004 so it cannot silently return.\\n\\n## The Catalog (eleven passes; a twelfth requires an RFC)\\n\\n**Transform (8):**\\n\\n| Pass | Consumes | Produces |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `intent-capture` | Principal utterance | Intent Statement (L0) |\\n| `proposal-generation` | Intent Statement | Proposal (L1) |\\n| `design-convergence` | accepted Proposal [+ Review Ledger on re-run] | Design (L2) |\\n| `implementation-planning` | accepted Design [+ Review Ledger] | Implementation Plan (L3) |\\n| `packetization` | accepted Implementation Plan | Work Graph (L4) |\\n| `build` | Work Packet + governing pins | Change Set (L5) |\\n| `integration` | Verified Change Sets + Work Graph | Product Artifacts (L6 delta) |\\n| `decision-generation` | accepted RFC-identity stage versions | Decision Record |\\n\\n**Analysis (3):**\\n\\n| Pass | Consumes | Produces |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `review` | any artifact version (decision-role included) | Review Ledger |\\n| `verification` | Change Set or product delta + pinned check identities | Receipts + Verification Report |\\n| `observation` | watched targets (product tree, upstream deps) | Exogenous Change Records |\\n\\nNotes:\\n- `review` is one parameterized contract. **Postures** (adversarial, falsification, second-opinion, plan-critique, test-gap, doc-freshness, dependency-audit, stale-scan, coherence, revalidation) are catalog entries with owned ledger-section schemas and versions that participate in the pin algebra. The capacity-harvest backlog references posture parameterizations; it may define no new passes.\\n- `verification` executes checks only in disposable verifier lanes; the trusted core validates sealed receipts and never executes. `build` must not self-certify: lane-local evidence is advisory; claims are promoted only via independent `verification` (RFC 0005).\\n- `integration` is the linker. A conflict is a typed failure attaching findings to the conflicting Change Sets; resolution is a re-run of `build` on the loser, never a hand-merge without provenance.\\n- `observation` is mechanical (D0) and is the sole admission path for world-authored change.\\n- Internal lane topology (divergent lanes + synthesizer, panels) is pass implementation, not contract — except that contracts declare `synthesis: single | synthesized-from-N` because it affects independence accounting, and lane attribution is always recorded in provenance.\\n\\n## Not Passes\\n\\n- **Gate evaluation** — pass-boundary semantics: the Driver mechanically evaluates declared gates over outputs and evidence at every pass exit. Deterministic, never delegated to a lane. If a gate needs judgment, the judgment must already exist as a Review Ledger; the gate evaluates a predicate over it.\\n- **Invalidation propagation** — Driver mechanics emitting ledger events; never scheduled, never delegated.\\n- **Revision** — a re-run of the producing pass with the Review Ledger as declared diagnostic input, producing the next candidate version. There are no fix-passes. Re-run bounds before escalation are driver policy.\\n- **Re-stamping** — the driver-mechanical act licensed by an accepting revalidation verdict (RFC 0005).\\n\\n## Composition: Pipelines\\n\\nA **Pipeline** is a catalog-resident template composing passes, gate wiring, and re-run bounds — no new semantics; it compiles to pass runs. Falsification treatments, cross-examination, and adjudicated panels are pipelines over `review` postures and gates. Epoch 2 populates `catalog/pipelines/`; the concept is fixed now so composition never lives in prompt conventions or scripts.\\n\\n## The Pass Contract Schema\\n\\nEvery entry in `catalog/passes/` declares:\\n\\n```yaml\\nid: implementation-planning\\nclass: transform                # transform | analysis\\ncontract_version: 1             # semantic; bump invalidates outputs\\nimpl_version: 1                 # prompts/harness; recorded, non-invalidating\\nconsumes:\\n  - kind: design\\n    level: L2\\n    lifecycle: accepted\\n    claim_min: Designed\\n  - kind: review-ledger          # declared diagnostic input for re-runs\\n    optional: true\\nenvironment:                     # declared reads; undeclared reads violate hermeticity\\n  decisions: [D0001, D0003, D0005]   # element grain where anchors exist\\n  policies: [repository]\\nproduces:\\n  - kind: implementation-plan\\n    level: L3\\n    enters_as: candidate         # outputs always enter as candidate; only gates move heads\\ninvariants:\\n  pre:  [\\\"input design is the accepted head and not stale (or last-accepted under a recorded deviation)\\\"]\\n  post: [\\\"every packet boundary cites design elements\\\",\\n         \\\"no L2 decision introduced or reversed\\\",\\n         \\\"verification strategy covers every boundary\\\"]\\ngates: [implementation-plan-review, implementation-plan-acceptance]\\ndeterminism: D2                  # D0 | D1 | D2\\nreplay: contract                 # bit | contract\\nidempotence: versioning          # re-run with identical pins yields a new candidate version;\\n                                 # passes are pure functions to new versions, never mutations\\neffects: E0                      # E0 | E1 | E2 (integration only) | E3 (forbidden without RFC)\\nfailure:\\n  modes: [gate_refusal, pass_error, partial, escalation, abandonment]\\ncommutes_with: []\\nresources:                       # advisory, scheduler-facing, never semantic\\n  context: large\\n  latency_class: batch\\n```\\n\\n**Version adjudication:** a change is contractual iff it alters consumed/produced schemas, invariants, or gate predicates; everything else is impl. Enforced by lint. Impl bumps invalidate nothing retroactively; the hermeticity deviation is visible in provenance.\\n\\n## The Replay Doctrine\\n\\n- **D0** — bit-replayable (local deterministic tools; gate evaluation; receipt validation; `observation`; target class for `decision-generation`).\\n- **D1** — bit-replayable from recorded transcript.\\n- **D2** — stochastic (LLM lanes). Guarantees: **provenance replay** (the run can be re-instantiated exactly — same pins, environment, prompt assets, backend identity) and **contract replay** (any re-execution with identical pins satisfies the same postconditions and gates).\\n\\nNo consumer may depend on bit replay of a D2 pass. A design that breaks when a regenerated artifact differs textually while passing the same gates is defective — semantics live in gates and invariants; bytes are an execution accident.\\n\\n## Failure Semantics\\n\\n- `gate_refusal` — outputs produced, gate failed; candidates remain, head unmoved.\\n- `pass_error` — no outputs; inputs untouched (purity makes abort rollback-free).\\n- `partial` — a partial result set submitted; the Driver gates admission per-output and re-dispatches a residual run for the missing lanes. Finished lanes' work is never discarded.\\n- `escalation` — an escalation ledger record with a closed reason code; the affected subgraph halts pending Principal resolution.\\n- `abandonment` — the execution vanished (crash-only backends); the packet is simply still unexecuted and may be re-dispatched.\\n\\n## Optimization Legality (fixed now, exercised later)\\n\\nPass reordering only within declared commutativity; lowering passes on one identity are totally ordered by level. Work-Graph-level optimization (packet fusion/fission, false-dependency pruning) operates only on unclaimed regions, must preserve plan-derivability, and re-passes work-graph-legality; an optimized Work Graph is a new version, `derived_from` the old. Speculative execution is legal only for E0/E1 with `speculative_on` pins; aborted speculation retires versions and keeps provenance. Memoization keys on (contract_version, input pins, environment pins); D2 cache hits are reused via revalidation stamping, never claimed bit-equivalent. Optimization is illegal across gates, in claim promotion, and in provenance.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers\\n\\nFull deliberation in the Epoch 1 record.
