Vocabulary: RFC 0001. This RFC is the single home of lifecycle, well-formedness, invalidation, and judgment semantics.\\n\\n## Stored Lifecycle (the whole machine)\\n\\nPer artifact version:\\n\\n```text\\ncandidate → accepted → superseded | retired\\n```\\n\\n- `candidate` — produced by a pass run, not yet admitted. The only state pass outputs may enter in.\\n- `accepted` — a gate-passing transition moved the identity's accepted head here. The only state other passes may consume (with the recorded-deviation exception for pending decision regeneration).\\n- `superseded` — a newer accepted version exists for the identity.\\n- `retired` — the identity was deliberately withdrawn.\\n\\nEverything else commonly called a \\\"state\\\" is a **computed predicate**: staleness, claim levels, pipeline positions, and target states are queries over the graph and ledger, never stored flags. The incubation twelve-state ladder (`Idea Captured … Verified Product`) survives only as a human-facing projection. This is the structural defense against hidden lifecycle state, state-machine migrations, and declared-but-not-true status.\\n\\n## Artifact-Graph Well-Formedness (W1–W10)\\n\\n- **W1 — Typed nodes.** Every node is an artifact version: (identity, version, kind, role, level, content_hash, schema_version). Identities are stable; versions are immutable and append-only.\\n- **W2 — Typed edges.** Exactly four kinds: `derived_from` (data dependency), `constrained_by` (environment dependency: decision records and policies, element grain where anchors exist), `evidences` (evidence → the artifact-version claim it supports), `supersedes` (version chain).\\n- **W3 — Acyclicity.** `derived_from ∪ constrained_by` is a DAG over versions. (Cycles across identities over time are fine — Product feeds future Intent Statements — because versions are distinct nodes.)\\n- **W4 — Single producer.** Every artifact version has exactly one producing pass run (provenance totality). World-authored change enters only through `observation`; the Driver produces no artifacts. A version with no producing pass run is refused at admission — this is the write-time enforcement that makes \\\"decision records are never hand-written\\\" structural.\\n- **W5 — Pinned references.** Every reference is a pin: (identity, content_hash), optionally element-scoped (identity, element anchor, element hash). Never \\\"latest.\\\" Pins make staleness decidable.\\n- **W6 — Accepted-head uniqueness.** Each identity has at most one accepted head. The head moves only via a gate-passing transition, with exactly one named exception: the **revalidation re-stamp** (below), which is provenance-recorded and licensed by an accepting revalidation verdict.\\n- **W7 — Gate results are immutable ledger records** binding (artifact_version, gate_id + predicate version, verdict, evidence pins, evaluated_at). Re-evaluation appends.\\n- **W8 — Claims are computed, never stored.** Any persisted claim value is a cache — a named derived store under the Derived-State Doctrine; head-movement events record the claim transitions they imply, so decay is event-visible for audit.\\n- **W9 — Environment totality.** A pass run records every decision record and policy version it read (element grain where anchors exist). An undeclared environment read is a hermeticity violation.\\n- **W10 — Plane discipline.** Evidence never enters lowering passes except as declared diagnostic input to a re-run. Lowering edges never originate from evidence.\\n\\n## The Invalidation Algebra (one home, one mechanism)\\n\\n### The dirty bit\\n\\n\\u003e stale(A@v) ≡ ∃ pin p of A@v such that p's identity's current accepted head (or bound element hash) differs, or A@v's producing pass contract_version changed invalidatingly.\\n\\nA computed, monotone, decidable predicate. Stored marks are caches refreshed by ledger events.\\n\\n### Revalidation (early cutoff)\\n\\nStale is not wrong. Before regenerating, the Driver schedules **revalidation** — the `review` posture asking whether the stale artifact still satisfies its gates against the new upstream (mechanical/D0 where only check gates apply). Two outcomes:\\n\\n- **revalidated** — a **re-stamp** follows: a new, body-identical version with moved pins, **produced by the licensing revalidation `review` run** (`production_mode: re_stamp`); the Driver performs only the mechanical append and head movement. Gate-exempt (W6's single exception), always provenance-recorded. Downstream pins match again; the cascade stops. Because pins are content hashes, downstream evidence bound to the unchanged body survives — claims survive revalidation. (Attribution clarified in the Epoch 2 Runtime Foundation Pass: W4 holds without exception; the Driver produces no artifacts.)\\n- **invalidated** — the producing pass re-runs with the old version and the delta as declared diagnostic inputs.\\n\\n### Policy\\n\\n- **Marking is eager and transitive**: on any accepted-head movement the Driver walks the dependent cone (element grain where bindings allow) and emits staleness events. No work is scheduled by marking.\\n- **Regeneration is lazy and demand-driven**: nothing re-runs until a requested target predicate needs the stale node fresh; revalidation is attempted before regeneration.\\n- **Soundness**: no gate passes and no claim promotes over a stale input. Staleness may be lazily serviced, never ignored.\\n\\n### What invalidates what\\n\\n| Change | Stales (via pins) | Does not stale |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Intent Statement superseded | Proposal → cone | unrelated evidence |\\n| Proposal head moves | Design (subject to revalidation cutoff) → cone | — |\\n| Design head/element moves | Plan, Work Graph, unbuilt packets; claims on built Change Sets whose closure bound the moved elements | Change Set bodies (bytes don't rot; claims decay) |\\n| Plan head moves | Work Graph, unclaimed packets | verified Change Sets, until integration's predicate demands current-plan conformance |\\n| Decision record regenerated | consumers of changed elements (via `constrained_by`), subject to revalidation | consumers of unchanged elements |\\n| Owning RFC head moves | its Decision Record (regeneration mandatory; consumers may use last-accepted under a recorded deviation; **revoked** records fail closed) | — |\\n| Target-predicate version bumps | gate results and acceptance standing evaluated under the old version (like a contract bump) | artifact bodies |\\n| Pass contract_version bump | that pass's outputs | — |\\n| Pass impl_version bump | nothing retroactively (recorded) | history |\\n| Exogenous change observed | claims whose closure bound moved tree hashes | — |\\n| Reschedule / backend swap | nothing semantic, ever | — |\\n\\n## The Judgment Layer\\n\\n### Gate trichotomy\\n\\nEvery quality gate is exactly one class (P7):\\n\\n- **Check Gate** — mechanical, deterministic, replayable predicates over evidence (receipts, schemas, presence, hashes). No judgment.\\n- **Review Gate** — a predicate over a Review Ledger produced by an independent `review` run (e.g. \\\"no unresolved findings ≥ major\\\"). Independence requirements attach here.\\n- **Acceptance Gate** — authority: the Principal, or policy explicitly delegated by the Principal. Delegation over decision-role artifacts requires an RFC, never a policy edit. An open acceptance gate is explicit state surfaced by the status projection — never an implicit pause.\\n\\nLayering: acceptance may require validation; validation may require verification; never sideways or backwards. Gate evaluation is Driver mechanics at pass boundaries — deterministic, never delegated to a lane. Gates and acceptance never read provenance for authority.\\n\\n### Verdicts\\n\\nClosed vocabulary, transferred intact: `accept`, `accept_with_findings` (accepting); `needs_revision`, `reject` (non-accepting). A `needs_revision` routes to revision (re-run with the ledger as diagnostic input) under driver-policy re-run bounds; a `reject` retires the candidate or escalates.\\n\\n### Claims (computed views)\\n\\n\\u003e claim(A@v) = the maximum lattice point (`Verified \\u003e Asserted \\u003e Designed`) for which valid evidence exists whose bindings match A@v's pins and the current accepted heads (or elements) of everything the evidence declared it binds.\\n\\n- **Designed** — backing is acceptance (a decision record or accepted design).\\n- **Asserted** — backing is at most validation (advisory lane evidence, review verdicts). Build outputs self-report at most Asserted: **build never self-certifies**.\\n- **Verified** — backing is verification: sealed receipts with complete **binding closure** — the evidence binds the subject's hash and the accepted-head or element hashes of every governing IR (packet, plan element, design elements). Promotion gates refuse incomplete closure: nothing stays Verified against a dead design.\\n\\n**Independence (anti-aliasing):** Verified requires that minting evidence share no provenance ancestry — lane, backend session, synthesis lineage — with the producing execution, evaluated over recorded lane attribution and backend **aliasing classes** (model family). Two backends over one model family are not independent. Co-blindness is aliasing.\\n\\n**Decay is arithmetic:** when a bound hash moves, the evidence no longer matches and the computed claim falls — `Verified → Asserted` without any actor demoting anything. Evidence itself is never invalidated; its force lapses. Head-movement ledger events record implied claim transitions, so \\\"when did production lose Verified, and what moved?\\\" is a ledger query, not archaeology.\\n\\n### Target states\\n\\nNamed, **versioned** predicates in `catalog/target-states/`. Gate results and acceptance records pin the predicate version they were evaluated under; predicate changes propagate through this algebra exactly like contract bumps — editing what Verified means is itself an invalidating, provenance-visible event. Illustrative:\\n\\n- `proposal-created(N)` ≡ an accepted, fresh Proposal exists for identity N.\\n- `design-accepted(N)` ≡ an accepted, fresh Design bound to accepted Proposal N.\\n- `verified(N)` ≡ every packet in N's accepted Work Graph has claims at Verified with unexpired evidence and all gates passed.\\n- `integrated(N)` ≡ verified(N) ∧ the integration pass run binds all Change Set hashes to the current observed product tree.\\n- `foundation-ready` ≡ Decision Records D0001–D0005 accepted and fresh.\\n\\nA compilation request names a subject and a target predicate; the Driver plans the pass sequence whose outputs satisfy the unmet conjuncts.\\n\\n## Decision-Record Semantics\\n\\n- Generated by `decision-generation` on every accepted-stage transition of the owning RFC identity; pins the exact accepted stage hashes; carries element structure (clauses with anchors) from day one.\\n- Mandatory human Acceptance Gate in Epoch 1; authority re-confirms on regeneration. Generation without acceptance would make the compiler the author of its own constitution.\\n- Consumers link at element grain via `constrained_by`. On staleness, consumers may continue against the last-accepted version — each such run appends a deviation warning. Only **revocation** (an explicit acceptance-authority act) fails closed.\\n- Hand-edits are refused at admission (W4). Regeneration marks only the cones of changed elements.\\n\\n## Failure Handling and Acceptance Semantics\\n\\n- Failure modes and their graph effects are defined per pass contract (RFC 0004); purity means failed and abandoned runs leave no durable residue beyond ledger records.\\n- Escalations are ledger records with closed reason codes; an unresolved escalation blocks its subgraph; resolution is an appended authority event.\\n- Acceptance is never implied: the accepted head moves only through its gate set (or a licensed re-stamp), each movement a ledger event. Nothing is true because someone said so in prose.\\n\\n## Archival\\n\\nEvidence and superseded versions migrate to sealed cold segments (hash-anchored manifests) without breaking derivability; `reconcile` verifies manifests without loading segment bodies. Compaction that breaks derivability remains illegal; archival behind verifiable manifests is the legal form.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers\\n\\nFull deliberation in the Epoch 1 record. Accepted semantic state: `decisions/D0005-artifact-lifecycle-and-state-machine.md` (generated).\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0005-artifact-lifecycle-and-state-machine/implementation.md\": \"# RFC 0005 Implementation: Artifact Lifecycle and State Machine\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nAccepted (Epoch 1). Documentation-first: implementation here means repository encoding.\\n\\n## Encoding\\n\\n- `docs/reference/artifact-lifecycle.md` points at this design; never restates.\\n- `catalog/gates/` entries carry a `class:` field (check | review | acceptance) and the predicate they evaluate.\\n- `catalog/target-states/` entries are versioned predicate definitions.\\n- `schema/quality-gate.schema.json`, `schema/artifact.schema.json`, `schema/provenance-event.schema.json` harden against W1–W10 in Epoch 2.\\n- `decisions/D0005-artifact-lifecycle-and-state-machine.md` is generated from this identity's accepted stages.\\n\\n## Epoch 2 Consequences (named, not designed)\\n\\n- The admission path enforces W4/W5/W6 at write time (the bootstrap compiler's doctor checks, moved from audit time to write time).\\n- The claim cache and status projection are built as named derived stores; staleness events carry implied claim transitions from the first ledger version.\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0005-artifact-lifecycle-and-state-machine/proposal.md\": \"# RFC 0005 Proposal: Artifact Lifecycle and State Machine\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nAccepted (Epoch 1 Foundation Compilation Pass, 2026-07-02).\\n\\n## Problem\\n\\nThe incubation documents propose a twelve-state stored pipeline ladder — hidden lifecycle state that migrates badly and invites declaration over demonstration. Invalidation is hand-waved (\\\"only downstream artifacts become invalid\\\") and scattered across three RFC charters, which is how a system grows three subtly different staleness mechanisms. The judgment layer (gates, verdicts, claims, evidence force) has no single home.\\n\\n## Target State\\n\\nOne RFC owning: the minimal stored lifecycle, artifact-graph well-formedness, the single invalidation algebra (dirty bit + revalidation, eager marking + lazy regeneration), the judgment layer (gate trichotomy, verdicts, computed claims, binding closure, independence), acceptance semantics, and decision-record lifecycle semantics. RFCs 0003 and 0004 reference these semantics; nothing redefines them.\\n\\n## Non-Goals\\n\\n- Ledger storage format (committed only to `schema_version`/upcast/refuse-newer and sealed segments; format is Epoch 2).\\n- Runtime enforcement machinery — Epoch 2.\\n\\n## Source Material\\n\\nIncubation docs 00, 01, 03; Striatum-0's claim lattice (RFC 0134/D227), sealed receipts, verification/validation/acceptance trichotomy; Epoch 1 lanes A/B/C and red-team reconciliation.\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0006-driver-control-surface/design.md\": \"# RFC 0006 Design: Driver Control Surface\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nAccepted (Epoch 2 Runtime Foundation Pass, 2026-07-02). Vocabulary: RFC 0001 plus the Language Amendments below. Binding context: D0001–D0005, especially D0002.C2 (Derived-State Doctrine), C4 (submit/admit seam), C5 (Driver is a program), C6 (crash-only backends, one recovery verb), C10 (status projection), and D0005 (lifecycle, W1–W10, invalidation algebra, gate trichotomy).\\n\\nThis RFC owns: compilation requests, the drive session, pipeline-to-plan compilation, revalidation economics, escalation issuance and resolution, authority mechanics, acceptance ergonomics, status projection, and `reconcile`. It does not own: ledger storage, locks, and the admission funnel (RFC 0009); submission bundle and spool shape (RFC 0007); placement policy and capacity pools (RFC 0008); packet and verifier runtime and the Partial-Admission Closure Rule (RFC 0010).\\n\\n## The Shape: No Daemon\\n\\n**Striatum-next has no daemon. The Driver is an invoked program over the graph and ledger, serialized by the Graph Store's crash-released locks. There is no process whose uptime is a truth condition.**\\n\\nStriatum-0's daemon existed to guard a live truth store, to answer lanes mid-run, to sweep for recovery, and to serve live status. All four reasons are gone: truth is files (graph + ledger, D0002.C2); lanes are sealed and have nothing to call (D0002.C6); recovery is the invoked `reconcile`; status is a derived store refreshed on read. What the daemon cost is documented at length — daemon-unreachable as a standing failure class, version skew, socket and token friction, boot parks, store split-brain. An invoked driver cannot be \\\"down\\\": the worst failure is a stale derived store, and the cure is a rebuild, not an incident. The Striatum-0 daemon is a recorded rejected alternative; it does not return.\\n\\n### Serialization without a resident process\\n\\nAll concurrency primitives live in the Graph Store and are owned by RFC 0009: the **append lock** (`ledger/LOCK`), held per append batch, serializing every ledger write; and the **drive lease** (`drive.lease`), held per drive session, so at most one planner/dispatcher/transitioner runs per repository graph. Neither lives in the target repository working tree. Rejected alternative (load-bearing): working-tree lockfiles (`.striatum/locks/`) were deleted because multiple clones or worktrees sharing one repository identity would each hold a private \\\"exclusive\\\" lock; the store is the single serialization point, and it detects and records multi-working-tree use at open.\\n\\n**Lock-first invariant (consumed contract, RFC 0009):** every mutating verb — `request`, `accept`, `resolve`, `revoke`, `cancel`, and the drive loop's own batches — is a client of the store's append API, and its first act is lock acquisition followed by a tail re-fold. No verb computes against a pre-lock snapshot.\\n\\nBoth primitives are `flock`-based and kernel-released on process death: the Driver is itself crash-only. A session killed mid-loop leaves a prefix-valid ledger, no partially-moved heads (head movement is one store append), and no cleanup obligation — the next invocation replans deterministically from the same truth. Locks are per repository graph (D0002.C8); drives on different target repositories proceed in parallel.\\n\\n### Liveness without authority: wakes\\n\\nNothing needs to be running for the system to be correct; things need to run for it to be *prompt*. Promptness is supplied by **wakes** — non-authoritative triggers that invoke `striatum drive`: a systemd **timer** (a timer unit, never a service unit), backend adapters after spooling a submission bundle (RFC 0007), a git hook on watched targets so `observation` is planned promptly, or a principal typing the verb. A missed wake delays; it can never corrupt or diverge. The standing timer is the documented liveness floor; each session additionally rewrites a durable timer unit to the session's computed `next_horizon` (earliest future obligation: dispatch horizons, deferral revisits, capacity resets), so promptness survives reboots without any resident process.\\n\\n### What is deliberately not built\\n\\n- **No RPC surface, no sockets, no capability tokens.** The only mutating boundary is one program operating on files owned by one OS user. Authority collapses to OS file permissions plus recorded attribution; every authority-bearing record reserves `authority_proof` so signing can attach later without a schema break. The v1 trust domain — a single OS user; integrity as crash-evidence, not tamper-evidence — is stated, with mitigations and the Epoch 3 hardening path, in RFCs 0007 and 0009.\\n- **No MCP server, no web UI.** Agent principals consume the same CLI with `--json` — stable schemas and exit codes. Any richer renderer or protocol shim is a read-only `tools/` client of the status store, not architecture.\\n- **No second ledger reader.** The `striatum` binary is the box's sole ledger reader. Adapters are ledger-illiterate by contract; where an operational tool needs ledger-derived facts (e.g., RFC 0007's workspace janitor's live-run set), the Driver passes them as verb input. All other tooling reads through `striatum … --json`. This contains version skew structurally: one reader, one upcast surface.\\n\\nThe control surface is therefore: one Go binary (`striatum`), a library core (`internal/driver`, `internal/core`), the Graph Store for truth and exclusion, timers and hooks for promptness.\\n\\n## Compilation Requests\\n\\n### The request record\\n\\nA compilation request is the Principal's command (RFC 0001): (subject, target state, constraints), recorded as a `compilation_request`:\\n\\n```yaml\\nrecord_type: compilation_request        # envelope (schema_version, record_id,\\nrequest_id: RQ-2031-000482              # appended_at, writer, repository) per RFC 0009\\nissuer:\\n  kind: principal | agent_principal\\n  identity: halbritt | harvest-agent    # declared; attribution, not proof\\n  delegation_ref: policy/gates.yaml#harvest-issuer   # required iff agent_principal\\n  authority_proof: null                 # reserved for future signing\\nsubject:\\n  repository: striatum-next             # repository-qualified (D0002.C8)\\n  identity: rfcs/0028                   # artifact identity or RFC identity\\n  element_anchor: null                  # optional element-scoped subject\\ntarget:\\n  state_id: verified                    # catalog/target-states/\\n  predicate_version: 3                  # pinned at issuance\\n  tracking: pinned | current            # default pinned\\nconstraints:\\n  pipeline: {id: adjudicated-panel, version: 2}   # optional template override\\n  priority_class: interactive | standard | harvest\\n  capacity_ceiling: null                # advisory ceiling handed to the Scheduler\\n  deadline_advisory: null               # advisory; never a gate\\n  freshness: allow_deviation | require_fresh\\ngroup_id: null                          # linked cross-repository request group\\nsupersedes: null                        # request revision chain\\nnote: \\\"free text; never semantic\\\"\\n```\\n\\nConstraints may never name a backend or model (P9): independence and capability requirements enter only through gates and lane requirements.\\n\\n### Issuance\\n\\n`striatum request rfcs/0028 --target verified` appends the record under the append lock and fires a wake. A **Principal** issues by running the verb. An **agent principal** (Language Amendments) issues the same way, but the record must carry a `delegation_ref` naming the `policy/gates.yaml` entry authorizing that identity to issue (and optionally cancel) requests; the Driver refuses issuance whose delegation reference is absent, expired, or out of scope. This is how capacity-harvest machinery (RFC 0008) lawfully creates maintenance work: every harvest-issued request is a visible, attributable ledger record. Delegation never extends to acceptance over decision-role artifacts without an RFC (D0005.C4).\\n\\n### Request lifecycle: two stored events, everything else computed\\n\\nA request stores only its authority events; its position is a computed predicate:\\n\\n- **issued** — the `compilation_request` exists.\\n- **planned** — the newest `plan_record` has a basis matching the current graph cursor, catalog versions, and policy versions (computed).\\n- **executing** — plan steps have `pass_run_opened` records without closure (computed).\\n- **blocked** — computed sub-states surfaced by status: `awaiting_principal` (acceptance items or unresolved escalations in scope), `awaiting_capacity` (no lawful binding yet), `awaiting_submissions` (dispatched, within horizon).\\n- **satisfied** — the target predicate evaluated true; the Driver appends a `satisfaction_record` pinning the evaluation, which closes the request.\\n- **canceled** — a `cancellation_record` exists (issuer of equal-or-greater authority, or the Principal).\\n- **escalated** — an unresolved escalation blocks the request's subgraph (computed; not terminal — a `resolution_event` returns it to planning).\\n\\nRequests are **one-shot advancement commands, not standing reconciliation loops**. Satisfaction is evaluated at a moment against pinned heads and recorded; later decay is a new fact surfaced as a status notice, and re-advancement requires a new request. Standing freshness is expressed as policy-issued requests from an agent principal — visible work, not a hidden control loop.\\n\\nOn cancellation the Driver stops planning and dispatching for the request. Running lanes are not killed (crash-only; the dispatch channel may carry RFC 0007's advisory abandon signal). Late submissions are still drained, check-gated, and admitted as candidates — finished lanes' work is never discarded (D0002.C4) — but no further advancement is planned.\\n\\n### Cross-repository requests\\n\\nA request whose target predicate spans repositories compiles as a **linked request group**: one `compilation_request` per repository graph sharing a `group_id`, each planned by a drive session against its own graph under its own repository policy (D0002.C8). Cross-graph pins are repository-qualified and treated by planning as opaque frozen environment (a stale cross-repo pin marks exactly like a local one); which decisions are constitutional versus repository-local is governed by where the owning RFC identity lives, with storage mechanics in RFC 0009. There is no global optimizer; group planning is linked per-repository planning.\\n\\n## Pipelines: Template versus Policy\\n\\nA Pipeline is a catalog-resident template composing passes, gate wiring, and re-run bounds, with no new semantics (D0004.C7). This RFC fixes the boundary (resolving Epoch 1 open question 7):\\n\\n**A pipeline template may declare:**\\n\\n- an ordered/branching composition of **cataloged passes** (references into `catalog/passes/`, pinned to contract major versions), including run-level fan-out — e.g. N `review` runs under distinct cataloged postures feeding one gate (falsification treatments, adjudicated panels); *lane* topology inside one pass run remains pass-internal (RFC 0004);\\n- **gate wiring**: which cataloged gates apply at each stage boundary, including additional review gates over posture-specific Review Ledger sections;\\n- **re-run bounds per edge**, which may *tighten* but never exceed the driver-policy ceiling;\\n- **parameters**: subject kind, posture selections, fan-out width.\\n\\n**A pipeline template may never declare:** new gate classes, new verdict values, acceptance delegation, claim or invalidation semantics, backends or models (P9), deadlines, budgets, priorities, batching, or capacity behavior. Those are driver policy (`policy/driver.yaml`) or scheduler policy (`policy/scheduler.yaml`).\\n\\n**Rule of thumb:** a pipeline says *what composes*; policy says *how much, when, and at what cost*. If removing an entry changes which gates a head movement must pass, it is pipeline (semantic composition, versioned catalog entry). If removing it only changes speed, cost, or attention load, it is policy.\\n\\n**Compilation to plan records.** Pipelines are planning macros with zero runtime footprint. At planning time the Driver selects a template — from the request constraint, else from a catalog default mapping (target state → pipeline), else the bare pass gate sets — substitutes parameters, and expands it into plan steps. Every expanded step carries `pipeline_ref: {id, version, stage}`, and the pipeline id+version participates in the plan basis (a version bump changes future plans; it invalidates nothing retroactively, like an impl bump, because a pipeline adds no semantics beyond the gates it wires). There is no stored pipeline position: position is the computed frontier of the plan.\\n\\nNew pipelines require catalog governance (schema-validated, versioned entries), not RFCs, precisely because they can introduce no new semantics.\\n\\n## The Drive Session\\n\\n`striatum drive` executes one **drive session**: acquire the drive lease through the Graph Store, loop to quiescence, append a `drive_session_record`, release. The loop is deterministic over (graph, ledger, catalog, policy) — same inputs, same decisions (D0002.C5); the plan basis pins every input, so the whole control plane is replayable-from-inputs. Each iteration:\\n\\n### Drain\\n\\nProcess the submission spool (shape and location owned by RFC 0007) in **canonical drain order: `dispatch_id`, then manifest end time** — recorded in the `drive_session_record`. Per bundle: validate the run-manifest seal against the dispatch-time `pass_run_opened`; hand outputs to the Graph Store's admission funnel, which enforces W1–W10 per output at write time and appends `admission_decision` records (RFC 0009); append a `pass_run_closed`; admit structurally-valid outputs as `candidate` versions (inert until gated); evaluate check gates immediately (deterministic, over submitted evidence — receipts validated, never executed); enter surviving candidates into gate progression.\\n\\n**Partial admission.** The **Partial-Admission Closure Rule is RFC 0010's**: an output is individually admissible iff its declared intra-run derivation closure is admitted; RFC 0007's bundle-integrity check is its projection at the seam, and RFC 0009's funnel enforces it per output. This RFC's role is downstream: for `submitted_partial` closures, plan one **residual run** covering only the missing outputs (RFC 0010's mechanism; exclusion-set inheritance per RFC 0008), opened as a new `pass_run_opened` after the partial closure.\\n\\n### Mark\\n\\nFor every accepted-head movement drained or performed (admission, re-stamp, decision regeneration, observation, revocation), walk the reverse-pin index (a derived store) and append one `staleness_event` carrying the marked cone — (identity, version, via-pin, element) at element grain where bindings allow, chunked at a record-size bound — with the implied claim transitions listed (W8). Implied claim transitions may be computed lazily and backfilled by the next fold. Marking is eager, transitive, and schedules nothing (D0005.C3). Aliasing-registry decay rides this same channel: the session that honors a staged registry change (RFC 0007 owns the registry; thresholds and acknowledgment are policy) appends `staleness_event` records with cause `aliasing_registry_changed`.\\n\\n### Plan\\n\\nFor each open request in priority order (policy):\\n\\n1. Evaluate the target predicate (Compiler Core). If satisfied → append `satisfaction_record`, close.\\n2. Compute unmet conjuncts. Planning is **graph reachability over catalog data**: from the current accepted-and-fresh heads (or deviation-eligible stale heads), find the pass sequence whose produced kinds and gate closures satisfy each unmet conjunct — an exact search over the eleven pass contracts' consumes/produces types, expanded through the selected pipeline template, with staleness-servicing steps inserted for stale nodes the plan demands fresh.\\n3. Content-address the plan. If identical to the request's latest `plan_record`, append nothing; else append a new `plan_record` with its basis (ledger cursor, catalog versions, policy versions, decision records read), steps with symbolic input pins for not-yet-produced upstream outputs, per-step gate sets, re-run bounds, `pipeline_ref`, and the request's `attention_forecast`.\\n\\nPlan records are provenance (\\\"what did the Driver intend, from what facts\\\"), never authority, never artifacts (D0002.C5).\\n\\n### Bound\\n\\nBefore dispatching any step, consult provenance **as planning data**: attempts per (subject identity, pass, contract_version) since the last accepted-head movement or plan change. Bounds come from `policy/driver.yaml`, with pipeline-edge tightening:\\n\\n- `revision_bound` (default 2) — non-accepting review verdicts routing back through revision.\\n- `redispatch_bound` (default 3) — presumed abandonments, counted separately: a dying backend is a placement problem, not an engineering-quality problem; the Scheduler sees abandonment telemetry (RFC 0008) and should move the work before the bound trips.\\n- `withdrawal_bound` (default 3) — automatic acceptance-queue withdrawals per (identity, gate) since the last accepted-head movement; withdrawal oscillation is livelock spending Principal attention.\\n- **Oscillation detection** — a new candidate whose content hash matches a previously refused candidate for the same (identity, pass) is livelock regardless of remaining bounds.\\n\\nExhaustion or oscillation → escalation `bounds_exhausted` carrying its `budget_kind`, never a silent retry loop. This is exactly the licensed use of provenance: planning reads it as data; no gate ever reads it for authority.\\n\\n### Dispatch\\n\\nGather the **ready frontier**: plan steps whose input pins resolve to accepted, fresh (or deviation-eligible) versions with upstream gates closed, and whose dispatch keeps the acceptance queue within its depth bound. Invoke the Scheduler as a pure library function — (ready pass runs, backend capability declarations, capacity state including attention telemetry, versioned policy) → lane bindings (RFC 0008).\\n\\n**Record-then-dispatch ordering is binding.** Per binding, in order: (1) append `pass_run_opened` with the sealed run manifest; (2) append the `scheduling_decision`/`lane_binding` records (shapes owned by RFC 0008; the Driver appends the mirror under the append lock); (3) materialize the dispatch bundle (RFC 0007's shape); (4) hand it to the backend adapter over the dispatch channel (the channel is the authority; the ledger entry is the record). Records always precede work. A crash inside the sequence leaves a visible prefix — an opened run with no binding, or a binding with no dispatched bundle — which the next session closes (`superseded_by_redispatch`) and reopens; nothing is ambiguous because nothing ran unrecorded. Adapters detach; the Driver never talks to lanes.\\n\\nThe dispatch horizon derives from the run's `deadline_class` × the policy multiplier. If the Scheduler reports no capable backend at all and policy forecasts no future supply, escalate `binding_unsatisfiable`; if independence supply specifically cannot be satisfied, escalate `independence_unsatisfiable` (distinct resolution path: procure a different-family backend, not merely any backend); if supply is merely exhausted until a reset horizon, the step is `awaiting_capacity` — not an escalation.\\n\\n### Deadline sweep\\n\\nFor each open run past its horizon with no submission, append `pass_run_closed{outcome: abandoned}` — a **provisional adjudication, not a fact of death**. The horizon is measured in **observed-active time**: wall-clock intervals containing no drive session and no adapter activity are discounted (a closed laptop lid is not a dead backend). Abandonment adjudications are capped per session (policy), with a warning when the cap is hit. Silence and death are deliberately indistinguishable (D0002.C6): the Driver manages expectations with ages, never liveness claims.\\n\\n**Re-dispatch is closure-then-new-run only** (RFC 0010's mechanism; RFC 0008's same-run re-entry is a rejected alternative): the prior run is closed (`abandoned`, or `superseded_by_redispatch` when replaced without an abandonment adjudication), then a new `pass_run_opened` is appended with the same manifest, `attempt+1` carried in the `lane_binding`. First admitted valid result wins across attempts.\\n\\n**Late submissions reopen the adjudication.** The admission funnel admits a late submission against a run whose only closure is `abandoned`, and the Driver appends `pass_run_closed{submitted_late}` — both facts were true; finished work is never discarded. Refusal applies only to `canceled`, satisfied, or already-won runs; a later valid result for a won run appends `redundant_candidate` (RFC 0009's funnel) — value counted, not discarded, and reusable by pin-keyed memoization (RFC 0004).\\n\\n### Deviation and fail-closed\\n\\nSteps constrained by a stale-but-not-revoked decision record may proceed against the last-accepted version, appending a `deviation_warning` per run, unless the request said `require_fresh` (D0005.C7). Steps constrained by a **revoked** decision record are not dispatchable — fail closed; if this blocks a request's every path, escalate `missing_authority` citing the revocation.\\n\\n### Quiescence\\n\\nThe loop ends at **quiescence**: nothing to drain, nothing dispatchable, no staleness servicing demanded by open requests. Append the `drive_session_record` (fields below, including `next_horizon` and quiescence reason), refresh the status projection, rewrite the `next_horizon` timer unit, release the lease — then **re-scan the spool**: if a bundle arrived during the session (its adapter's wake landed on exit 4), re-acquire and loop. Adapters retry on exit 4 (RFC 0007). This closes the wake-drop race; the standing timer remains the liveness floor beneath it.\\n\\nExit codes: `0` satisfied/idle, `5` quiescent-blocked (for wake scripts), `4` drive lease held (busy; adapters retry), `3` parked (integrity or refuse-newer stop; do not retry without a human), `2` refusal, `1` usage.\\n\\nA session that observes reconcile-red findings against **truth** stores (segment hash mismatch, anchor mismatch) parks instead of dispatching: the surface offers no verb that can author artifacts or move heads around a red doctor, so the failure cannot be papered over, only fixed.\\n\\n## Gate Evaluation and Admission Sequencing\\n\\nGate evaluation is Driver mechanics at pass boundaries — deterministic predicates over structured data, never delegated to a lane (D0004.C3). Per candidate, in strict order:\\n\\n1. **Structural admission** — the Graph Store's admission funnel enforces W1–W10 per output and appends `admission_decision` (RFC 0009), including the Partial-Admission Closure Rule (RFC 0010). Candidate exists or the output is refused.\\n2. **Check gates** — evaluated immediately at drain over submitted evidence; receipts validated against seals, never executed. Refusal → `gate_result{refuse}`; the candidate remains inert; revision or escalation per bounds.\\n3. **Review gates** — predicates over Review Ledgers. If the required independent review run has not happened, the gate is not \\\"failed\\\"; the plan contains the review step and the candidate waits. Verdict routing: `accept`/`accept_with_findings` close the gate; `needs_revision` plans a revision re-run under bounds; `reject` retires the candidate or escalates (RFC 0005).\\n4. **Acceptance gates** — never evaluated by computation. An acceptance-ready candidate (all prior gates closed, inputs not stale) becomes an item in the **acceptance queue**. The gate closes only by a `gate_result` of class acceptance (below).\\n5. **Head movement** — with the full gate set closed, the Driver performs the transition (P4) by invoking the Graph Store's head-movement append: `head_movement` (RFC 0009; movement `initial_accept | supersede | re_stamp | retire`, carrying gate-result refs or, for `re_stamp`, the licensing revalidation verdict pin — W6's single exception). Then mark. Per the Epoch 2 re-stamp attribution ruling, the re-stamped version's producing pass run **is the licensing revalidation review run** (`production_mode: re_stamp`); the Driver performs only the mechanical append and movement, keeping W4 literally exception-free and the Driver artifact-free.\\n\\nNo gate is ever evaluated over a stale input; if an input goes stale mid-progression, the candidate's progression suspends and its acceptance-queue item is withdrawn (computed — the queue is derived; the staleness event already explains it).\\n\\n## Staleness Servicing and Revalidation Economics\\n\\nThe algebra is fixed (D0005.C3): marking eager, regeneration lazy, revalidation before regeneration. This RFC supplies the economics — when to revalidate, when to regenerate, when to ignore, under what budget (resolving Epoch 1 open question 2).\\n\\n### Ignore is the default\\n\\nStaleness outside the support of any open request's unmet conjuncts is serviced by nobody. It is marked (cheap, already done), visible (status notice, aggregated), and inert. At 2031 scale — one decision regeneration marking hundreds of consumers across dozens of repositories — this is the load-bearing choice; this RFC refuses to add any eager servicing.\\n\\n### Revalidation is tiered inside the posture\\n\\nThe doctrinal sequence stays unconditional, but its cost collapses where revalidation is hopeless, by making the `revalidation` review posture itself **tiered** (a posture-contract fact, cataloged and versioned):\\n\\n- **Tier 0 — mechanical short-circuit (D0, free).** Compare the pin delta against the artifact's declared element bindings. Gross deltas — upstream rewritten beyond a policy threshold of bound elements, contract-version bumps declared invalidating, revocations — return `invalidated` without any judgment lane. Artifacts whose gate set is checks-only are fully decidable here (re-run checks mechanically → `revalidated` or `invalidated`).\\n- **Tier 1 — judgment (D2, costed).** A review lane answers whether the stale artifact still satisfies its gates against the new upstream, seeing exactly the old version, the delta, and the gate predicates.\\n\\nAn accepting verdict licenses the re-stamp (attributed to the revalidation run, above); downstream pins re-match; claims survive (RFC 0005). Tier-1 results are memoized by (artifact version, upstream delta pins) — the same question is never asked twice (RFC 0004).\\n\\n### The economic asymmetry, priced\\n\\nRegeneration is almost always the expensive branch, for a reason invisible to pure compute accounting: **regeneration re-crosses acceptance gates and resets downstream evidence** — it spends Principal attention and destroys Verified standing in the cone; revalidation preserves both. `policy/driver.yaml` prices this explicitly:\\n\\n```yaml\\nrevalidation:\\n  tier0_invalidate_threshold: 0.5   # fraction of bound elements moved → mechanical invalidated\\n  tier1_budget_per_request: 12      # judgment revalidations per request per drive session\\n  tier1_prior_floor: 0.2            # skip tier 1 (regenerate) when learned clear-rate prior falls below\\n```\\n\\n`tier1_prior_floor` uses provenance as planning data: a derived table of revalidation outcomes keyed by (artifact kind, upstream kind, delta size class). Where history says revalidation of this shape almost never clears, tier 1 is skipped — legal because tier 0 already ran; the posture's mechanical stage *is* the revalidation. The priors table is the calibration instrument for open question 2, and it is a rebuildable derived store, not semantics. Cold start: until history accumulates, the floor never fires and the tier-1 budget bounds alone.\\n\\n### Ordering and batching\\n\\nStaleness is serviced **top-down the derivation DAG**: highest stale ancestor first, because an upstream `invalidated` verdict re-marks the cone and would moot downstream work. Within a request, servicing steps are ordinary plan steps competing under the same priority and capacity as everything else. There is no batch-revalidation mechanism: tier 0 absorbs scale mechanically; tier-1 volume is bounded by budget; if the budget exhausts while the request still demands freshness, remaining subjects regenerate only where the tier-0/priors path says so — otherwise the request rests at `awaiting_capacity` and drains across sessions. Budgets defer; they never skip soundness: no gate passes over a stale input, ever.\\n\\n## Escalation\\n\\n### Issuance\\n\\nEscalation is the Driver's only interruptive act (RFC 0002). An `escalation` record carries the closed reason code (RFC 0001's set of eight, as amended by Epoch 2), the subject pins, the request, a **context bundle** (pins to the artifacts, gate results, Review Ledger findings, and attempt history that make it legible without archaeology), and the blocking scope (the subgraph cone it halts). An unresolved escalation blocks its subgraph; other requests and unrelated subgraphs proceed. Reason-code semantics at the Driver:\\n\\n- `ambiguous_goal` — planning cannot reduce a conjunct to pass steps (underspecified target or subject).\\n- `missing_authority` — a required authority is absent: revoked decision record in every path, expired delegation, acceptance explicitly declined without disposition.\\n- `contradicting_decisions` — planning derives conflicting constraints from decision records in force (cited at element grain).\\n- `committee_stalemate` — a pipeline's adjudication gate cannot close within its wiring.\\n- `override_required` — a gate refusal policy marks Principal-overridable-only (never silently overridable by the Driver).\\n- `bounds_exhausted` — a bound or oscillation detector tripped; the record's closed `budget_kind` (`revision | redispatch | attempt_total | integration_conflict | withdrawal`) names which budget, absorbing RFC 0010's packet attempt budgets into one code.\\n- `binding_unsatisfiable` — no capable backend exists and none is forecast.\\n- `independence_unsatisfiable` — independence supply specifically cannot be satisfied (RFCs 0007/0008); distinct resolution path from `binding_unsatisfiable`.\\n\\n### Resolution\\n\\nResolution is an appended authority event, never an edit. `striatum resolve \\u003cid\\u003e --disposition \\u003cd\\u003e` appends a `resolution_event`: resolver attribution (plus delegation ref if an agent principal resolves a class policy permits), disposition from a closed set — `proceed` (unblock, e.g. after external repair), `cancel_request`, `reissue` (pins a superseding compilation request), `redirect` (pins a new artifact version produced *through passes*; the resolution itself never authors anything), `override` (names the overridden gate result and the policy basis; permitted only where the gate's catalog entry declares overridability). The Driver consumes resolutions at the next session: unblocked subgraphs re-enter planning. Status shows reason, age, context bundle, and the exact resolve verb to type.\\n\\n## Authority\\n\\n### Acceptance\\n\\nAcceptance gates close only by a `gate_result` of class acceptance: subject pin, gate id + predicate version, verdict, authority (`principal` or `delegation_ref`), request context, session attribution, reserved `authority_proof`. Produced by `striatum accept \\u003citem\\u003e`; `striatum reject \\u003citem\\u003e --reason` appends a refusing acceptance result (routes to revision or escalation per bounds); `striatum defer \\u003citem\\u003e --reason` appends nothing to the gate but records triage intent in the status store's queue state, folded into the next `drive_session_record`'s deferrals — ledger-visible triage without a new record type. Per P4 the Driver transitions: the accept verb appends the authority fact, then runs a bounded transition step (same binary, drive lease permitting) so the head moves promptly.\\n\\n### Delegation\\n\\nDelegation is data in `policy/gates.yaml`: (delegate identity, gate scope, conditions, expiry, `authorized_by`). The Driver enforces two rules mechanically: (1) a delegation whose scope includes any decision-role artifact is honored only if `authorized_by` pins an accepted, fresh decision record from an RFC that grants it — D0005.C4's \\\"requires an RFC, never a policy edit,\\\" machine-checked; (2) every exercised delegation is recorded on the record it licensed. Agent-principal grants cover request issuance/cancellation and named escalation-resolution classes; acceptance delegation defaults to none.\\n\\n### Revocation\\n\\n`striatum revoke \\u003cdecision-id\\u003e --reason` appends a `revocation_record` — an acceptance-authority act (RFC 0005). Consumers fail closed; the Driver marks the cone, suspends dispatch of constrained steps, and escalates affected open requests with `missing_authority`. Un-revoking does not exist; recovery is regeneration and re-acceptance through `decision-generation`.\\n\\n### Agent principals\\n\\nAn **agent principal** is an agent runtime exercising a recorded, bounded delegation of Principal-issuable acts. It is not the Principal, not a component, and never an acceptance authority for decision-role artifacts without an RFC. Its every act carries its identity and delegation reference. The term exists to keep \\\"the harvest policy filed a request at 3am\\\" inside the ontology instead of inside a cron script.\\n\\n## Status Projection\\n\\n### The store\\n\\n`derived/status/` is a named derived store (D0002.C10): rebuildable from graph + ledger, refreshed at session end and incrementally on read (ledger-tail scan; each derived store persists its own cursor transactionally per RFC 0009's rules — no shared cursor). `striatum status [--json|--watch]` renders it; `striatum explain \\u003csubject\\u003e` answers why-questions (why stale, why not Verified, what blocks a request, which delta broke which binding) as pure computed reads. A workstation-level derived store folds capacity and Principal attention over all registered graphs (owned by RFC 0008, stored per RFC 0009's rules); drive sessions snapshot it, and attention is summed globally — the Principal is one person no matter how many graphs are registered.\\n\\n### The questions it answers\\n\\n- **Open requests** with computed phase and blocked sub-state.\\n- **Dispatched expectations**: per open run — pass, subject, binding, age versus horizon. Never \\\"running\\\": under crash-only backends the honest vocabulary is *dispatched, awaiting submission, age 34m of 60m horizon*. **Wedged is an overdue expectation**, not a liveness fact; past-horizon bindings surface as warnings with re-dispatch bound state shown. The second wedge class is **driver starvation**: a dispatchable frontier with no drive session for longer than the timer period (warning: the timer is broken — the one infrastructure fact worth a warning).\\n- **The acceptance queue** with ages.\\n- **Unresolved escalations** with reason, age, context, and the resolve verb.\\n- **Staleness debt**: marked-not-demanded counts (notice, aggregated); demanded-but-budget-deferred (notice with horizon).\\n- **Claim regressions**: Verified→Asserted decays since the Principal's last status read (from staleness events' implied transitions).\\n- **Post-satisfaction decay** on closed requests (notice).\\n- **Reconcile health** and last drive session + quiescence reason.\\n\\n### Warnings, notices, and the attention budget\\n\\nStriatum-0's doctor legibility lesson is adopted as a rule: **a warning must name the verb that discharges it; anything without an action is a notice.** Warnings: overdue expectation, acceptance item older than policy age, unresolved escalation, revocation in an active cone, reconcile truth-finding, driver starvation, abandonment-sweep cap hit. Notices: undemanded staleness, decay events, deviation warnings within tolerance, capacity waits, post-satisfaction decay. Anti-rot rule: a warning persisting unchanged across N sessions is itself surfaced (\\\"permanent warning — triage policy or fix\\\"), because permanent warnings train the reader to ignore warnings.\\n\\n**The v1 Principal ceiling, stated out loud:** acceptance throughput bounds compiled-intent throughput. One human's acceptance rate is the system's hard ceiling; everything below defers work to protect that ceiling, and nothing may raise it except the named Epoch 3 graduated-acceptance/delegation RFC. `principal_attention.size` is declared policy — a lint forbids telemetry-derived values (RFC 0008 owns the pool).\\n\\n**Acceptance ergonomics** (resolving Epoch 1 open question 4) — the defense against rubber-stamping is structural:\\n\\n1. **Principal attention is a scheduled capacity dimension.** RFC 0008 owns the `principal_attention` pool; this RFC owns the deferral behavior. Both read the same derived store (acceptance queue / attention telemetry). The Driver computes an `attention_forecast` per plan and defers dispatching acceptance-*terminal* steps while the queue exceeds its policy depth bound, preferring evidence-plane work that ripens candidates without demanding authority. Attention pressure defers *reaching* gates; it never weakens one.\\n2. **Friction proportional to blast radius.** Queue items carry the element-grain diff, the review-evidence summary, claim consequences, and downstream cone size. Items moving decision-record heads or large cones require item-wise interactive confirmation with the diff shown; small-cone leaf items are batchable (`striatum accept --batch` renders a digest but appends one acceptance `gate_result` per item with shared session attribution — no blanket accept record exists).\\n3. **Nothing auto-accepts.** Defaults: zero delegation; `defer` is first-class with a reason; items whose inputs go stale are withdrawn automatically (never accept against a stale input). Repeated automatic withdrawal trips `withdrawal_bound` → `bounds_exhausted{budget_kind: withdrawal}`.\\n4. **Batching by shape**: the queue groups by request and kind, ordered by (age, blast radius), so one sitting clears one coherent story.\\n\\n## `reconcile`\\n\\n**Invocation.** `striatum reconcile [--deep] [--migrate] [--json]`. Every drive session runs the cheap tail check (open-segment integrity, spool orphan scan) at start; a systemd timer may run full reconcile off-hours. One verb; flags select depth (`--deep` re-hashes sealed bodies) or the explicit offline refold (`--migrate`, RFC 0009's upcast refold), never a second behavior kind — a second recovery verb is evidence of hidden state (D0002.C6).\\n\\n**Behavior, incremental over sealed segments.** Verify sealed segment manifests by hash (verified segments skipped unless `--deep`); verify the open tail chain; verify git anchors for source-like artifacts and blob hashes for evidence; rebuild every derived store (reverse-pin index, dirty marks, claim cache, attempt counters, revalidation priors, status projection) and compare against live copies; verify accepted-head gate closure (every head movement has its complete record set); scan the spool for orphan bundles (no matching `pass_run_opened`).\\n\\n**Report.** Structured findings with closed codes — `segment_manifest_mismatch`, `open_tail_break`, `anchor_missing`, `anchor_hash_mismatch`, `blob_hash_mismatch`, `body_missing` (park class), `head_without_gate_closure`, `orphan_submission`, `derived_store_divergence`, `record_newer_than_reader` — triaged as warnings/notices under the rules above, each naming its discharge (rebuild performed; restore required; park).\\n\\n**May:** rebuild derived stores (divergence self-healed and reported as a notice); quarantine orphan spool bundles (moved aside, recorded); **park** on `record_newer_than_reader` and `body_missing` (park with instructions, never crash-loop — Striatum-0's exit-79 lesson, exit code 3).\\n\\n**May not:** author artifacts, move heads, mint evidence or claims, resolve escalations, delete or rewrite ledger records, \\\"repair\\\" truth. Damage to truth is reported and the affected range fenced; restoring truth is a Principal-level act from git/backups (restore order — objects first, ledger second — documented in RFC 0009). Reconcile is a doctor, never a surgeon.\\n\\n## Record Types\\n\\nAll records share RFC 0009's envelope (`record_type`, `schema_version`, `record_id`, `appended_at`, `writer`, `repository`), live under `schema/ledger-records/`, and register in `catalog/ledger-record-types/` (one owner per type, snake_case). Owned by this RFC, full v1 field lists:\\n\\n| Record | Fields (beyond envelope) | Writer verb/phase |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `compilation_request` | request_id, issuer{kind, identity, delegation_ref, authority_proof}, subject{repository, identity, element_anchor?}, target{state_id, predicate_version, tracking}, constraints{pipeline?, priority_class, capacity_ceiling?, deadline_advisory?, freshness}, group_id?, supersedes?, note | `request` |\\n| `cancellation_record` | request_ref, issuer{…}, reason | `cancel` |\\n| `plan_record` | request_ref, plan_seq, basis{ledger_cursor, catalog_versions, policy_versions, decisions_read}, unmet[], steps[{step_id, pass, contract_version, pipeline_ref{id, version, stage}?, input_pins (symbolic-capable), gate_set, re_run_bound, depends_on, staleness_service{subject, mode}?}], attention_forecast | drive/plan |\\n| `pass_run_opened` | pass, contract_version, impl_version, run_manifest{input_pins, environment_pins, prompt_asset_hashes, lane_requirements} (sealed), subject_pins, plan_ref{plan, step_id}, request_ref, deadline_class, speculative_on (absent v1) — run_id is this record's seq; absorbs the lane designs' `pass_run`, `run-request`, `run-manifest` | drive/dispatch |\\n| `pass_run_closed` | run_ref, outcome{submitted, submitted_partial, submitted_late, abandoned, canceled, error, superseded_by_redispatch}, submission_ref?, residual{missing_outputs}?, deadline_policy_pin, observed_active? (abandoned adjudications) | drive/drain, deadline sweep |\\n| `gate_result` (W7 semantics: RFC 0005) | subject_pin, gate_id, class, predicate_version, outcome, verdict?, evidence_pins, request_ref?, authority{principal \\\\| delegation_ref, authority_proof}? (acceptance class), session_attribution | drive/gate; `accept`/`reject` |\\n| `staleness_event` | cause_ref (head movement, revocation, aliasing_registry_changed, …), marked[{identity, version, via_pin, element?}] (chunked), implied_claim_transitions[] (lazily backfillable) | drive/mark |\\n| `deviation_warning` | run_ref, decision_identity, used_version, stale_head | drive/dispatch |\\n| `escalation` | escalation_id, reason_code (closed set of 8), budget_kind{revision, redispatch, attempt_total, integration_conflict, withdrawal}? (iff bounds_exhausted), detail, subject_pins, request_ref, context_bundle_pins, blocking_scope | drive |\\n| `resolution_event` | escalation_ref, resolver{identity, delegation_ref?, authority_proof}, disposition{proceed, cancel_request, reissue→request_ref, redirect→artifact_pin, override→gate_result_ref+policy_basis}, note | `resolve` |\\n| `satisfaction_record` | request_ref, target_pin{state_id, predicate_version}, evaluation{ledger_cursor, conjunct_evidence_pins} | drive/plan |\\n| `revocation_record` | decision_identity, version, authority{…}, reason | `revoke` |\\n| `drive_session_record` | session_id, trigger{principal, timer, adapter_wake, hook}, cursor_range, drained[] (canonical order: dispatch_id, then manifest end time), action_counts (incl. abandonment adjudications vs cap), deferrals[], next_horizon, quiescence_reason{satisfied, awaiting_submissions, awaiting_principal, awaiting_capacity, escalated, parked} | drive/quiescence |\\n\\nThe former `admission_record` is deleted: per-output admission is `admission_decision` and head movement is `head_movement`, both owned by RFC 0009.\\n\\n**Consumed:** submission bundles with atomic-group/derivation-closure declarations (0007/0010); `submission_received`/`submission_refused` and the closed refusal vocabulary (0007/0009); `admission_decision`, `head_movement`, `redundant_candidate`, the append protocol and locks, segment manifests, envelope + upcast/refuse-newer (0009); `lane_binding`, `scheduling_decision`, `dispatch_lapse`, capacity state including attention telemetry and the workstation-global fold (0008); backend capability declarations (0007, via the Scheduler); catalog entries (passes, gates, postures, pipelines, target states); `policy/driver.yaml`, `policy/gates.yaml`; decision records; prior ledger records as planning data.\\n\\n## Scale Posture (2031)\\n\\nDrive sessions never scan history: all hot state (dirty set, reverse-pin index, attempt counters, priors, queues) lives in incremental derived stores, each with its own transactional cursor; full scans happen only in `reconcile --deep`. Planning is per-request reachability over an eleven-pass catalog; cone walks are index-bounded; staleness events chunk; per-repository locks parallelize repositories. Principal attention is the scarcest resource and every mechanism above (depth-bounded queue, blast-radius friction, warning discipline, harvest issuance as visible requests) is designed so the human reads less as the system grows. Nothing in this RFC names a backend; three generations of backend churn land entirely in `backends/` + policy and invalidate nothing.\\n\\n## Language Amendments (N8)\\n\\nPer the Epoch 2 amendment mechanism (terms admitted with per-term layer assignment; operational conventions defined in owning RFCs and glossaried by reference; record-type names never enter the term list):\\n\\n**Admitted terms.**\\n\\n- **Agent Principal** (agency layer) — an agent runtime exercising a recorded, bounded delegation of Principal-issuable acts (request issuance/cancellation, named escalation-resolution classes). Never acceptance authority over decision-role artifacts without an RFC.\\n- **Drive Session** (agency layer) — one invocation-to-quiescence execution of the Driver loop, serialized per repository graph by the Graph Store's drive lease and recorded as a `drive_session_record`. A fact about the Driver, not a component.\\n- **Wake** (agency layer) — a non-authoritative trigger that invokes the Driver (timer, adapter, repository hook, human). A missed wake delays and never corrupts. Cross-referenced with RFC 0007's Advisory Pulse.\\n- **Acceptance Queue** (judgment layer) — the derived projection of open acceptance gates awaiting authority; a named derived store.\\n\\n**Merged terms.** Submission Spool is owned by RFC 0007; this RFC uses it by reference.\\n\\n**Operational conventions (glossary by reference only).** *Quiescence* — the drive-session end condition (defined in The Drive Session above): nothing drainable, nothing dispatchable, no staleness servicing demanded. Defined here, listed in the glossary by reference, not admitted as an ontology term.\\n\\n**Closed-vocabulary extension.** The escalation reason set gains `bounds_exhausted` and `binding_unsatisfiable` from this RFC; `independence_unsatisfiable` enters from RFCs 0007/0008; the set is fixed at eight codes. Budget discrimination is the `budget_kind` record field, not a ninth code.\\n\\n**Record-type registry.** New entries: `compilation_request`, `cancellation_record`, `satisfaction_record`, `revocation_record`, `drive_session_record`, `pass_run_closed`; RFC 0001's \\\"pass-run record\\\" registers as `pass_run_opened`; `plan_record`, `gate_result`, `staleness_event`, `deviation_warning`, `escalation`, `resolution_event` register under their existing names with this RFC as owner. Registry names are not ontology terms.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers\\n\\nFull deliberation in the Epoch 2 record (RFC 0000 implementation) — lane design, seam synthesis rulings R1–R12, and red-team reconciliation adjudications 1–19, which this design applies inline. Accepted semantic state: `decisions/D0006-driver-control-surface.md` (generated).\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0006-driver-control-surface/implementation.md\": \"# RFC 0006 Implementation: Driver Control Surface\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nAccepted (Epoch 2 Runtime Foundation Pass, 2026-07-02).\\n\\n## Encoding\\n\\n- `schema/ledger-records/`: v1 schemas for the thirteen record types owned by this RFC; each registers in `catalog/ledger-record-types/` (owner, writer, schema, upcasts).\\n- `catalog/pipelines/`: the pipeline template schema and the default target-state→pipeline mapping; governance is catalog validation, never an RFC.\\n- `policy/driver.yaml`: re-run bounds (revision, redispatch, withdrawal), deadline-class multipliers, abandonment sweep cap, revalidation tiers and budgets, acceptance-queue depth bound, warning aging.\\n- `policy/gates.yaml`: delegation entries (agent principals; acceptance delegation defaults to none; decision-scope delegations machine-checked against an authorizing decision record).\\n- `cmd/striatum` + `internal/driver`: verbs `request`, `cancel`, `drive`, `accept`, `reject`, `defer`, `resolve`, `revoke`, `status`, `explain`, `reconcile` — all clients of RFC 0009's store API under the lock-first invariant; stable `--json` schemas; exit codes 0/1/2/3/4/5. The one binary is the box's sole ledger reader.\\n- `tools/`: systemd timer unit template (standing timer plus per-session `next_horizon` rewrite); a timer unit, never a service unit.\\n\\n## The v0 Spine\\n\\nThis RFC's slice of the Epoch 2 cutline: **the minimal drive loop and the status projection.**\\n\\nBuilt first: `request`/`cancel`;
