`pipeline_ref` already exists in `plan_record` v1, so templates arrive without a schema break.\\n- **Cross-repository request groups** — `group_id` exists in `compilation_request` v1; planning is single-graph meanwhile.\\n- **`speculative_on`** — absent from `pass_run_opened` v1 by ruling.\\n- **`authority_proof` signing** — reserved fields only; the v1 trust domain is stated in RFCs 0007/0009.\\n- **Revalidation priors floor** — cold start; the tier-1 budget bounds alone until outcome history accumulates.\\n- **The dual-signal `verified` predicate** (RFC 0010) — requests target earlier predicate versions until it registers.\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0006-driver-control-surface/proposal.md\": \"# RFC 0006 Proposal: Driver Control Surface\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nAccepted (Epoch 2 Runtime Foundation Pass, 2026-07-02).\\n\\nRetired alias: this directory was formerly `rfcs/0006-meta-operator-control-surface/`; it was renamed with its content at activation, per the Epoch 1 residual-debt note.\\n\\n## Problem\\n\\nEpoch 1 fixed the Driver as a deterministic program that produces no artifacts (RFC 0002) and named the status projection and `reconcile` as the only operator-facing runtime surfaces the foundation authorizes. It deliberately left the surface itself unfixed: how a compilation request is issued and recorded, how the driver loop is invoked and serialized without becoming a resident process, how pipeline templates compile to plans (Epoch 1 open question 7), when staleness is revalidated versus regenerated versus ignored (open question 2), how Principal attention survives acceptance at scale (open question 4), and what `reconcile` may and may not do.\\n\\nThe bootstrap compiler's answer — a daemon guarding a live database, with an RPC/MCP surface, capability tokens, leases, and heartbeats — is documented operational pathology: daemon-unreachable as a standing failure class, client/daemon version skew, socket and token friction, migration-hash boot parks, store split-brain. A resident process is a second failure domain layered over the work. Under the Derived-State Doctrine and crash-only backends, every reason that daemon existed has dissolved, and nothing in Epoch 1 requires one.\\n\\nWithout a fixed control surface, lifecycle state leaks into the places the foundation forbids — terminal output, chat transcripts, marker files — and the human interacting with the compiler has no honest answer to \\\"what is running, what is wedged, what waits on me.\\\"\\n\\n## Target State\\n\\nA complete control surface for the invoked Driver: compilation requests and their authority as ledger records; the drive session loop (drain, mark, plan, bound, dispatch, sweep, quiesce) serialized by the Graph Store's locks with record-then-dispatch ordering; the pipeline/policy boundary; revalidation economics with tiered postures and budgets; escalation issuance and resolution under the closed reason vocabulary; acceptance, delegation, revocation, and agent-principal mechanics; a status projection with warning/notice triage and an attention-bounded acceptance queue; and `reconcile` as the single recovery verb. Thirteen ledger record types with v1 field lists, registered in `catalog/ledger-record-types/`.\\n\\n## Non-Goals\\n\\n- Ledger storage format, append protocol, locks, the admission funnel, `admission_decision`/`head_movement` — RFC 0009 (this RFC is a client of the store's API).\\n- Submission bundle and spool shape, adapter contract, adapter-side wake mechanics — RFC 0007.\\n- Placement policy, capacity pools (including `principal_attention`), harvest policy — RFC 0008.\\n- Packet and verifier runtime, the Partial-Admission Closure Rule, packet attempt-budget semantics — RFC 0010.\\n- Any resident service: daemon, RPC endpoint, MCP server, web UI. All four are recorded rejected alternatives, not deferred work.\\n\\n## Source Material\\n\\nThe Epoch 2 lane design for this RFC (`design-0006-driver-surface.md`); the Epoch 2 seam synthesis (rulings R1–R12) and red-team reconciliation (adjudications 1–19); Striatum-0 operational experience — the daemon's failure classes, doctor legibility lessons, and the lock-first invariant of its RFC 0104; Epoch 1 open questions 2 (revalidation calibration), 4 (acceptance-fatigue trajectory), and 7 (pipeline template semantics), which this RFC resolves.\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0007-agent-runtimes-and-execution-backends/design.md\": \"# RFC 0007 Design: Agent Runtimes and Execution Backends\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nAccepted (Epoch 2 Runtime Foundation Pass, 2026-07-02). Vocabulary: RFC 0001 plus the Language Amendments section below. Binding context: D0001–D0005; RFC 0002 §Execution Backends and §The Submit/Admit Seam; RFC 0004 failure semantics; RFC 0005 independence and claim decay.\\n\\n## Scope and Position\\n\\nThis RFC makes the submit/admit seam concrete. It owns:\\n\\n- the **dispatch bundle** (what crosses the seam downward) and the **submission bundle** (what crosses it upward),\\n- the **backend contract** — the verbs, exchange discipline, and conformance rules every execution backend satisfies,\\n- the **backend declaration schema** (`backends/*/backend.yaml`), the **aliasing registry**, and their maintenance under model churn,\\n- **lane mechanics at dispatch** — how multi-lane pass runs execute without collapsing independence,\\n- the crash-only contract stated honestly, including the v1 trust domain.\\n\\nIt does not own: gate evaluation, planning, and run closure (RFC 0006); binding policy and capacity arithmetic (RFC 0008); the record envelope, canonical form, locks, and admission write-path enforcement (RFC 0009); packet dispatch ordering, verifier-lane runtime, and the Partial-Admission Closure Rule (RFC 0010). `lane_binding` is RFC 0008's single schema — this RFC contributes fields to it. The submission-refusal reason vocabulary is RFC 0009's single closed set — this RFC contributes codes to it.\\n\\nBackend identifiers in this document (`local`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `agy`) are opaque references to declarations living in `backends/`; model-family facts appear only inside declaration examples (N7).\\n\\n## The Seam Is Files\\n\\nEverything that crosses the seam is a content-addressed file tree on the one workstation — not environment variables, not stdin, not RPC. In crash-only terms:\\n\\n- Files survive the crash of both sides. A dispatch delivered by env/stdin dies with the process that received it; `reconcile` cannot re-derive what was never durable.\\n- Agent runtimes are file-native; several handle long stdin badly (a Striatum-0 friction pattern was an agent asking a question into a stdin pipe).\\n- POSIX `rename(2)` gives one atomic commit point for submission; no protocol handshake can be half-completed.\\n\\n### The spool\\n\\nAll seam traffic lives under a runtime exchange directory per target repository — the **Spool**, explicitly non-authoritative:\\n\\n```text\\n\\u003cruntime-root\\u003e/exchange/\\n  dispatch/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/            # dispatch bundles (written by the Driver runtime, read-only after seal)\\n  spool/incoming/\\u003cnonce\\u003e/            # submission temp dirs (adapter-private, ignored by everyone else)\\n  spool/submissions/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/   # committed submission bundles (rename target)\\n  cas/                               # content-addressed store for prompt assets and materialized inputs\\n  workspaces/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/          # per-dispatch workspaces (E1: git worktrees)\\n  advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/            # advisory signals (never semantic; deletable at will)\\n```\\n\\nDoctrine: the spool is in-flight work — not truth and not a derived store. Losing it, in whole or part, is exactly mass abandonment (RFC 0004 failure mode `abandonment`): every affected dispatch is simply still unexecuted and is re-dispatched. No reconcile semantics depend on it; `reconcile` re-derives the live dispatch set from the ledger and regenerates dispatch bundles bit-identically. Nothing under the spool is ever committed to any repository (P10).\\n\\nTwo placement rules: the spool lives on the same durable filesystem as the Graph Store (conformance rule A8 — rename atomicity and crash-ordering hold only within one filesystem) and on a separate subtree from it (trust domain, below). Admission drains committed submissions in canonical order — `dispatch_id`, then manifest end time — recorded in the drive session record (RFC 0006).\\n\\n### The dispatch bundle\\n\\nThe unit of dispatch is **one lane of one pass run, at one attempt**. Ordering is binding: `pass_run_opened` → `scheduling_decision` / `lane_binding` → bundle materialization → adapter `dispatch`. Records always precede work. The scheduler binds (RFC 0008); the Driver runtime materializes the bundle and invokes the backend's `dispatch` verb. The bundle is sealed before delivery: every file content-addressed, the manifest hashing the whole.\\n\\n```text\\ndispatch/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/\\n  manifest.json          # the dispatch manifest; its hash is mirrored via the lane_binding record\\n  inputs/                # materialized input artifact versions, read-only (hardlinks/reflinks into cas/)\\n  environment/           # materialized environment excerpt: decision clauses + policy versions\\n  assets/                # content-addressed pass prompt assets (D0004: prompt assets are catalog references)\\n  siblings/              # for synthesis lanes: the pinned sibling submission bundles (read-only)\\n```\\n\\n`dispatch_id ≔ H(run_manifest_hash ‖ lane_id ‖ attempt)` — deterministically derivable from ledger contents, so re-derivation after any crash produces the same identifier and the same bundle bytes. `attempt` is the Driver-incremented ordinal carried in `lane_binding`; incrementing it is always a recorded re-dispatch decision (see The Crash-Only Contract).\\n\\n**Dispatch manifest** (`schema/dispatch-manifest.schema.json`):\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"schema_version\\\": 1,\\n  \\\"dispatch_id\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n  \\\"run\\\": { \\\"run_ref\\\": 812, \\\"run_manifest_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"pass_id\\\": \\\"build\\\",\\n           \\\"contract_version\\\": 3, \\\"impl_version\\\": 7 },\\n  \\\"lane\\\": { \\\"lane_id\\\": \\\"divergent-2\\\", \\\"role\\\": \\\"producer\\\",\\n            \\\"attempt\\\": 1,\\n            \\\"independence_partition\\\": \\\"p1\\\",\\n            \\\"sibling_lanes\\\": [\\\"divergent-1\\\", \\\"divergent-3\\\", \\\"synthesis-1\\\"] },\\n  \\\"objective\\\": { \\\"summary\\\": \\\"\\u003cpacket objective or posture parameterization text\\u003e\\\",\\n                 \\\"packet_pin\\\": { \\\"identity\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"content_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n                                 \\\"element_anchor\\\": \\\"packet/7\\\" } },\\n  \\\"inputs\\\": [ { \\\"identity\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"version\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"content_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n                \\\"element_anchor\\\": null, \\\"path\\\": \\\"inputs/design.md\\\" } ],\\n  \\\"environment\\\": {\\n    \\\"decisions\\\": [ { \\\"id\\\": \\\"D0003\\\", \\\"clause\\\": \\\"C5\\\", \\\"element_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n                     \\\"path\\\": \\\"environment/D0003.C5.md\\\" } ],\\n    \\\"policies\\\":  [ { \\\"id\\\": \\\"repository\\\", \\\"version_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n                     \\\"path\\\": \\\"environment/repository.yaml\\\" } ] },\\n  \\\"prompt_assets\\\": [ { \\\"asset_id\\\": \\\"build/preamble\\\", \\\"hash\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"path\\\": \\\"assets/…\\\" } ],\\n  \\\"workspace\\\": { \\\"effect_class\\\": \\\"E1\\\",\\n                 \\\"base_tree\\\": { \\\"repository\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"commit\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"tree_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\" },\\n                 \\\"write_scope\\\": { \\\"allow\\\": [\\\"internal/store/**\\\"], \\\"deny\\\": [\\\"schema/**\\\"] } },\\n  \\\"expected_outputs\\\": [ { \\\"output_id\\\": \\\"change-set\\\", \\\"kind\\\": \\\"change-set\\\",\\n                          \\\"schema\\\": \\\"schema/…\\\", \\\"required\\\": true } ],\\n  \\\"synthesis\\\": { \\\"mode\\\": \\\"synthesized-from-N\\\",\\n                 \\\"consumes_siblings\\\": [ { \\\"lane_id\\\": \\\"divergent-1\\\",\\n                                          \\\"submission_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\" } ] },\\n  \\\"submission\\\": { \\\"spool_path\\\": \\\"spool/submissions/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e\\\" },\\n  \\\"advisory\\\": { \\\"abort_after_s\\\": 7200, \\\"context_estimate_tokens\\\": 60000 }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n- **The environment excerpt is at element grain.** W9 says a pass run records every decision record and policy version it read; dispatch inverts this into a hermeticity aid — the bundle materializes exactly the declared environment (the specific decision clauses, by anchor and element hash, that the pass contract names) and nothing else. The adapter must not expose repository paths beyond `inputs/`, `environment/`, `assets/`, `siblings/`, and the workspace (conformance rule A6). For LLM runtimes, hermeticity over model priors is unclaimable and is not claimed; what is claimed: every read of compiler state was declared, pinned, and materialized. That is what W9 honestly means for D2 passes.\\n- **Sealed** means: after the Driver runtime writes and hashes the bundle, nothing edits it; adapters treat it read-only. The dispatch manifest is the run manifest's lane-grain projection plus placement facts; it carries nothing that cannot be re-derived from ledger + catalogs + store.\\n- **The advisory block is advisory.** `abort_after_s` and context estimates are scheduler courtesy, enforceable by the adapter as mechanics, never a semantic deadline. There are no leases.\\n\\n### The submission bundle\\n\\nThe adapter assembles results in `spool/incoming/\\u003cnonce\\u003e/` (its private temp), fsyncs, then `rename(2)`s the directory to `spool/submissions/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/`. **The rename is the sole commit point.** Before it, nothing exists above the seam; after it, a durable submission exists that admission can evaluate. The seam sees exactly two states. After the rename commits, the adapter invokes the non-authoritative wake (RFC 0006); exit 4 signals transient contention and the adapter retries; a lost wake is safe — the standing timer is the documented liveness floor.\\n\\n```text\\nspool/submissions/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/\\n  manifest.json\\n  outputs/\\u003coutput_id\\u003e/…        # candidate artifact bodies\\n  evidence/…                   # sealed receipts (verifier lanes), review ledgers (review lanes)\\n  exhaust/…                    # bulky non-artifact lane exhaust (transcripts, drafts) — blob-bound\\n  diagnostics.json\\n```\\n\\n**Submission manifest** (`schema/submission-manifest.schema.json`; the shape RFC 0009's admission funnel validates at seam intake):\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"schema_version\\\": 1,\\n  \\\"dispatch_id\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"run_ref\\\": 812, \\\"run_manifest_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n  \\\"lane_id\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"attempt\\\": 1,\\n  \\\"status\\\": \\\"complete | partial | failed\\\",\\n  \\\"outputs\\\": [ { \\\"output_id\\\": \\\"change-set\\\", \\\"kind\\\": \\\"change-set\\\",\\n                 \\\"content_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"path\\\": \\\"outputs/change-set/\\\",\\n                 \\\"status\\\": \\\"present | missing\\\", \\\"missing_reason\\\": null } ],\\n  \\\"evidence\\\": [ { \\\"kind\\\": \\\"receipt\\\", \\\"content_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"path\\\": \\\"evidence/r3.json\\\" } ],\\n  \\\"exhaust\\\":  [ { \\\"label\\\": \\\"transcript\\\", \\\"content_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"path\\\": \\\"exhaust/t.jsonl\\\" } ],\\n  \\\"synthesized_from\\\": [ { \\\"lane_id\\\": \\\"divergent-1\\\", \\\"submission_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\" } ],\\n  \\\"attribution\\\": {\\n    \\\"backend_id\\\": \\\"claude-code\\\",\\n    \\\"declaration_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n    \\\"agent_runtime\\\": { \\\"id\\\": \\\"claude-code\\\", \\\"version\\\": \\\"2.1.34\\\" },\\n    \\\"session_nonce\\\": \\\"uuid-v4-fresh-per-dispatch\\\",\\n    \\\"rendered_prompt_hash\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n    \\\"prompt_asset_hashes\\\": [\\\"…\\\"],\\n    \\\"internal_relaunches\\\": 0,\\n    \\\"started_at\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"ended_at\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n    \\\"advisory\\\": { \\\"token_usage\\\": { \\\"input\\\": 0, \\\"output\\\": 0 }, \\\"sampler\\\": {} } },\\n  \\\"diagnostics\\\": { \\\"classes\\\": [], \\\"assumptions\\\": [], \\\"captured_questions\\\": [] },\\n  \\\"seal\\\": { \\\"scheme\\\": \\\"plain\\\", \\\"algo\\\": \\\"sha256\\\", \\\"manifest_digest\\\": \\\"…\\\" }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nSemantics:\\n\\n- **`status` maps onto RFC 0004 failure modes.** `complete` — all required outputs present. `partial` — at least one required output present and at least one missing, each miss carrying a `missing_reason`. `failed` — no admissible outputs (maps to `pass_error` from the run's perspective); diagnostics explain. **`abandonment` is never a status** — it is the absence of a submission, by construction.\\n- **Candidate artifact bodies** live under `outputs/`, one directory per declared expected output, hashed individually. For a `build` lane the body is the Change Set: bounded diff (workspace commits exported as a patch series + result tree hash), the packet pin, and advisory lane-local evidence per RFC 0003.\\n- **Evidence vs. exhaust.** Evidence entries are bodies of the four evidence kinds only (Review Ledger, Receipt, Verification Report bodies from analysis lanes). Everything else bulky — transcripts, divergent drafts a synthesis consumed, tool logs — is **Exhaust**: content-addressed blobs referenced from provenance records but not artifacts (the twelve-kind catalog stays closed; RFC 0003). Admission moves exhaust to blob storage (RFC 0009); the spool copy becomes garbage.\\n- **Attribution is the backend's provenance contribution** (RFC 0002). The `provenance_fields.required` list in the backend declaration is enforced at admission: incomplete attribution is a refusal, because independence (RFC 0005) is computed over these fields. The **Session Nonce** is the opaque runtime-session identifier that makes \\\"share no backend session\\\" checkable. `rendered_prompt_hash` hashes the exact prompt the adapter composed — dispatch pins prompt assets; this pins their rendering. Usage figures are advisory scheduler food (they feed `capacity_observation`, RFC 0008), never truth.\\n- **`diagnostics.classes`** is a small closed set of structured friction classes translated from Striatum-0: `strategy_then_exit`, `ask_and_exit`, `output_shape_error`, `context_exhausted`, `runtime_crash`, `write_scope_violation`. `captured_questions` preserves any clarifying question the runtime attempted — fuel for the Driver's `ambiguous_goal` escalations.\\n- **`seal.scheme`** is `plain` in v1 (an unkeyed digest); the field is reserved for keyed seals at the Epoch 3 hardening boundary (trust domain, below).\\n- **Nothing here is true.** A submission confers no lifecycle state, moves no head, mints no claim. It is an offer. Admission (RFC 0009) turns accepted outputs into `candidate` artifact versions with the pass run as sole producer (W4); the Driver's gates do the rest (RFC 0006).\\n\\n### The admission surface (declared for RFC 0009)\\n\\nBundle-grain validation obligations on a committed submission, enforced inside RFC 0009's admission funnel, in order, all mechanical:\\n\\n- **V1 — Binding and run.** A `lane_binding` record (RFC 0008) exists for (run, lane, attempt) whose `dispatch_id` matches; the named `pass_run_opened` is admissible for intake — open, or closed only by `abandoned` (see the winner rule below; `canceled`, satisfied, and already-won runs refuse).\\n- **V2 — Integrity.** Every listed path exists; every content hash verifies; the seal verifies over the canonical manifest.\\n- **V3 — Schema.** Each present output body validates against its declared artifact-kind schema.\\n- **V4 — Write scope.** For E1 lanes: the Change Set's touched paths ⊆ `write_scope.allow` minus `deny`. Violations refuse the whole submission — never silently trimmed, because trimming would fabricate a body no runtime produced.\\n- **V5 — Attribution completeness** per the pinned backend declaration's `provenance_fields.required`.\\n- **V6 — Session distinctness.** `session_nonce` is unique among admitted submissions sharing an `independence_partition`.\\n- **V7 — Synthesis closure.** Every `synthesized_from` reference resolves to a committed submission with matching hash; a synthesis output whose divergent inputs are absent is refused (`synthesis_closure_broken`). This is the bundle-integrity projection of the Partial-Admission Closure Rule, which RFC 0010 owns. (Epoch 1 open question 6, seam side.)\\n- **V8 — Winner rule.** At most one winning submission per (run, lane) **across attempts**; the first admitted valid result wins (see The Crash-Only Contract). A later valid result for a won lane is refused (`duplicate_lane_result` / `superseded_attempt`) and a `redundant_candidate` record (RFC 0010) is appended — value counted, never silently discarded; the bundle is retained as exhaust for forensics.\\n- **V9 — Bounds.** Exhaust and body sizes within repository policy bounds (advisory refusal class; policy-tunable).\\n- **V10 — Refusals are ledger records.** Bundle-level refusals append `submission_refused`, reason-coded from RFC 0009's single closed refusal vocabulary, so telemetry sees every failure shape. Per-output admission verdicts are `admission_decision` records (RFC 0009).\\n\\nGate evaluation, per-output partial-admission decisions, and residual re-dispatch are Driver semantics over this validated surface (RFCs 0006 and 0010).\\n\\n## The Crash-Only Contract\\n\\n### What \\\"result or nothing\\\" means when CLIs half-write\\n\\nAgent CLIs half-write constantly: partial files, stray `TODO.md`, aborted refactors. The contract does not pretend otherwise; it makes half-writes unobservable:\\n\\n1. All runtime writes are confined to the per-dispatch **Workspace** (E1: a git worktree checked out detached at the pinned `base_tree.commit`; E0: a read-only materialization, no worktree). Worktree mechanics are adapter-internal — above the seam there is no \\\"worktree\\\", only the effect-class declaration and the write scope.\\n2. The adapter — not the runtime — extracts the result: it diffs the workspace against the pinned base, validates shape locally, assembles the submission in `spool/incoming/`, and renames. A half-written workspace that never reaches rename simply never happened.\\n3. The workspace is never state (P10). Its only durable trace is whatever survived into a committed submission.\\n\\nSo \\\"result or nothing\\\" is precise: *the rename happened, or the dispatch is indistinguishable from never having run.* There is no third state to recover, which is why one recovery verb suffices (RFC 0002).\\n\\n**E2 is not a backend write.** Integration's outputs target the repository, but the backend still only submits (a staged integration tree + conflict findings); the movement of the target repository is admission mechanics (RFCs 0009/0010 — lanes stage, the store moves the product ref). No backend ever writes the artifact store or the target repository directly; `effects` in a declaration bounds the workspace semantics a backend can host, not a write privilege.\\n\\n### Cleanup by abandonment\\n\\nWorkspaces, dispatch bundles, incoming temp dirs, and advisory files are garbage the moment their dispatch is no longer live. A dispatch is live iff its `lane_binding` exists, its run has no closure covering it, and no winning admission exists for its (run, lane). The Driver runtime computes this fold and passes the live set to the backend's `janitor` verb as input — adapters are **ledger-illiterate by contract**: they never read or write the ledger; the one `striatum` binary is the box's sole ledger reader. (Rejected alternative: the janitor deriving liveness from a ledger read surface — that couples every adapter to ledger version skew.) Anyone, including a human with `rm -rf`, may reclaim non-live residue at any time; deleting it is never data loss — the Derived-State Doctrine extended to the spool. Committed-but-unadmitted submissions are the one class the janitor leaves alone until adjudicated.\\n\\n### Re-dispatch, provisional abandonment, and the winner rule\\n\\nPass purity (idempotence-by-versioning, D0004) makes re-dispatch safe: a duplicated execution yields two candidate submissions, never a corrupted state.\\n\\n- **Re-dispatch is closure-then-new-run, only.** The Driver appends `pass_run_closed{superseded_by_redispatch}` (RFC 0006's record) and a new `pass_run_opened` with the same sealed manifest; `attempt+1` is carried in the new `lane_binding`. `dispatch_id` derivation makes the new bundle distinct and the old one garbage. There is no same-run re-entry and no dispatch-abandoned record — abandonment adjudication lives in run closure, not in a parallel dispatch ledger.\\n- **Abandonment is provisional.** `pass_run_closed{abandoned}` is a reopenable adjudication, not a death certificate. A late submission against a run whose only closure is `abandoned` is admitted at seam intake, recording `submitted_late`. Refusal applies only to `canceled`, satisfied, or already-won runs. The abandonment sweep (RFC 0006) measures observed-active time — intervals containing no drive session and no adapter activity are discounted — and caps per-session abandonment adjudications with a warning.\\n- **The winner rule.** The backend was slow, not dead — Striatum-0's lease-expiry-under-load, dissolved. The first admitted valid result wins per (run, lane) across attempts. If the slow attempt's valid submission arrives before any successor wins, it wins; the Driver issues `abort` for the superseding attempt (advisory; the adapter kills and cleans). If it arrives after another attempt has won, V8 applies: refused, `redundant_candidate` appended, bundle retained as exhaust. Deterministic; no lease, no clock authority. (Rejected alternative: treating abandonment as final and refusing late results outright — that discards finished work and smuggles clock authority back into semantics.)\\n- **Workstation reboot:** all adapter processes die; no submissions appear; advisory pulses go stale; the scheduler's silence policy (RFC 0008 `dispatch_lapse`) eventually recommends abandonment; the Driver re-dispatches; the janitor reclaims. Reboot is just mass slowness. If the spool itself was lost, `reconcile` regenerates live dispatch bundles from the ledger, bit-identically.\\n\\n### Health without liveness vocabulary\\n\\nThe core admits no liveness vocabulary (RFC 0001 retired the family). Silence-vs-death is the scheduler's interpretation problem, fed by exactly two advisory channels, both non-semantic:\\n\\n1. **Ledger-derived telemetry** (durable, historical): binding timestamps, submission timestamps, refusal reasons, closure outcomes, per-backend latency and failure-class distributions. This is the telemetry RFC 0008 consumes; it requires nothing from adapters beyond ordinary seam traffic.\\n2. **The Advisory Pulse** (live, disposable): the adapter MAY maintain `advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/pulse.json` — `{ \\\"phase\\\": \\\"accepted | workspace_ready | runtime_launched | runtime_active | validating | submitting\\\", \\\"updated_at\\\": … }` — touching mtime on activity. Contract: gates, admission, and claim computation are forbidden to reference it; the scheduler MAY read mtime/phase to time re-dispatch recommendations; the abandonment sweep MAY read it as adapter-activity evidence for its observed-active-time discount — adjudication timing, never truth, and the adjudication it times is itself provisional. Deleting every pulse file changes no semantic outcome anywhere. It exists because re-dispatch after fixed silence wastes capacity on multi-hour `build` lanes, and because a progress trace is operationally priceless — but it enters the design fenced, as a signal, not a lease.\\n\\nThere is no heartbeat verb, no session table, no attestation class. A backend that never writes a pulse is merely scheduled more conservatively.\\n\\n## The v1 Trust Domain\\n\\nStated honestly, as a recorded downgrade shared with RFC 0009:\\n\\n\\u003e The v1 trust domain is a single OS user on one workstation. Ledger and seal integrity are **crash-evidence, not tamper-evidence** against co-resident writers. Lanes and checks are assumed non-adversarial.\\n\\nAn unkeyed hash chain written by the same uid that runs lanes cannot prove the absence of tampering; the conformance rules below are engineering discipline against accident, not defense against malice. (Rejected alternative: claiming tamper-evidence from the unkeyed chain — Striatum-0's RFC 0110-era overreach, declined.)\\n\\nRequired cheap v1 mitigations: the Graph Store directory is mode `0700`; the spool and workspaces live on a separate subtree from the Graph Store (same filesystem, A8); sandbox profiles are recorded in receipts (RFC 0010).\\n\\nThe hardening path is a named Epoch 3 boundary, not silence: per-lane uid isolation with the Graph Store unwritable to lanes; keyed seals via the reserved `seal.scheme` field; an optional external chain anchor. This records the disposition of Striatum-0's RFC 0110/0113/0114 lessons.\\n\\n## Backend Declarations\\n\\n### The declaration schema\\n\\n`backends/\\u003cid\\u003e/backend.yaml`, validated by `schema/execution-backend.schema.json` (placeholder replaced). Normative example (`claude-code`):\\n\\n```yaml\\nschema_version: 1\\nid: claude-code\\nkind: execution-backend\\ndeclaration_version: 1          # any change bumps; content hash pinned by every binding\\nagent_runtimes:\\n  - id: claude-code\\n    version_discovery: probe    # the probe verb reports the live version string\\naliasing:\\n  aliasing_class: anthropic-claude    # model family; drawn from backends/aliasing.yaml\\n  basis: vendor-stated                # vendor-stated | weights-verified | inferred | structural\\n  as_of: 2026-07-02\\n  review_by: 2026-10-01               # freshness horizon\\ncapabilities:\\n  effects: [E0, E1]                   # max workspace semantics hostable\\n  supported_pass_types: [proposal-generation, design-convergence, implementation-planning,\\n                         packetization, build, review]\\n  forbidden_pass_types:  [observation, decision-generation, verification, integration]\\n  context_profile: { window_class: large, practical_input_tokens: 400000 }\\n  latency_profile: { class: batch, p50_s: 600, p95_s: 3600 }   # advisory, telemetry-corrected\\n  concurrency: { max_lanes: 2 }\\ncapacity:\\n  model: rolling-window               # rolling-window | fixed-window | metered-budget | unmetered\\n  window: { duration_h: 5, anchor: rolling }\\n  estimate: { basis: ledger-accounting, unit: token-equivalents, confidence: coarse }\\n  exhaustion_behavior: refuse-dispatch\\nconstraints:\\n  network: vendor-endpoint-only       # none | vendor-endpoint-only\\n  interactive_input: none             # one-shot discipline; no questions\\n  internal_retry: { max: 1 }          # adapter-internal relaunch bound; recorded in attribution\\nprovenance_fields:\\n  required: [agent_runtime.version, session_nonce, rendered_prompt_hash, prompt_asset_hashes]\\n  optional: [token_usage, sampler, internal_relaunches]\\nscheduler_hints: []                   # free-form advisory; policy may read, semantics may not\\n```\\n\\nDeclarations **describe**; preference lives in `policy/` (RFC 0002). The only declaration facts that touch semantics are the ones RFC 0005's independence rule names: `aliasing_class` (independence) and `provenance_fields.required` (attribution completeness at admission). `forbidden_pass_types` is mirrored by catalog pass constraints (the authority-adjacent passes pin themselves to the deterministic backend class). Everything else is scheduler food.\\n\\nAny declaration commit appends `backend_declaration_changed` carrying the full post-state (below).\\n\\n### Capacity without vendor APIs\\n\\nNo declared runtime exposes a trustworthy quota API, and local-first forbids depending on one. So `capacity.estimate.basis: ledger-accounting`: the adapter reports advisory usage in attribution; the scheduler integrates usage over the declared window model to estimate remaining capacity and the reset horizon (`anchor: rolling` — horizon = oldest-usage-in-window + duration; `fixed-window` anchors to a declared clock). Estimation error is a policy problem by construction: a wrong estimate mis-schedules, it never mis-states truth. `exhaustion_behavior: refuse-dispatch` makes the adapter the backstop — a typed `capacity_exhausted` refusal at the `dispatch` verb, folded into `capacity_observation` records (RFC 0008) to correct the estimator.\\n\\n## The Aliasing Registry and Independence\\n\\n### The registry\\n\\n`backends/aliasing.yaml` (schema-validated) is the single home of model-family facts:\\n\\n```yaml\\nschema_version: 1\\nclasses:\\n  - { id: anthropic-claude, basis: vendor-stated, as_of: 2026-07-02, review_by: 2026-10-01 }\\n  - { id: openai-gpt,       basis: vendor-stated, as_of: 2026-07-02, review_by: 2026-10-01 }\\n  - { id: google-gemini,    basis: vendor-stated, as_of: 2026-07-02, review_by: 2026-10-01 }\\n  - { id: deterministic,    basis: structural,    review_by: none }\\nkinship:\\n  # appended when the market consolidates; each edge is provenance-bearing\\n  - { a: vendor-x-frontier, b: vendor-y-rebrand,\\n      relation: same-base-weights,        # same-base-weights | distilled-from | fine-tune-of\\n      basis: vendor-stated, as_of: 2026-08-01 }\\n```\\n\\n### The independence rule (this RFC's operationalization of RFC 0005 independence)\\n\\nTwo executions are independent iff:\\n\\n1. distinct `backend_id`s, *or* the pass contract requires only session-independence;\\n2. distinct `session_nonce`s;\\n3. their `aliasing_class`es are distinct **and** connected by no kinship path;\\n4. **at evidence-mint time only:** both backend declarations and both classes are fresh (`review_by` unexpired).\\n\\nKinship conjuncts (1)–(3) are re-evaluated at **claim-read time against the registry current then**; freshness conjunct (4) applies at mint time only. (Rejected alternative: read-time freshness — a lapsed quarterly review would silently decay every Verified claim on the workstation; mint-time freshness keeps the honesty incentive without ambient decay.)\\n\\n### Governed registry decay\\n\\nIf we learn in 2028 that two vendors were serving the same base weights, appending the kinship edge makes previously \\\"independent\\\" evidence pairs evaluate as aliased now, and computed claims fall arithmetically — RFC 0005's decay discipline extended from hash movement to aliasing knowledge. Evidence is untouched; its force lapses. The change is governed and visible, never ambient:\\n\\n- A registry edit appends `aliasing_registry_changed` (full post-state; below). The edit is **staged**, not yet honored.\\n- The next drive session computes a **claim-impact diff**. Below a policy threshold the change is honored automatically; above it, only after an authority acknowledgment event.\\n- The honoring session appends `staleness_event` records with cause `aliasing_registry_changed`, carrying the implied claim transitions — registry decay rides the existing event channel (W8), so \\\"when did production lose Verified, and what moved?\\\" stays a ledger query.\\n\\n(Rejected alternative: auto-honored registry edits with silent claim fallout — a one-line yaml change demoting a fleet's worth of Verified claims with no acknowledgment trail.)\\n\\n### Failure closed, production open\\n\\n- **Staleness fails independence closed, not production.** An expired `review_by` makes the backend ineligible to mint independence-bearing evidence (second-signal review, verification pairing) but leaves it fully usable for production lanes. Independence built on stale market facts is the co-blindness failure mode wearing a costume; refusing it is cheap because production capacity is unaffected. A `probe`-surfaced notice nags the Principal to refresh the registry — a two-line, quarterly, human-attention-priced duty.\\n- **`deterministic` never aliases.** Local deterministic tools share no model prior with anything; receipts minted by the `local` backend are structurally independent of every LLM lane. Consequence: the dual-signal `verified` predicate (RFC 0010) is usually satisfiable even in a consolidated model market, because verification runs on `local` are structurally non-aliased. The real supply crunch is model-diverse review pairs.\\n\\n### When independence is unsatisfiable\\n\\nThe scheduler, asked to bind an independence-bearing lane pair, finds no eligible pairing and returns a typed binding refusal; the Driver escalates with reason code `independence_unsatisfiable` (a closed-vocabulary amendment to RFC 0001 N6, converged with RFC 0008; distinct from `binding_unsatisfiable` — no capable backend at all — because the resolution paths differ: procure *any* backend versus procure a *different-family* backend). Resolution is Principal authority, recorded: (a) re-plan toward a target predicate whose claims cap at Asserted, (b) procure and declare a new non-kin backend, or (c) correct the registry. What may never happen: policy silently relaxing the independence predicate — capacity pressure never touches claim minting (RFC 0002), and unsatisfiability is capacity pressure in its Sunday clothes.\\n\\n## The Backend Contract\\n\\nEach backend is implemented by an adapter program — `striatum-backend-\\u003cid\\u003e` — the backend-internal supervisory process the seam talks to. (\\\"Adapter\\\" names the implementation of an Execution Backend, not an ontology category; see Language Amendments.)\\n\\n### Four verbs\\n\\n- **`dispatch \\u003cmanifest-path\\u003e`** — validate the bundle against the declaration (supported pass, effect class, capacity) and the spool placement (A8), create the workspace, fork the per-dispatch supervisor child, exit 0. Non-zero exit = typed refusal on stdout: `capacity_exhausted | runtime_unavailable | unsupported_pass | effect_class_unsupported | declaration_mismatch | spool_unsuitable`. Refusals are recorded by the caller as binding telemetry (`capacity_observation` where applicable). Acceptance is durable: after exit 0, either a submission eventually commits or the run is closed; there is no third obligation.\\n- **`abort \\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e`** — advisory kill: terminate the runtime, reclaim the workspace, never touch a committed submission. Idempotent; safe against unknown ids.\\n- **`janitor --live \\u003cpath\\u003e`** — reclaim residue for non-live dispatches. The live set arrives as verb input, computed by the Driver runtime's ledger fold; the adapter never derives it.\\n- **`probe`** — self-describe: runtime binary present, live version string, auth state, spool-placement check, declaration-vs-reality mismatches, registry-freshness notices. Output feeds the status projection (notices, not warnings) and scheduler telemetry. Probe is the honest replacement for attestation: it answers \\\"could this backend work right now?\\\", never \\\"is this specific work alive?\\\".\\n\\nNo status verb, no heartbeat verb, no lease renewal. The pulse file is a convention, not a verb.\\n\\n### Conformance rules (testable; the suite lives under `tools/`)\\n\\n- **A1** — One dispatch = one runtime session. Never batch two lanes into one process or context window.\\n- **A2** — Fresh workspace per dispatch; internal relaunch resets it to pristine base first.\\n- **A3** — No session or context reuse across dispatches sharing an `independence_partition` (no resume flags, no shared conversation files); `session_nonce` fresh per dispatch.\\n- **A4** — Submission only by rename into the spool; nothing else the adapter writes is read by anyone.\\n- **A5** — Runtime writes confined to the workspace; adapter writes confined to workspace + `spool/incoming` + `advisory/`.\\n- **A6** — No exposure of undeclared compiler state: the runtime sees the bundle's materialized trees and its workspace, nothing else of the repository.\\n- **A7** — Ledger-illiteracy: adapters never read or write the ledger; advisory files only under `advisory/`; the janitor's live set arrives as input; backends submit, only admission writes.\\n- **A8** — The spool must live on the same durable filesystem as the Graph Store; `probe` verifies and `dispatch` refuses (`spool_unsuitable`) otherwise.\\n\\n### Harness-friction countermeasures (Striatum-0 patterns, fenced inside adapters — never core semantics)\\n\\n| Striatum-0 pattern | Countermeasure (inside the adapter) | Surface above the seam |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Strategy-then-exit | Pre-submission validation: required `expected_outputs` present in workspace; if the runtime exited leaving only a plan, one bounded internal relaunch with a corrective preamble, workspace reset first | `failed` submission with `diagnostics.classes: [strategy_then_exit]` if the retry also fails |\\n| Ask-and-exit | Standing one-shot preamble rendered into every prompt: never ask; choose the conservative interpretation; record every assumption as a structured entry | `rendered_prompt_hash` pins the discipline; `diagnostics.assumptions` and `captured_questions` carry what would have been asked — Driver fuel for `ambiguous_goal` |\\n| Lease-expiry-under-active-load | **Dissolved by architecture** — there are no leases to expire; slowness is handled by the winner rule | nothing |\\n| Front-matter / output-shape errors | Mechanical schema validation of every output body before submission; one repair relaunch feeding the validator's error text back | `output_shape_error` diagnostic class if unrepaired |\\n\\nInternal relaunches are supervision, hence legal inside the adapter (RFC 0002), but bounded by the declaration (`internal_retry.max`) and recorded in attribution (`internal_relaunches`) so telemetry sees the friction and D2 provenance replay stays honest.\\n\\n## The Four Declared Backends\\n\\nAll four satisfy the contract identically; their deltas:\\n\\n- **`local`** — deterministic tools (D0). Aliasing: `deterministic`. Effects E0/E1, plus it is the only backend hosting **verifier lanes** (`verification`: executes checks pinned by Check Identity — content-addressed argv + binary hash, allowlisted by the check registry as defense-in-depth (RFC 0010) — in disposable workspaces, under recorded sandbox profiles, minting sealed receipts; the trusted core validates seals, never executes) and the E2-workspace staging for `integration`'s mechanical steps. Also hosts `observation` (mechanical watch) and `decision-generation` (D0 target class). Capacity: unmetered, CPU-bounded concurrency. Its \\\"prompt assets\\\" are check identities; `interactive_input` is meaningless; the friction table is empty. Deliberately boring — boring is what the gate path leans on.\\n- **`claude-code`** — LLM runtime, headless one-shot invocation, tool permissions confined to the workspace, network `vendor-endpoint-only`. Effects E0/E1. Supported: the transform lowering passes plus `review`; forbidden: `verification`, `observation`, `decision-generation`, `integration`. Capacity: rolling-window, ledger-accounted. Aliasing: `anthropic-claude`.\\n- **`codex`** — LLM runtime, full-auto sandbox profile confined to the workspace. Same pass-support shape. Historically the strongest strategy-then-exit offender; its adapter's expected-output validation is the load-bearing countermeasure. Aliasing: `openai-gpt`.\\n- **`agy`** — LLM runtime. Historically the front-matter offender; its adapter's schema-validate-then-repair loop is load-bearing. Same pass-support shape. Aliasing: `google-gemini`.\\n\\nPass-support asymmetry is the point: the passes whose outputs carry authority-adjacent weight (`verification`, `decision-generation`, `observation`) are pinned to the deterministic backend; LLM backends are producers and reviewers whose every output faces gates. This is consistent with RFC 0010's LLM-free verifier lanes and RFC 0004's D0 target for `decision-generation`, and is recorded both as `forbidden_pass_types` and as catalog pass constraints.\\n\\n## Lane Mechanics Inside a Pass Run\\n\\nThe chain (RFCs 0001/0002): pass contract declares lane requirements → pass run instantiates lanes → scheduler binds each lane (`lane_binding`) → one dispatch bundle per lane per attempt.\\n\\n**Divergent + synthesis** (contracts declare `synthesis: single | synthesized-from-N` per RFC 0004):\\n\\n1. Divergent lanes dispatch in parallel, each bound under the run's `independence_partition` constraints. Divergence usually requires *session* independence (distinct nonces, A1–A3), not full anti-aliasing — three lanes on one backend are legal when the contract says so, but the adapter may never collapse them into one session; A1/A3 and V6 make that structural rather than aspirational.\\n2. Each divergent lane submits normally. Its submission is durable in the spool; a `submission_received` record is appended at seam intake even though divergent lane products are **not artifacts** — they are recorded lane submissions whose bodies flow to blob exhaust. The closed twelve-kind catalog is not disturbed.\\n3. The Driver dispatches the synthesis lane only when its declared inputs exist: the synthesis dispatch bundle pins the divergent submissions by hash and materializes them under `siblings/`. The synthesis submission's `synthesized_from` must reproduce those pins (V7).\\n4. Only the pass run's declared outputs become candidate artifacts. Lane attribution — every lane's binding, backend, session nonce, and synthesis lineage — lands in provenance, which is exactly what RFC 0005's anti-aliasing evaluation reads.\\n\\n**Partial results across lanes** (Epoch 1 open question 6, seam side; partial admission is owned by RFC 0010's Partial-Admission Closure Rule):\\n\\n- The unit of partial admission at the seam is the lane submission (and, within one, the declared output). Finished lanes' work is never discarded: committed divergent submissions survive any sibling's death.\\n- Synthesis dead, divergents alive → the residual run (RFC 0010) re-dispatches the synthesis lane alone, pinning the same sibling submissions. Nothing is recomputed.\\n- One divergent dead, synthesis pending → synthesis is not dispatchable. The Driver either re-dispatches the dead lane or re-plans to `synthesized-from-(N−1)` — the latter is a plan change with independence-accounting consequences, a recorded Driver decision under contract rules, never adapter improvisation.\\n- A synthesis submission can never be admitted ahead of its inputs (V7): cross-lane consistency is enforced at write time, not by convention.\\n\\n**Independence enforcement at dispatch** is split across three parties, none trusted alone: the scheduler binds within partition constraints (policy), the adapter is conformance-bound not to collapse sessions (mechanics), and admission verifies nonce distinctness and synthesis closure (semantics). A silently collapsed lane pair fails V6 and never becomes evidence.\\n\\n## Evolution: A Fifth Backend Joins\\n\\nClaim: a new harness joins with declaration + adapter, zero core changes. Hypothetical `harness-x`, 2027:\\n\\n1. **Declare.** Write `backends/harness-x/backend.yaml` (schema-validated) and `runtime.md`. Diligence reveals its model is a licensed serving of an existing family: register its class in `backends/aliasing.yaml` with a `same-base-weights` kinship edge, `basis: vendor-stated`.\\n2. **Implement.** Ship `striatum-backend-harness-x` satisfying the four verbs and passing the conformance suite (A1–A8, rename discipline, refusal typing). Its auth dance, sandbox flags, and ask-and-exit flavor are invisible above the seam.\\n3. **Admit into policy.** One edit in `policy/scheduler.yaml`; a conservative first posture (harvest-class review parameterizations) while ledger telemetry accumulates.\\n4. **Run.** Bindings pin its declaration hash; submissions carry its attribution; admission validates against its declared required fields.\\n\\nWhat did **not** change: `catalog/` (no pass knows it exists — P9), `schema/` artifact shapes, the Driver, the admission path, the ledger record vocabulary, any other backend. What the seam got right shows in step 1: the fleet gained capacity but **not** independence supply — a `harness-x` pairing against its kin evaluates as aliased, automatically, at claim-read time (subject to the governed staging above). A model generation churning is: edit declarations, append registry entries, retire adapters; the graph, ledger, and claims never migrate. The same walkthrough covers a structured-form *human* runtime (`aliasing_class: human`) with no core change; scheduling humans is future policy work, not proposed here.\\n\\n## Record Types and Seam Declarations\\n\\nBackends never write the ledger. Every record below is appended above the seam (admission path or Driver runtime) under RFC 0009's envelope and canonical form. Each registers in `catalog/ledger-record-types/` with owner, writer, schema, and upcasts.\\n\\n**Owned by this RFC — full v1 field lists, snake_case:**\\n\\n`submission_received` — writer: admission, at seam intake after V1–V10 pass.\\n\\n```text\\nschema_version · dispatch_id · run_ref · lane_id · attempt\\nsubmission_manifest_hash · status: complete | partial | failed\\noutputs: [{output_id, kind, content_hash, present, missing_reason?}]\\nattribution_digest\\n```\\n\\n`submission_refused` — writer: admission, on bundle-level validation failure.\\n\\n```text\\nschema_version · dispatch_id · run_ref? · lane_id? · attempt?\\nreason            # from RFC 0009's single closed refusal vocabulary\\nbundle_hash       # retained as exhaust for forensics\\ndetail\\n```\\n\\nReason codes this RFC contributes to RFC 0009's vocabulary: `duplicate_lane_result`, `superseded_attempt`, `write_scope_violation`, `schema_invalid`, `attribution_incomplete`, `pin_mismatch`, `synthesis_closure_broken`, `bounds_exceeded`, `seal_invalid`.\\n\\n`backend_declaration_changed` — writer: Driver runtime, at declaration commit.\\n\\n```text\\nschema_version · backend_id\\nold_declaration_hash · new_declaration_hash\\npost_state        # pin of the complete new declaration — full post-state, never a diff;\\n                  # content-addressed into the object store at first pin\\n```\\n\\n`aliasing_registry_changed` — writer: Driver runtime, at registry commit; honored only after the staged claim-impact protocol above.\\n\\n```text\\nschema_version\\nold_registry_hash · new_registry_hash\\npost_state        # pin of the complete new registry — full post-state, never a diff\\nchanged_classes · changed_kinship_edges    # legibility deltas; the post-state is authoritative\\n```\\n\\nPin resolution never depends on git history: declaration and registry bodies are content-addressed into the object store at first pin.\\n\\n**Contributed to RFC 0008's `lane_binding` (one schema, owned there):** `dispatch_id`, `attempt`, `declaration_hash`, `independence_partition`.\\n\\n**Adjudications recorded elsewhere:** abandonment, late submission, and re-dispatch are `pass_run_closed` outcomes (RFC 0006: `abandoned`, `submitted_late`, `superseded_by_redispatch`); lapse detection is `dispatch_lapse` (RFC 0008); redundant late results append `redundant_candidate` (RFC 0010); adapter capacity signals fold into `capacity_observation` (RFC 0008). There is no dispatch-abandoned record.\\n\\n**Consumed:** dispatch manifests (self-defined above); pass contracts' `environment` and lane-requirement blocks (RFC 0004); `lane_binding` records (RFC 0008); artifact-kind schemas at pre-submission validation (RFC 0003).\\n\\n**Interfaces declared to neighbors:** to **0009** — the submission bundle layout, V1–V10 (the bundle-grain admission surface), and the exhaust-to-blob handoff; to **0008** — the declaration schema, capacity-model fields, typed dispatch refusals, ledger telemetry fields, the advisory pulse convention, and the `independence_unsatisfiable` binding refusal; to **0006** — statuses and diagnostics for re-run and escalation policy, the winner rule, the wake-after-commit convention, and residual re-dispatch pins; to **0010** — verifier-lane hosting on `local`, receipt sealing at the seam, and per-lane partial semantics.\\n\\n**New or replaced repository files:** `schema/dispatch-manifest.schema.json`, `schema/submission-manifest.schema.json`, `schema/execution-backend.schema.json` (real shape), `backends/aliasing.yaml` (+ schema), the four hardened `backends/*/backend.yaml`, and the conformance suite under `tools/`.\\n\\n## Scale Posture\\n\\n- **Fan-out:** dispatch bundles reference the CAS by hardlink/reflink; a thousand dispatches over one design cost one materialization. Bundle regeneration is deterministic, so no dispatch archive exists — the ledger is the archive.\\n- **Spool growth:** admitted bodies move into the store, exhaust into blobs, spool entries become janitor fodder; steady-state spool size ≈ in-flight lanes, not history.\\n- **Human attention:** the recurring human costs introduced here are quarterly aliasing-registry review (minutes, probe-nagged), above-threshold registry acknowledgments, and `independence_unsatisfiable` escalations (rare, genuinely Principal-grade). Everything else is machine-priced.\\n- **Reality moves:** backend death mid-run costs one re-dispatch; reboot costs one silence window; model churn costs declaration edits and registry entries, never migrations.\\n\\n## Language Amendments (N8)\\n\\nAdmitted into RFC 0001's Epoch 2 amendment, with layer assignment:\\n\\n- **Dispatch** *(Agency)* — the delivery of one lane of one pass run, at one attempt, to an execution backend. **Dispatch Bundle / Dispatch Manifest** *(Agency)* — the sealed, content-addressed file tree delivered / its manifest.\\n- **Submission** *(Agency)* — a backend's committed offer of results for one dispatch; nothing in it is true until admitted. **Submission Bundle / Submission Manifest** *(Agency)* — its file tree / manifest.\\n- **Spool** *(Agency; owned by this RFC)* — the non-authoritative exchange area for dispatches and submissions; loss is equivalent to abandonment.\\n- **Workspace** *(Agency)* — the per-dispatch scratch execution tree (E1: worktree); never state.\\n- **Attempt** *(Agency)* — the Driver-incremented dispatch ordinal for one lane, carried in `lane_binding`; a new attempt is always a new pass run.\\n- **Advisory Signal** *(Agency)* — a non-semantic hint readable by scheduler policy only; deletable without semantic effect.\\n- **Aliasing Registry / Kinship** *(Agency)* — the declared model-family classes and their relatedness edges (`same-base-weights`, `distilled-from`, `fine-tune-of`); kinship conjuncts of independence are evaluated against the registry current at claim-read time, under the governed staging protocol.\\n- **Escalation reason `independence_unsatisfiable`** — closed-vocabulary amendment to RFC 0001 N6 (converged with RFC 0008): no eligible backend pairing satisfies a required independence constraint.\\n\\nDefined here as owning-RFC conventions, listed in the RFC 0001 glossary by reference only: **Exhaust** (bulky non-artifact lane output retained as content-addressed blobs referenced from provenance), **Session Nonce** (the opaque per-dispatch runtime-session identifier over which session-independence is evaluated), **Advisory Pulse** (the disposable per-dispatch progress file; cross-referenced with RFC 0006's Wake).\\n\\nClarifications: \\\"adapter\\\" in this RFC names the implementation program of an Execution Backend — backend-internal supervision per RFC 0002 — not an ontology category; it does not revive the retired Striatum-0 sense. Backend identifiers are opaque tokens legal in policy and RFC prose; N7 continues to govern vendor and model names, which appear only in `backends/`. Record-type names (`submission_received`, …) are registry entries in `catalog/ledger-record-types/`, never glossary terms.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers\\n\\nFull deliberation in the Epoch 2 record (RFC 0000 implementation): the lane design for this RFC, seam synthesis rulings R1, R2, R5, R8, R11, and reconciliation adjudications 2, 3, 4, 8, 10, 15, 17, 18. Striatum-0 sources: operational brief §§1, 2, 5, 6 — the supervision/lease/attestation layer this design deletes and the friction patterns it fences into adapters. Accepted semantic state: `decisions/D0007-agent-runtimes-and-execution-backends.md` (generated).\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0007-agent-runtimes-and-execution-backends/implementation.md\": \"# RFC 0007 Implementation: Agent Runtimes and Execution Backends\\n\\n## Status\\n\\nAccepted (Epoch 2 Runtime Foundation Pass, 2026-07-02).
