Vocabulary: RFC 0001, plus the Language Amendments (N8) section below. Binding constraints honored: D0002.C2 (Derived-State Doctrine), D0002.C4 (submit/admit seam), D0002.C5 (Driver is a program), D0002.C6 (crash-only, one recovery verb), D0002.C8 (per-repository graphs), D0005.C2 (W1–W10), D0005.C3 (one invalidation algebra), D0005.C8 (archival).\\n\\nThis RFC owns the durable substrate: the ledger format, the record envelope and the governed record-type registry, the Artifact Store, the admission funnel and the unified refusal vocabulary, the store verbs, and all concurrency primitives. Everything the other Epoch 2 RFCs write, read, or rebuild passes through what is defined here.\\n\\n## The Graph-in-Ledger Principle\\n\\nD0002.C2 states truth is \\\"the artifact graph + the append-only provenance ledger.\\\" This design makes that one thing, not two: **the artifact graph has no durable encoding other than ledger records plus content-addressed bodies.** Every node is an `artifact_admitted` record, every edge is a pin inside that record, and every lifecycle transition is a `head_movement` record; artifact bodies live in a content-addressed object store the records reference; git anchors are secondary references minted by `integration`. No graph database is authoritative. Consequences:\\n\\n- Durable truth per graph = ledger segments + object store (+ the target repository's git history for integrated bodies).\\n- Every index, head pointer, staleness mark, claim value, and status view is a **fold** over ledger records — derived, destroyable, rebuildable (`rm \\u0026\\u0026 rebuild`).\\n- `reconcile` has exactly one job: refold.\\n\\nThis is the strongest available form of the Derived-State Doctrine and the structural answer to Striatum-0's defining pain: a live relational schema as truth forced 47 schema versions of migrations, hash-mismatch boot parks, and a split-brain cutover. Here there is nothing to migrate: sealed segments are immutable, bodies are content-addressed, and derived stores are rebuilt, never migrated.\\n\\n## Physical Layout\\n\\n### The Graph Store\\n\\nEach target repository's graph lives in a **Graph Store** — a plain-file directory outside the repository working tree:\\n\\n```text\\n$XDG_DATA_HOME/striatum/\\n  registry.json                       # workstation config: registered graphs (path, repo_id, alias, seen working trees)\\n  derived/                            # workstation-global folds (capacity, Principal attention) — RFC 0008\\n  graphs/\\u003crepo_id\\u003e/                   # the Graph Store; directories 0700\\n    drive.lease                       # drive-session exclusion primitive (semantics: RFC 0006)\\n    ledger/\\n      LOCK                            # exclusive flock; the append lock\\n      open/\\u003cfirst_seq\\u003e.scf            # the active (unsealed) segment\\n      sealed/\\u003cfirst_seq\\u003e-\\u003clast_seq\\u003e.scf\\n      sealed/\\u003csegment\\u003e.manifest.json  # sidecar cache of the manifest record\\n      cold/                           # archived sealed segments\\n    objects/\\n      sha256/ab/cd/\\u003chex\\u003e.zst          # loose content-addressed bodies\\n      cold/pack-\\u003cn\\u003e.pack              # cold packs + per-pack manifest\\n      cold/pack-\\u003cn\\u003e.manifest.json\\n    derived/                          # rm -rf safe in its entirety; each store embeds its own cursor\\n      index.sqlite                    # identities, versions, edges, heads, anchor maps\\n      claims.sqlite                   # claim cache\\n      status.json                     # status projection snapshot\\n      telemetry.sqlite                # scheduler-facing history (RFC 0008)\\n```\\n\\nIn the target repository itself:\\n\\n```text\\n.striatum/graph.json                  # committed: { repo_id, ledger_format } — identity only\\n.striatum/scratch/                    # gitignored; never state (P10)\\n```\\n\\nNothing concurrency-bearing lives in the working tree. `$XDG_DATA_HOME` (not `STATE_HOME`): this is durable user data, snapshot- and rsync-friendly — sealed segments and packs are immutable after seal, so incremental backup is trivial. RFC 0007's conformance rule A8 requires the submission spool to live on the same durable filesystem as the Graph Store.\\n\\n### Body placement\\n\\nThree **body placement** outcomes, decided per artifact kind by repository policy within fixed bounds:\\n\\n| Placement | What | Where bytes live |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| **stored** | all Evidence (Review Ledgers, Receipts, Verification Reports, Exogenous Change Records), Work Graphs, Change Sets, superseded bodies | object store only |\\n| **integrated** | Product Artifacts always; doc-like IRs and Decision Records where the repository's conventions want them in-tree (Striatum-next's own `rfcs/`, `decisions/`) | object store (primary) **and** target-repo git via the `integration` pass (anchor recorded) |\\n| **ledger-resident** | provenance records only — never artifact bodies | ledger segments |\\n\\nFixed bounds: Evidence may never be `integrated`; Product Artifacts may never be merely `stored`; no body is ever inlined in a ledger record — the ledger stays metadata-lean (Striatum-0's audit chain proved the value of metadata-only append surfaces).\\n\\n**Only `integration` (effect class E2) ever writes to the target repository.** The Artifact Store never touches the working tree. An `integrated` artifact's canonical body remains the object-store copy; the git anchor `{commit, path, blob_hash}` is a secondary reference. If the repository's history is rewritten and an anchor becomes unreachable, derivability survives (the body is still in the object store), `observation` records the exogenous movement, and the status projection raises a notice — Striatum-0's `worktree_head_unreachable` / `artifact_anchor_missing_file` doctor-problem class is retired from \\\"integrity emergency\\\" to \\\"recorded fact.\\\"\\n\\nStriatum-0's D273 found provenance accumulation in git \\\"a primary architectural drag\\\" and had to exfiltrate 1,755 historical bodies into blob storage with byte-identical reconstruction proof. This layout makes that failure unrepresentable: nothing lands in the target repository except what the repository's humans co-own, and only through the linker. Evidence is blob-stored from day one (RFC 0002's explicit requirement). The Doctrine's `rm \\u0026\\u0026 rebuild` drill is a directory boundary: `rm -rf graphs/\\u003cid\\u003e/derived \\u0026\\u0026 striatum reconcile`.\\n\\n### Self-hosting\\n\\nThe compiler's own repository is an ordinary target repository (D0002.C8): it carries `.striatum/graph.json`, its Graph Store lives under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/striatum/graphs/\\u003crepo_id\\u003e/` like any other, and its `rfcs/`, `decisions/`, `docs/` trees are `integrated` bodies. Its only distinction is constitutional: other graphs' pass runs pin its decision records as environment (see Constitutional Decisions).\\n\\n## Trust Boundary (v1)\\n\\nStated explicitly, carried jointly with RFC 0007: **the v1 trust domain is a single OS user. Ledger integrity is crash-evidence, not tamper-evidence against co-resident writers; lanes and checks are assumed non-adversarial.** Required v1 mitigations: Graph Store directories `0700`; spool and lane workspaces on a separate subtree, with the Graph Store never inside any lane write scope; sandbox profiles recorded in receipts (RFC 0010).\\n\\nThe hardening path is a named Epoch 3 boundary, not silence: per-lane uid isolation with the Graph Store unwritable to lanes; keyed seals via the receipt seal's reserved `seal.scheme` field (RFC 0010); optional external anchoring of the manifest chain. Rejected alternative: implying tamper-evidence the v1 mechanics do not provide — Striatum-0's RFC 0110/0113/0114 lessons receive a recorded disposition instead.\\n\\n## Ledger Format\\n\\n### Record envelope\\n\\nEvery provenance record is one **frame** in a segment file:\\n\\n```text\\nframe := magic(\\\"SLF1\\\") | frame_len:u32be | canonical_record_bytes | crc32c:u32be\\n```\\n\\nThe canonical record (SCF-1, below) contains the envelope and payload:\\n\\n```yaml\\nledger_format: 1          # frozen framing+envelope+hash-alg version\\ngraph_id: \\u003crepo_id\\u003e       # UUIDv7\\nseq: u64                  # per-graph monotonic; assigned by the single writer; THE record id\\ntype: \\u003crecord type id\\u003e    # from the governed record-type registry\\nschema_version: u16       # per-type; upcast-on-read; refuse-newer-than-reader\\nwritten_at: \\u003cRFC3339 UTC\\u003e # informational only; never ordering, never authority\\nactor: { component: driver|admission|scheduler|reconcile|principal, instance: \\u003cwriter boot id\\u003e }\\ncauses: [u64, ...]        # seqs of records this record causally follows\\nprev_record_hash: \\u003chex\\u003e   # intra-segment chain (previous record's hash; seeds from prior segment's final hash)\\npayload: { ... }          # type-specific\\n```\\n\\n`record_hash = SHA-256(canonical_record_bytes)`. It is not stored inside the record (it is derivable); the sidecar manifest and derived indexes cache it. References between records use `seq`; references to artifacts use pins.\\n\\n### Canonical serialization: SCF-1\\n\\nStriatum-0's RFC 0110 lesson: hashing over ad-hoc serializations diverges across implementations; the fix was a versioned, length-prefixed canonical form byte-identical across languages. SCF-1 adopts the lesson and goes one step further: **the canonical bytes are the stored bytes.** There is no separate storage serialization; hashing is `SHA-256(stored frame body)`, so any future reader in any language verifies the ledger with nothing but a frame parser and SHA-256 — no re-canonicalization ambiguity can ever exist.\\n\\nSCF-1 value model and encoding:\\n\\n- Types: `null`, `bool`, `int` (signed 64-bit), `string` (UTF-8, bytes as given, no normalization), `bytes`, `array`, `map` (string keys).\\n- Encoding: one tag byte per value; big-endian `u64` length prefixes for strings/bytes/arrays/maps; map entries sorted bytewise by key; nesting recursive; **no floats** (quantities that need fractions are scaled integers — floats are a canonicalization tarpit).\\n- Timestamps are fixed-width RFC3339 UTC strings (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`).\\n- Golden byte vectors live in `testdata/scf1/`; conformance is a CI ratchet.\\n\\n`striatum ledger cat` renders frames as JSON for humans; JSON is a projection, never an input.\\n\\n### Hash chaining: chains and sealed segments\\n\\n**Decision: intra-segment linear record chain + inter-segment manifest chain + per-segment Merkle root.**\\n\\n- Within the active segment each record carries `prev_record_hash`. Cost is one hash per append with zero contention — Striatum-0's chain pain was head-row serialization under concurrent appenders; the contention was removed (one writer process, below), not the chain. The live chain buys torn/tampered-tail detection in the mutable window, corruption localization (first divergent record), and a free seal (the final record hash accumulates as you append).\\n- On seal, the segment's manifest records `first_record_hash`, `final_record_hash`, `record_count`, and a **Merkle root** over record hashes (selective verification of single records inside cold segments without replaying the chain).\\n- Manifests chain to each other via `prev_manifest_hash`. The ledger's integrity anchor at any moment is (latest manifest hash, active-segment tail chain).\\n\\nRejected alternatives: no per-record chain (CRC-only framing) loses tamper evidence and localization for negligible savings; a global unsegmented chain makes verification O(history) and archival impossible — precisely what D0002.C2's sealed segments exist to prevent.\\n\\n### Append discipline and concurrency\\n\\nAll concurrency primitives live in the Graph Store and are owned by this RFC. There are exactly two:\\n\\n- **The append lock.** One runtime process holds the exclusive `flock` on `ledger/LOCK` per graph. All components (Driver, admission, scheduler mirror) live behind it; the `actor` field records which. The single-writer property required by D0002.C4 is this lock at this boundary. Rejected alternatives: per-working-tree lock directories in the target repository (RFC 0006's `.striatum/locks/` is deleted from that design); a resident daemon (confirmed rejected — locks and non-authoritative wakes are the concurrency model).\\n- **The drive lease.** `drive.lease` is a second flock-based exclusion primitive ensuring at most one drive session per graph (session semantics: RFC 0006). It is mutual exclusion, not a liveness claim; no heartbeat exists anywhere in the system.\\n\\n**Lock-first invariant.** Every mutating verb is a client of the store's append API, and its first act is append-lock acquisition followed by a tail re-fold of derived state (Striatum-0 RFC 0104's lock-first invariant, translated). No mutating decision is ever computed against pre-lock state.\\n\\n**Multi-working-tree use.** Multiple clones or worktrees sharing one `repo_id` serialize through the one Graph Store. The workstation registry records the working-tree paths seen per `repo_id`; open from a previously unseen path is detected, recorded in the registry, and surfaced as a status-projection notice.\\n\\nWrite mechanics:\\n\\n- **Write-ahead ordering.** Bodies before records: object-store puts are fsynced before any ledger record referencing them is appended. A crash between leaves orphan objects — harmless (content-addressed, never referenced), reported by `reconcile` as notices and prunable after a grace period.\\n- **Durability before acknowledgment.** Appends are `O_APPEND` writes followed by `fdatasync`; group commit is permitted with a bounded window (default 5 ms), but no admission is acknowledged to a submitter and no derived store is updated past a record until it is durable.\\n- **Torn-tail recovery.** On open: scan the active segment, verify CRC and chain; an incomplete or CRC-failing tail frame was never acknowledged and is truncated; a doctor notice is raised. No ledger record is written about bytes that never became a record.\\n- **Derived lag is legal.** Derived stores fold synchronously in memory and persist lazily; each store persists its own cursor transactionally with its content — there is no shared cursor. On open each store catches up from its own cursor. A store's persisted state lagging the ledger is never an error — that is the Doctrine working.\\n\\nAt 2031 scale (millions of records × ~1 KiB average) a graph's ledger is single-digit GiB across a few hundred segments; NVMe fsync group-commit sustains admission far beyond any realistic pass-run rate.\\n\\n## Record Types\\n\\n### The governed registry\\n\\n`catalog/ledger-record-types/\\u003cid\\u003e.yaml` — one entry per type: `{ id, owner_rfc, writer, schema_version, schema: schema/ledger-records/\\u003cid\\u003e.schema.json, purpose, upcasts: [v1→v2, ...] }`. Names are snake_case. Record types are the sanctioned extension surface, but **governed**: adding one requires a catalog entry + schema + owner RFC citation; changing meaning requires a `schema_version` bump with a registered upcast. Record-type names are registry entries, never language terms.\\n\\n### The unified v1 registry\\n\\nOne registry, one owner per type:\\n\\n| Owner | Types |\\n|---|---|\\n| **0009** | `graph_genesis`, `segment_manifest`, `archival_event`, `artifact_admitted`, `admission_decision`, `head_movement` |\\n| **0006** | `compilation_request`, `cancellation_record`, `plan_record`, `satisfaction_record`, `revocation_record`, `drive_session_record`, `pass_run_opened`, `pass_run_closed`, `gate_result`, `staleness_event`, `deviation_warning`, `escalation`, `resolution_event` |\\n| **0007** | `submission_received`, `submission_refused`, `backend_declaration_changed`, `aliasing_registry_changed` |\\n| **0008** | `lane_binding`, `scheduling_decision`, `dispatch_lapse`, `capacity_observation` |\\n| **0010** | `redundant_candidate`, `packet_quarantine`, `quarantine_release`, `integration_conflict`, `application_record`, `check_flake`, `graph_rewrite` |\\n\\nMerges fixed by synthesis: `pass_run_opened` absorbs the earlier `pass_run`, `run-request`, and `run-manifest` — the sealed run manifest, `plan_ref`, `request_ref`, subject pins, `deadline_class`, and `speculative_on` (absent v1) all live there, and the run id is that record's `seq`. `pass_run_closed` absorbs `pass_run_outcome` and `run-closure`; its closed outcome set is `submitted | submitted_partial | submitted_late | abandoned | canceled | error | superseded_by_redispatch`, carrying `residual` and the deadline policy pin. `admission_decision` + `head_movement` replace the earlier `admission_record`. `dispatch-abandoned` is deleted — abandonment adjudication is `pass_run_closed{abandoned}`. `aliasing_registry_changed` and `backend_declaration_changed` carry **full post-state**, never diffs, so pin resolution and independence folds never depend on git history.\\n\\nTypes owned by other RFCs are registered here and defined there; this RFC fixes only the envelope (all types) and the admission-facing minimums below (`gate_result`, `staleness_event`, `deviation_warning`, `redundant_candidate`, `escalation`, `resolution_event`, `pass_run_opened`, `plan_record` are owned by RFCs 0006/0010 — their full field lists live in the owning designs; the payloads below are the store-enforced minimums). Field sets that follow are v1 payloads, envelope omitted; every type registers in `catalog/ledger-record-types/`.\\n\\n### Types owned by this RFC\\n\\n**`graph_genesis`** (writer: admission; always `seq = 0`) — repository identity:\\n\\n```yaml\\nrepo_id: uuid7\\nrepo: {vcs: git, root_commit: hex, human_name, path_at_registration}\\ncore_graph: repo_id                # which graph is constitutional\\nledger_format: 1\\ncompiler_version\\n```\\n\\n**`artifact_admitted`** (writer: admission) — the graph node itself; the write-ahead of the Artifact Store:\\n\\n```yaml\\nidentity, version: seq             # version id = this record's seq\\nkind, role: ir|decision|evidence|product, level: L0..L6?\\ncontent_hash: hex                  # over canonical body bytes, uncompressed\\nkind_schema_version: u16\\nplacement: stored | integrated\\nbody: {store: object, address: sha256/\\u003chex\\u003e, size, compression: zstd}\\nanchor_map: [{anchor, element_hash}]          # extracted at admission\\nedges:\\n  derived_from: [pin]\\n  constrained_by: [pin]            # element grain where anchors exist\\n  evidences: [{subject: pin, claim: string, binding_closure: [pin]}]  # evidence role only\\n  supersedes: artifact_pin?\\nproduced_by_run: seq\\nproduction_mode: pass | observation | re_stamp\\nattribution: {backend_id, backend_version, aliasing_class, agent_runtime, lane_id, lane_role, prompt_hashes}\\nlifecycle: candidate               # the only admissible entry state\\n```\\n\\n`binding_closure` mirrors the evidence body's binding-closure pins into the record at admission, so claim folds never open bodies.\\n\\n**`admission_decision`** (writer: admission) — per-output verdict of the admission funnel, including refusals (partial admission per D0002.C4):\\n\\n```yaml\\nrun_ref: seq\\noutput: {index, content_hash}\\ndecision: admitted (→ artifact_admitted seq) | refused\\nrefusal_code: \\u003cthe unified closed set, below\\u003e\\ndetail: string\\n```\\n\\n**`head_movement`** (writer: driver) — the only lifecycle mutation surface (W6):\\n\\n```yaml\\nidentity\\nmovement: initial_accept | supersede | re_stamp | retire\\nfrom_version: seq?                 # absent for initial_accept\\nto_version: seq?                   # absent for retire\\nlicensed_by:\\n  gate_results: [seq]              # required for initial_accept and supersede\\n  re_stamp_license: {revalidation_run: seq, review_ledger: artifact_pin,\\n                     verdict: accept|accept_with_findings}?   # required for re_stamp\\nimplied_claim_transitions: [{claim, from, to}]?\\n```\\n\\n`supersede` implies supersession of `from_version` in the same record. `implied_claim_transitions` may be omitted at append time: transitions are a deterministic fold over recorded events, may be computed lazily by the claim-cache fold, and are backfilled by the next fold — W8's audit query (\\\"when did production lose Verified, and what moved\\\") remains a ledger query either way.\\n\\n**`gate_result`** (owner: RFC 0006; W7 semantics: RFC 0005 — store-enforced minimum):\\n\\n```yaml\\nsubject: artifact_pin\\ngate_id, gate_class: check|review|acceptance\\ngate_predicate_version: u32\\ntarget_state: {id, version}?       # when evaluated as a target-predicate conjunct (D0005.C6)\\noutcome: pass | fail\\nverdict: accept|accept_with_findings|needs_revision|reject?   # review gates; vocabulary RFC 0001\\nevidence: [pin]                    # receipts, review ledgers evaluated\\ninputs_fresh: bool                 # false blocks head movement (D0005.C3 soundness)\\nauthority: {kind: principal | delegated_policy, policy: policy_pin?}   # acceptance gates\\n```\\n\\n**`staleness_event`** (owner: RFC 0006 — store-enforced minimum; eager transitive marking):\\n\\n```yaml\\nwave: seq                          # the triggering head_movement / artifact_admitted /\\n                                   # registry-honoring record\\ncause:\\n  kind: head_moved | element_moved | contract_bump | predicate_bump | exogenous |\\n        decision_regenerated | aliasing_registry_changed\\n  moved: {identity, old_hash, new_hash, elements: [{anchor, old_element_hash, new_element_hash}]?}?\\n  contract: {pass_id, from_version, to_version}?\\n  registry_change: seq?            # the aliasing_registry_changed record being honored\\nsubjects:                          # chunked; max 1024 per record\\n  - pin: artifact_pin\\n    via: derived_from | constrained_by\\n    element_grain: bool\\n    implied_claim_transitions: [{claim, from: Verified|Asserted|Designed, to, evidence_lapsed: [pin]}]?\\nchunk: {index, of}\\n```\\n\\nImplied claim transitions ride the event (W8), with the same lazy-backfill allowance as `head_movement`. The `aliasing_registry_changed` cause is how registry decay rides the existing event channel: the honoring drive session appends the wave; below a policy threshold it is honored automatically, above it only after an authority acknowledgment event.\\n\\n**`deviation_warning`** (owner: RFC 0006 — store-enforced minimum):\\n\\n```yaml\\nrun_ref: seq\\nclass: stale_decision_link | anchor_retired_fallback | partial_residual_pending   # closed; extension via registry\\ndecision: {repo_id?, identity, last_accepted_hash}\\nelements: [anchor]\\ndetail: string\\n```\\n\\nThe sanctioned last-accepted-under-deviation path of D0005.C7 lands here, once per consuming run.\\n\\n**`redundant_candidate`** (owner: RFC 0010; writer: admission — store-enforced minimum) — a valid late result for a run whose objective another attempt already won; value counted, never discarded:\\n\\n```yaml\\nrun_ref: seq                       # the losing attempt's run\\noutput: {index, content_hash}\\nwon_by: {run_ref: seq, version: seq}   # the winning attempt and its admitted version\\ndetail: string?\\n```\\n\\n**`escalation`** (owner: RFC 0006 — store-enforced minimum):\\n\\n```yaml\\nreason: \\u003cRFC 0001's closed escalation set (eight codes, Epoch 2 amendment)\\u003e\\nbudget_kind: revision | redispatch | attempt_total | integration_conflict | withdrawal\\n                                   # present iff reason = bounds_exhausted; names which budget\\nsubjects: [pin]\\nblocking_scope: identity           # subgraph root blocked while unresolved\\nrun_ref: seq?\\ndetail: string\\n```\\n\\nThe reason vocabulary is RFC 0001's, never restated here; `budget_kind` is a closed record field, machine-legible without reopening that vocabulary.\\n\\n**`resolution_event`** (owner: RFC 0006; writer: principal via control surface — store-enforced minimum):\\n\\n```yaml\\nescalation_ref: seq\\nauthority: principal\\ndisposition: {action: proceed|retire|amend|override, refs: [pin|seq]}\\n```\\n\\n**`segment_manifest`** (writer: admission, on seal; appended as the **first record of the successor segment** — it cannot live inside the segment it seals, since it contains that segment's final hash):\\n\\n```yaml\\nsegment_id, first_seq, last_seq, record_count\\nfirst_record_hash, final_record_hash, merkle_root\\nprev_manifest_hash\\ntype_census: {\\u003ctype\\u003e: {count, min_schema_version, max_schema_version}}\\ntime_range: [written_at, written_at]\\nledger_format: 1\\nlocation: open|sealed|cold\\n```\\n\\n**`archival_event`** (writer: admission) — cold movement stays ledger-derivable:\\n\\n```yaml\\nmoved: {segments: [segment_id], packs: [{pack_id, manifest_hash, object_count}]}\\npolicy: policy_pin\\n```\\n\\n### Minimums fixed here for driver-owned types\\n\\n**`pass_run_opened`** (owner: RFC 0006). This RFC fixes the admission-facing minimum — the sealed run manifest that makes provenance replay defined before execution:\\n\\n```yaml\\npass_id, contract_version, impl_version\\nmanifest:\\n  input_pins: [pin]                # element grain permitted\\n  environment:\\n    decisions: [element_pin|artifact_pin]   # repo-qualified; W9 basis\\n    policies:  [policy_pin]\\n    catalogs:  [content hashes of catalog entries read]\\n  prompt_asset_hashes: [hex]\\n  lane_requirements: [{lane_req_id, role, write_scope, independence}]\\n  synthesis: single | synthesized-from-N\\n  determinism: D0|D1|D2\\n  effects: E0|E1|E2\\nplan_ref: seq\\nrequest_ref: seq\\n```\\n\\nThe run's id **is** this record's `seq`. RFC 0006 fixes the remainder (subject pins, `deadline_class`; `speculative_on` absent in v1).\\n\\n**`plan_record`** (owner: RFC 0006). This RFC fixes the minimum:\\n\\n```yaml\\nrequest_ref: seq\\nsubject: identity\\ntarget_state: {id, version, hash}\\nbasis: {ledger_seq: u64, heads_digest: hex}   # the graph state the plan was computed against\\nunmet_conjuncts: [string]\\nplanned_runs: [{pass_id, input_pins, after: [index]}]\\npolicy_pins: [policy_pin]\\n```\\n\\n`basis` makes Driver determinism auditable: same basis + same catalogs ⇒ same plan. Scheduling is likewise snapshot-pinned (RFC 0008); the whole control plane is replayable from inputs.\\n\\n`lane_binding` (owner: RFC 0008) is one schema — the union of the scheduler's fields, the co-declared dispatch fields (`dispatch_id`, `attempt`, `declaration_hash`, `independence_partition`), and the store's mirror minimum. Rescheduling appends a new binding; nothing invalidates.\\n\\n## Segments\\n\\n- **Sealing triggers:** active segment reaches 64 MiB **or** 131,072 records **or** 30 days of age; explicit `striatum ledger seal`; always sealed before archival and before `ledger_format`-affecting upgrades. Sealing = fsync, write manifest record into the new active segment, write sidecar manifest cache, rename into `sealed/`.\\n- **Manifest content:** integrity anchors (chain endpoints, Merkle root), inventory (`type_census` with schema-version ranges — a reader can refuse-newer *per segment* without scanning), time range, location.\\n- **Cold archival (D0005.C8):** sealed segments whose records are all past the archival horizon move to `ledger/cold/` unchanged (immutability makes archival a `rename` + `archival_event`). Object bodies of Evidence and superseded versions migrate into `objects/cold/pack-N.pack` — concatenated compressed bodies with a manifest of `{content_hash, offset, len, crc32c}` plus a whole-pack hash. Derivability-preserving by construction: bytes never change, only addresses; the object index maps hash → (loose | pack, offset).\\n- **Incremental `reconcile`:** each derived store records its own last-folded `(segment, seq)`. Reconcile verifies sealed segments by manifest (hash the file streamwise, compare `final_record_hash`/Merkle root — no frame parsing, no body loads), replays only each store's unfolded tail, then re-verifies derived stores by export digest. `reconcile --deep` refolds everything from `seq 0` into shadow stores and diffs digests.\\n- **Park classes:** a reader older than a record parks with a typed error naming the type and version (`schema_newer_than_reader`); a record whose referenced body is absent from the object store parks with `body_missing`, naming the record and hash. Park, never crash-loop, never partially read (Striatum-0's exit-79 lesson).\\n- **Backup order:** objects first, ledger second — a restored ledger then never references bodies the backup missed. This is the write-ahead ordering, applied to backups.\\n- **Integrity without bodies:** pack verification is a streaming hash against the pack manifest; segment verification is chain/Merkle math over record hashes cached in manifests. Bodies load only when a consumer actually reads one.\\n\\n## The Admission Funnel\\n\\nAll writes enter through one funnel inside the append-lock holder. The Store owns structural enforcement; the Driver owns gate evaluation (with Compiler Core semantics); the Store refuses head movements that lack licenses. Records always precede work: `pass_run_opened` → `scheduling_decision`/`lane_binding` → bundle materialization → adapter dispatch. Stages run cheap-and-structural before judgment:\\n\\n- **Stage 0 — seam intake.** A submission bundle (shape: RFC 0007) names a `pass_run`, outputs (bodies + metadata), attribution, and lane evidence; intake consumes the spool in the canonical drain order (RFC 0006). Refusals: `run_unknown`; `manifest_mismatch`; `run_closed` **only** when the named run is canceled, satisfied, or already won. Abandonment is provisional: `pass_run_closed{abandoned}` (appended by the deadline sweep, RFC 0006) is a reopenable adjudication — a late submission against a run whose only closure is `abandoned` admits, and the funnel appends `pass_run_closed{submitted_late}`. A valid result for an already-won run refuses with `superseded_attempt` and appends `redundant_candidate`. Re-dispatch is closure-then-new-run only: `pass_run_closed{superseded_by_redispatch}` + a new `pass_run_opened` with the same manifest, attempt+1 carried in `lane_binding`; first admitted valid result wins across attempts. Rejected alternative: same-run re-entry — deleted; terminal abandonment — deleted.\\n- **Stage 1 — form (W1).** Kind/role/level valid against `catalog/artifact-kinds/`; `kind_schema_version` readable (refuse-newer); body present, `content_hash` verifies; placement legal for the kind; size within policy; anchor map extracted.\\n- **Stage 2 — provenance totality (W4).** Exactly one producing pass run, and it must be the named run. No run ⇒ `W4_no_producing_run` (the write-time teeth behind \\\"decision records are never hand-written\\\"). Driver-attributed outputs ⇒ `W4_driver_authored`. Decision-record kinds must come from a `decision-generation` run.\\n- **Stage 3 — references (W2, W3, W5).** Every pin resolves: local pins against the identity/version index, element pins against the pinned version's stored anchor map (`W5_anchor_unknown` if absent), repo-qualified pins through the registry. Edge kinds ∈ the four. Acyclicity holds by construction (edges point only at already-admitted versions); intra-batch edges are toposorted and checked. Remint detection runs here: a retired anchor's element hash reappearing under a new id refuses with `anchor_reminted`.\\n- **Stage 4 — environment totality (W9).** Every environment read recorded by the lane must appear in the sealed manifest's environment pins. Undeclared read ⇒ `W9_hermeticity`. (The *sanctioned* stale-decision case is not a hermeticity violation: the read was declared; freshness lapsed — that admits with a `deviation_warning`.)\\n- **Stage 5 — plane discipline (W10).** Evidence appears among a transform's inputs only as the contract's declared diagnostic input; no lowering edge originates from evidence.\\n- **Stage 6 — candidate admission.** Surviving outputs append as `artifact_admitted(lifecycle: candidate)` + per-output `admission_decision`, in intra-run derivation order. The **Partial-Admission Closure Rule** (owner: RFC 0010 — an output is individually admissible iff its declared intra-run derivation closure is admitted) is enforced per-output here; a closure containing a refused output refuses with `synthesis_closure_broken`. RFC 0007's bundle-level V7 check is the same rule's bundle-integrity projection. **Candidates admit even if inputs went stale since manifest seal** — finished lanes' work is never discarded (D0002.C4); staleness blocks promotion, not existence.\\n- **Stage 7 — gate evaluation (Driver mechanics).** Per the kind's gate wiring: check gates (receipt seal validation — the core validates, never executes), review gates (predicates over admitted Review Ledgers, independence evaluated over recorded lane attribution + aliasing classes), acceptance gates (Principal event or delegated policy). Each evaluation appends a `gate_result`; `inputs_fresh: false` hard-blocks (D0005.C3: no gate passes over a stale input).\\n- **Stage 8 — transition.** Full gate set satisfied ⇒ `head_movement(initial_accept | supersede)` referencing licensing `gate_result` seqs; W6 uniqueness enforced by the writer against the head fold; supersession of the prior head is implicit in the same record; implied claim transitions computed (or lazily backfilled) and recorded; **eager marking** fires one staleness wave over the dependent cone (element grain where bindings allow), chunked.\\n\\nPartial results (`failure.modes: partial`): stages run per-output; the run closes with `pass_run_closed{submitted_partial, residual: [unmet lane requirements]}`; the Driver re-dispatches the residual as a new run whose manifest cites the original. The residual-run mechanism is owned by RFC 0010; the Store's contribution is per-output decisions plus the `residual` field.\\n\\n### Exogenous change and re-stamps through the funnel\\n\\n- **Exogenous:** `observation` (D0, driver-scheduled) is an ordinary pass: `pass_run_opened` → Exogenous Change Record submitted → same stages (it is Evidence: `stored` placement, `evidences`/vcs pins to moved tree hashes) → admission triggers claim decay recorded as a staleness wave with `cause.kind: exogenous`. The world's writes get no side door; they get a fast lane through the same door.\\n- **Re-stamp:** an accepting revalidation verdict licenses the Driver to append `artifact_admitted(production_mode: re_stamp)` — body-identical (`content_hash` unchanged), pins moved — followed by `head_movement(movement: re_stamp, re_stamp_license: …)`, the single gate-exempt movement (W6). Stages 1/3 still run (pins must resolve); Stages 2/7 are satisfied by the license.\\n\\n**Re-stamp attribution (authoritative; amends RFC 0005's wording).** The re-stamped version's producing pass run **is the licensing revalidation `review` run** — `produced_by_run` names it, `production_mode: re_stamp`. The Driver performs only the mechanical append and head movement. W4 is literally exception-free; the Driver remains artifact-free; W6 keeps re-stamp as the single gate-exempt head movement, now with clean attribution. RFC 0005's phrase \\\"driver-mechanical creation\\\" is superseded by this attribution rule.\\n\\n### The unified refusal vocabulary\\n\\nRefusals are facts, and the vocabulary is one closed set, owned by this RFC, defined once in the `admission_decision` schema and referenced by `submission_refused` (RFC 0007's bundle-level integrity record):\\n\\n- Intake: `run_unknown`, `run_closed`, `manifest_mismatch`.\\n- Bundle/structural (typically bundle grain via `submission_refused`): `schema_invalid`, `attribution_incomplete`, `pin_mismatch`, `duplicate_lane_result`, `superseded_attempt`, `write_scope_violation`, `synthesis_closure_broken`, `bounds_exceeded`, `seal_invalid`.\\n- Funnel per-output: `W1_kind_invalid`, `W1_schema_newer_than_reader`, `W1_body_hash_mismatch`, `W1_placement_illegal`, `W2_edge_kind`, `W3_cycle`, `W4_no_producing_run`, `W4_driver_authored`, `W4_wrong_producer`, `W5_pin_unresolvable`, `W5_anchor_unknown`, `W9_hermeticity`, `W10_plane`, `anchor_reminted`.\\n\\nThe submitter receives a typed error mirroring the record (the seam's in-band failure lesson from Striatum-0). The Driver's planning may read refusal history as data (D0002.C5) to bound retries and escalate; gates never read it for authority.\\n\\n## Artifact Store\\n\\n### Object layout\\n\\n`objects/sha256/ab/cd/\\u003c64-hex\\u003e.zst` — zstd-compressed with a 16-byte header `{magic \\\"SOB1\\\", algo, uncompressed_len}`. **`content_hash` is always over uncompressed canonical body bytes**; compression is invisible to identity. Puts are idempotent (`link`+`rename` atomic); the store never overwrites. Structured kinds (Work Graph, Receipts, manifests-as-bodies) store SCF-1 bytes; prose kinds store UTF-8 markdown bytes as authored.\\n\\n**Policy files are content-addressed into the object store at first pin.** A `policy_pin`'s `content_hash` always resolves against the store, never against git history — repository rewrites can never orphan a pinned policy. Rejected alternative: resolving policy pins through repository history.\\n\\n### Identity and version indexing (derived)\\n\\n`derived/index.sqlite` tables — all rebuildable folds over `artifact_admitted` + `head_movement`:\\n\\n- `identities(identity, kind, role, level, head_version, head_hash, lifecycle)`\\n- `versions(identity, version_seq, content_hash, lifecycle, produced_by_run, admitted_at)`\\n- `edges(from_version, edge_kind, to_identity, to_version?, anchor?, element_hash?)`\\n- `anchors(identity, version_seq, anchor, element_hash)` — element-grain staleness never reparses bodies\\n- `stale_marks(version_seq, wave, cause)` — cache of `stale()`, refreshed by staleness events\\n\\nBecause binding-closure pins are mirrored into `artifact_admitted.edges.evidences`, claim computation is index-only: no fold ever opens an evidence body.\\n\\n### Pin grammar (one grammar, everywhere)\\n\\n```text\\npin           := artifact_pin | element_pin | vcs_pin | contract_pin | policy_pin | predicate_pin\\nartifact_pin  := {repo_id?, identity, version_seq?, content_hash}\\nelement_pin   := {repo_id?, identity, anchor, element_hash}\\nvcs_pin       := {repo_id?, ref_kind: commit|tree|blob, hash}\\ncontract_pin  := {pass_id, contract_version, contract_hash}\\npolicy_pin    := {policy_id, version, content_hash}\\npredicate_pin := {target_state_id, version, content_hash}\\n```\\n\\n`repo_id` absent ⇒ the local graph. Pins are never \\\"latest\\\" (W5). **Resolution is hash-first:** the index answers \\\"does this exact hash exist / what identity-version carries it\\\"; the Driver separately resolves current heads when planning; the two operations are deliberately distinct verbs (`Get(pin)` vs `ResolveHead(identity)`) so freshness checks can never be accidentally skipped.\\n\\n### Accepted-head tracking\\n\\n**There is no authoritative head pointer anywhere.** The accepted head of an identity is *defined* as the fold of that identity's `head_movement` records in ledger order: the last `initial_accept`/`supersede`/`re_stamp` not followed by `retire`. `identities.head_version` is a cache of this fold. W6 uniqueness is enforced operationally by the single writer serializing `MoveHead` against its in-memory fold; it is enforced *definitionally* by the fold itself — two heads cannot exist because the ledger is totally ordered. `reconcile --deep` proves the cache: refold, compare export digests. Corollary: restoring a Graph Store from backup can lose a ledger tail but can never disagree with itself about heads.\\n\\n## Element-Anchor Discipline\\n\\nAnchors must survive D2 regeneration or element-grain pins are decorative (Epoch 1 open question 1). The discipline:\\n\\n- **A1 — Anchors are authored, never derived.** Explicit ids in the body (ATX heading suffix `{#el:\\u003cdotted.name\\u003e}` for prose kinds; schema-native ids — packet ids, clause ids — for structured kinds). Never positional, never heading-text-derived: renumbering and rewording must not move identity.\\n- **A2 — Continuity is a contract postcondition, gate-checked.** Every regenerating transform receives the prior accepted version's anchor map as declared input, and its contract carries the postcondition *\\\"every prior anchor is present, or listed in `retired_anchors` with a reason.\\\"* The **`anchor-continuity`** check gate enforces presence/retirement; silent disappearance is a gate refusal. The gate carries a **policy retirement budget**: retirements beyond the budget in one regeneration escalate the outcome from mechanical pass to review-required. New anchors are free. Anchor ids are never reused for a different element (retire, don't recycle) — and never laundered: remint detection (`anchor_reminted`, Stage 3) refuses a retired anchor's element hash reappearing under a new id.\\n- **A3 — Element hash = exact bytes of the element slice.** Slice = the anchored heading's subtree minus nested anchored subtrees (slices tile the document without overlap); `element_hash = SHA-256(SCF-1(kind, anchor, slice_bytes))`. **No fuzzy hashing, no whitespace normalization.** Benign D2 drift (rewording that changes bytes but not meaning) fires element staleness — and the revalidation-before-regeneration algebra (D0005.C3) is precisely the shock absorber that clears it cheaply. We buy anchor stability with authored ids and buy hash-churn absorption with revalidation, instead of building a second, fuzzy identity mechanism.\\n- **A4 — Semantic hijack is review's job.** A changed meaning under a stable anchor changes the element hash ⇒ dependents go stale ⇒ revalidation reads the delta. Mechanical gates check presence; judgment gates check meaning. The split is the gate trichotomy applied to anchors.\\n- **A5 — Dangling pins degrade, never lie.** An element pin whose anchor was retired is permanently stale at element grain; consumers fall back to whole-artifact revalidation; the consuming run appends `deviation_warning(class: anchor_retired_fallback)`.\\n- **Decision records** get continuity structurally: clause anchors derive from the design element anchors they distill, so regeneration preserves them wherever the design's anchors survive — the same discipline, transitively.\\n\\nAdmission extracts the anchor map (Stage 1) and stores it in `artifact_admitted`; all downstream element-grain computation is index-only.\\n\\n## Multi-Repository Model\\n\\n### Repository identity\\n\\n`repo_id` is a UUIDv7 minted at `graph init`, bound by the `graph_genesis` record to the git root commit and recorded in the committed `.striatum/graph.json`. Identity survives path moves, renames, and re-clones (clones share `graph.json`; the Graph Store is found by `repo_id`, not path). Two Graph Stores claiming one `repo_id` on one workstation is a registry error, refused at open; multiple working trees sharing one `repo_id` are legal and serialize through the one store (see Append discipline).\\n\\n### Cross-graph pins\\n\\nAny pin may carry `repo_id`. Resolution goes through the registry to the referenced Graph Store's read surface. Rules:\\n\\n- **Eager marking is graph-local; cross-graph freshness is lazy.** A head movement in graph A does not push staleness events into graph B — cross-graph event routing would couple ledgers and fan out unboundedly across dozens of repos. Instead, the Driver evaluates cross-graph pin freshness at demand time (planning and gate evaluation), where soundness is actually enforced (\\\"no gate passes over a stale input\\\" holds regardless of when staleness was noticed). Only marking eagerness — a legibility/scheduling optimization — is relaxed across graphs. A periodic sweep (driver policy, RFC 0006) may pre-warm cross-graph stale marks for status projection.\\n- The executing repository's policy governs its passes (D0002.C8); cross-repository intents compile as linked per-repository compilations exchanging repo-qualified pins.\\n\\n### Constitutional decisions\\n\\nDecision records split by owning graph, and the split *is* the scope rule (Epoch 1 open question 3):\\n\\n- **Constitutional decisions** (D0001–D000N…) live in the compiler repository's own graph — the graph named by every other graph's `graph_genesis.core_graph`. Pass contracts in `catalog/` declare environment decisions by identity; at run time these resolve against `core_graph`, and manifests record fully repo-qualified element pins. What Striatum's compiler *is* is read from where it is decided, with ordinary pin/staleness semantics — no embedded copies in the binary (a second source of truth that would rot), no per-repo duplication.\\n- **Repository-local decisions** are RFC identities inside a target repository's own graph; they constrain only that graph and enter environments via that repository's policy.\\n- If `core_graph` is unregistered or a required constitutional record is revoked, the Driver refuses to plan (fail-closed exactly and only where D0005.C7 fails closed); merely-stale constitutional records follow last-accepted-plus-deviation like any decision.\\n\\n## Derived Stores\\n\\nEvery derived store is registered in `catalog/derived-stores/\\u003cid\\u003e.yaml`: `{ id, consumes: [record types], fold_version, export_digest: \\u003ccanonical dump definition\\u003e }`. Each store persists its own cursor transactionally with its content; there is no shared cursor. Bumping `fold_version` **is** the migration story — `rm \\u0026\\u0026 rebuild`, spelled `reconcile --migrate`, the explicit offline refold flag. `reconcile --verify` rebuilds each store in shadow and compares export digests; mismatch is a bug in the fold, never in the ledger.\\n\\n| Store | Consumes | Purpose |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `identity-index` | artifact_admitted, head_movement | identities, versions, edges, anchor maps |\\n| `head-index` | head_movement | accepted heads (the cache of the head fold) |\\n| `stale-marks` | staleness_event, head_movement | cached `stale()`; element grain |\\n| `claim-cache` | artifact_admitted (evidence mirrors), head_movement, staleness_event | computed claim levels (named store, D0005 W8); rebuild = recompute claim() from mirrored binding closures vs current heads — bodies never opened |\\n| `status-projection` | pass_run_opened/closed, escalation, resolution_event, gate_result, deviation_warning, admission_decision | what runs, what's wedged, what waits on the Principal; warnings-vs-notices triage (D0002.C10; semantics RFC 0006) |\\n| `telemetry` | pass_run_closed, lane_binding, gate_result, admission_decision | backend success history, latency, refusal rates — the ledger-derived capacity input for RFC 0008 |\\n| `capacity-and-attention` (workstation-global, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/striatum/derived/`) | capacity_observation, lane_binding, pass_run_closed across all registered graphs | owner RFC 0008, stored under this RFC's rules; drive sessions snapshot it; Principal attention is summed globally |\\n| `graph-registry` (workstation-level) | registry.json + graph_genesis records | path/alias/repo_id resolution, seen working trees; rebuilt by probing registered paths |\\n\\nThe `rm \\u0026\\u0026 rebuild` guarantee is testable and tested: the golden ledger corpus plus digest comparison is a CI ratchet.\\n\\n## Seam Interfaces\\n\\n**Store verbs (what RFC 0006's Driver calls):**\\n\\n```text\\nOpenRun(manifest) → run_ref                    # appends pass_run_opened\\nAdmit(run_ref, bundle) → [admission_decision]  # funnel stages 0–6\\nRecordGateResult(gate_result) → seq            # stage 7 output\\nMoveHead(head_movement) → seq | refusal        # stage 8; license-checked\\nReStamp(identity, revalidation_license) → seq\\nAppend(type, payload) → seq                    # per-type writer ACL\\nCloseRun(run_ref, outcome, residual?) → seq    # outcome vocabulary: RFC 0006\\nSeal() / Verify(scope)\\nReconcile(deep? | verify? | migrate?)\\nReads: Get(pin), ResolveHead(identity), Stale(pin), Claim(pin), AnchorMap(pin), Query(...)\\n```\\n\\nEvery mutating verb runs under the lock-first invariant. Records precede work: no dispatch exists before its `pass_run_opened` and binding records.\\n\\n**Read surface:** the `striatum` binary is the workstation's sole ledger reader. Adapters are ledger-illiterate by contract (RFC 0007) — the Driver passes any live set they need as verb input; all other tooling reads through `striatum … --json`.\\n\\n**Consumed from RFC 0007 (submission bundle — fields this RFC requires):** `run_ref`, per-output `{kind, body, content_hash, edges, anchor_map?}`, attribution `{backend_id, backend_version, aliasing_class, agent_runtime, lane_id, lane_role, prompt_hashes}`, lane evidence refs, bundle digest. Refusals return the unified closed code set in-band.\\n\\n**Provided to RFC 0008:** the `lane_binding` registry slot and mirror minimum, the `telemetry` and workstation-global derived stores; capacity state is derived from records, not asserted.\\n\\n**Provided to RFC 0010:** per-output admission decisions, `residual` on partial closes, receipt/verification admission (evidence placement `stored`), seal validation as a check-gate primitive, per-output enforcement of the Partial-Admission Closure Rule.\\n\\n**Provided to RFC 0006:** the `pass_run_opened` and `plan_record` minimums, registry slots for the driver record types, the status-projection fold substrate, `reconcile` as specified here (RFC 0006 owns the verb's operator surface).\\n\\n## Format Evolution\\n\\nStriatum-0 reached live schema 47 with owner-bundle 0024 because truth lived in a mutable relational schema: every semantic change was a migration, every migration a hash bundle, every mismatch a parked boot. The equivalent churn here lands as **additive facts**:\\n\\n1. **One frozen commitment.** `ledger_format: 1` covers framing, envelope, SCF-1, and SHA-256. It is deliberately tiny. Algorithm agility exists (a format bump applies to *new segments only*; old segments verify forever under their recorded format) but the bar is an RFC.\\n2. **Per-type `schema_version`, upcast-on-read, refuse-newer.** Upcasts are pure registered functions `v→v+1`, tested against a **golden ledger corpus** (`testdata/ledger-corpus/` — one sealed segment per historical type-version, appended forever, read by CI forever). A reader older than a record parks with a typed error naming the type and version.\\n3. **Sealed segments are never rewritten.** There are no ledger migrations, by construction. History is upcast in memory at read time, byte-stable on disk for eternity.\\n4. **Derived stores never migrate.** `fold_version` bump ⇒ `rm \\u0026\\u0026 rebuild` via `reconcile --migrate`. The entire class of \\\"database migration\\\" work Striatum-0 drowned in is structurally absent.\\n5. **The record-type registry is the pressure valve.** New runtime needs arrive as new governed record types or new type versions — additive appends old readers skip by type — instead of ALTERs to shared truth.\\n6. **The one forbidden move** is changing the meaning of an existing (type, schema_version) pair. Lint + golden corpus enforce it.\\n7. **Bodies evolve independently** via `kind_schema_version` with the same upcast/refuse rules — an Epoch 3 Design schema change never touches the ledger.\\n\\n## Language Amendments (N8)\\n\\nNew terms, each with its RFC 0001 layer:\\n\\n- **Graph Store** (memory) — the per-repository durable directory holding a graph's ledger segments, object store, derived stores, and concurrency primitives; located outside the target repository's working tree.\\n- **Object Store** (memory) — the content-addressed body storage inside a Graph Store; the primary home of every artifact body.\\n- **Body Placement** (memory) — the per-kind routing of artifact bodies: `stored` (object store only) or `integrated` (also anchored into the target repository by the `integration` pass). Ledger records are never a body placement.\\n- **Canonical Form (SCF)** (memory) — the versioned, length-prefixed, language-independent serialization whose bytes are both the stored and the hashed representation of a ledger record.\\n- **Anchor Map** (subject) — the (anchor → element hash) table extracted from an artifact version at admission; the index basis of element-grain staleness.\\n- **Anchor Continuity** (judgment) — the gate-checked postcondition that a regenerating pass preserves or explicitly retires every prior element anchor (`anchor-continuity` check gate).\\n- **Graph Genesis** (memory) — the first ledger record of a graph, binding repository identity.\\n- **Repository Identity (`repo_id`)** (subject) — the durable identifier binding a target repository to its graph across paths and clones.\\n- **Constitutional Decision** (subject) — a decision record owned by the compiler repository's graph, constraining all graphs; contrasted with a repository-local decision.\\n\\nRecord-type names (`pass_run_opened`, `head_movement`, `admission_decision`, …) are registry entries under RFC 0001's existing \\\"Ledger Record types\\\" term, never term-list entries.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers\\n\\nStriatum-0 lessons consumed: D273 provenance-in-git drag (layout), RFC 0110 canonical hashing (SCF-1), audit-chain contention vs single-writer (chaining), RFC 0104 lock-first invariant (concurrency), migration treadmill and exit-79 park (format evolution), doctor warnings/notices legibility (status projection), split-brain cutover (why truth is append-only files, not a live DB), metadata-only audit (placement bounds). Full deliberation: the Epoch 2 record in RFC 0000's implementation (lane design `design-0009-ledger-store`, seam synthesis, red-team reconciliation).
