Vocabulary: RFC 0001, plus the Language Amendments section below (N8). Decisions in force: D0001–D0005.\\n\\nBoundaries: the record envelope, canonical form, store verbs, locks, and admission funnel are RFC 0009's; the driver loop, verbs, and run records are RFC 0006's; the submission bundle and backend conformance are RFC 0007's; scheduling, deadline classes, and capacity are RFC 0008's. This RFC owns execution-facing run semantics, Change Set admission predicates, the Partial-Admission Closure Rule, the verification runtime, integration, and failure containment.\\n\\n## 1. Trust Model\\n\\nOne sentence governs everything below:\\n\\n\\u003e **Execution is untrusted and parallel; admission is trusted and serial; the trusted core is execution-free.**\\n\\nBackends execute in isolation and submit. The Driver admits through gates evaluated by the Compiler Core, which computes only pure functions over content — hashes, schemas, patch application, seal arithmetic — and never invokes product-tree code, check commands, or any agent runtime. Everything that must run (builds, checks) runs below the submit/admit seam in disposable lanes; everything that must be believed is validated above it. Verified is minted by evidence admission plus claim computation, never by execution on the gate path.\\n\\nThe v1 trust domain is a single OS user. The recorded downgrade in RFCs 0007/0009 is binding here: ledger integrity is crash-evidence, not tamper-evidence against co-resident writers; lanes and checks are assumed non-adversarial. This RFC's contributions to the v1 mitigations are sandbox profiles recorded in receipts (§5.2) and the versioned `seal.scheme` hardening hook (§5.3); per-lane uid isolation and keyed seals are the named Epoch 3 boundary. The rejected alternative was silence — claiming tamper-evidence the design does not have.\\n\\nThree consequences of the decisions in force are used constantly:\\n\\n1. **Purity makes duplication safe** (D0004.C5, idempotence-by-versioning). Two executions of the same packet produce two candidate versions; admission's single writer picks at most one. No correctness property in this design ever depends on at-most-once execution.\\n2. **Claims decay arithmetically** (D0005.C5). Wherever the world or a sibling moves under an in-flight result, the consequence routes through binding closure and decay — never through a new invalidation mechanism.\\n3. **The ledger is memory, not input** (P3). Wherever a re-run needs diagnostic context, it is supplied as pinned artifacts (prior Change Set versions, Review Ledgers), never as ledger records fed into lowering.\\n\\nThe trust model carries a consequence worth stating as its own binding clause, because it is what the whole arrangement buys and it is silently losable. Because admission is a pure, content-addressed function and graph evolution is deterministic, **compiler soundness is independent of execution behavior**: no lane — however nondeterministic, redundant, or adversarial — can change which artifact versions the compiler admits or which target-state predicate it computes. Execution nondeterminism, and equally the judgment nondeterminism of review and acceptance, lives below the submit/admit seam and is frozen into admitted content; the graph's evaluation over that content is deterministic. This is not independence in general — execution behavior fully governs *liveness*, and it should: a compiler whose lanes never produce admissible work must refuse to reach the target, not manufacture progress. The asymmetry is the point — execution may touch liveness; it must never touch soundness. And the reduction is honest only relative to two things this design does not claim away: the completeness of the checks a gate enforces (garbage that satisfies weak checks is still admitted), and the seal/trust boundary (a lane inside the v1 single-user trust domain forges content rather than corrupting the admission function — the RFC 0012 boundary). The property is self-evident *of the model* and silently decayable *in the artifact*; it is therefore encoded not as a state to advance toward but as a standing guard — an adversarial-lane, metamorphic, and static execution-freeness conformance suite (`internal/driver/soundness_guard_test.go`) that fails any commit letting a lane admit invalid output or making the admitted result execution-dependent. The clause below names the invariant; the guard, not the clause, holds the artifact to it. This is clause C11 (extends C1).\\n\\n## 2. Packet Execution\\n\\n### 2.1 Dispatch\\n\\nThe Driver's loop (RFC 0006 owns the loop; this RFC defines the execution-facing semantics) advances a target predicate such as `verified(N)` by planning `build` runs for ready packets:\\n\\n\\u003e **ready(P)** ≡ P is a packet element of the accepted Work Graph head, P is not quarantined (§9), P has no open run (§2.2), and every Work Graph dependency of P has an admitted (accepted) Change Set.\\n\\nReadiness requires dependency Change Sets at `accepted`, not Verified. Verification proceeds concurrently with dependent builds; the risk of building on a later-refuted upstream is priced by the pin algebra (§2.5), not by serialization. Repository policy may tighten readiness to require Verified dependencies; that is driver policy, not semantics.\\n\\nFor each ready packet the Driver opens a run: a `pass_run_opened` record (owned by RFC 0006; envelope by RFC 0009) whose content includes the **run manifest**, sealed at dispatch — the backend receives sealed work (RFC 0002). This RFC fixes the manifest content for `build` runs:\\n\\n- `pass`: contract id + `contract_version` + `impl_version`\\n- `packet_pin`: (work-graph identity, work-graph version hash, packet element anchor, **packet element hash**)\\n- `governing_pins`: plan element pin, design element pins, decision clause pins (element grain, per W9), policy versions read\\n- `base_composition`: observed product tree hash + the ordered list of admitted ancestor Change Set hashes + the resulting **composed base** tree hash (§2.5)\\n- `prompt_asset_hashes`, `lane_requirements` (role, write scope, independence constraints)\\n- `diagnostic_inputs`: optional pins — prior Change Set version and/or Review Ledger for revision runs (W10-compliant)\\n- `deadline_class`: scheduler policy, derived from the backend's declared latency profile plus a policy multiplier\\n- `speculative_on`: optional pin list, **absent in v1** (§8)\\n\\n### 2.2 Record-then-dispatch and the Open-Run Invariant\\n\\nLeases, claims, heartbeats, and session liveness are retired vocabulary and retired machinery. Two rules replace them.\\n\\n**Record-then-dispatch (binding system-wide).** The dispatch chain is `pass_run_opened` → `scheduling_decision`/`lane_binding` (RFC 0008) → bundle materialization → adapter dispatch. Records always precede work: a crash anywhere in the chain leaves an open recorded run that reconciles as abandoned, never launched work with no record. The rejected alternative — schedule first, record after — leaves a crash window in which a launched lane's eventual submission fails binding checks and finished work is discarded at intake, which D0002.C4 forbids.\\n\\n**Open-Run Invariant (economy, not correctness).** open(P) ≡ ∃ `pass_run_opened` for subject P with no matching `pass_run_closed`. The Driver never opens a run for a subject with an open run. If the invariant is ever violated — a falsely-adjudged-dead lane submits late, a reconcile race double-dispatches — the system remains correct: both submissions enter as candidate versions in isolated workspaces; admission's single writer moves the head at most once; the surplus is recorded and retired (§2.4). Because correctness never depends on exclusivity, no lease, heartbeat, or liveness attestation is needed above the seam, and none may be introduced (D0002.C6).\\n\\n**Abandonment is a provisional adjudication.** A dead backend is indistinguishable from a slow one. When a run's `deadline_class` expires without a submission, the Driver appends `pass_run_closed{abandoned}`. The deadline sweep measures **observed-active time**: intervals containing no drive session and no adapter activity (suspend, reboot, clock step) are discounted, and per-session abandonment adjudications are capped, with a warning, so a resumed workstation cannot mass-abandon its whole in-flight set. `abandoned` is reopenable by exactly one event: the late submission actually arriving (§2.4). There is no process inspection above the seam. Purity guarantees an abandoned run left no durable residue beyond its records (RFC 0004).\\n\\n**Re-dispatch is closure-then-new-run — the sole re-dispatch mechanism, system-wide.** The prior run is closed first (`abandoned` by deadline, or `superseded_by_redispatch` by Driver decision); then a new `pass_run_opened` is appended with the identical manifest, `attempt+1` carried in its `lane_binding`. First admitted valid result wins across attempts. The rejected alternative — re-entering the same run at attempt+1 — made the intake funnel's closed-run refusal either discard finished work or become dead code.\\n\\n**Crash recovery.** `reconcile` (the one verb) re-derives the open-run set from the ledger, applies deadline adjudication, and reports nothing else — no worktree scanning, no process hunting. Backend adapters are crash-only and rebuild their own world from the dispatch channel; their scratch is disposable and invisible (§2.6).\\n\\n### 2.3 Packet pins at element grain\\n\\nEvery Change Set carries the `packet_pin` from its run manifest. Pinning the **packet element hash** — not merely the Work Graph version — is what makes in-flight work survive graph-level churn: if packetization emits a new Work Graph version in which packet P's element hash is unchanged, an in-flight or submitted Change Set for P still pin-matches at admission. Only movement of P's own element invalidates work on P. This is D0003.C5 cashed out at runtime.\\n\\nTwo rules make the stability claim true rather than aspirational:\\n\\n- **Sibling references are by anchor id only.** The packet element hash is computed over the canonical serialization of the packet element alone (purpose, inputs, outputs, write scope, acceptance check identities, dependency **anchor ids**). Dependency lists carry sibling anchor ids, never sibling content or hashes — so sibling churn cannot move an untouched packet's element hash. The rejected alternative — content-bearing dependency references — made in-flight survival false by construction in exactly the sibling-reshaping case it was sold for.\\n- **Anchor ids are the continuity-gated stable names.** Their stability is enforced by RFC 0009's `anchor-continuity` check, which carries a policy retirement budget (excess retirement refuses or routes to review) and remint detection (a retired anchor's element hash reappearing under a new id refuses with `anchor_reminted`). The identity-preservation predicate of §10 applies to **all** packetization re-runs, not only rewrite-parameterized ones: ordinary plan-driven regeneration may not retire-and-remint claimed packets.\\n\\n### 2.4 Late and redundant submissions\\n\\nFinished work is never discarded (D0002.C4). A submission arriving after its run was adjudged abandoned is received: the funnel admits it against a run whose only closure is `abandoned`, appending `pass_run_closed{submitted_late}` as the superseding adjudication. Refusal at intake applies only to `canceled` runs and to subjects already won. Then:\\n\\n- if the packet has no admitted Change Set, the late submission is gate-evaluated normally (a re-dispatched run, if still open, continues; first admission wins and the other run's eventual output is retired);\\n- if the packet already has an admitted Change Set, the Driver appends a `redundant_candidate` record pinning the late output, and the candidate is retired without gate evaluation. It remains in the store as provenance-complete history; the scheduler may read redundancy rates as telemetry.\\n\\nWhether unsatisfied-subject late submissions are always gate-evaluated (telemetry value) or only when useful is policy-visible either way; the records are fixed so policy can iterate without schema churn.\\n\\n### 2.5 Composed bases\\n\\nA packet whose Work Graph ancestors produced Change Sets must build against them. The **composed base** for packet P is:\\n\\n\\u003e observed product tree T_obs + admitted Change Sets of all Work Graph ancestors of P, applied in the Work Graph's explicit application order.\\n\\nApplication order is pinned by an **explicit application index** recorded in the Work Graph by packetization — a total order consistent with the dependency topology — never by anchor lexicographics. The rejected alternative (lexicographic tie-break on anchors) let a sibling anchor rename reorder patch application for untouched packets, moving composed bases and decaying Verified with no semantic change.\\n\\nComposition is pure patch arithmetic performed by the backend adapter when materializing the workspace, but its definition is semantic and its pins live in the manifest (`base_composition`), so:\\n\\n- a later revision of ancestor A (new Change Set hash) moves P's pinned base ⇒ P's Change Set claims decay by ordinary closure arithmetic — no new mechanism;\\n- verification of P (§5) materializes the identical composed base from pins, so what is verified is exactly what was built against.\\n\\n### 2.6 Write-scope isolation\\n\\nWorktrees are **E1 adapter behavior**: the backend materializes an isolated workspace at the composed base, confines the agent runtime to it, and dismantles it after submission. Nothing above the seam names, tracks, or cleans worktrees; a lost worktree with unsubmitted work is work that never existed.\\n\\nSemantic enforcement of write scope happens twice, both above the seam:\\n\\n1. **Statically at packetization**: `work-graph-legality` (check gate, RFC 0003) requires parallel packets to declare disjoint write scopes.\\n2. **Mechanically at admission**: `packet-checks` verifies the actual diff ⊆ declared write scope (§3).\\n\\nBackends may additionally sandbox writes as defense in depth; that is advisory adapter behavior and never a substitute for admission enforcement.\\n\\n## 3. Change Set Admission\\n\\n`packet-checks` (the check gate on Change Sets, RFC 0003) is **execution-free**: every predicate is computable by the Compiler Core from content alone. Its predicates, in evaluation order:\\n\\n1. **Schema validity** — the Change Set validates against `schema/change-set` (bounded diff, packet pin, base composition pins, result tree hash, attribution, advisory-evidence section).\\n2. **Packet-pin match** — the Change Set's packet element hash equals the packet's element hash in the *current accepted* Work Graph head. Element-grain matching means graph churn that left the packet untouched still passes (§2.3). A mismatch is a gate refusal with typed cause `packet_moved`; the candidate remains, and the Driver plans either a revision run against the new packet element or retirement.\\n3. **Write-scope conformance** — every path touched by the diff lies inside the packet's declared write scope (allowed minus forbidden paths).\\n4. **Base coherence** — applying the diff to the pinned composed base (pure patch arithmetic) yields exactly the declared result tree hash.\\n5. **Attribution completeness** — lane attribution and backend identity are present and consistent with the run's `lane_binding` (needed for independence evaluation).\\n\\n**Buildability is deliberately not an admission predicate.** Whether the result compiles and its tests pass requires executing the product tree, which the trusted core never does. Buildability lives in the packet's `acceptance_checks`, executed by `verification` in verifier lanes (§5), whose receipts feed the `verified` predicate — not the accepted-head movement. A Change Set can therefore be accepted (head) while its claim stands at Asserted; \\\"integration eligibility requires Verified\\\" (RFC 0003) is where buildability bites, exactly once, exactly where the target predicate demands it.\\n\\n`packet-review` (review gate) applies per repository policy on packets flagged review-required; unchanged from RFC 0003.\\n\\n**Advisory lane evidence** — the build lane's own test runs, self-review notes, tool transcripts — is:\\n\\n- **recorded**: carried in the Change Set's advisory section (bulky bodies to blob storage per RFC 0009), attribution-marked as originating inside the producing lane;\\n- **never promoting**: it enters no gate predicate and no claim computation; its provenance ancestry (same lane as producer) structurally fails independence, so even receipt-shaped advisory output cannot back Verified;\\n- **legitimately consumed** as (a) scheduler telemetry — a lane that self-reports green tests raises the priority of scheduling real verification; one that self-reports red suggests routing to review first — and (b) declared diagnostic input to revision runs, alongside Review Ledgers.\\n\\nBuild never self-certifies; this section is the runtime enforcement of that sentence.\\n\\n## 4. Partial Admission\\n\\n### 4.1 The Partial-Admission Closure Rule (owned here; Epoch 1 open question 6)\\n\\nThe submission bundle (owned by RFC 0007) lists typed outputs, each carrying an **intra-run derivation map** entry: the set of sibling outputs (by within-run output id and lane attribution) it was derived from.\\n\\n\\u003e **Partial-Admission Closure Rule.** An output of a partial submission may be gate-evaluated and admitted iff every output in its declared intra-run derivation closure is present in this bundle or already admitted from a prior bundle of the same run. Outputs declaring no intra-run inputs are always individually admissible.\\n\\nThis is the one rule with two enforcement points: RFC 0007's bundle-integrity synthesis-closure check is its bundle-level projection; RFC 0009's admission funnel enforces it per-output. Consequences:\\n\\n- **Independent divergent drafts: admissible alone.** Each declares an empty intra-run input set. They enter as candidate versions (or recorded run exhaust, per the pass contract's output typing) regardless of sibling lanes' fate.\\n- **A synthesis without its inputs: not admissible.** A synthesis output declares its divergent inputs; if any is missing from the union of submitted-and-admitted outputs, the output is refused with the funnel's typed cause `synthesis_closure_broken` (RFC 0009's closed refusal vocabulary) — an admission refusal, not a gate refusal: the output is recorded but not gate-evaluated, because its provenance would be a lie. A synthesis whose inputs were never submitted has unverifiable ancestry, which also breaks independence accounting downstream, since anti-aliasing evaluates synthesis lineage.\\n- **The rule is pass-agnostic and applies identically to evidence**: receipts declare no intra-run inputs (individually admissible); a Verification Report declares its receipts (admissible only with its receipt closure).\\n\\nPer-output gating is sound because admissibility follows the derivation order — nothing admitted ever depends on something refused or missing, and nothing present is ever discarded.\\n\\n### 4.2 Residual runs\\n\\nWhen a bundle is partial (`failure.modes: partial`; closure outcome `submitted_partial` with a `residual` flag), the Driver plans a **residual run**: a new pass run of the same contract whose manifest pins (a) the identical packet/governing pins and (b) the admitted partial outputs as declared inputs. For a divergent-plus-synthesis topology missing lane 3: the residual run re-executes only lane 3 and the synthesis, consuming admitted drafts 1–2 by pin. For verification missing two checks: the residual run executes the two checks and assembles a report referencing the previously admitted receipts (evidence consumed by an analysis pass — W10-clean). Finished lanes' work is preserved as pinned input, not re-executed. Residual runs are ordinary runs — new `pass_run_opened`, same Open-Run Invariant keyed on the same subject; RFC 0006 dispatches them, RFC 0008 inherits their exclusion sets; the pins are defined here.\\n\\n## 5. The Verification Runtime\\n\\n### 5.1 Checks: identity, declaration, registry, evolution\\n\\nA **check** is one mechanical predicate execution: pinned argv, pinned binary, sealed environment. Its **check identity** is content-addressed:\\n\\n\\u003e `check_id = hash(canonical{argv[], binary_hash, env_spec, cwd_spec, input_spec, resource_limits, network: false})`\\n\\n**Declaration chain:**\\n\\n1. The Implementation Plan's **verification strategy** (L3, human-reviewed and accepted) states verification intent per packet boundary (\\\"unit tests green\\\", \\\"linter clean\\\", \\\"migration idempotent\\\").\\n2. `packetization` compiles each strategy item into concrete `acceptance_checks` on the packet: a list of check_ids that must exist in the repository's **check registry**. An unresolvable item is a typed packetization finding — against the plan (underspecified strategy) or against the registry (missing check) — never license to improvise a command.\\n3. Repository policy additionally declares the **integration check set**: whole-tree, link-time checks (full build, full test suite, repository lints) evaluated at integration (§7).\\n\\n**Authority.** Check *identities* pinned inside accepted packet and plan elements carry acceptance authority — what may run in a verifier lane for a packet is already gated by the acceptance of the artifacts that pin it. The check **registry** (`policy/checks/\\u003crepository\\u003e.yaml`) is a defense-in-depth allowlist maintained as policy commits, recorded via policy pins in receipts. Registry changes never retroactively authorize or deauthorize pinned checks: a check removed from the registry fails closed at the next verification with a deviation-visible refusal; it does not silently decay standing evidence. No new acceptance gate exists for the registry.\\n\\n**Registry entries:** `check_id`, `argv`, `binary_hash`, `env_spec` (explicit allowlist, no ambient environment), `resource_limits` (cpu, memory, wall clock), `network: false` (E1; a network-requiring check is E3 and forbidden without an RFC), `runtime_class` (advisory, scheduler-facing), optional `supersedes: \\u003cold check_id\\u003e` for telemetry lineage. The registry contents are versioned data under policy discipline; the *rules* — only registered checks mint receipts, every receipt pins the registry version — are compiler semantics fixed by this RFC.\\n\\n**Evolution rides the existing algebra.** Because `acceptance_checks` are part of the packet element, changing a check (new toolchain ⇒ new binary_hash ⇒ new check_id ⇒ packetization re-run updates packets) changes packet element hashes; Verified claims bound to the old element hash decay arithmetically; re-verification under the new checks restores them. No bespoke check-invalidation mechanism exists, and none is permitted.\\n\\n### 5.2 Verifier lanes\\n\\nA **verifier lane** (RFC 0001) is a lane whose agent runtime is a local deterministic tool runtime — no LLM — launched by a backend declaring the `verifier_sandbox` capability (declaration shape owned by RFC 0007). Its lifecycle per check execution:\\n\\n1. **Materialize** a fresh workspace purely from pins: composed base (from the manifest's `base_composition`) + Change Set diff = subject tree; hash-verify the materialized tree against the pinned result tree hash before executing anything. Materialization is always from content-addressed inputs, never from another lane's workspace.\\n2. **Execute** the registered argv under the sandbox profile: no network, explicit env, resource limits from the registry entry, fresh temp dirs. The **sandbox profile hash** (canonical hash of the confinement configuration — mount plan, uid strategy, limit set) is recorded in the receipt so profiles are comparable for independence.\\n3. **Mint** the receipt (§5.3) and dismantle the workspace.\\n\\nVerifier lanes are disposable by construction: nothing persists but the submitted receipt. A verifier lane that dies mid-check is an abandoned run like any other.\\n\\nThe `verification` pass run orchestrates one lane per check (or batched serially in one lane — adapter detail), then assembles the Verification Report. Determinism: D1 — replayable from receipts as transcript; the honest caveat is that check commands themselves can be flaky, which is surfaced (§5.6), never averaged away.\\n\\n### 5.3 Receipt minting and sealing\\n\\nReceipt fields (fixing `schema/receipt` concretely):\\n\\n```yaml\\nschema_version: 1\\ncheck_id:            # content-addressed identity (§5.1)\\nregistry_version:    # pin of the registry version resolved against\\nsubject:\\n  change_set_hash:\\n  base_composition_hash:   # composed base actually materialized\\n  result_tree_hash:        # hash-verified before execution\\nexecution:\\n  exit_code:\\n  stdout_digest:\\n  stderr_digest:\\n  output_digests: {}       # named auxiliary outputs (coverage, junit xml)\\n  started_at: / finished_at:\\nattribution:\\n  backend_id:\\n  lane_id:\\n  aliasing_class:\\n  sandbox_profile_hash:\\nseal:\\n  scheme: v1-hash          # versioned; future HMAC under a runtime key needs no schema change\\n  seal_digest:             # hash over canonical serialization of all fields above\\n```\\n\\n**Seal validation (validate-never-execute).** At admission the Compiler Core evaluates `receipt-checks` (check gate): recompute the canonical hash and compare to `seal_digest`; confirm `check_id` exists in the pinned `registry_version` and its argv/binary_hash match the registry entry byte-for-byte; confirm subject pins correspond to a submitted Change Set and that base + diff = result tree (pure patch arithmetic); confirm attribution consistency with the `lane_binding`. The core executes nothing.\\n\\nWhat the seal proves, honestly: within the v1 trust domain (§1), `v1-hash` proves internal consistency, registry conformance, and tamper-evidence against accident — not remote attestation that the execution occurred as described, and not integrity against a co-resident writer. That residual trust is rooted in the verifier adapter being deployment-local code plus the dual-signal rule below; the versioned `seal.scheme` field is the named hardening hook (per-runtime HMAC keys) requiring no schema migration.\\n\\n### 5.4 Verified: the Dual-Signal Rule\\n\\nD0005.C5 fixes the floor: minting evidence must share no provenance ancestry with the producing execution, evaluated over lane attribution and backend aliasing classes. The v1 `verified` target predicate strengthens this for mechanical evidence — a predicate-version fact, **not** an amendment to D0005 (predicates may require more than the claim floor, never less):\\n\\n\\u003e **Dual-Signal Rule (v1 `verified` predicate).** For every acceptance check of every packet, promotion to Verified requires two accepting receipts from two verification pass runs V1 and V2 such that: V1 ⊥ build, V2 ⊥ build (no shared lane, backend session, or synthesis lineage — the D0005 rule, evaluated per RFC 0007's independence semantics), and V2 is **execution-independent** of V1: disjoint lane instances, independent workspace materialization from pins, and distinct backend instance or, minimally, distinct sandbox profile hash. Memoized receipts (§10) may satisfy either signal only if their bindings match current closure; the two signals must be two distinct execution instances, never one receipt counted twice.\\n\\nRationale, compressed: for judgment evidence, independence defeats co-blindness (aliasing classes). For mechanical evidence the failure modes differ — flake, environment leakage, single-sandbox compromise — and the defense is fresh re-execution, not model diversity. On one workstation both signals share an OS; that is recorded honestly (identical `sandbox_profile_hash` fails the distinctness requirement, forcing at least two profiles), and the aliasing-class machinery stands ready when verifier backends diversify; whether the predicate should then bump to require distinct aliasing classes for verifier runtimes is a carried open item. Scheduling of the second signal is policy: it may run immediately, or be deferred and harvested from expiring capacity — the canonical capacity-harvest sink (RFC 0008). Until V2 lands, the claim stands at Asserted; nothing new in the lattice.\\n\\n### 5.5 Verified minting, end to end, as ledger events\\n\\n1. Driver plan record: `verified(N)` unmet for ChangeSet@v → plan verification.\\n2. `pass_run_opened` (V1) with sealed manifest: subject pins, acceptance check_ids, registry version pin, deadline_class.\\n3. `lane_binding` (scheduler, RFC 0008): verifier backend, aliasing class.\\n4. Backend executes checks in verifier lanes; submits bundle: receipts + Verification Report.\\n5. Admission: `receipt-checks` per receipt (individually admissible; empty intra-run inputs); `verification-report-checks` on the report — schema validity, receipt closure present (§4.1), and **binding closure completeness**: the report binds `change_set_hash`, `base_composition_hash`, packet element hash, plan element hash, governing design element hashes, decision clause hashes, and registry version. Incomplete closure is refused at promotion (D0005.C5) — the report admits but cannot participate in claim computation, and the gate result records the gap.\\n6. `gate_result` records appended (W7 shape); `pass_run_closed{submitted}`.\\n7. Same for V2 under the execution-independence constraints.\\n8. The claim cache (named derived store) recomputes: claim(ChangeSet@v) = Verified iff both reports' closures match current accepted heads/elements, all receipts accept, and the independence predicate holds over recorded attribution. The admitting event carries the implied claim transition (W8), so the mint is event-visible.\\n\\nNo record anywhere stores \\\"verified: true\\\". Deleting the claim cache and recomputing from graph + ledger yields the same answer (Derived-State Doctrine).\\n\\n### 5.6 Flake handling\\n\\nTwo admitted receipts with identical `check_id` and `result_tree_hash` but different exit codes are a contradiction the system must surface, not launder: the Driver appends a `check_flake` record pinning both receipts. Policy decides the response (re-execution count, quarantine of the check via registry supersession, escalation); semantics fixes only that a flake-flagged check's accepting receipt cannot silently satisfy the Dual-Signal Rule while the contradiction stands unresolved — the packet's Verified promotion blocks on flake resolution, which is a registry/policy act, event-visible.\\n\\n## 6. Verification and the Moving World\\n\\nExogenous change (D0002.C7) decays claims whose closure bound moved hashes — and §5's closure binds the composed base. Every 2am human commit that moves the observed product tree decays Verified on pending Change Sets whose base composition included the moved tree. This is sound (\\\"stale is not wrong; it is unproven\\\") and its economics are rescued the same way revalidation rescues IR churn:\\n\\n\\u003e **Re-verification is the revalidation of Change Sets.** The Change Set body does not rot (RFC 0003); only claims decay. To restore Verified against the new tree, the Driver plans a fresh verification run whose composed base uses the new observed tree. If the diff still applies cleanly and checks pass, new receipts bind the new base and Verified recomputes — no build re-run, no re-stamp machinery (evidence is additive; the re-stamp exception stays reserved for IR pin movement). If the diff no longer applies, the verification run submits a mechanical `apply_failed` receipt, and the Driver plans a rebase-style build revision (§7.3).\\n\\nThis single rule unifies upstream drift and sibling revision (§2.5): both are \\\"base moved\\\", both decay claims, both are serviced lazily when a target predicate demands freshness — never eagerly on every commit (marking eager, regeneration lazy, D0005.C3).\\n\\n## 7. Integration: the Linker\\n\\n### 7.1 Frontier, ordering, batching\\n\\n\\u003e **Integration frontier** ≡ the set of Change Sets that are Verified (per the current `verified` predicate version), integration-eligible per gates, and whose Work Graph ancestors are all already integrated.\\n\\nIntegration is incremental: an integration run consumes a batch drawn from the frontier (batch size and cadence are driver/scheduler policy; whole-graph linking is the degenerate single batch). Application order within a batch is deterministic: topological by Work Graph edges, tie-broken by the Work Graph's explicit application index (§2.5) — never by anchor lexicographics. Determinism here is load-bearing — the linker is D1 (replayable from its application records) and contains no judgment: **no smart merging, ever**; an LLM never touches conflict resolution inside `integration`.\\n\\n### 7.2 Mechanics: stage, verify, then E2 at admission\\n\\n1. **Stage (E1).** The integration lane materializes the current observed product tree T_obs (pinned from the latest Exogenous Change Record or prior integration), applies the batch in canonical order, and produces a **linked tree** as a staged object (git objects/staging ref — adapter detail; the linked tree hash is what crosses the seam).\\n2. **Link-time verification.** The repository's integration check set (§5.1) executes against the linked tree in verifier lanes, minting ordinary receipts. The integration run submits: linked tree hash, per-Change-Set `application_record`s, link receipts, and conflict records for any losers (§7.3).\\n3. **Admit, then effect (E2 as an admission act).** The Driver evaluates `integration-checks` (check gate: link receipts accepting, application arithmetic valid, T_obs pin still current). On pass, the Artifact Store — owner of durable truth and git anchoring — moves the target repository's product ref to the linked commit and records the Product Artifact versions as accepted. **No lane ever writes the product ref.** The pass contract remains E2 (D0004 unchanged); this design fixes *where* E2 is realized: at the single-writer admission boundary, by the store, under a gate-passing transition. The lane side of integration is E1 staging only.\\n4. **Compare-and-set against reality.** If a world-authored commit moved the live ref between staging and admission, the T_obs pin no longer matches: admission refuses with typed cause `tree_moved`; an `observation` run records the new tree; integration re-stages against it. Cheap, mechanical, and the only correct answer to a 2am human.\\n\\nThree policy facts govern the economics of this loop on an active human repository:\\n\\n- **The integration target ref is striatum-owned by default policy.** Integration moves a ref the compiler owns; humans merge it into their branches explicitly, and human-authored movement enters through `observation`. Integration never moves a ref a human has checked out.\\n- **Integration scheduling prefers telemetry-derived commit-quiet windows** (scheduler policy), so the stage→verify→CAS span races the world as rarely as possible.\\n- **Integration run closures carry a `cas_retry` count** (content of `pass_run_closed`), surfaced as a warning by the status projection — CAS churn is visible, never silent capacity burn.\\n\\n### 7.3 Conflict is a typed partial failure\\n\\nA Change Set whose diff fails to apply onto the batch-in-progress, or whose inclusion makes link-time checks fail while the remainder passes (bisected mechanically by deterministic re-staging without it), is a **loser**. The integration run does not fail wholesale: it completes as `partial` — the non-conflicting majority integrates; for each loser the run submits an `integration_conflict` record (§11). `scope_overlap` should be impossible (`work-graph-legality` guarantees disjoint parallel scopes) and is therefore also a finding against packetization when it occurs.\\n\\n**Resolution is a re-run of `build` on the loser, never a hand-merge** (RFC 0004). The rebase-style revision run's manifest pins: the unchanged packet element, the new composed base (post-integration tree), and the loser's prior Change Set version as declared diagnostic input — all artifacts, honoring \\\"the ledger is never a lowering input.\\\" The conflict record itself serves Driver planning and human legibility; the lane recomputes the mechanical conflict from the pinned artifacts (old diff vs new base), which is strictly more reliable than prose about it. The revision produces the next candidate Change Set version; admission, verification, and the next frontier proceed normally. Repeated conflict losses count against the packet's attempt budget (§9.1).\\n\\n### 7.4 The `integrated` predicate\\n\\n\\u003e **integrated(N)** ≡ every packet in N's accepted Work Graph has an `application_record` binding its Change Set hash into the product lineage, and the integrated commit is an ancestor of the currently observed product head.\\n\\nAncestry (a mechanical git query at evaluation time, or derivable from the Exogenous Change Record chain) makes the predicate stable under subsequent unrelated commits — the world moving *after* integration does not un-integrate N. One honest nuance: ancestry is not presence; a world-authored revert leaves the predicate satisfied while the effect is gone. That is correct by construction — the revert is an observed exogenous change that decays product-level claims and is fresh input for new intent; `integrated` records that compilation delivered, not that the world kept it.\\n\\n## 8. Speculation: Deferred, Not Foreclosed\\n\\n**v1 excludes speculative execution of independent subgraphs.**\\n\\nJustification, compressed: on a single workstation, capacity is the binding resource and the scheduler already owns a conversion path for expiring capacity with *certain* value — verification second signals, re-verification after drift, review postures — all producing durable evidence. Speculation's expected value is positive only when capacity would otherwise expire unused *and* upstream acceptance probability is high; estimating that probability requires dispatch/refusal telemetry that cannot exist before the runtime has history.\\n\\nNothing forecloses it, by construction:\\n\\n- `speculative_on` is a defined optional field of the run manifest from day one (schema present, always absent in v1), so activation needs no ledger `schema_version` churn;\\n- admission already parks candidates whose manifests carry unsatisfied `speculative_on` pins (inadmissible-yet, retained; retired with provenance if the pin dies) — vacuously exercised in v1;\\n- purity plus candidate-only outputs mean speculative results are ordinary candidates with extra pins; D0004.C8's legality (E0/E1 only, aborted speculation retires versions and keeps provenance) is honored verbatim.\\n\\nOne nearby behavior is *not* speculation and is legal immediately: verifying a submitted candidate Change Set before its review/acceptance gates conclude is ordinary evidence-gathering (E1, analysis), and policy may use it to pipeline verification behind admission.\\n\\n## 9. Failure Containment\\n\\n### 9.1 Attempt budgets and the poison-packet circuit breaker\\n\\nStriatum-0's D268 lesson: repeated automatic failure must stop consuming capacity. Driver planning may read provenance as data (D0002.C5) — this is that clause's canonical use:\\n\\n\\u003e Each packet carries an **attempt budget** (repository policy defaults; per failure mode): max gate refusals with revision (default 3), max abandonment re-dispatches (default 2), max integration-conflict losses (default 2), max total attempts (default 5). The Driver's planner counts `pass_run_closed` records per packet; on exhaustion it appends a `packet_quarantine` record and raises an escalation.\\n\\nThe escalation reason is `bounds_exhausted` (RFC 0001's closed vocabulary), carrying the closed `budget_kind` enum on the escalation record: `revision | redispatch | attempt_total | integration_conflict | withdrawal` (the last owned by RFC 0006's acceptance-queue semantics). A distinct escalation code was rejected to keep the vocabulary at eight; machine legibility — which budget tripped, without grep archaeology — is preserved by the enum field. Budgets gate *planning*, never gates or claims — a quarantined packet's existing candidates and evidence remain exactly as valid as they were (capacity pressure and its inverse never touch gates, D0002.C9).\\n\\n### 9.2 Quarantine one, finalize the majority\\n\\nQuarantine is a computed planning predicate — a `packet_quarantine` record without a matching `quarantine_release` — never artifact lifecycle state and never a stored flag on the packet. Consequences fall out of existing semantics with no new machinery:\\n\\n- **Siblings proceed.** ready(P) of independent packets never referenced the quarantined one; their builds, verifications, and integrations continue.\\n- **Dependents wait naturally.** Downstream packets are simply not-ready (missing dependency Change Set) — ordinary dependency semantics, not a second blocking mechanism.\\n- **Integration finalizes the majority.** The frontier excludes the quarantined cone; everything else links (§7.1).\\n- **Honest target state.** `verified(N)` and `integrated(N)` remain unmet; the status projection shows exactly which packet blocks, its budget history, and the open escalation — Principal attention goes to the one true blocker.\\n\\nRelease is the Principal's escalation resolution (appended resolution event + `quarantine_release` record), optionally with budget reset, packet retirement, or a packetization re-run reshaping the packet — the latter being upstream lowering work, as it should be: a packet that repeatedly poisons is usually a plan defect.\\n\\n### 9.3 Abandoned-run cleanup under crash-only\\n\\nComplete inventory of what abandonment leaves, and who cleans it:\\n\\n- **Ledger:** an open run → closed by deadline adjudication (`pass_run_closed{abandoned}`, provisional per §2.2) in the Driver loop or during `reconcile`. Nothing else exists above the seam.\\n- **Backend scratch (worktrees, temp dirs, terminals):** owned and garbage-collected by the adapter; adapters boot from zero, treat all local scratch as disposable, and re-derive obligations from the dispatch channel. `reconcile` never inspects backend internals — a second recovery verb hiding as \\\"cleanup\\\" is forbidden (D0002.C6).\\n- **Late arrivals:** §2.4 — admitted against provisional abandonment, evaluated if useful, retired as `redundant_candidate` otherwise. Never discarded unrecorded.\\n\\n## 10. Optimization Hooks (named, not built)\\n\\nAttachment points per D0004.C8 legality, all inert in v1:\\n\\n- **Fusion / fission / false-dependency pruning** attach as a parameterization of `packetization` re-runs requested by the Driver: consumes the accepted plan plus the prior Work Graph version as declared diagnostic input; produces a new Work Graph version `derived_from` the old, accompanied by a `graph_rewrite` record naming the rewrite class. Legality is enforced by extending `work-graph-legality` with an **identity-preservation predicate**: every *claimed* packet — one with an admitted Change Set or an open run — must appear element-hash-identical in the new version (so packet pins survive, §2.3); rewrites touch only unclaimed regions and must preserve plan-derivability. The predicate applies to **all** packetization re-runs, rewrite-parameterized or ordinary plan-driven regeneration alike. False-dependency pruning is statically decidable today (an edge between packets with disjoint write scopes and no output-to-input data flow is prunable — D0 analysis over declared scopes); fusion/fission heuristics await scheduler telemetry. The trigger is Driver planning reading provenance as data; the legality stays semantic.\\n- **Receipt memoization** keys on `(check_id, result_tree_hash)` — an admitted receipt is reusable evidence wherever those pins recur (e.g., re-verification after a base move that reproduces an identical result tree). **Input-slice memoization** — keying on a check's declared `input_spec` slice of the tree rather than the whole tree hash, so path-disjoint world commits do not invalidate memoized receipts — is the sanctioned deferred optimization of this family. Constraint restated from §5.4: memoized reuse never counts as the second execution instance of the Dual-Signal Rule.\\n- **Batch-maximizing conflict selection** in integration (choosing losers to maximize the integrated majority) may replace canonical-order loser selection later; it must remain deterministic given the ledger, or it becomes scheduler-flavored semantics.\\n\\n## 11. Record Types and Seam Interfaces\\n\\n### 11.1 Owned ledger record types\\n\\nAll record types below register in `catalog/ledger-record-types/`, carry RFC 0009's envelope (`schema_version`, upcast-on-read, refuse-newer-than-reader, sealed segments), and are appended by the Driver. Content fields, v1:\\n\\n**`redundant_candidate`** — a valid late or surplus output for an already-won subject, value counted, not discarded.\\n\\n```yaml\\npacket_pin: {work_graph_id, work_graph_version_hash, packet_anchor, packet_element_hash}\\nrun_ref:               # seq of the pass_run_opened whose submission was redundant\\noutput_pin: {kind, content_hash}\\nsuperseding_ref:       # admission ref of the already-admitted winner\\n```\\n\\n**`packet_quarantine`** — the poison-packet breaker tripping.\\n\\n```yaml\\npacket_pin: {...}\\nbudget_kind:           # closed: revision | redispatch | attempt_total | integration_conflict\\nbudget_snapshot: {}    # per-budget_kind counts vs policy bounds at exhaustion\\nescalation_ref:        # seq of the bounds_exhausted escalation raised\\n```\\n\\n**`quarantine_release`** — the Principal's resolution taking effect.\\n\\n```yaml\\npacket_pin: {...}\\nquarantine_ref:        # seq of the packet_quarantine being released\\nresolution_ref:        # seq of the resolution event\\ndisposition:           # closed: budget_reset | packet_retired | repacketize\\n```\\n\\n**`integration_conflict`** — one loser in one integration batch.\\n\\n```yaml\\nbatch_id:\\nlosing_change_set_pin: {identity, content_hash}\\npacket_pin: {...}\\nbase_pins: {t_obs_hash, applied_change_set_hashes: []}\\nconflict_class:        # closed: apply_failure | link_check_failure | scope_overlap\\nconflicting_paths: []\\nreceipt_refs: []\\n```\\n\\n**`application_record`** — one Change Set bound into product lineage.\\n\\n```yaml\\nbatch_id:\\nchange_set_hash:\\npacket_pin: {...}\\napplication_index:     # the Work Graph's explicit application index (§2.5)\\nlinked_tree_hash:\\nintegrated_commit:\\n```\\n\\n**`check_flake`** — contradicting receipts for one check identity on one subject tree.\\n\\n```yaml\\ncheck_id:\\nresult_tree_hash:\\nreceipt_refs: []       # the contradicting receipt pins\\nregistry_versions: []\\n```\\n\\n**`graph_rewrite`** — one optimization-parameterized Work Graph rewrite (inert v1).\\n\\n```yaml\\nold_graph_pin: {identity, version_hash}\\nnew_graph_pin: {identity, version_hash}\\nrewrite_class:         # closed per D0004.C8: fusion | fission | dependency_pruning\\nclaimed_packet_anchors: []   # packets covered by the identity-preservation predicate\\n```\\n\\n### 11.2 Content contributed to records owned elsewhere\\n\\n- **`pass_run_opened`** (owner RFC 0006): for `build`/`verification`/`integration` runs, this RFC fixes the manifest content (§2.1, §5.5), the subject pins, `deadline_class`, and `speculative_on` (defined, absent v1). The run id is this record's seq.\\n- **`pass_run_closed`** (owner RFC 0006): this RFC's semantics use outcomes `submitted | submitted_partial | submitted_late | abandoned | canceled | error | superseded_by_redispatch`, the `residual` flag, the deadline policy pin, and — on integration closures — the `cas_retry` count (§7.2).\\n- **`lane_binding`** (owner RFC 0008): consumed for attribution consistency (§3), independence evaluation (§5.4), and `attempt` accounting (§2.2).\\n- **`gate_result`** (W7 shape, RFC 0005): appended for `packet-checks`, `receipt-checks`, `verification-report-checks`, `integration-checks` — all Driver-evaluated, execution-free Core predicates defined by this RFC.\\n\\n### 11.3 Evidence artifacts\\n\\nMinted here (kinds existing per D0003.C2): **Receipt** (`schema/receipt`, §5.3) and **Verification Report** (`schema/verification-report`: subject pins, check outcomes, receipt refs, binding closure per §5.5) — stored by RFC 0009 with bulky bodies in blob storage.\\n\\n### 11.4 Consumed interfaces\\n\\n- **From RFC 0007:** the submission bundle — per output: kind, content hash, role-in-run, intra-run derivation map entry, lane attribution, partial flag with missing-output declaration; advisory evidence structurally separated from outputs; the `verifier_sandbox` capability declaration.\\n- **From RFC 0008:** deadline classes, backend aliasing classes, capacity state for second-signal harvest scheduling, quiet-window telemetry for integration cadence.\\n- **From RFC 0009:** the admission funnel (W1–W10 at write time, per-output closure enforcement, the closed refusal vocabulary including `synthesis_closure_broken`); element-anchor mechanics — this RFC requires that packet element hashes be computable over the canonical packet element serialization alone, with sibling references by anchor id (§2.3), and stands on the `anchor-continuity` check's retirement budget and `anchor_reminted` detection.\\n- **From RFC 0006:** the driver loop and control surface — **no new verbs**. Recovery remains `reconcile` alone; quarantine release is escalation resolution.\\n\\n## 12. Language Amendments (N8)\\n\\nAdmitted to the RFC 0001 glossary (Epoch 2 amendment), with layer assignment:\\n\\n- **Check Registry** (judgment layer) — the repository's content-addressed allowlist of check identities that may mint receipts; policy-maintained, defense-in-depth beneath the acceptance authority carried by pinned check identities (§5.1).\\n- **Attempt Budget** (agency layer) — the per-packet, per-failure-mode planning bound whose exhaustion trips quarantine (§9.1).\\n- **Residual Run** (transform layer) — a new pass run of the same contract pinning admitted partial outputs as declared inputs, completing a partial submission (§4.2).\\n- **Partial-Admission Closure Rule** (judgment layer) — the per-output admissibility rule over intra-run derivation closures (§4.1).\\n- **Dual-Signal Rule** (judgment layer) — the v1 `verified` predicate's requirement of two execution-independent verification runs, both independent of build (§5.4).\\n\\nDefined in this RFC and listed in the glossary **by reference only** (owning-RFC conventions, per the Epoch 2 amendment's admit/by-reference split): **Composed Base** (§2.5), **Integration Frontier** (§7.1), **Linked Tree** (§7.2), **Intra-Run Derivation Map** (§4.1), **Open-Run Invariant** (§2.2), plus the operational vocabulary **Check / Check Identity** (§5.1), **Integration Check Set / link-time check** (§5.1), **Verifier Sandbox Profile (hash)** (§5.2), **Execution Independence** (§5.4), and **Packet Quarantine** (computed planning predicate, §9.2).\\n\\nRecord-type names (`redundant_candidate`, `packet_quarantine`, `quarantine_release`, `integration_conflict`, `application_record`, `check_flake`, `graph_rewrite`) are registry entries, never glossary terms. \\\"Submission Bundle\\\" is used here but owned by RFC 0007. \\\"Verifier lane\\\" already exists in RFC 0001 and is not amended.\\n\\n## Decision (clauses)\\n\\n- **D0010.C1 — Trust model.** Execution is untrusted and parallel; admission is trusted and serial; the trusted core is execution-free — it computes hashes, schemas, patch arithmetic, and seal validation, never invoking product code or checks.\\n- **D0010.C2 — No leases.** At-most-one-active-dispatch is a Driver-loop economy invariant computed over ledger records (open run without closure; record-then-dispatch ordering — adopted system-wide). Correctness never depends on it: purity + isolated workspaces + single-writer admission make double execution safe; redundant results are recorded, never discarded.\\n- **D0010.C3 — Packet pins at element grain.** Change Sets pin the packet element hash; packet elements reference sibling anchors **by id only** (never sibling content), and composed-base application order is pinned by an explicit Work Graph index — Work Graph churn that leaves a packet untouched never invalidates in-flight builds. The identity-preservation predicate applies to all packetization re-runs.\\n- **D0010.C4 — Admission is execution-free.** `packet-checks` verify schema, packet-pin match, write-scope conformance, base coherence, attribution; buildability lives in verification; advisory lane evidence is recorded and structurally cannot promote (same-lane ancestry fails independence).\\n- **D0010.C5 — Composed bases and re-verification.** Dependents build against observed tree + admitted ancestor Change Sets; sibling revision and human commits decay claims via ordinary closure arithmetic; re-verification (fresh receipts against the new base) restores Verified without re-build or re-stamp; apply-failure routes to a rebase-style build revision with the prior Change Set as pinned diagnostic input.\\n- **D0010.C6 — The verification runtime.** A content-addressed check registry (policy-owned contents; acceptance authority flows from pinned check identities in accepted plans; registry is defense-in-depth — removed checks fail closed with visible deviation); LLM-free disposable verifier lanes materialize purely from pins; receipts carry a versioned seal scheme; the core validates seals, never executes. **Dual-signal Verified** — two execution-independent verification runs, both independent of build — is the v1 `verified` predicate. Check flakes surface as contradiction records that block promotion until resolved.\\n- **D0010.C7 — Partial-Admission Closure Rule.** An output is individually admissible iff its declared intra-run derivation closure is admitted (divergent drafts: yes; synthesis without inputs: refused). Pass-agnostic; residual runs pin admitted partial outputs.\\n- **D0010.C8 — Integration.** Deterministic topological linking of the Verified frontier; conflict is a typed partial outcome (finalize-the-majority at link level) with `integration_conflict` records and build re-runs for losers; **E2 is realized at admission** — lanes only stage; the Artifact Store moves the striatum-owned product ref under a gate-passing transition with `tree_moved` compare-and-set; `cas_retry` counts surface churn; integration prefers telemetry-derived quiet windows; humans merge explicitly, observation mediates.\\n- **D0010.C9 — Containment.** Attempt budgets (planner reads provenance as data) → `packet_quarantine` + escalation `bounds_exhausted (budget_kind: attempt_total)`; quarantine is a computed planning predicate; siblings and the frontier proceed. Speculation is deferred with live hooks (`speculative_on` defined, absent in v1).\\n- **D0010.C10 — Owned record types (7):** redundant_candidate, packet_quarantine, quarantine_release, integration_conflict, application_record, check_flake, graph_rewrite. Evidence minted here: Receipts and Verification Reports with binding closure.\\n- **D0010.C11 — Execution-independence of soundness (extends C1).** Execution is nondeterministic and untrusted; admission is deterministic, execution-free, and content-addressed; graph evolution — head movement and the invalidation algebra — is deterministic. Judgment (review verdicts, acceptance) is frozen into admitted evidence at the seam, so the graph's evaluation of it is deterministic even though its formation is not. Soundness is therefore a function of admitted content and its deterministic evaluation alone, never of execution behavior; execution behavior bounds liveness and must never touch soundness. The reduction is relative: it holds only to the completeness of the gates' checks and to the seal/trust boundary (a lane inside the trust domain forges content rather than corrupting the function — D0012). Self-evident of the model and silently decayable in the artifact, the property is held to the artifact by the standing execution-independence guard, not by this clause.\\n\\n## Consequences\\n\\nEngineering work executes without any liveness machinery; Verified means two independent mechanical signals against pinned bases; a poisoned packet stops consuming capacity while its siblings ship.\\n\\nSoundness is backend-agnostic: lanes are swappable, redundant, and adversarial-tolerant without ever changing what the graph admits or which target-state predicate it computes (C11).\\n\\n## Constrains\\n\\nThe verifier runtime, check registry policy, integration mechanics, partial-admission enforcement at the funnel, the deferred speculation design, and the standing execution-independence guard (adversarial-lane, metamorphic, and static execution-freeness fences) that holds C11 to the artifact.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers\\n\\nFull deliberation in the Epoch 2 record (RFC 0000 implementation): the lane design, synthesis rulings (R1, R2, R4, R6, R8, R11), and red-team reconciliation (adjudications 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 17) that repaired and bound this design. Carried open items live there too: deadline-class calibration, second-signal supply on one workstation, late-submission evaluation policy. Vocabulary: RFC 0001; no\\nlanguage amendments. Decisions in force: D0001–D0010. This RFC owns the\\nself-hosting boundary: the registration of the compiler's own repository as a\\ntarget repository, the bootstrap procedure, the entry predicate, and the\\nevolution discipline that binds every subsequent pass on this repository. It\\nadds no record types, no passes, no gates, and no scheduler semantics —\\nself-hosting is an act performed with the machinery of D0006–D0010, not a new\\nmachine.\\n\\n## The Bootstrap Claim\\n\\n**Self-hosting is registration, not privilege.** D0002.C8 already states that\\nthe compiler's repository is an ordinary target repository; RFC 0009's\\nself-hosting section already fixes its layout. This RFC cashes the claim: the\\nrepository gains a committed `.striatum/graph.json`, its Graph Store lives\\nunder `$XDG_DATA_HOME/striatum/graphs/\\u003crepo_id\\u003e/` like any other, its passes\\nrun on declared backends through the file seam, and its writes enter through\\nthe one admission funnel. Nothing in the compiler knows it is compiling\\nitself. The repository's only distinction remains constitutional: its graph\\nis the `core_graph` every other graph's `graph_genesis` names, and its\\ndecision records are the environment other graphs' pass runs pin (RFC 0009,\\nConstitutional Decisions).\\n\\n## The Bootstrap Procedure (v0)\\n\\nOne procedure, executed once, recorded forever:\\n\\n1. **Register.** `striatum init` on the compiler repository mints its\\n   `repo_id` (UUIDv7), binds it to the root commit in a `graph_genesis`\\n   record (`seq 0` of its ledger), writes the committed identity file, and\\n   registers the working tree in the workstation registry. Repository\\n   discipline: `.striatum/graph.json` is committed (identity only);\\n   `.striatum/scratch/` is gitignored and never state (P10).\\n2. **Request.** The Principal issues the first compilation request on the\\n   compiler's own graph: subject `striatum-next/self-hosting`, target\\n   `self-hosting-bootstrapped@1`, note carrying the command verbatim.\\n3. **Drive.** One drive session plans and executes through the v0 spine:\\n   `intent-capture` (D0, `local`) captures the command verbatim into an\\n   Intent Statement, admitted through funnel stages 0–6 and accepted through\\n   its check gate; `observation` (D0, `local`) records the repository at\\n   bootstrap as an Exogenous Change Record, admitted as evidence through the\\n   same door. The session ends `satisfied`, appending the\\n   `satisfaction_record` that closes the request.\\n\\nThe bootstrap is idempotent at the identity layer (`init` on a registered\\nrepository re-opens the existing graph) and at the predicate layer\\n(re-driving a satisfied request appends only a `drive_session_record`).\\n\\n## The Entry Predicate\\n\\n`catalog/target-states/self-hosting-bootstrapped.yaml`, machine-evaluated\\nunder the v0 conjunct vocabulary:\\n\\n- `accepted_head: intent-statement` — the Principal's self-hosting command,\\n  captured verbatim under this request (source-pass conjuncts demand a head\\n  produced under the requesting request), accepted through `capture-checks`.\\n- `evidence_admitted: exogenous-change-record` — the bootstrap observation,\\n  admitted as evidence. Loss of a key is not data loss: mint a fresh key; in-flight\\n  submissions sealed under the old key refuse and re-dispatch — ordinary\\n  abandonment economics, no recovery machinery.\\n- **Fail-closed verification.** At drain, a keyed manifest verifies under\\n  its backend's key; a plain manifest **refuses when a key exists** for\\n  that backend (`seal_invalid`) — a submission that should have been keyed\\n  and is not is indistinguishable from a forged one. Vocabulary: RFC 0001 plus the Language Amendments section below (N8). Binding context: D0006 (no daemon; wakes; the drive session and its lease), D0007 (C1–C4, C7 — the seam, deterministic dispatch identity, leases dissolved, ledger-illiteracy, fenced friction), D0008 (C7 — dispatch horizons, lapse-as-observation, re-dispatch), D0012 (C4 — isolation changes credentials, never contracts). Pinned inputs: `rfcs/0013-adapter-supervision/proposal`; the refused prior design text; review ledger 133.\\n\\n## Scope and Position {#el:scope-and-position}\\n\\nThis RFC decides the supervision architecture for **LLM execution backends**: the execution shape of the `dispatch` verb (synchronous v1 versus forked per-dispatch supervision), the obligation set of the detached supervisor, the fate binding between a supervisor and its runtime children, the ownership order for wall-clock limits, the discovery convention by which `abort` reaches detached work — including the readiness ordering that makes its kill handle usable from the first accepted instant — and the conformance rules that make the decided shape testable.\\n\\nIt does not own: the dispatch and submission bundle schemas, the rename-only commit point, admission V1–V10, the winner rule, or late-submission semantics (D0007; RFCs 0009/0010 — all fixed); binding rules and capacity arithmetic (RFC 0008); uid-isolation delivery (RFC 0012); the `local` backend's execution shape (verifier and deterministic lanes are out of scope); scheduling of human or remote runtimes.\\n\\nOne sentence of position: RFC 0007's accepted dispatch-verb text already names this shape — \\\"validate, create the workspace, fork the per-dispatch supervisor child, exit 0.\\\" The Epoch 3 Packet E3 bound (\\\"adapter execution is synchronous inside the dispatch verb; forked supervision arrives when lane concurrency matters\\\") was an implementation bound honestly recorded, not a decided architecture. This design therefore **realizes accepted text rather than amending it**; nothing in D0007 moves.\\n\\n## The Decision Structure {#el:decision-structure}\\n\\nOne primary decision and four subordinate questions that any detached supervisor must answer by name:\\n\\n1. **Shape** — affirm the v1 synchronous dispatch verb, or evolve to forked per-dispatch supervision.\\n2. **Relaunch supervision** — what owns the bounded internal-relaunch loop once the dispatch verb has exited, and explicitly: what supervises the supervisor.\\n3. **Runtime fate** — what happens to a still-running runtime child when its Lane Supervisor dies: does it die with the supervisor, remain abort-reachable, or survive as an orphan — and if any orphan state exists, whether it is bounded.\\n4. **Wall-clock ownership** — precedence among the three clocks that exist today (adapter invocation limit, manifest advisory `abort_after_s`, Driver dispatch horizon), and what a limit-kill leaves above the seam.\\n5. **Abort reachability** — how `dispatch_id` → running-work discovery works without reintroducing the liveness state D0007.C3 dissolved.\\n\\nQuestion 3 entered the structure at the ledger-97 revision, which closed that ledger's major finding — a SIGKILLed supervisor leaving a live runtime that no clock bounds and no abort reaches — by construction (the fate-sharing property below) rather than by declaring it acceptable. The ledger-116 revision moved the Supervisor Hint write into the dispatch verb, ordered before exit 0, so no accepted lane is hintless; priced hint deletion honestly instead of claiming abort's cleanup-only branch complete in all worlds; and tiered the fate-sharing reference mechanics for process trees. This revision answers ledger 133 against that text. Its major finding — the hint-before-exit ordering did not also order the creation of the kill domain the hint names, so an `abort` issued immediately after exit 0 could verify a hint whose process group was not yet a signalable target, reintroducing an accepted live lane that abort's verified-hint branch fails to stop — is closed two ways at once: the normative dispatch order is extended to **fork, kill-domain ready, hint, exit 0**, so the hint is never published before the domain it names exists and is signalable; and `abort` gains an explicit rule for the residual world — a verifying start token whose named kill domain cannot be signaled is a **failed abort over a live lane**, never complete cleanup. Its minor finding — S2, read literally, made the lawful runtime-only crash/relaunch path a conformance failure — is closed by splitting S2 into supervisor-death cases (no surviving lane-tree process, per S7) and runtime-only cases (the supervisor lawfully survives and relaunches within `internal_retry.max`).\\n\\nThe primary decision is: **forked per-dispatch supervision is adopted.** The trigger condition named in Packet E3 has arrived and is verifiable: three LLM adapters probe live on the workstation; the scheduler's slot arithmetic (`concurrency.max_lanes`, in-flight write-scope disjointness) computes against concurrency that synchronous dispatch can never exhibit; independence partitions exist to put lanes of different aliasing classes in flight *together*; and the horizon/lapse/winner-rule apparatus was built for lanes that outlive the session that dispatched them. Under the synchronous shape all of it idles, the drive lease is held for a lane's full wall-clock (inverting the architecture's posture — the Driver becomes a resident executor), lane lifetime couples to Driver lifetime (exactly the coupling the seam exists to prevent), and `abort` cannot stop work. The affirmation alternative is rejected with reasons below.\\n\\n## The Shape: Forked Per-Dispatch Supervision {#el:forked-supervision}\\n\\n### The dispatch verb lifecycle {#el:dispatch-verb-lifecycle}\\n\\nThe `dispatch` verb becomes, in order:\\n\\n1. **Validate** — declaration conformance, supported pass, effect class, runtime binary present, spool placement (A8), exactly as today; a failure is the same typed refusal from the closed set (`capacity_exhausted | runtime_unavailable | unsupported_pass | effect_class_unsupported | declaration_mismatch | spool_unsuitable`). The refusal set does not grow.\\n2. **Idempotence check** — if `spool/submissions/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/` exists, exit 0 (two states only, exactly as today). If a Supervisor Hint (below) for this `dispatch_id` exists and its start token verifies against a live process, exit 0 without forking a second supervisor — a non-authoritative optimization; if the hint is wrong the worst case is a duplicate execution, which pass purity and the atomic rename already make lawful.\\n3. **Create the workspace** (A2 pristine).\\n4. **Fork the Lane Supervisor, establish its kill domain, write the hint, exit 0 — in that order, normatively.** The verb forks the detached child process owning the rest of the dispatch lifecycle. The Supervisor Hint may not be written, and the verb may not exit 0, until the **kill domain** the hint will name — the supervisor's own process group, the single target of `abort`'s group signal, transitively containing or fate-binding the runtime tree per the confinement obligation below — **exists and is verified signalable on the verb's side**. The pid and start token are fixed at fork; the process group is fixed at kill-domain establishment (the parent's act or the child's, per the reference mechanics below, but always confirmed by the verb before the write); the verb then **writes (or overwrites) the Supervisor Hint** naming that domain, and only then **exits 0**. The hint is written exactly once per fork, by the verb, and the supervisor never writes or rewrites it. Acceptance is therefore never abort-visible without a *usable* kill handle already on disk: by the time the Driver can observe exit 0, the hint exists, verifies, and aims at a process group a signal can reach. The ledger-97 text allowed the supervisor to write the hint as its first act after fork; ledger 116 closed the fork-before-hint race by moving the write into the verb; ledger 133 identified the gap that ordering still left — a hint published between fork and the child's `setsid` verifies (the pid and start token are already real) while naming a process group that does not yet exist — and this text closes it by ordering kill-domain readiness before the write.\\n\\nAcceptance stays durable exactly as D0007 states it: after exit 0, either a submission eventually commits or the run is closed, with the closure lawfully suppliable from above (lapse → provisional abandonment); the backend owes no recovery. A dispatch verb killed *between* fork and exit 0 leaves the Driver seeing an error while a supervisor runs — and the window subdivides at the hint write. Killed **before the hint write** (including before kill-domain readiness), the supervisor is **hintless**: unreachable by `abort` (the absent-hint branch below degrades to cleanup) but not unbounded — its own dispatch budget kills it from below and the horizon adjudicates it from above. Killed **after the hint write**, the supervisor is fully reachable: its hint verifies and aims at a live domain, a same-id retry's verb finds that hint at its idempotence check and exits 0 without forking a second supervisor, and an `abort` lands normally. In either sub-window the Driver's ordinary response (note the failure; eventually re-dispatch as attempt+1 or retry the same `dispatch_id`) yields at most two attempts in flight — the winner rule already adjudicates that race, and a same-id retry's verb, finding no verifiable hint, forks a second supervisor and writes a hint naming *it* (S5's single-rename-winner covers the pair). These windows exist only for a dispatch whose acceptance never became visible — no obligation of acceptance had attached when the verb died.\\n\\n**Process mechanics are adapter-internal and non-normative — but the readiness property they must realize is normative.** The reference shape: the verb fork/execs the adapter's own binary at an adapter-internal supervision entry point (not a fifth verb; invisible above the seam and to conformance); the child establishes a new session and process group (`setsid`), detaches stdio into the workspace, sets up any runtime-containment scaffolding (per the fate-sharing property), and then **signals readiness to the verb over a synchronization channel** — a pipe written or closed after `setsid` is the reference; the verb confirms readiness (and MAY additionally verify against the process table that the child's process group now exists), writes the hint, and exits 0. A **parent-established process group** (`setpgid` from both sides, the standard race-closing idiom) is a lawful alternative where the adapter's detachment does not require a fresh session — noting the kernel's own exclusion: a process made group leader by its parent cannot later call `setsid`. Double-fork and similar shapes are lawful provided the handshake carries the **final** supervisor's identity (pid, pgid, start token) back to the verb before the hint is written — the hint must name the domain that actually contains the supervisor at the instant it is published. A child that dies before signaling readiness yields a verb error, not exit 0: nothing was accepted and no hint is written. Adapters MAY use other mechanics (cgroup placement, namespaces) provided the conformance rules below hold — including the fate-sharing property, which the chosen mechanics must realize, and S1's readiness assertion. The contract may not *require* an init system or any facility that constitutes a process registry readable above the seam.\\n\\nThe four-verb contract is unchanged. A1–A8 hold verbatim.\\n\\n### The Lane Supervisor's obligations {#el:lane-supervisor-obligations}\\n\\nThe Lane Supervisor owns, for exactly one dispatch:\\n\\n- **Runtime invocation** — the one-shot headless CLI, cwd-confined to the workspace, prompt rendered deterministically from the sealed bundle (`rendered_prompt_hash` pinned). Everything it needs rides the bundle; it reads no ledger, ever (A7 holds for the supervisor exactly as for the verbs).\\n- **Runtime confinement and fate-binding** — every runtime invocation runs inside the supervisor's session and process group, bound to the supervisor's life by the fate-sharing property below. The supervisor never starts a process it cannot kill with one group signal, and never starts one that outlives it.\\n- **The bounded internal-relaunch loop** — the strategy-then-exit and output-shape countermeasures of RFC 0007's friction table, with pristine workspace reset before each relaunch (A2), bounded by the declaration's `internal_retry.max`, recorded in attribution as `internal_relaunches`. This loop moves out of the verb and into the supervisor unmodified; it is the direct answer to \\\"what supervises internal relaunches.\\\"\\n- **Pre-submission validation** — expected-output presence and the mechanical shape predicates, feeding the repair relaunch.\\n- **The commit** — assembly in `spool/incoming/\\u003cnonce\\u003e/`, fsync, `rename(2)` into `spool/submissions/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/` (A4; sole commit point), sealed under the backend's Runtime Seal Key (D0012.C2).\\n- **The post-commit wake** — invoke the Driver (`striatum drive`, trigger `adapter_wake`) after rename; retry boundedly on exit 4; abandon safely (the standing timer and the drive loop's post-quiescence spool re-scan remain the liveness floor). No wake is load-bearing.\\n- **Wall-clock enforcement as mechanics** — per the ownership order below.\\n- **Self-termination and residue cleanup** — reclaim its workspace and its advisory residue (the hint included) after commit; exit.\\n- **Optionally, the Advisory Pulse** — the supervisor is the natural writer of `advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/pulse.json`; the convention is unchanged and remains forbidden to gates, admission, and claims. The pulse, not the hint, is the supervisor's advisory surface: the hint belongs to the verb.\\n\\nSupervisor writes stay confined to workspace + `spool/incoming/` + `advisory/` (A5); attribution (`started_at`, `ended_at`, nonce, relaunches, usage hints) spans the whole supervision, as today. Vendor capacity signals observed mid-run (`exhausted`, `throttled`) can no longer surface as dispatch refusals — they surface in the committed submission's diagnostics and usage hints and fold into `capacity_observation` at drain; the refusal path remains for what verb-time validation can see.\\n\\n### The runtime shares the supervisor's fate {#el:runtime-fate-sharing}\\n\\nThe direct answer to the runtime-fate question, and the closure of ledger 97's major finding. Stated as a normative property, with mechanics deliberately non-normative:\\n\\n**No runtime process may outlive its Lane Supervisor beyond kernel teardown.** When the supervisor dies — cleanly, by limit, by `abort`, or by SIGKILL at any instant — every runtime process it started dies with it, promptly (a mechanics grace measured in seconds, never horizon-scale), grandchildren and helpers included: the property is a property of the runtime's **process tree**, not of its first process. The state ledger 97 named — dead supervisor, live runtime, no clock enforcing, no abort reaching — is thereby excluded by construction, not tolerated as an operational cost.\\n\\n**Reference mechanics (Linux, adapter-internal, non-normative), tiered** — because the property is a tree property and the simplest mechanic is not (ledger 116, minor finding):\\n\\n- **Parent-death signaling** — the runtime child sets a kernel-delivered parent-death signal (`prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL)`) before exec, re-checking its parent pid after setting to close the fork/death race. This covers exactly the one process the supervisor forked: parent-death signaling **does not propagate** to grandchildren or helper processes the runtime starts. Alone, it realizes the property only when the runtime invocation is genuinely single-process.\\n- **Tree-capable containment** — required whenever the runtime may spawn descendants, which for real vendor CLIs must be assumed. The reference composition: the supervisor forks the runtime's direct ancestor as init (pid 1) of a **private PID namespace** — the runtime itself or a minimal exec shim — with parent-death signaling set on that init. Supervisor death kills the namespace init; the kernel then tears down every process in the namespace, descendants included, with no surviving actor required. Cgroup-scoped kill (`cgroup.kill`) is a lawful alternative on paths where an actor exists at teardown time (orderly supervisor exit, `abort`'s group kill); it is not by itself sufficient for SIGKILL-at-any-instant, which needs a kernel-mediated path that fires when nothing is left alive to act.\\n- **A group-owning wrapper that forwards termination** is lawful plumbing for orderly teardown, but cannot carry the property alone: a wrapper SIGKILLed together with its supervisor forwards nothing.\\n\\nWhatever mechanics an adapter chooses, S7 below is the arbiter — and its harness fake runtime spawns descendants, so single-process-only mechanics do not pass it by accident.\\n\\n**Fate-sharing is not supervision.** No process watches another; no watchdog polls; nothing relaunches anything. The kernel delivers teardown as part of ordinary process death, which is crash-equivalent and requires no resident machinery, no registry, and no reader above the seam. It is a property of how the runtime is *started*, not a service that runs alongside it. D0007.C3 is untouched.\\n\\n**The residual, bounded and named.** Kernel fate-binding covers the tree the supervisor confines; a runtime CLI that itself daemonizes — double-forks out of the supervisor's session, process group, namespace, or cgroup scope — can escape it. This design bounds that residual three ways rather than pretending it away:\\n\\n- **Runtime-shape obligation.** Adapters must invoke runtimes as one-shot, headless, non-daemonizing CLIs (already the invocation shape in this design). A runtime that detaches from the supervisor's confinement is an adapter conformance defect against S7 — a defect in the adapter's choice or configuration of runtime, caught by the suite, not a lawful mode.\\n- **Never a semantic hazard.** An escaped process cannot break the seam.
