It holds no path to an admissible commit — assembly, sealing, and the rename are the supervisor's acts, and even a hostile write into the spool faces admission V1–V10 and the winner rule. Committed-or-nothing holds above the seam in every case; escape is a **resource-consumption** problem only (vendor spend, host load), never a correctness problem.\\n- **Naturally bounded.** A conforming one-shot CLI terminates on its own when its work or its vendor connection ends; its workspace is janitor fodder either way. What escape costs is bounded operational waste inside one invocation's natural lifetime — not an unbounded orphan population.\\n\\nWith fate-sharing in place, the claims ledger 97 found soft become exact — within stated bounds: a dead supervisor *implies* a dead runtime tree, so `abort`'s cleanup-only path over a **stale hint** is complete rather than degraded (the absent-hint case is priced separately in Abort Reachability below), and the wall-clock enforcement gap closes because the lane whose clocks lost their enforcer no longer exists (Wall-Clock Ownership below).\\n\\n### Nothing supervises the supervisor {#el:nothing-supervises-the-supervisor}\\n\\nStated explicitly, because this is where Striatum-0 drowned: **nothing supervises the Lane Supervisor.** No watchdog, relauncher, pidfile poller, or resident recovery machinery may exist **as contract, as a recovery authority for the Lane Supervisor, or as anything readable above the seam**. A dead supervisor is a lapsed dispatch — indistinguishable from a slow one, by design — recovered entirely above the seam by the existing chain: dispatch horizon elapses → `dispatch_lapse` (observation, not adjudication) → provisional abandonment (`pass_run_closed{abandoned}`, reopenable) → closure-then-new-run re-dispatch at attempt+1 → the winner rule if the \\\"dead\\\" supervisor was merely slow. Every rung of a watchdog chain re-poses the question it answers; the horizon sweep answers it once, at the cost of one lapse window, with machinery that already exists and is already tested.\\n\\nTwo clarifications that keep this prohibition exactly as wide as it needs to be and no wider:\\n\\n- Adapter-internal process mechanics — double-fork, cgroup placement, kernel parent-death signaling, PID-namespace confinement, even an init facility used as a launch convenience — remain lawful provided they neither relaunch nor recover a dead supervisor, create no registry readable above the seam, and leave every S-rule passing. The prohibition targets recovery *authority*, not launch *plumbing*.\\n- Fate-sharing (above) is not a rung on this ladder: nothing in it watches, relaunches, or recovers. Kernel teardown of a process tree is the opposite of recovery machinery — it makes death *complete* rather than making it *reversible*.\\n\\nKill -9 at any instant remains a legal conformance test. The instants and their outcomes:\\n\\n| Killed at | Above the seam |\\n|---|---|\\n| verb, before fork | dispatch error at the Driver; re-dispatch; nothing ran |\\n| verb, between fork and hint write (including before kill-domain readiness) | possible duplicate attempt; winner rule adjudicates; the orphan supervisor is hintless — unreachable by `abort`, still bounded by its dispatch budget and the horizon |\\n| verb, between hint write and exit 0 | dispatch error at the Driver while a live, hinted, abort-reachable supervisor runs; a same-id retry exits 0 off the verifying hint without a second fork; the winner rule covers a racing attempt+1 |\\n| supervisor, before/during runtime | nothing; the runtime tree dies with it (fate-sharing); lapse → re-dispatch; workspace and hint are janitor fodder |\\n| runtime only (supervisor survives) | nothing yet; the supervisor observes `runtime_crash` and the relaunch loop proceeds within its bounds — the lawful runtime-only branch S2(b) pins |\\n| mid-validation / mid-relaunch | nothing; lapse → re-dispatch; same |\\n| mid-assembly in `spool/incoming/` | nothing; incoming temp is janitor fodder |\\n| between rename and wake | **submission committed**; wake lost; standing timer drains it |\\n| after wake | submission committed and drained; residue reclaimed |\\n\\nTwo states, no third, at every row — and no row leaves a process behind that anything above or below the seam must remember.\\n\\n## Wall-Clock Ownership {#el:wall-clock-ownership}\\n\\nThree clocks exist today with no stated precedence. The ownership order, decided:\\n\\n1. **The invocation limit** (adapter configuration, `adapter:` block; today `WallClockLimit`, default 30m) bounds **one runtime invocation**. The supervisor enforces it; expiry kills the invocation and feeds the relaunch loop as a `runtime_crash` diagnostic, exactly as the v1 code does. Mechanics only.\\n2. **The dispatch budget** — the manifest's advisory `abort_after_s` when present, else an adapter-block default — bounds **the whole supervision** (all invocations plus validation). The supervisor enforces it as mechanics and clamps invocation limits so attempts fit inside it. On expiry the supervisor kills the runtime and **commits a `failed` submission** carrying diagnostics (the existing `runtime_crash` class; the transcript exhaust names the limit — no vocabulary change), whatever usage hints it observed, and full attribution. This is best-effort, never owed: a supervisor killed before it can commit leaves nothing, and that is equally lawful. Failed-with-diagnostics is preferred over silence because it closes the run at the next drain instead of waiting out the horizon, and it feeds the capacity estimator facts instead of a lapse fold.\\n3. **The Driver's dispatch horizon** is affirmed as **the only wall-clock with semantics above the seam** — and its semantics are deliberately weak: it times an observation (`dispatch_lapse`) and a provisional adjudication, never a death certificate. It needs nothing from the supervisor's clocks; they exist so lanes normally conclude well inside it.\\n\\n**Enforcer death closes the gap it opens.** The version refused at ledger 97 left unstated what bounds a runtime whose clock-enforcer has died. Fate-sharing answers it: a dead supervisor implies a dead runtime tree, so no clock ever needs an enforcer for a lane that no longer exists. The only wall-clock that survives a supervisor's death is the Driver's horizon — which is exactly the ownership order above, now holding under process death and not merely under orderly operation. The sole residual (a non-conforming runtime that escaped confinement) is an S7 defect bounded as described in the fate-sharing section, and even it faces the horizon's above-seam adjudication like every other lane.\\n\\nThe advisory block stays advisory in the D0007 sense: no supervisor clock is ever a semantic deadline, no lease exists to expire, and \\\"wall-clock is not a pool\\\" (D0008) is untouched. Enforcement precedence as mechanics: invocation limit ≤ dispatch budget; the horizon sits above both and belongs to the Driver. The dispatch budget is also what bounds every lane `abort` cannot stop — the hintless orphan supervisor, the live lane whose hint was deleted, and the defective world of a verifying hint whose kill domain cannot be signaled: each concludes by commit or budget-kill without any actor needing to find it.\\n\\n## Abort Reachability {#el:abort-reachability}\\n\\nThe verb's semantics are fixed and unchanged: advisory, idempotent, safe against unknown ids, never touches a committed submission. What changes is that it can now actually stop work — and this revision states exactly how far that reach extends, when it begins (from the first accepted instant — ledger 133, major finding), and what its one genuine failure mode reports. The discovery convention:\\n\\n- **The dispatch verb writes the Supervisor Hint — after fork, after kill-domain readiness, before exit 0**: `advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/supervisor.json` — `{ pid, pgid, start_token, written_at }`, where `start_token` binds the supervisor pid to a specific process incarnation (boot id plus the kernel's process start time, or equivalent), making pid reuse detectable, and `pgid` names a process group that **already exists and is verified signalable at the moment of the write** (the readiness ordering in the lifecycle above). The pid and token are fixed at fork, the pgid at kill-domain establishment — the supervisor's incarnation, not the runtime's, is the anchor across the relaunch loop — so the hint is written once per fork and never rewritten by the supervisor. The normative ordering (fork, kill-domain ready, hint, exit 0) means no *accepted* lane is ever hintless **or hinted-but-unkillable** by construction: any abort issued against an acceptance the Driver has actually observed — including one issued at the earliest instant after exit 0 — finds a hint on disk that verifies and aims at a signalable group, unless something has since removed it. The ledger-97 text's alternative — the supervisor writing the hint as its first act — was withdrawn at ledger 116 for the fork-before-hint race; ledger 133 showed the verb-side write alone still left a hint-before-kill-domain race, withdrawn here the same way.\\n- `abort \\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e` reads the adapter's **own** advisory file, verifies the start token against the live process table, and if it verifies: signals the process group (SIGTERM, bounded grace, SIGKILL), then reclaims the workspace and advisory directory. Because the supervisor confines every runtime to its own session and process group (fate-binding obligation), the group signal reaches supervisor and runtime alike — abort kills the work, not just its steward.\\n- **A verifying token whose named kill domain cannot be signaled is a failed abort over a live lane — never cleanup.** If the start token verifies but the group signal cannot be delivered (the pgid names no existing process group, or the supervisor demonstrably survives the TERM–grace–KILL escalation while its token still verifies), `abort` reclaims nothing: deleting the workspace or the hint on this branch would destroy a live lane's only kill handle on the strength of a failed signal and misreport abort's one genuine failure mode as success. The verb reports the abort as incomplete, leaves all residue in place, and stays idempotent — a later retry may find the token stale (the supervisor has since concluded or died; cleanup then completes by fate-sharing) or may succeed outright. Under the normative ordering a conforming adapter cannot produce this state — a hint that verifies but aims at nothing is an S1 defect — but abort's behavior in it is defined anyway, because abort must stay honest against defect and hostility alike. The lane stays bounded below by its dispatch budget and above by the horizon, like every lane abort cannot stop.\\n- **A present-but-unverifiable hint yields cleanup that is complete.** A hint whose start token no longer verifies names a supervisor that died (or a reused pid, which the token exists to detect); by fate-sharing its runtime tree died with it. On this branch cleanup-only is the *whole* job — there is no live-runtime state hiding behind a stale hint. The one racy instant — abort arriving while kernel teardown of a just-killed tree is still in flight — has abort's cleanup racing a dying process, which is crash-equivalent and lawful (the same argument that lets the janitor delete a workspace under a live runtime).\\n- **An absent hint yields cleanup that is honestly partial.** Three worlds produce an absent hint, and `abort` cannot distinguish them: the dispatch was never accepted (no fork happened, or the verb died before the hint write); the lane already concluded and its residue was reclaimed; or the hint was deleted out from under a live lane — which the advisory subtree's deletable-at-will posture expressly permits and S6 exercises. In the first two worlds cleanup-only is complete; in the third, **live detached work continues unreached**. This design names that state instead of claiming it away: `abort` is advisory and best-effort by its fixed semantics, nothing above the seam depends on abort succeeding, and the unreached lane remains bounded twice over — below the seam by its own dispatch budget (the supervisor kills the runtime and best-effort commits `failed`), above it by the dispatch horizon, provisional abandonment, and the winner rule if it commits late. Deleting a hint costs `abort` its reach over that one lane's remaining budget window; it never costs correctness. Committed submissions are never touched on any branch.\\n- The hint is an **Advisory Signal** in RFC 0007's exact sense: non-authoritative, non-semantic, deletable at will, janitor-reclaimable with the rest of `advisory/`, and unreadable by the core — the `striatum` binary never opens it; the Driver's whole interface remains `abort \\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e` on the adapter surface. Deleting every hint on the box changes no semantic outcome anywhere — no binding, admission verdict, claim, or closure moves — but it is not free, and this design prices it: every still-running lane's `abort` degrades from kill to residue cleanup, an operational cost in vendor spend and host load, bounded by each lane's dispatch budget and the horizon. The ledger-97 phrasing (\\\"only degrades abort to residue cleanup, which the horizon and janitor already cover\\\") understated the live-lane world and is replaced by this pricing.\\n- The hint is **not a process registry**, and the distinction is structural, not rhetorical: nothing enumerates hints to answer \\\"what is running.\\\" In-flight accounting stays ledger-derived (`lane_binding` versus submission/closure records) — the scheduler, the status projection, and the janitor's live set never consult a hint. A hint answers exactly one question — \\\"if you must kill dispatch X, where do you aim\\\" — for a caller who already holds the `dispatch_id` from the ledger fold. D0007.C3 stands.\\n- The janitor stays file-only. It never signals processes; killing is `abort`'s job, and the Driver's abort-before-janitor ordering (as in the winner rule's \\\"issue abort for the superseding attempt\\\") is operational courtesy, not a correctness requirement — a janitor deleting the workspace under a live runtime is crash-equivalent and lawful.\\n\\n## Concurrency Above the Seam {#el:concurrency-above-the-seam}\\n\\nWith dispatch returning promptly, `concurrency.max_lanes` becomes load-bearing where it was always supposed to bind: **in the scheduler's hard-constraint filter**, computed against ledger-derived in-flight (bindings without submission or closure), per RFC 0008. Adapters do **not** enforce concurrency: an A7-clean adapter has no lawful way to count its running lanes without growing exactly the liveness surface this contract forbids (counting live hints *is* a process registry in a costume). Over-dispatch beyond declared lanes is therefore a scheduler bug with promptness costs, never a correctness hazard — every lane still commits or lapses independently. The dispatch refusal vocabulary does not grow a concurrency code.\\n\\n## Wake and Quiescence {#el:wake-and-quiescence}\\n\\nUnder the synchronous shape the wake convention was structurally unexercised — the Driver was already in session when the submission committed. Forked supervision is what makes it real, unchanged: the supervisor fires the wake after rename; exit 4 (drive lease busy) gets a bounded retry with backoff; giving up is safe because the standing timer is the documented liveness floor and the drive loop's post-quiescence spool re-scan closes the wake-drop race (RFC 0006). Drive sessions now dispatch their frontier and reach quiescence `awaiting_submissions` in seconds; the lease is held for verbs, not executions; the status projection's honest vocabulary — \\\"dispatched, awaiting submission, age 34m of 60m horizon\\\" — describes reality again.\\n\\n## Conformance {#el:conformance}\\n\\nThe A1–A8 suite is untouched (it is D0007's). This RFC owns seven supervision rules, testable per adapter against fake CLI harnesses under `tools/`:\\n\\n- **S1 — Detachment, kill-domain readiness, and hint ordering.** The dispatch verb exits 0 without awaiting runtime completion (testable with a fake CLI that blocks until externally released); at the instant of exit 0 the Supervisor Hint for the dispatch is already on disk, verifies against the forked supervisor, **and names a signalable kill domain** — the harness asserts readiness at the tightest race by issuing `abort` immediately after dispatch returns and requiring the group kill to land (supervisor and runtime tree dead within the S7 grace); in the un-aborted variant the submission later commits with no dispatch verb alive.\\n- **S2 — Kill-at-any-instant, two states — split by who dies.** **(a) Supervisor-death cases:** SIGKILL of the supervisor — alone or together with the runtime — at every lifecycle point in the table above leaves committed-or-nothing and **no surviving process from the lane's tree** (per S7); all residue is janitor-reclaimable. **(b) Runtime-only cases:** SIGKILL of runtime processes while the supervisor survives leaves committed-or-nothing above the seam while the supervisor lawfully continues — it observes `runtime_crash` and relaunches within `internal_retry.max`; no assertion in this rule requires lane-tree extinction while the supervisor lives, and the relaunch path passing is the *expected* outcome, not a defect.\\n- **S3 — Limit-kill.** An exceeded dispatch budget yields a `failed` submission carrying diagnostics and attribution; a supervisor killed before that commit yields nothing; both legal, tested separately.\\n- **S4 — Abort.** Four branches, tested separately. **(a) Live, verifiable hint with signalable domain:** the supervisor's process group — runtime included — dies and residue is reclaimed; tested both mid-flight and at the earliest instant the Driver can act (immediately after dispatch's exit 0). **(b) Present but unverifiable hint** (supervisor SIGKILLed first): cleanup only, and the test asserts this branch is complete — no process from the lane's tree survives it (fate-sharing makes dead-supervisor imply dead-runtime). **(c) Absent hint over a live lane** (the harness deletes the hint mid-flight): cleanup only; the lane is *not* killed and runs to a lawful conclusion (commit, budget-kill, or lapse), and the test asserts exactly that — the degradation is the specified behavior, not a defect, and no completeness claim attaches to this branch. **(d) Verifying token, unsignalable kill domain** (the harness synthesizes a hint whose start token verifies against a live stooge process but whose pgid names no signalable group): `abort` reports failure, reclaims nothing, deletes nothing, and remains idempotent — the test asserts no cleanup occurs and no completeness is claimed; adapter-produced instances of this state are S1 defects. On every branch: idempotent, unknown-id-safe, committed submissions untouched.\\n- **S5 — Duplicate dispatch.** Dispatch of an already-committed `dispatch_id` exits 0 without forking; dispatch of a `dispatch_id` whose hint verifies against a live supervisor (the verb-died-after-hint world) exits 0 without forking; two racing supervisors for one `dispatch_id` (including the hintless-orphan case from a verb killed between fork and hint write) resolve to a single rename winner with the loser's residue reclaimable; the hint, when present, names the most recently forked supervisor.\\n- **S6 — Hint non-semantics.** Deleting `advisory/` contents mid-flight changes no above-seam **semantic** outcome — bindings, admission verdicts, claims, and closures are identical with and without the deletion — and nothing above the seam reads a hint (import-graph conformance extends over the hint reader exactly as A7's does). The acknowledged non-semantic effect of deletion is S4(c): abort over the deleted hint degrades to residue cleanup. The test asserts semantic invariance, not operational equivalence.\\n- **S7 — Fate-sharing.** SIGKILL of the Lane Supervisor mid-invocation leaves the runtime **process tree** dead within the harness grace (seconds, never horizon-scale) — and the harness fake CLI spawns at least one descendant of its own and is held open, so mechanics that cover only the direct child (bare parent-death signaling) fail this rule; tree-wide conformance requires tree-capable containment whenever runtimes may spawn descendants. A subsequent `abort` on the same `dispatch_id` is cleanup-only and idempotent. A runtime observed to detach from the supervisor's session/process group (or namespace/cgroup scope) fails this rule — daemonizing runtimes are non-conforming by construction.\\n\\n## Interaction with the Trust Ladder {#el:trust-ladder-interaction}\\n\\nDetachment changes process ancestry, not credentials — D0012.C4's shape is preserved by construction. When rung 2 (per-lane uid isolation) is enforced: the dispatch verb forks the supervisor under the backend's lane uid and writes the hint into the per-backend-owned advisory subtree; the Runtime Seal Key stays readable to exactly that uid; and `abort`'s kill runs on the adapter surface under the same credentials, so no cross-uid signaling privilege is ever needed — the readiness handshake, a pipe between parent and child, is likewise credential-indifferent. Fate-sharing survives rung 2 unchanged: supervisor and runtime share the lane uid, so kernel parent-death delivery is unaffected (the one caveat — parent-death signals are cleared across setuid exec — cannot arise, because the runtime is never a privilege-changing binary under this ladder), and the namespace/cgroup variants land as the same credential-scoped mechanics. Nothing in this design forecloses rung 2, and nothing in it delivers rung 2.\\n\\n## Alternatives Considered and Rejected {#el:alternatives}\\n\\n- **Affirm the synchronous v1 shape** (re-scope `concurrency` declarations to 1, record `abort`'s kill half as vacuous, define a new evolution trigger). Rejected: the trigger recorded at Packet E3 has demonstrably arrived; affirmation would convert the scheduler's slot arithmetic, the independence partitions, and the horizon/winner apparatus into permanently dead weight, and would keep the Driver a resident executor holding the drive lease for lane wall-clocks — the inverted posture the no-daemon architecture exists to prevent.\\n- **Async execution inside the Driver process** (goroutines or threads instead of a fork). Rejected: lane lifetime stays coupled to Driver lifetime — the session either holds the lease until its lanes finish or exits and kills them; both horns lose. The Driver is an invoked program (D0006); it cannot be the container for hours of vendor wall-clock.\\n- **A resident per-backend supervisor daemon / workstation lane manager.** Rejected: reintroduces a process whose uptime is a truth condition, plus version skew, sockets, and a registry of running lanes — precisely the supervision layer whose deletion is this architecture's founding move (D0006's daemon rejection; D0007.C3).\\n- **Supervising the supervisor** (watchdog chains, relauncher processes, per-dispatch systemd transient units as contract). Rejected: each rung re-poses the recovery question; the horizon sweep already answers it at the cost of one lapse. Systemd-as-contract additionally couples conformance to an init system and constitutes a core-readable process registry. Adapters may use such facilities internally as launch plumbing only — never as recovery authority for a dead supervisor — where the S-rules still pass and nothing above the seam can read them.\\n- **Declaring orphaned runtime survival lawful and unbounded** (ledger 97's second horn: supervisor dies, runtime lives on until it happens to finish, abort cannot reach it). Rejected as the primary shape: it leaves vendor spend and host load unbounded by anything but luck, makes `abort`'s cleanup-only branch silently incomplete, and turns S2's \\\"committed-or-nothing\\\" into \\\"committed-or-nothing-plus-a-ghost.\\\" Fate-sharing buys the closed state for the cost of launch plumbing. The bounded form is retained only as the S7-defect residual for runtimes that break their non-daemonizing obligation — named, resource-only, and never semantic.\\n- **The supervisor writes its own hint as its first act after fork.** Rejected (this was the ledger-97 text): it leaves a fork-before-hint race inside the accepted window — a live, accepted, hintless lane that `abort` cannot reach while every claim says it can. The verb-side write before exit 0 closes that race; ledger 133 extended the same reasoning to the kill domain (next entry).\\n- **Publishing the hint at fork, before the kill domain exists** (the ledger-116 text's residual ordering: fork, hint, exit 0, with `setsid` left to the child on its own schedule). Rejected (this was ledger 133's major finding): between fork and the child's `setsid`, a hint naming the supervisor's eventual process group *verifies* — the pid and start token are already real — while `kill(-pgid, …)` has no target, so an abort issued in the accepted window can fail to stop work or, worse, reclaim advisory residue while the supervisor runs on. The readiness ordering (fork, kill-domain ready, hint, exit 0) closes the race for the price of one synchronization on the dispatch path — either a parent-established process group or a child-ready handshake — and every field the hint needs is available at that point anyway.\\n- **Treating a failed group signal over a verifying token as stale-hint cleanup.** Rejected: it deletes a live lane's only kill handle on the strength of a failed signal and misreports `abort`'s one genuine failure branch as success — the same overclaim ledger 116 removed from the absent-hint branch, reappearing one branch over. The honest shape is the adopted one: failure reported, residue retained, retry lawful and idempotent, the lane bounded by budget and horizon.\\n- **Making the hint load-bearing for abort** — forbidding deletion of a live lane's hint, or treating hint durability as a semantic precondition of the lane's validity. Rejected: it promotes an advisory file into authoritative liveness state — a one-entry process registry whose integrity someone must now guarantee, with the core as its eventual reader — exactly what D0007.C3 dissolved. The honest shape is the one adopted: best-effort kill over advisory discovery, with the dispatch budget and the horizon as the bounds that never depend on any file surviving.\\n- **Verifying the hint against the runtime child instead of (or in addition to) the supervisor.** Rejected as the discovery basis: runtime pids churn across the relaunch loop, so the hint would need racy rewrites mid-supervision, and a runtime-pid hint still leaves the enforcement gap open when the supervisor dies between relaunches (no runtime exists at that instant to verify against). Fate-sharing makes the supervisor's incarnation the single sufficient anchor: while it lives, the group signal reaches everything; once it dies, there is nothing left to reach.\\n- **A reaper or subreaper that adopts orphaned runtimes** (`PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` in a resident process, or re-parenting to a cleanup daemon). Rejected: adoption is supervision — a resident process whose uptime becomes the orphan-boundedness truth condition, exactly the rung D0013.C3 forbids. Fate-sharing needs no adopter because it produces no orphans.\\n- **Bare parent-death signaling as the sole fate-sharing mechanic for all runtimes.** Rejected as insufficient for the normative property (ledger 116, minor): `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` covers the direct child only and does not propagate to descendants, so it realizes tree-wide fate-sharing only for genuinely single-process runtimes — an assumption real vendor CLIs do not honor. Retained as one tier of the reference mechanics, composed with PID-namespace (or equivalent tree-capable) containment when descendants are possible; S7's descendant-spawning harness enforces the distinction.\\n- **Making `abort_after_s` a semantic deadline** (run dead at expiry). Rejected: smuggles clock authority back into semantics — Striatum-0's lease-expiry-under-load in new clothes; the winner rule exists precisely so slow-not-dead work keeps its value.\\n- **Silence as the declared limit-kill behavior** (kill and commit nothing). Rejected as the declared shape: it spends the full horizon window on a conclusion the supervisor already knows and starves the capacity estimator; retained as the lawful outcome when the supervisor itself dies.\\n- **Abort discovery via a central pidfile registry or process-table scanning.** Rejected: a central registry is liveness state with a reader above the seam; command-line scraping is racy, unverifiable against pid reuse, and privilege-fragile under rung 2. The per-dispatch advisory hint is discoverable from the `dispatch_id` alone, crash-safe (a stale hint degrades to cleanup that fate-sharing makes complete; an absent one to cleanup that is honestly partial), and owned by the subtree adapters already write.\\n- **Adapter-side concurrency refusal** (dispatch refuses when declared lanes are exceeded). Rejected: requires the adapter to count live processes — a liveness registry in a costume; the scheduler's ledger-derived slot arithmetic is the single lawful enforcement point.\\n\\n## Decision (clauses) {#el:decision-clauses}\\n\\n- **D0013.C1 — Forked per-dispatch supervision is adopted for LLM execution backends.** The `dispatch` verb validates, checks committed-idempotence, creates the workspace, forks the detached Lane Supervisor, **establishes and verifies the supervisor's signalable kill domain**, writes the Supervisor Hint naming that domain, and exits 0 — in that order, realizing RFC 0007's accepted verb text; the hint both postdates kill-domain readiness and precedes exit 0, so acceptance is never abort-visible without a *usable* kill handle on disk. The four-verb contract, bundle schemas, rename-only commit, typed refusal set, and A1–A8 are unchanged; the Epoch 3 synchronous bound is closed (its trigger, lane concurrency mattering, has arrived and is retired with it). Acceptance stays durable: after exit 0, a submission eventually commits or the run is closed from above; the backend owes no recovery. Process mechanics (setsid with a child-ready handshake, parent-established process groups, double-fork, groups, namespaces) are adapter-internal and non-normative provided the readiness property holds; the supervision entry point is not a fifth verb.\\n- **D0013.C2 — The Lane Supervisor owns the dispatch lifecycle.** For exactly one dispatch: runtime invocation from the sealed bundle, confined to the supervisor's session and process group and fate-bound per C10; the bounded internal-relaunch loop with pristine workspace reset (A2, `internal_retry.max`, recorded as `internal_relaunches`) — this names what supervises internal relaunches; pre-submission validation and shape repair; sealed submission assembly, fsync, and the rename commit (A4); the post-commit wake with bounded exit-4 retry; wall-clock enforcement as mechanics; self-termination and residue cleanup. The supervisor never writes the Supervisor Hint — that is the verb's act. A5/A6/A7 hold for the supervisor verbatim; everything it needs rides the sealed bundle.\\n- **D0013.C3 — Nothing supervises the supervisor.** A dead supervisor is a lapsed dispatch, recovered above the seam solely by the existing chain — dispatch horizon → `dispatch_lapse` → provisional abandonment → closure-then-new-run re-dispatch → winner rule. No watchdog, relauncher, pidfile poller, or resident recovery machinery may exist **as contract, as a recovery authority for the Lane Supervisor, or as anything readable above the seam**; adapter-internal process mechanics that neither relaunch nor recover a dead supervisor and create no registry readable above the seam remain lawful where the S-rules pass. Kernel-mediated fate-sharing (C10) is launch plumbing, not a supervision rung: it watches nothing and recovers nothing. Kill -9 at any instant is a legal conformance test and leaves committed-or-nothing.\\n- **D0013.C4 — Wall-clock ownership order.** (a) The adapter's invocation limit bounds one runtime invocation; expiry feeds the relaunch loop as a `runtime_crash` diagnostic. (b) The manifest's advisory `abort_after_s` (else an adapter-block default) is the supervisor's whole-dispatch budget, enforced as mechanics; on expiry the supervisor kills the runtime and best-effort commits a `failed` submission carrying diagnostics, usage hints, and full attribution — never owed, since a killed supervisor lawfully leaves nothing. (c) The Driver's dispatch horizon is affirmed as the only wall-clock with semantics above the seam, and those semantics remain observation-then-provisional-adjudication. (d) Enforcer death is not an enforcement gap: by C10 a dead supervisor implies a dead runtime tree, so no supervisor clock ever needs a survivor to enforce it; the horizon is the only clock that outlives the supervisor, which is precisely its role. The budget is likewise what bounds any lane `abort` cannot stop (C5). No supervisor clock is ever a semantic deadline; the diagnostics vocabulary does not grow.\\n- **D0013.C5 — Abort reaches detached work through the Supervisor Hint; the hint is never published before its kill domain is signalable; and the hint's loss or failure is priced, not papered over.** The dispatch verb writes `advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/supervisor.json` (pid, process group, start token guarding pid reuse) after fork, **after the named process group exists and is verified signalable**, and before exit 0; the supervisor never writes or rewrites it. `abort` verifies the token and signals the group (TERM, bounded grace, KILL) — reaching the runtime, which C10 confines to that group — then reclaims workspace and advisory residue. A **verifying token whose named kill domain cannot be signaled** is a failed abort over a live lane: `abort` reclaims nothing, deletes nothing, reports incompleteness, and stays idempotent — never cleanup, never a completeness claim; a conforming adapter cannot produce this state (S1), but abort's behavior in it is defined against defect and hostility alike. A **present but unverifiable** hint yields residue cleanup that is complete by C10: the supervisor it names is dead and its runtime tree died with it. An **absent** hint yields residue cleanup that is complete when the dispatch was never accepted or has already concluded, and **partial when the hint was deleted out from under a live lane**: that lane continues unreached — lawfully, because `abort` is advisory and nothing above the seam depends on it succeeding, and boundedly, by the lane's dispatch budget (C4b) below the seam and the horizon, abandonment, and winner rule above it. The verb stays advisory, idempotent, unknown-id-safe, and never touches a committed submission. The hint is an Advisory Signal: non-authoritative, deletable at will, janitor-reclaimable, never read above the seam, never enumerable as a registry — and deleting it costs `abort` its reach over that lane's remaining budget window, never correctness.\\n- **D0013.C6 — In-flight accounting and concurrency enforcement stay above the seam.** The scheduler learns what is running from `lane_binding` versus submission/closure records, never from process liveness; `concurrency.max_lanes` binds in the scheduler's hard-constraint filter and is now load-bearing. Adapters never count their own processes and gain no concurrency refusal code; over-dispatch is a promptness bug, never a correctness hazard.\\n- **D0013.C7 — The wake convention is exercised unchanged.** The supervisor fires the non-authoritative wake after rename, retries boundedly on exit 4, and may abandon safely; the standing timer and the post-quiescence spool re-scan remain the liveness floor. Drive sessions dispatch and quiesce promptly; the drive lease is held for verbs, never for lane execution.\\n- **D0013.C8 — Supervision conformance rules S1–S7** extend the per-adapter suite: S1 detachment with kill-domain readiness and hint ordering (exit 0 follows the hint write, which follows a verified-signalable kill domain; an abort issued immediately after acceptance kills), S2 kill-at-any-instant two-states **split by who dies** (supervisor death leaves no surviving lane-tree process, per S7; runtime-only death lawfully feeds the relaunch loop within `internal_retry.max`, with no extinction assertion while the supervisor lives), S3 limit-kill failed-or-nothing, S4 abort quaternity — kill on a verified hint with signalable domain, tested to the earliest accepted instant; cleanup asserted complete on a stale hint; cleanup asserted honestly partial on a hint deleted over a live lane; failure asserted, with nothing reclaimed, on a verifying token whose domain cannot be signaled — with committed submissions untouched on every branch, S5 duplicate-dispatch idempotence with single rename winner, S6 hint non-semantics (semantic invariance under advisory deletion, with abort degradation acknowledged as S4's third branch), S7 fate-sharing (supervisor death kills the runtime tree, descendant-spawning fake included, within harness grace; daemonizing runtimes are non-conforming). A1–A8 remain D0007's and are unmodified.\\n- **D0013.C9 — No new records; hardening unforeclosed.** This design demonstrates no owned-record gap: D0007.C10's four record types stand, and no new ledger record, verb, lease, heartbeat, session table, or recovery verb is introduced. Detachment changes process ancestry, not credentials: rung-2 uid isolation lands on this shape as credential and ownership changes only, per D0012.C4.\\n- **D0013.C10 — The runtime shares the supervisor's fate, as a tree property.** No runtime process outlives its Lane Supervisor beyond kernel teardown (a mechanics grace measured in seconds, never horizon-scale) — grandchildren and helpers included. The supervisor confines every runtime invocation to its own session and process group and binds its whole tree kernel-mediated to its own life. Reference mechanics are tiered and non-normative provided S7 passes: parent-death signaling on the direct child suffices only for genuinely single-process runtimes; whenever the runtime may spawn descendants — the default assumption — tree-capable containment is required, with the reference composition a private PID namespace whose init carries the parent-death signal (namespace teardown kills every descendant with no surviving actor needed); cgroup kill is lawful where an actor exists at teardown. Fate-sharing is a property of how work is started, not a resident watcher: it introduces no supervision rung, no registry, and no reader above the seam. Adapters must invoke runtimes as one-shot, headless, non-daemonizing CLIs; a runtime that detaches from the supervisor's confinement is an S7 conformance defect — and even then a resource-consumption problem only, never a semantic hazard: it has no path to an admissible commit, and committed-or-nothing holds above the seam in every case.\\n\\n## Consequences {#el:consequences}\\n\\nDeclared concurrency becomes real: divergent topologies execute their lanes simultaneously, and the scheduler's slot and write-scope arithmetic binds against work that is actually in flight. Drive sessions return to quiescence in seconds — the Driver is again an invoked program, with promptness carried by wakes and the standing timer rather than by a lease held hostage to vendor wall-clock. Lane lifetime decouples from Driver lifetime: a session crash orphans nothing and kills nothing. `abort` stops work instead of only sweeping residue — its kill handle is on disk *and signalable* before acceptance is even visible, its cleanup-only path is complete wherever a hint survives to be verified, the one branch where the kill itself can fail (a verifying hint aiming at nothing — producible only by defect or hostility) is a reported failure with residue retained rather than a silent false success, and the one branch where it cannot stop work (a hint deleted out from under a live lane) is named and priced — bounded by the lane's own dispatch budget and the horizon — rather than silently claimed complete. Limit-kills convert what were silent lapses into `failed` submissions with diagnostics and usage facts, closing runs a drain earlier and feeding the capacity estimator. No process outlives the lane that justified it: a SIGKILLed supervisor takes its entire runtime tree with it, descendants included, leaving no ghost burning vendor budget while the horizon lapses and re-dispatches around it — while a crashed runtime under a living supervisor feeds the relaunch loop exactly as designed, and the conformance suite now distinguishes the two instead of outlawing the second. The wake convention, the horizon sweep, provisional abandonment, and the winner rule — all previously idle or degenerate under synchronous dispatch — are now exercised on every LLM lane, which means the conformance suite finally tests the architecture that was designed rather than a serialization of it. The costs: one new adapter-internal moving part (the detached supervisor), one synchronization on the dispatch path (kill-domain readiness confirmed before the hint write — a pipe read or a `setpgid`, milliseconds against a lane's hours), one new advisory file shape written by the verb, one runtime-shape obligation (one-shot, non-daemonizing CLIs, kernel-fate-bound as a tree), and one honestly-priced degradation (advisory deletion downgrades abort's kill to cleanup) — all crash-only, all reclaimable, all bounded, none visible to the core.\\n\\n## Constrains {#el:constrains}\\n\\nAll LLM adapter implementations and their four-verb process surfaces (`internal/backend/llm`, the three `cmd/striatum-backend-*` surfaces, and any fifth backend joining under RFC 0007's evolution walkthrough), including each adapter's choice and configuration of runtime CLI, which must satisfy the one-shot non-daemonizing shape and the tree-wide fate-sharing property (D0013.C10), and each adapter's dispatch verb, which must establish and verify the supervisor's signalable kill domain and write the Supervisor Hint after fork and before exit 0, in that order (D0013.C1/C5); each adapter's `abort` verb, which must treat a verifying token whose kill domain cannot be signaled as a failed abort over a live lane — residue retained, nothing reclaimed (D0013.C5); the conformance suite under `tools/` (S1–S7 join the per-adapter obligations, with S1 asserting kill-domain readiness at exit 0, S2 split by who dies, S4 exercising all four abort branches, and S7's harness exercising descendant-spawning fakes); the Driver's dispatch step (must treat exit 0 as durable acceptance and must not block on execution) and its abort issuance under the winner rule (which remains courtesy ordering, aware that a deleted hint lawfully degrades the kill to cleanup and that a reported abort failure over a live lane is bounded by that lane's budget and horizon, not retried into a guarantee); the scheduler's treatment of `concurrency.max_lanes` as a live binding constraint; the `advisory/` subtree's contents (the Supervisor Hint joins the pulse as the only sanctioned shapes; the hint is verb-written, the pulse supervisor-written); and the RFC 0012 rung-2 enforcement work, which must land on this shape as credentials-only changes and must not break kernel fate-delivery (no setuid runtime binaries on the lane path).\\n\\n## Language Amendments (N8) {#el:language-amendments}\\n\\nAdmitted to the RFC 0001 glossary (Epoch 3 amendment), layer-assigned:\\n\\n- **Lane Supervisor** *(Agency)* — the detached per-dispatch process, forked by an LLM backend's `dispatch` verb, that owns runtime invocation, the bounded internal-relaunch loop, pre-submission validation, the rename commit, and the post-commit wake for exactly one dispatch. Nothing supervises it; its death is a lapsed dispatch — and, by fate-sharing, the death of every runtime process it started, descendants included. Realizes RFC 0007's \\\"per-dispatch supervisor child.\\\"\\n\\nDefined here as owning-RFC conventions, glossaried by reference only: **Supervisor Hint** — the advisory per-dispatch file (`advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/supervisor.json`), written by the dispatch verb after fork and kill-domain readiness, before exit 0, naming the signalable kill target for `abort`; an Advisory Signal, never a registry; its deletion degrades `abort` to residue cleanup for that lane and changes nothing else. **Kill Domain** — the Lane Supervisor's own process group, the single target of `abort`'s group signal, containing or fate-binding the entire runtime tree; it must exist and be verified signalable before the Supervisor Hint that names it is published (D0013.C1/C5). **Fate-Sharing** — the D0013.C10 property that no process of a runtime's tree outlives its Lane Supervisor beyond kernel teardown; launch plumbing, never a supervision rung.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers {#el:rationale-pointers}\\n\\nRFC 0007 design — the dispatch-verb definition, the harness-friction table, the winner rule, the advisory-pulse fencing — and D0007.C1–C4, C7. The Epoch 3 plan, Packet E3 (the recorded synchronous bound and its trigger). The v1 mechanics this design detaches: `internal/backend/llm/adapter.go` (synchronous execute/commit, `WallClockLimit`, abort-as-cleanup) and `internal/driver/session.go` (in-process dispatch under the drive lease, post-quiescence spool re-scan). RFC 0008 design and D0008.C7 (horizons, lapse-as-observation, re-dispatch policy). RFC 0006 design (no daemon, wakes, exit codes, quiescence). RFC 0012 design and D0012.C4 (the trust ladder; credentials, never contracts). Review ledger `evidence/review/rfcs-0013-adapter-supervision-design/97` — the major finding (dead-supervisor/live-runtime orphan state) answered by C10/S7; the minor finding (overbroad C3 wording) answered by C3's narrowed prohibition. Review ledger `evidence/review/rfcs-0013-adapter-supervision-design/116` — the major finding (a live-supervisor/no-hint state contradicting the completeness claimed for abort's cleanup-only branch) answered by the verb-ordered hint write together with the narrowed and priced completeness claims; the minor finding (parent-death signaling described too broadly for process trees) answered by the tiered reference mechanics (C10) and S7's descendant-spawning harness. Review ledger `evidence/review/rfcs-0013-adapter-supervision-design/133` — the major finding (the hint-before-exit ordering left the creation of the kill domain unordered, so an abort issued immediately after exit 0 could verify a hint naming a not-yet-signalable process group) answered by the extended normative order — fork, kill-domain ready, hint, exit 0 — with verb-side readiness confirmation (C1, C5, S1) and by the failed-live rule for a verifying token whose domain cannot be signaled (C5, S4(d)); the minor finding (S2's wording outlawed the lawful runtime-only crash/relaunch path) answered by the split S2 (C8). Proposal: `rfcs/0013-adapter-supervision/proposal`.\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0013-adapter-supervision/implementation.md\": \"# RFC 0013 Implementation Plan: Adapter Supervision {#el:rfc-0013-implementation-plan}\\n\\n## Status {#el:status}\\n\\nProduced by `implementation-planning` (contract v1) for RQ-53; principal halbritt. Plans the encoding of the converged RFC 0013 design (pinned input `rfcs/0013-adapter-supervision/design`, the post-ledger-133 revision) into the `striatum-next` repository. This plan makes **no architectural decisions**: every shape below is D0013.C1–C10 realized against the code as it stands; where the design leaves mechanics non-normative, the choice made here is flagged as an *encoding choice* and constrained to the design's stated latitude. Assumptions made during planning are recorded in `outputs/ASSUMPTIONS.md`.\\n\\n## Grounding: the v1 code this plan detaches {#el:grounding}\\n\\nVerified against the working tree of `~/git/striatum-next` (2026-07-02):\\n\\n- `internal/backend/llm/adapter.go` (530 lines) — the synchronous v1: `Dispatch` runs validate → committed-idempotence check → `execute` (the `1+InternalRetryMax` relaunch loop with A2 pristine reset, per-invocation `WallClockLimit` via `context.WithTimeout`, default 30m) → `commit` (assemble in `spool/incoming/\\u003cnonce\\u003e/`, fsync via `writeFileDurable`, `os.Rename` into `spool/submissions/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/`, sealed per D0012.C2). `Abort` is cleanup-only (`RemoveAll` workspace + advisory). `Janitor` is file-only with the live set as verb input (A7).\\n- `internal/backend/llm/cmdmain.go` — the four-verb process surface (`dispatch|abort|janitor|probe`), exit codes 0/1/2, shared by `cmd/striatum-backend-{agy,claude-code,codex}`.\\n- `internal/driver/session.go` — the drive session calls the in-process `Adapter` interface (`Dispatch(manifestPath) (string, error)`) synchronously at `dispatchStep` (~line 1695), under the drive lease; the post-quiescence spool re-scan (~line 143) and `nextHorizon` exist; abandonment (`abandonedInThis`, `AbandonmentCap`) exists. `internal/cli/root.go:466` wires `llm.Adapter` values into `Session.Adapters`; exit code 4 = drive lease held.\\n- `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go` — pure placement library; `Declaration` has **no** `MaxLanes` field and `Bind` takes no in-flight input: declared concurrency is currently parsed by nothing and enforced by nothing.\\n- `backends/*/backend.yaml` — declarations already carry `capabilities.concurrency: { max_lanes: N }` and `constraints.internal_retry: { max: N }`; `internal/backend/llm/config.go` parses the adapter block (`command`, `prompt_mode`, `version_command`) and `internal_retry.max`, and does not parse `max_lanes` (correct: concurrency is never the adapter's).\\n- `internal/backend/spool.go` — the spool layout including `advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/`; `internal/backend/manifest.go` — `DispatchManifest.Advisory map[string]any` exists, so `abort_after_s` rides an existing field and **no bundle-schema change is needed**.\\n- `internal/records/payloads.go` — `dispatch_lapse`, `lane_binding`, `capacity_observation`, `submission_refused` are all registered, satisfying D0013.C9 (no new records) with zero record work.\\n- `tools/backend-conformance/main.go` — mechanical A4/A7/A8 checks only; A1–A3/A5/A6 live in adapter test suites (`adapter_test.go`, 357 lines).\\n\\nThe recovery chain the design leans on (horizon → `dispatch_lapse` → provisional abandonment → re-dispatch → winner rule) is already built and tested; this plan adds nothing to it and nothing above the seam except scheduler concurrency (C6) and courtesy abort issuance.\\n\\n## Plan shape and ordering rationale {#el:plan-shape}\\n\\nSeven stages, ordered so that (a) the one genuinely platform-risky piece — tree-capable fate-sharing on this deployment's kernel — is de-risked first, before anything depends on it; (b) the supervisor is extracted as a pure refactor while the dispatch path is still synchronous, so the existing test suite pins behavior across the seam-relevant move; (c) detachment, the kill domain, and the hint land as one stage because the design's normative order (fork → kill-domain ready → hint → exit 0) is indivisible — there is no useful intermediate state where some of it is live; (d) abort's rewrite lands only after the hint exists to read; (e) above-seam work (scheduler, driver) lands after the seam behaves as designed; (f) the S-suite lands last but its harness is built early enough that stages 2–5 develop against it.\\n\\nEach work item states: **Where** (files), **Work**, **Acceptance** (checkable criteria), and **Verifies** (the design clauses and S-rules it discharges). \\\"Green\\\" always includes the existing suites: `adapter_test.go`, `session_test.go`, and `tools/backend-conformance` A-rules unchanged — A1–A8 are D0007's and this plan may not move them.\\n\\n## Stage 0 — fate-sharing mechanics spike {#el:stage-0-fate-sharing-spike}\\n\\n### W0: containment primitive and platform validation {#el:w0-containment-primitive}\\n\\n**Where:** new package `internal/backend/supervise` (shared by all LLM surfaces; nothing above the seam imports it — enforced by W16).\\n\\n**Work:** Implement the tiered reference mechanics of D0013.C10 as a single primitive, `StartConfined(argv, dir, stdio) (*ConfinedProc, error)`, that starts a runtime invocation whose **entire process tree** dies with the caller:\\n\\n- Reference composition: spawn the runtime's direct ancestor as init of a **private PID namespace** with `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL)` set on that init (re-checking the parent pid after `prctl` to close the fork/death race). Namespace teardown then kills every descendant with no surviving actor — the SIGKILL-at-any-instant path the design requires.\\n- Provide `Kill()` (TERM → bounded grace → KILL on the containment scope) for orderly paths (budget expiry, abort forwarding); this is plumbing, not the property carrier.\\n- **Platform validation, first thing:** Ubuntu 24.04 restricts unprivileged user namespaces by default (`apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`), and unprivileged `CLONE_NEWPID` requires a user namespace. Validate on the deployment host which composition works unprivileged: user+PID namespace (if permitted for this binary), a profile/sysctl adjustment recorded in the `proximal` desired-state repo, or the cgroup-scoped fallback *composed with* PDEATHSIG on a namespace-less init — the fallback must still pass S7's SIGKILL-at-any-instant case or it is not a lawful fallback. The spike's output is a written note in the package doc naming the chosen mechanics and why, plus a passing S7-shaped test.\\n\\n**Acceptance:** a Go test (skipped where the kernel forbids the mechanics, loud about why) that starts a confined fake which spawns a blocking descendant, SIGKILLs the *caller* mid-flight, and observes the whole tree dead within a small grace (seconds); a second case observes `Kill()` tearing down the tree on the orderly path; a third case shows a bare-PDEATHSIG-only start *failing* the descendant case, pinning why the tiering exists.\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C10 mechanics feasibility; the harness kernel of S7. Nothing merges beyond this stage until W0's mid-flight case passes on the deployment host — this is the plan's single go/no-go gate.\\n\\n## Stage 1 — supervisor extraction (still synchronous) {#el:stage-1-supervisor-extraction}\\n\\n### W1: extract the Lane Supervisor as a type {#el:w1-extract-supervisor}\\n\\n**Where:** `internal/backend/llm/supervisor.go` (new), `adapter.go` (shrinks).\\n\\n**Work:** Move the post-acceptance lifecycle — `execute` (relaunch loop), `collect` (pre-submission validation), `commit` (assembly/fsync/rename/seal), attribution assembly — out of `Adapter` into a `Supervisor` struct with a single `Run(manifest, bundleDir) error` entry. `Adapter.Dispatch` still calls it synchronously; observable behavior is bit-identical. Workspace layout is restructured now, while everything is still in-process: the runtime's cwd and `outputs/` move to `workspaces/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/work/`, which is what the A2 pristine reset removes per attempt; the outer `workspaces/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/` becomes supervisor-owned residue (detached stdio log lands here in W3) so the per-attempt reset never unlinks the supervisor's own file handles. (Encoding choice within A2's intent: pristine-per-attempt is a property of the tree the runtime sees.)\\n\\n**Acceptance:** `adapter_test.go` and `session_test.go` green with no test-body changes beyond workspace-path constants; `backend-conformance` A-rules green against a real spool.\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C2's obligation set exists as one owned unit (relaunch loop, validation, commit — \\\"what supervises internal relaunches\\\" now has a name in the code); no seam behavior moved yet.\\n\\n### W2: the supervision entry point {#el:w2-supervision-entry}\\n\\n**Where:** `cmdmain.go`, `supervisor.go`.\\n\\n**Work:** Add the adapter-internal supervision entry to the backend binary: an undocumented argv shape (e.g. leading token `__supervise` with `-manifest`, `-spool`, `-store-root`, and the readiness-pipe fd number) that `CmdMain` intercepts before verb parsing, never prints in usage, and that constructs `Supervisor` and calls `Run`. Not a fifth verb: excluded from the documented verb set, from usage text, and from conformance's verb enumeration; invisible above the seam (the Driver never invokes it).\\n\\n**Acceptance:** invoking the entry directly with a valid manifest executes one dispatch end-to-end and commits (integration test via the fake runtime); `usage` output and verb docs unchanged; refusal exit codes unreachable from this entry (it is post-acceptance by construction).\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C1's \\\"supervision entry point is not a fifth verb\\\".\\n\\n## Stage 2 — detachment, kill domain, hint (the normative order) {#el:stage-2-detachment}\\n\\nThese three items land as **one change set**; the design's order — fork, kill-domain ready, hint, exit 0 — has no lawful partial encoding.\\n\\n### W3: fork, kill-domain readiness, and the handshake {#el:w3-fork-and-readiness}\\n\\n**Where:** `adapter.go` (`Dispatch` tail), new `internal/backend/llm/detach.go`.\\n\\n**Work:** Replace the synchronous `Supervisor.Run` call in `Dispatch` with:\\n\\n1. Spawn the supervision entry via `os/exec` with `SysProcAttr{Setsid: true}` — the kernel establishes the new session and process group between fork and exec, so the kill domain (pgid = child pid) exists the instant `Start` returns. This is the design's \\\"parent-established\\\" lawful alternative fused with the reference `setsid` shape; the caveat the design notes (a parent-made group leader cannot later `setsid`) does not arise because `Setsid` at spawn *is* the session creation.\\n2. The exec target self-selects by context: the process surface uses `/proc/self/exe`; the in-process Driver adapter uses a configured surface binary (see W11). One code path, two exec targets.\\n3. **Readiness handshake:** the child inherits a pipe; the supervision entry writes `{pid, pgid, start_token}` and closes it as its first act (post-exec, so readiness also proves exec succeeded). The verb reads with a short deadline. Child dead or EOF before the payload ⇒ **verb error, no hint, no exit 0** — nothing was accepted.\\n4. **Signalability verification, verb-side:** after the handshake, the verb confirms `kill(-pgid, 0)` succeeds and computes/cross-checks the start token (boot id from `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` + starttime field of `/proc/\\u003cpid\\u003e/stat` — the design's \\\"or equivalent\\\").\\n5. Supervisor stdio is detached into `workspaces/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/supervisor.log` (outer tree, per W1).\\n\\n**Acceptance:** dispatch against a blocking fake returns exit 0 in milliseconds while the fake runs; the child's pgid is signalable at the instant `Dispatch` returns (asserted by an immediate `kill(-pgid, 0)` in the test); a fake whose supervision entry aborts pre-handshake yields a verb error and no advisory residue.\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C1 steps 4's fork and kill-domain-readiness legs; the ledger-133 major-finding closure at its root; S1's readiness half.\\n\\n### W4: the Supervisor Hint, verb-written {#el:w4-supervisor-hint}\\n\\n**Where:** `detach.go`, `internal/backend/spool.go` (path helper only).\\n\\n**Work:** After signalability verification and before returning success, the verb writes `advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/supervisor.json` — `{pid, pgid, start_token, written_at}` — as create-or-replace via temp-file + rename within the advisory dir (the \\\"writes (or overwrites)\\\" the design requires for the same-id-retry world). The supervisor never touches this file; its only advisory surface is the (deferred) pulse. `written_at` comes from the adapter's clock; no fsync (the hint is advisory — its loss is priced, never load-bearing).\\n\\n**Acceptance:** at every exit-0 return from `Dispatch`, the hint exists, parses, its token verifies against the live child, and its pgid is the child's session group; a second fork for the same `dispatch_id` (S5 race case) leaves the hint naming the most recent fork.\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C5's write ordering (\\\"after fork, after the named process group exists and is verified signalable, before exit 0\\\"); S1's hint half; the S5 hint-freshness clause.\\n\\n### W5: idempotence extension {#el:w5-idempotence-extension}\\n\\n**Where:** `adapter.go` (`Dispatch` head).\\n\\n**Work:** After the existing committed-submission check, add the non-authoritative optimization: if the hint for this `dispatch_id` exists and its start token verifies against a live process, exit 0 without forking. Token verification only — no signalability requirement on this branch (a wrong hint's worst case is a duplicate execution, already lawful under pass purity and the rename winner).\\n\\n**Acceptance:** dispatching a `dispatch_id` whose supervisor is alive returns 0, forks nothing (asserted by process-table diff), and leaves the hint untouched; dispatching one whose hint is stale forks a fresh supervisor and overwrites the hint.\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C1 step 2; S5's verb-died-after-hint and racing-supervisor cases.\\n\\n## Stage 3 — the supervisor's full obligation set {#el:stage-3-supervisor-obligations}\\n\\n### W6: runtime confinement via the containment primitive {#el:w6-runtime-confinement}\\n\\n**Where:** `supervisor.go` (`invoke` path), consuming `internal/backend/supervise` (W0).\\n\\n**Work:** Replace the bare `exec.CommandContext` invocation with `StartConfined`: every runtime invocation runs inside the supervisor's session/process group and inside the W0 containment scope, so (a) abort's single group signal reaches supervisor and runtime alike, and (b) supervisor death — any cause, any instant — tears down the whole runtime tree by kernel mediation. The invocation remains cwd-confined to `workspaces/\\u003cid\\u003e/work/`, prompt delivery per `prompt_mode`, transcript capture into exhaust unchanged.\\n\\n**Acceptance:** W0's test matrix re-run with the real supervisor in the caller role: SIGKILL the supervisor mid-invocation with a descendant-spawning fake ⇒ tree dead within grace; runtime-only SIGKILL ⇒ supervisor survives, observes `runtime_crash`, relaunch loop proceeds within `internal_retry.max` (the lawful S2(b) branch).\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C2 confinement/fate-binding obligation; D0013.C10; S7's positive case; S2(b).\\n\\n### W7: wall-clock ownership {#el:w7-wall-clock-ownership}\\n\\n**Where:** `supervisor.go`, `config.go`.\\n\\n**Work:** Encode the decided precedence as supervisor mechanics:\\n\\n- **Invocation limit** (clock 1): the existing `WallClockLimit` semantics move into the supervisor per invocation; expiry kills the confined invocation and feeds the loop as `runtime_crash` — behavior identical to v1, ownership relocated. Source it from a new optional `adapter:` declaration key (encoding choice: `adapter.invocation_limit_s`, compiled default 30m as today).\\n- **Dispatch budget** (clock 2): read `abort_after_s` from `DispatchManifest.Advisory` when present (existing field; no schema change), else a new optional `adapter.dispatch_budget_s` declaration key, else a compiled default (encoding choice: 3600s). The supervisor sets one deadline over the whole supervision and clamps each invocation limit to the remaining budget. On expiry: `Kill()` the confined runtime, then **best-effort commit a `failed` submission** — existing `runtime_crash` diagnostics class, transcript exhaust naming the limit, observed usage hints, full attribution (no vocabulary growth). A supervisor killed before that commit lawfully leaves nothing.\\n- **The horizon** (clock 3): no code — it is the Driver's and already exists; the plan's only obligation is to *not* teach the supervisor about it, which W16's illiteracy checks pin.\\n\\n**Acceptance:** budget-expiry integration test yields a committed `failed` submission whose diagnostics include `runtime_crash`, whose exhaust names the limit, and whose attribution spans the supervision; a variant killing the supervisor just before commit yields nothing (two states); an invocation-limit expiry mid-budget yields a relaunch, not a commit.\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C4(a)(b); S3 both legs; the diagnostics-vocabulary freeze.\\n\\n### W8: post-commit wake and self-termination {#el:w8-wake-and-cleanup}\\n\\n**Where:** `supervisor.go`, `cmdmain.go`/`detach.go` (flag pass-through).\\n\\n**Work:** After the rename, the supervisor fires the non-authoritative wake: exec a configured wake argv appending `-trigger adapter_wake`. The wake argv reaches the supervisor as a dispatch-verb flag (encoding choice: `dispatch -wake-cmd \\u003cargv-json\\u003e`, forwarded to the supervision entry; the in-process Driver adapter populates it from its own session config — the adapter still reads no ledger and learns nothing but a command line, so A7 is undisturbed). Exit 4 (lease busy) gets a bounded retry with backoff (encoding choice: 3 retries at 2s/10s/30s with jitter); any other outcome, or exhaustion, abandons safely — the standing timer and the post-quiescence spool re-scan are the documented liveness floor and already exist. Then: reclaim `workspaces/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/` (outer tree included) and `advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/` (the hint), and exit. Absent `-wake-cmd`, skip the wake entirely (lawful: no wake is load-bearing).\\n\\n**Acceptance:** commit-then-wake observed end-to-end (fake `striatum` recording its invocation and trigger); exit-4 fake exhausts retries and the supervisor still exits 0-equivalently with residue reclaimed; the kill-table row \\\"between rename and wake\\\" (SIGKILL there) leaves the submission committed and the wake lost, drained by the next session — asserted in S2(a).\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C2 wake/self-termination obligations; D0013.C7; the kill-table rename/wake rows.\\n\\n## Stage 4 — abort rewrite {#el:stage-4-abort}\\n\\n### W9: the four-branch abort verb {#el:w9-abort-four-branches}\\n\\n**Where:** `adapter.go` (`Abort`), `cmdmain.go`.\\n\\n**Work:** Rewrite `Abort(dispatchID)` on the fixed semantics (advisory, idempotent, unknown-id-safe, never touches committed submissions):\\n\\n1. Read `advisory/\\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e/supervisor.json`. **Absent** ⇒ cleanup-only (today's behavior verbatim): remove workspace + advisory; honestly partial by design and no claim otherwise.\\n2. Present ⇒ verify the start token against the live process table. **Unverifiable** ⇒ cleanup-only, complete by fate-sharing (dead supervisor ⇒ dead tree).\\n3. **Verifies and signalable** ⇒ SIGTERM the group, bounded grace (encoding choice: 5s, overridable via `adapter.abort_grace_s`), SIGKILL the group; then reclaim workspace + advisory.\\n4. **Verifies but the group signal cannot be delivered** (ESRCH on the pgid, or the token still verifies after the full TERM–grace–KILL escalation) ⇒ **failed abort over a live lane**: reclaim nothing, delete nothing, return an error (exit 1 under the existing 0/1/2 convention, with a typed detail line `abort_incomplete: \\u003creason\\u003e` — encoding choice; the refusal set does not grow because this is verb *failure*, not dispatch refusal). Idempotent: a retry re-runs the branches and may find the token stale (then branch 2 completes cleanup) or succeed.\\n\\n**Acceptance:** the S4 quaternity below, plus: aborting an unknown id exits 0 having touched nothing; aborting a committed dispatch never opens `spool/submissions/`.\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C5 in full, including the ledger-133 failed-live rule; S4(a)–(d).\\n\\n## Stage 5 — above the seam {#el:stage-5-above-the-seam}\\n\\n### W10: driver dispatch integration {#el:w10-driver-integration}\\n\\n**Where:** `internal/cli/root.go` (adapter construction), `internal/driver/session.go` (no interface change expected).\\n\\n**Work:** The in-process `llm.Adapter.Dispatch` now returns at acceptance (post-hint), so `dispatchStep` stops blocking for lane wall-clock with **no signature change** — the `Adapter` interface already returns `(string, error)` and the session already treats a nil error as dispatched and moves on (record-then-dispatch order is untouched). Two integration facts to encode: (a) the returned path becomes the *expected* submission target rather than a committed one — audit the one call site (~line 1695) which already discards it; (b) the adapter needs the exec target and wake argv: `root.go:466` construction gains the surface-binary path (encoding choice: declared optional `adapter.surface_command`, default `striatum-backend-\\u003cid\\u003e` resolved on PATH) and the wake command derived from the session's own store/config flags. Audit `session_test.go` for tests that assumed a submission exists immediately after dispatch and convert them to release-the-fake-then-drain shape.\\n\\n**Acceptance:** a drive session over a blocking fake dispatches its frontier and quiesces `awaiting_submissions` in seconds while lanes run; releasing the fakes then invoking drive (as the wake would) drains the submissions; a session crash after dispatch neither kills nor orphans lanes (they commit; the standing-timer path drains).\\n\\n**Verifies:** the Constrains clause on the Driver's dispatch step (exit 0 / nil error as durable acceptance, no blocking on execution); D0013.C7's \\\"lease held for verbs, never executions\\\".\\n\\n### W11: scheduler concurrency becomes load-bearing {#el:w11-scheduler-concurrency}\\n\\n**Where:** `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, `internal/driver/catalog.go` (declaration parsing), `internal/driver/fold.go` + `session.go` (in-flight derivation).\\n\\n**Work:** Add `MaxLanes int` to `scheduler.Declaration`, parsed from `capabilities.concurrency.max_lanes` (0/absent ⇒ unlimited — encoding choice, recorded). The Driver derives per-backend in-flight strictly from the ledger fold — `lane_binding` records with neither a drained submission nor a closure for their run/lane — and passes it into `Bind` as a new input (pure-function shape preserved: same inputs, same bindings). The hard-constraint filter drops saturated backends from a run's candidate set; a run whose every capable backend is saturated is **deferred** — left unbound this session, retried next session — with a session-report note, not a new refusal code (per D0013.C6 the refusal vocabulary does not grow; deferral-not-refusal is recorded as an assumption against RFC 0008's filter semantics). Adapters get **no** concurrency logic of any kind.\\n\\n**Acceptance:** scheduler unit tests: `max_lanes: 1` with one in-flight lane defers a second run for the same backend and binds it to an alternative capable backend when one exists; determinism test (same inputs ⇒ same bindings) still passes; a driver-level test shows over-dispatch impossible through the normal path and harmless (lawful) when forced.\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C6; the Consequences claim that slot arithmetic binds against real in-flight.\\n\\n### W12: courtesy abort issuance under the winner rule {#el:w12-driver-abort-courtesy}\\n\\n**Where:** `internal/driver/session.go` (the `superseded_by_redispatch` path, ~line 1809), `internal/cli/root.go`.\\n\\n**Work:** Where the session supersedes an attempt, issue `abort \\u003cdispatch_id\\u003e` for the superseded dispatch on the adapter surface before any janitor action — courtesy ordering, never correctness. The abort runs with the session's ordinary credentials via the same surface-command plumbing as W10. A failed abort (W9 branch 4) is noted in the session report and **not retried into a guarantee**; a degraded abort (deleted hint) is indistinguishable from success at this layer and treated as such, both per the design's Constrains.\\n\\n**Acceptance:** a superseded in-flight lane's supervisor and runtime are dead after the sweep (fake-based test); an abort failure leaves a note and the session proceeds; no janitor call precedes the abort for the same id in the sweep path.\\n\\n**Verifies:** the Constrains clause on Driver abort issuance; exercises S4(a) from above the seam.\\n\\n## Stage 6 — conformance: the S-suite {#el:stage-6-conformance}\\n\\n### W13: fake runtime harness {#el:w13-fake-harness}\\n\\n**Where:** `tools/backend-conformance/fakes/` (a small Go binary; test-only, never in dist).\\n\\n**Work:** One configurable fake CLI covering every S-rule posture: block-until-released (watches for a release file/fifo); spawn a blocking descendant of its own (mandatory default, so single-process-only mechanics cannot pass S7 by accident); write required outputs on release; `--daemonize` mode (double-fork out of the session) for S7's negative case; `--crash-n-times` for relaunch-loop cases; plus a stooge helper for S4(d) (a live process whose pid/token the harness lends to a synthesized hint naming a bogus pgid). Backend declarations for the fakes live under `tools/backend-conformance/fakes/backends/`.\\n\\n**Acceptance:** the fake is driven by every S-test below; no production code path references it.\\n\\n### W14: S1–S7 as an executable suite {#el:w14-s-suite}\\n\\n**Where:** Go integration tests in `internal/backend/llm` (development harness, fault-injection-friendly via library seams) **and** a per-adapter runner mode `backend-conformance -supervise -backend-cmd \\u003cbinary\\u003e -spool \\u003croot\\u003e` that exercises the process surface black-box, mirroring how A4/A7/A8 already run per adapter. The S-rules bind on the black-box runner; the Go tests are scaffolding.\\n\\n**Work and acceptance, per rule (each maps to D0013.C8's text):**\\n\\n- **S1** — dispatch against a blocking fake exits 0 without awaiting completion; at exit-0 the hint is on disk, verifies, and names a signalable domain — asserted at the tightest race by issuing `abort` immediately after dispatch returns and requiring the tree dead within the S7 grace; un-aborted variant: release the fake, submission commits with no dispatch verb alive.\\n- **S2(a)** — SIGKILL the supervisor at every kill-table row (before/during runtime, mid-validation, mid-relaunch, mid-assembly, between rename and wake, after wake; the verb-window rows — before fork, fork→hint, hint→exit-0 — via library-level fault injection since no black-box hook exists there, recorded as such): committed-or-nothing, no surviving lane-tree process, residue janitor-reclaimable.\\n- **S2(b)** — SIGKILL runtime processes only: supervisor survives, observes `runtime_crash`, relaunches within `internal_retry.max`; the test asserts the relaunch happens (expected outcome, not defect) and no extinction assertion applies while the supervisor lives.\\n- **S3** — budget expiry ⇒ `failed` submission with diagnostics and attribution; supervisor killed pre-commit ⇒ nothing; separate cases.\\n- **S4** — (a) verified+signalable ⇒ group dead + residue reclaimed, tested mid-flight *and* at the earliest instant after exit 0; (b) present-unverifiable (supervisor SIGKILLed first) ⇒ cleanup asserted *complete* — no lane-tree survivor; (c) harness deletes the hint mid-flight ⇒ cleanup-only, lane *not* killed, runs to lawful conclusion — asserted exactly, no completeness claim; (d) synthesized verifying-token/unsignalable-domain hint ⇒ abort reports failure, reclaims nothing, deletes nothing, idempotent on retry. All branches: unknown-id-safe, committed submissions untouched.\\n- **S5** — committed id ⇒ exit 0 no fork; live-hint id ⇒ exit 0 no fork; racing supervisors (hintless-orphan world included, forced via fault injection) ⇒ single rename winner, loser residue reclaimable, hint names the most recent fork.\\n- **S6** — delete `advisory/` contents mid-flight; run the full drive/drain cycle twice (with and without deletion) and assert identical ledger outcomes (bindings, admission verdicts, claims, closures) — semantic invariance, not operational equivalence; plus the W16 static check that nothing above the seam reads a hint.\\n- **S7** — SIGKILL supervisor mid-invocation with the descendant-spawning fake held open ⇒ tree dead within harness grace; subsequent same-id abort is cleanup-only and idempotent; `--daemonize` fake ⇒ the suite *fails* the adapter (asserted: the negative case is detected, pinning daemonizing runtimes as non-conforming).\\n\\n**Verifies:** D0013.C8 in full; each S-test's body cites its clause.\\n\\n### W15: run the suite against the three real adapters {#el:w15-real-adapters}\\n\\n**Where:** operational, on the deployment workstation.\\n\\n**Work:** Run `backend-conformance -supervise` against `striatum-backend-agy`, `-claude-code`, `-codex` with the fake-runtime declarations substituted (the S-rules test the adapter's supervision mechanics, not vendor CLIs), then one live smoke lane per real backend end-to-end (dispatch → detached commit → wake → drain).\\n\\n**Acceptance:** all S-rules pass for all three surfaces;
