Generated by `proposal-generation` (contract v1) for RQ-53; principal halbritt.\\n\\n## Problem {#el:problem}\\n\\nRFC 0007 fixed the backend contract: dispatch and submission are content-addressed file trees over a non-authoritative spool, `rename(2)` is the sole commit point, adapters are ledger-illiterate (A7), and supervision is backend-internal. Its accepted dispatch-verb text even names a shape — validate, create the workspace, *fork the per-dispatch supervisor child*, exit 0 — with acceptance durable: after exit 0, either a submission eventually commits or the run is closed; there is no third obligation.\\n\\nThe Epoch 3 implementation recorded a narrower v1 bound: **adapter execution is synchronous inside the dispatch verb.** The Driver invokes the adapter's dispatch in-process during a drive session, and the verb returns only after the LLM runtime has run to a committed submission, a failed submission, or a typed refusal. The bound was recorded honestly — \\\"forked supervision arrives when lane concurrency matters\\\" — but the trigger was never defined, and the synchronous shape carries consequences the architecture was built to avoid:\\n\\n- **Declared concurrency is dead weight.** Backend declarations carry `concurrency.max_lanes` and the scheduler binds only where a slot exists — but with execution inside the dispatch verb, at most one lane runs at any moment regardless of what declarations promise. Divergent topologies whose entire value is simultaneous independent lanes execute serially.\\n- **The drive lease is held for the whole execution.** A session dispatching one LLM lane holds the lease for that lane's full wall-clock (advisory `abort_after_s` runs to hours). Wakes bounce with exit 4 for the duration, submissions from other backends wait for admission, and the status projection ages. The architecture's own posture — nothing needs to be running for the system to be correct; things run so it is *prompt* — is inverted: the Driver becomes a resident executor.\\n- **Lane lifetime is coupled to Driver lifetime.** The seam was designed so a dead backend is indistinguishable from a slow one; under synchronous dispatch the backend's runtime dies whenever the Driver's process does. Crash-only semantics make this safe (the dispatch lapses and is re-dispatched) but wasteful, and it is exactly the coupling the seam exists to prevent.\\n- **`abort` is partially vacuous.** The verb is defined — advisory kill, reclaim the workspace, never touch a committed submission — but a separately invoked `abort` has no handle on a runtime living inside the Driver's process. Today it can clean residue; it cannot stop work.\\n\\nIf the forked shape is adopted, RFC 0007's text leaves three questions unnamed that any detached supervisor must answer:\\n\\n1. **What supervises internal relaunches** once the dispatch verb has exited — and, explicitly, what supervises the supervisor. The bounded relaunch loop (strategy-then-exit and output-shape countermeasures, `internal_retry.max`, recorded as `internal_relaunches`) currently lives inside the verb; detached, it must live somewhere named.\\n2. **Who owns wall-clock limits** when the only process present at the deadline is detached. Three clocks exist today with no stated precedence: the adapter's own invocation limit, the manifest's advisory `abort_after_s`, and the Driver's dispatch horizon (the only one with semantics above the seam).\\n3. **How abort reaches a detached supervisor** given A7 (no ledger reads) and D0007.C3 (no leases, no liveness registry): `dispatch_id` → running-work discovery must be possible without reintroducing the liveness state the contract dissolved.\\n\\n## Motivation {#el:motivation}\\n\\nThe trigger condition has arrived. LLM backends are live — three adapters probe on this workstation — and the machinery that assumes concurrency already exists on both sides of the seam: the scheduler computes bindings against declared slots and in-flight write scopes (RFC 0008), independence partitions demand multiple lanes of different aliasing classes in flight together, and the horizon/lapse/winner-rule apparatus (dispatch horizons, provisional abandonment, `submitted_late`, `redundant_candidate`) was designed for lanes that outlive the session that dispatched them. Under synchronous dispatch, all of it idles: the scheduler's slot arithmetic never binds a second lane, and a lapse can only mean the Driver itself died mid-verb.\\n\\nLeaving the evolution criterion undefined invites drift: each adapter could grow its own forking mechanics ad hoc, outside the A1–A8 conformance suite, and the three unnamed questions would get answered by accident in code rather than by decision. Deciding once keeps the four-verb contract testable across every adapter and keeps the supervision complexity that consumed Striatum-0 — leases, heartbeats, recovery verbs — structurally absent rather than absent by luck.\\n\\n## Target State {#el:target-state}\\n\\nA recorded decision on the supervision architecture for LLM execution backends — **whether** the v1 synchronous shape is affirmed or the dispatch verb evolves to forked per-dispatch supervision, and if the latter, **how**, with the three unnamed questions answered by name:\\n\\n- The per-dispatch supervisor's obligations are stated: what it owns (runtime invocation, the bounded internal-relaunch loop with workspace reset, pre-submission validation, the rename commit, the post-commit wake with exit-4 retry) — and the explicit statement that *nothing supervises the supervisor*. A dead supervisor is a lapsed dispatch, recovered above the seam by the existing horizon sweep, provisional abandonment, and re-dispatch — never by resident recovery machinery.\\n- One ownership order for wall-clock is stated: which limit the detached supervisor enforces as mechanics, what a limit-kill leaves above the seam (a `failed` submission carrying diagnostics versus nothing), and the Driver's dispatch horizon affirmed as the only wall-clock with semantics.\\n- An abort path that reaches detached work is stated in obligation form: discovery is file-shaped and crash-safe, the verb stays advisory, idempotent, safe against unknown ids, and never touches a committed submission; whatever discovery residue exists is non-authoritative, janitor-reclaimable, and unreadable by the core — never a process registry.\\n- The conformance suite covers the decided shape (kill-at-any-instant remains a legal test; the two-states property is testable per adapter), the concurrency declarations become load-bearing, and drive sessions return to quiescence promptly with admission driven by wakes.\\n\\nIf instead the synchronous shape is affirmed, the affirmation is equally explicit: the concurrency declarations are re-scoped honestly, the vacuous portion of `abort` is recorded as such, and the evolution criterion — today the undefined phrase \\\"when lane concurrency matters\\\" — is replaced by a stated condition.\\n\\n## Non-Goals {#el:non-goals}\\n\\n- **No seam changes.** Dispatch and submission bundle schemas, the rename-only commit point, admission V1–V10, the winner rule, and late-submission semantics are fixed (D0007; RFCs 0009/0010).\\n- **No liveness vocabulary.** No leases, heartbeats, sessions, supervisor registries, or recovery verbs (D0007.C3). Any mechanism that requires the core to know whether a process is alive is out of scope by construction.\\n- **No scheduler policy work.** Binding rules, capacity arithmetic, and horizon multipliers stay RFC 0008's; this decision only makes the already-declared slots real.\\n- **No process-mechanics selection.** Double-fork versus setsid, process groups, pidfile formats, cgroup placement — design-stage material, not proposal commitments.\\n- **No change to the `local` backend's execution shape.** Verifier lanes and deterministic passes are out of scope; the decision covers LLM execution backends.\\n- **No Epoch 3 hardening delivery.** Per-lane uid isolation and keyed-seal enforcement remain RFC 0012's; the supervision shape must not foreclose uid isolation but does not deliver it.\\n- **No scheduling of human or remote runtimes.**\\n\\n## Constraints {#el:constraints}\\n\\n- **Crash-only, result-or-nothing.** The seam sees exactly two states; a supervisor killed at any instant leaves either a committed submission or nothing above the seam. Kill -9 at any point in the lifecycle is a legal conformance test.\\n- **A7 holds for the supervisor** exactly as for the verbs: no ledger reads, ever. Everything detached execution needs rides in the sealed dispatch bundle; everything the janitor needs arrives as verb input.\\n- **The wake stays non-authoritative.** The supervisor fires the wake after rename, retries on exit 4, and a lost wake is covered by the standing timer and the drive loop's post-quiescence spool re-scan. No wake may become load-bearing.\\n- **Acceptance stays durable.** After dispatch exits 0, either a submission eventually commits or the run is closed — with the closure lawfully suppliable from above (lapse → abandonment adjudication); the backend owes no recovery.\\n- **Declared bounds are the only bounds.** Internal relaunches per `internal_retry.max`, recorded in attribution; concurrency per declaration; refusals from the closed typed set; the advisory block advisory.\\n- **In-flight accounting stays ledger-derived.** The scheduler learns what is running from `lane_binding` versus submission/closure records, never from process liveness.\\n- **Abort semantics are fixed.** Advisory, idempotent, safe on unknown ids, never touches a committed submission — properties the existing adapter conformance tests already pin.\\n- **A8 and workspace confinement unchanged.** The spool and any supervisor working state live on the declared durable subtree; fresh workspace per dispatch with pristine reset before relaunch (A2); confined writes (A6).\\n- **Decisions D0001–D0012 in force.** No new record types unless the design demonstrates an owned-record gap beyond D0007.C10's four.\\n\\n## Source Material {#el:source-material}\\n\\n- RFC 0007 design — the dispatch-verb definition naming the per-dispatch supervisor child; the harness-friction table and bounded-relaunch rules; the winner rule; the wake-after-commit convention — and D0007 clauses C1–C4, C7.\\n- The Epoch 3 plan, Packet E3 entry: the recorded v1 bound (\\\"adapter execution is synchronous inside the dispatch verb; forked supervision arrives when lane concurrency matters\\\").\\n- The v1 LLM adapter core and Driver runtime: `internal/backend/llm/adapter.go` (synchronous mechanics, invocation wall-clock limit, abort-as-residue-cleanup) and `internal/driver/session.go` (in-process dispatch under the drive lease).\\n- RFC 0008 design and D0008 — concurrency slots as a hard binding constraint, dispatch horizons and `dispatch_lapse` as observation-not-adjudication, wall-clock-is-not-a-pool.\\n- RFC 0006 design — the non-authoritative wake convention, exit codes, and the drive loop's spool re-scan closing the wake-drop race.\\n- RFC 0012 — the v1 trust domain and the uid-isolation boundary the supervision shape must not foreclose.\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0014-cross-repository-compilation/design.md\": \"# RFC 0014 Design: Cross-Repository Compilation {#el:rfc-0014-design-cross-repository-compilation}\\n\\n## Status {#el:status}\\n\\nConverged for RQ-1442; principal halbritt. Vocabulary: RFC 0001 plus the Language Amendments section below (N8). Binding context: D0001 (the Artifact Graph — one per target repository; the Exogenous Change Record evidence kind), D0002.C2/C8 (Derived-State Doctrine; the executing repository's policy governs its passes), D0008 (C1 pure-function scheduler, C3 workstation-level capacity fold, C6 repository policy as a placement input), D0009 (C1 graph-in-ledger, C2 layout and registry, C5 governed record registry and corpus ratchet, C8 multi-repo, C10 trust boundary; the `### Cross-graph pins` section), D0010 (C8 integration, C11 execution-independence and the standing guard), D0012 (C4/C5 the trust ladder). Pinned inputs: `rfcs/0014-cross-repository-compilation/proposal`.\\n\\n## Scope and Position {#el:scope-and-position}\\n\\nThis RFC decides the **cross-repository compilation flow**: how a compilation whose intent originates in one repository resolves and produces artifacts bound to another. It decides the freshness reconciliation (how a cross-repository pin is evaluated on the gate path without a live cross-graph read), the integration of a change into a foreign repository's product lineage, and the cross-repository trust boundary.\\n\\nIt does not own, and does not move: the pin grammar (D0009 — `repo_id` is already its optional field), the per-repository Graph Store layout and the registry (D0009.C2), the invalidation algebra (P; D0009.C8 keeps marking graph-local), the scheduler's pure-function shape and its capacity fold (D0008), the integration mechanics (D0010.C8), or the trust ladder (D0012). One sentence of position: **the substrate for multi-repository compilation is already decided (D0009.C8, D0008.C3/C6, RFC 0001); this design realizes the flow over it and reconciles the one tension the flow exposes, amending no accepted clause.**\\n\\n## The Decision Structure {#el:decision-structure}\\n\\nOne primary decision and four subordinate questions:\\n\\n1. **The cross-repository pin** — a new pin kind, or D0009's repo-qualified pin realized?\\n2. **Freshness reconciliation** — how is a cross-repository pin's freshness evaluated on the gate path, given D0009.C8 (\\\"lazy at plan/gate time\\\") and D0010.C11 (no live cross-graph read on the gate path)?\\n3. **Cross-repository integration** — how does a change produced under an intent concerning repository A enter repository B's product lineage, and how does the execution-independence guard hold across the two graphs?\\n4. **The trust boundary** — what does a cross-repository pin trust, and where does the v1 single-OS-user trust domain end?\\n\\nThe primary decision is: **cross-repository compilation is realized as linked per-repository compilations exchanging repo-qualified pins, with cross-graph freshness resolved on the gate path against locally-admitted content-addressed evidence — the Foreign Head Attestation — and never a live cross-graph read.** This strengthens the accepted substrate; it re-decides nothing.\\n\\n## The cross-repository pin is D0009's repo-qualified pin {#el:cross-repository-pin}\\n\\nRFC 0001 already says cross-graph references are \\\"ordinary pins qualified by repository identity,\\\" and D0009's pin grammar already carries `repo_id` as an optional field: `artifact_pin := {repo_id?, identity, version_seq?, content_hash}`, with `repo_id` absent ⇒ the local graph. A **cross-repository pin** is simply that pin with `repo_id` present. Nothing new is minted (P2/N11): no pin kind, no artifact role, no invalidation algebra. The `store.Pin` type gains the one optional field the grammar already specifies; every existing record, having never carried it, is byte-identical under an absent-⇒-omitted encoding (the corpus ratchet does not drift — D0009.C5).\\n\\nA cross-repository *compilation* is, as D0009 design states, **linked per-repository compilations exchanging repo-qualified pins**. There is no cross-repository graph and no shared mutable store: repository A's compilation admits into A's graph, repository B's into B's, and the binding between them is a repo-qualified pin plus the evidence that resolves it. Each compilation is governed by its own repository's policy (D0002.C8). The single graph-of-record per repository stands (D0009.C1).\\n\\n## The freshness reconciliation: the Foreign Head Attestation {#el:foreign-head-attestation}\\n\\nTwo accepted statements must be reconciled. D0009.C8: \\\"eager marking is graph-local; cross-graph freshness is lazy at plan/gate time.\\\" D0010.C11: admission is execution-free and content-addressed, and the standing guard fences the gate path against a live cross-graph read. D0009 design was more specific and, read literally, now conflicts with C11: it evaluated cross-graph freshness \\\"at demand time (planning **and gate evaluation**)\\\" — a live foreign read on the gate path.\\n\\nThe reconciliation splits the two demand points that D0009 conflated:\\n\\n- **Planning** (off the gate path) is where the live cross-graph read is lawful. When the Driver plans a compilation that carries a cross-repository pin to repository B, it may read B's Graph Store read surface — through the registry, exactly as D0009 states — and, if B's accepted head for the pinned identity has moved, admit a fresh **Foreign Head Attestation** into the *local* graph. This is an ordinary `observation` pass (D0009: the observation pass is the admission path for world-authored change; from A's perspective, B moving its head *is* world-authored change). The read is demand-driven and lazy — performed at planning, for the pins a plan actually touches — which is the laziness D0009.C8 names.\\n\\n- **Gate and admission** (on the gate path) read **only** the locally-admitted attestation. A cross-repository pin's freshness is evaluated against the latest Foreign Head Attestation for its `(repo_id, identity)` — a local, content-addressed evidence artifact — with no foreign read whatsoever. C11 holds across graphs by construction: the gate path computes hashes and compares content, exactly as for any local pin.\\n\\nA **Foreign Head Attestation** is the Exogenous Change Record evidence kind (D0001) with a typed body capturing one foreign accepted head: `{ repo_id, identity, content_hash, foreign_ledger_seq, seal_domain, as_of }`. It is admitted into the local graph under the ordinary funnel, `stored` placement, with an `evidences` edge to the foreign head it attests. Being evidence, it is never invalidated and its force decays when the hashes it binds change — precisely the semantics cross-graph freshness needs.\\n\\nThis refines D0009.C8 without contradicting it: \\\"lazy at plan/gate time\\\" stands; the attestation is *how* it is lazy at gate time (the gate reads frozen local evidence), and the live read is confined to planning. It extends D0010.C11 across graphs without amending it: the reduction to admitted content and its deterministic evaluation now spans repositories, with the seal/trust boundary of C11's \\\"relative reduction\\\" supplied by D0014.C5.\\n\\n## Cross-repository pin freshness rides the existing algebra {#el:cross-repository-freshness}\\n\\nA cross-repository pin `{repo_id: B, identity: X, content_hash: H}` is **fresh** iff the latest Foreign Head Attestation admitted locally for `(B, X)` reports content hash `H`. The resolution is the existing `PinFresh` algebra over one local indirection: instead of resolving the local head of `X` (which does not exist locally), the driver resolves the local head of the attestation stream for `(B, X)` and compares the foreign content hash it captured against `H`.\\n\\nWhen B's head moves, a fresh attestation reporting `H' ≠ H` is admitted at planning; its admission is an ordinary `artifact_admitted` + `head_movement` on the attestation identity, which fires a staleness wave with `cause.kind: exogenous` (D0009), decaying every local claim bound to the now-stale cross-repository pin — no second mechanism, no cross-graph event routing (marking stays graph-local; D0009.C8). Revalidation before regeneration, no gate over a stale input, and the rest of the one algebra apply unchanged. The attestation itself is evidence and never a freshness input in its own right (it never head-moves in the sense that promotes a claim); it is the *carrier* the cross-repository pin's freshness reads — the `FreshnessPins` treatment of evidence is respected: the pin that carries freshness is the repo-qualified pin, resolved via the attestation, not a pin onto the attestation identity.\\n\\n## Cross-repository integration {#el:cross-repository-integration}\\n\\nA cross-repository compilation may carry a Change Set produced under an intent concerning repository A into repository B's product lineage. Integration is D0010.C8's mechanism, unchanged, executed against **B's** Graph Store: deterministic topological linking of the Verified frontier, E2 realized at admission in B (lanes only stage), B's product ref moved under B's gate-passing transition with `tree_moved` compare-and-set. The producing intent lives in A; the integrating admission lives in B; the two are bound by the cross-repository pin (the Change Set, or the plan that produced it, carries a repo-qualified pin) and the Foreign Head Attestation that resolves it on B's gate path.\\n\\nThe **execution-independence guard (D0010.C11) is held across graphs.** Its three fences extend: the trusted core stays execution-free for cross-graph resolution (attestation comparison is hash arithmetic, no foreign read, no exec); an adversarial or nondeterministic lane can never admit an invalid cross-repository pin (a forged or stale attestation resolves to *stale*, never to a spurious accept — safety is execution-independent across graphs); and the admitted cross-repository result — which pin resolves fresh, which target-state predicate the graph computes — is invariant to execution noise (a byte-identical foreign head yields a byte-identical cross-graph admission regardless of how many times or how badly a lane misbehaved). The standing guard gains cross-graph cases; the property is self-evident of the model and held to the artifact by the guard, exactly as C11 states for the single-graph case.\\n\\n## The cross-repository trust boundary {#el:trust-boundary}\\n\\nA Foreign Head Attestation captures repository B's seal domain, and the local graph trusts it under the v1 keyed-seal discipline (D0012.C2): a cross-repository pin trusts B's graph exactly as far as B's seal domain warrants. Within one workstation's data-home, every registered graph shares the **single OS-user trust domain** (D0009.C10, D0012.C5) — so a same-workstation cross-repository pin is *crash-evidence, not tamper-evidence*, exactly as a local pin, and adds no trust surface. The v1 reach is a fleet of repositories under one workstation's trust domain.\\n\\nA cross-**workstation** attestation — a foreign graph under a different OS-user or a different host, whose seal domain the local workstation cannot vouch for — is **refused in v1** and named as a rung-3 external-anchoring deferral (D0012.C1: external anchoring is deferred and optional). The single-OS-user trust statement of RFCs 0007/0009/0012 is not silently widened; the honest bound is stated. When rung-2 uid isolation lands, cross-repository resolution changes credentials — key readability across per-repository uids — not this contract (D0012.C4: isolation changes credentials, never contracts).\\n\\n## Scheduling needs no amendment {#el:scheduling}\\n\\nRepository-scoped placement is already decided. D0008.C3 folds capacity and attention \\\"at the workstation level over all registered graphs\\\" — the fleet capacity substrate exists. D0008.C6 makes repository policy a placement input that \\\"can restrict, never relax.\\\" The scheduler stays the deterministic pure function of D0008.C1; a run's **target repository** is one more content-addressed placement input, and a repository's policy overlay binds at placement for runs concerning it. Cross-repository compilation adds no scheduler semantics and amends no D0008 clause. This is recorded here so the implementation does not grow a repository-scoped scheduler that shadows D0008.\\n\\n## Alternatives Considered {#el:alternatives-considered}\\n\\n- **A live cross-graph read on the gate path (the literal D0009 design prose).** Rejected: it violates D0010.C11 and the standing guard, couples repository B's gate outcomes to A's live process state, and makes the gate path nondeterministic in a foreign ledger's timing. The Foreign Head Attestation gives the same freshness with a local, content-addressed read.\\n- **A new \\\"cross-repository pin\\\" artifact kind or a new ledger record type for attestations.** Rejected (P2/N11): the repo-qualified pin already exists in the grammar and the Exogenous Change Record already models world-authored change. Minting new ontology would shadow existing homes and drift the corpus ratchet for no capability the existing kinds lack.\\n- **Cross-graph staleness event routing** (a head movement in B pushing marks into A). Rejected: D0009.C8 already rejected it — it couples ledgers and fans out unboundedly across a fleet. Lazy demand-time freshness at planning, frozen into the attestation, is the decided posture.\\n- **A shared cross-repository graph or index either repository writes.** Rejected: it breaks the single graph-of-record per repository (D0009.C1) and introduces a mutable store outside the Doctrine. Linked per-repository compilations exchanging pins keep each graph the sole owner of its truth.\\n- **Widening the trust domain to any registered graph on any host.** Rejected: it claims tamper-evidence the v1 single-uid deployment does not deliver (D0012.C5). Cross-workstation trust is a rung-3 deferral, stated as such.\\n- **A repository-scoped scheduler.** Rejected: it shadows D0008.C1/C3/C6, which already place over the fleet. The target repository is a placement input, not a new scheduler.\\n\\n## Decision (clauses) {#el:decision-clauses}\\n\\n- **D0014.C1 — The cross-repository pin is D0009's repo-qualified pin; nothing new is minted.** A compilation whose intent originates in repository A may require or produce artifacts bound to repository B by a **cross-repository pin** — the repo-qualified pin D0009 already fixed (`artifact_pin := {repo_id?, identity, version_seq?, content_hash}`; `repo_id` absent ⇒ the local graph). RFC 0014 adds no pin kind, no artifact role, and no invalidation algebra (P2/N11; P holds). A cross-repository compilation is **linked per-repository compilations exchanging repo-qualified pins** (D0009 design): each compilation admits into its own repository's graph, each is governed by its own repository's policy (D0002.C8), and the single graph-of-record per repository stands (D0009.C1) — there is no cross-repository graph and no shared mutable store. `store.Pin` gains the one optional `repo_id` field the grammar already specifies; every existing record is byte-identical under absent-⇒-omitted encoding, so the golden corpus does not drift (D0009.C5).\\n- **D0014.C2 — Cross-graph freshness resolves on the gate path against a Foreign Head Attestation, never a live read (refines D0009.C8; extends D0010.C11 across graphs).** A **Foreign Head Attestation** is the Exogenous Change Record evidence kind (D0001) with a typed body capturing one foreign accepted head — `{ repo_id, identity, content_hash, foreign_ledger_seq, seal_domain, as_of }` — admitted into the *local* graph by the observation pass with an `evidences` edge to the head it attests. The live cross-graph read that produces an attestation happens exclusively at **planning**, off the gate path, demand-driven for the pins a plan touches (the laziness D0009.C8 names). The **gate and admission** path reads only the locally-admitted attestation — content-addressed, execution-free, no foreign read — so D0010.C11 holds across graphs by construction. D0009.C8's \\\"lazy at plan/gate time\\\" stands: the attestation is how it is lazy at gate time; only D0009 design's \\\"gate evaluation\\\" as a *live-read* site is struck, superseded by this clause.\\n- **D0014.C3 — Cross-repository pin freshness rides the one invalidation algebra (P).** A cross-repository pin `{repo_id: B, identity: X, content_hash: H}` is fresh iff the latest Foreign Head Attestation admitted locally for `(B, X)` reports content hash `H` — the existing `PinFresh` algebra resolving the local attestation-stream head over one indirection, never a cross-graph read. A moved foreign head is admitted at planning as a fresh attestation reporting `H' ≠ H`; its admission fires a staleness wave with `cause.kind: exogenous` (D0009), decaying every local claim bound to the stale cross-repository pin exactly as any head movement does. No second invalidation mechanism, no cross-graph event routing (marking stays graph-local; D0009.C8); revalidation-before-regeneration and \\\"no gate over a stale input\\\" apply unchanged.\\n- **D0014.C4 — A change under an intent concerning A integrates into B's product lineage under the guard, held across graphs (extends D0010.C8/C11).** Integration is D0010.C8's deterministic topological linking, unchanged, executed against **repository B's** Graph Store: E2 realized at admission in B (lanes only stage), B's product ref moved under B's gate-passing transition with `tree_moved` compare-and-set. The producing intent (A) and the integrating admission (B) are bound by the cross-repository pin (C1) and the Foreign Head Attestation that resolves it (C2). The **execution-independence guard (D0010.C11) is held across graphs**: the trusted core stays execution-free for cross-graph resolution (hash comparison, no foreign read, no exec); an adversarial or nondeterministic lane can never admit an invalid cross-repository pin (a forged or stale attestation resolves to *stale*, never a spurious accept); and the admitted cross-repository result is invariant to execution noise. The standing guard gains cross-graph fences.\\n- **D0014.C5 — The cross-repository trust boundary trusts B's seal domain exactly as far as B warrants; the v1 domain is not widened (affirms D0012).** A Foreign Head Attestation captures B's seal domain; the local graph trusts it under the v1 keyed-seal discipline (D0012.C2). Within one workstation's data-home every registered graph shares the single-OS-user trust domain (D0009.C10, D0012.C5), so a same-workstation cross-repository pin is crash-evidence, exactly as a local pin, and adds no trust surface — the v1 reach is a fleet under one workstation's trust domain. A cross-**workstation** attestation (a foreign graph under a different OS-user or host trust domain) is refused in v1 and named as a rung-3 external-anchoring deferral (D0012.C1); the single-OS-user trust statement is not silently widened. Rung-2 uid isolation lands on this shape as credentials-only changes (D0012.C4).\\n- **D0014.C6 — No new record types, verbs, or leases; scheduling is unamended; the corpus ratchet holds.** The Foreign Head Attestation is the existing exogenous-change-record kind produced by the existing observation pass — no new artifact kind, ledger record type, verb, or lease (D0009.C5's registry unchanged; the golden corpus does not drift). The one governed addition is the attestation's evidence-body schema under `schema/` (a versioned artifact-body kind, not a ledger record type) and the optional `repo_id` pin field D0009 already spec'd. Repository-scoped placement needs no amendment: D0008.C3 folds capacity over all graphs and D0008.C6 makes repository policy a placement input; the scheduler stays D0008.C1's pure function with a run's target repository as one more content-addressed input. Constitutional decisions remain read from the compiler repository's graph, failing closed only on revocation or absence (D0009.C8).\\n\\n## Consequences {#el:consequences}\\n\\nThe compiler's reach becomes a fleet under one workstation's trust domain: a change worked under an intent in one repository is verified and integrated into another's product lineage under that repository's closed gates and Principal acceptance, with provenance bound across the two by content. Every guarantee that made single-repository compilation sound holds across graphs unchanged — execution-free admission (the gate path never reads a foreign graph), one invalidation algebra (cross-graph freshness is the existing algebra over a local attestation), the single graph-of-record per repository (linked compilations exchange pins; neither writes the other's truth), and honest trust bounds (same-workstation crash-evidence; cross-workstation refused and named). The costs are minimal and all strengthenings: one optional pin field (already in the grammar), one evidence-body schema (an existing evidence kind, typed), one plan-time observation that admits attestations, and cross-graph cases added to the standing guard. No new ledger record type, no new verb, no second invalidation mechanism, no scheduler, and no widening of the trust domain enter the system.\\n\\n## Constrains {#el:constrains}\\n\\nThe pin type and its admission/fold encoding (`internal/store/admission.go` `Pin`, `internal/driver/fold.go` `pinsOf`), which surface the optional `repo_id` without drifting the golden corpus; the fold's freshness algebra (`PinFresh`/`FreshnessPins`), which resolves a cross-repository pin against the local Foreign Head Attestation stream and never reads a foreign graph on the gate path; the observation pass and the Driver's planner, which perform the sole lawful live cross-graph read at planning and admit attestations off the gate path; the Foreign Head Attestation evidence-body schema under `schema/`; cross-repository integration against a foreign Graph Store (D0010.C8 mechanics, B-owned product ref, `tree_moved` CAS); the standing execution-independence guard (`internal/driver/soundness_guard_test.go`), which gains cross-graph adversarial and metamorphic fences; the workstation registry as the sole cross-graph resolver (`internal/store/registry.go`); and the trust-claim prose discipline for every cross-repository document (same-workstation crash-evidence; cross-workstation refused until rung 3).\\n\\n## Language Amendments (N8) {#el:language-amendments}\\n\\nDefined here as owning-RFC conventions, glossaried by reference only (no new durable ontology — each names a specialization of an existing home, per P2):\\n\\n- **Cross-Repository Pin** — a repo-qualified pin (`repo_id` present) binding a local artifact to an accepted head in another repository's graph; the D0009 pin grammar's optional form, named. Not a new pin kind.\\n- **Foreign Head Attestation** — the Exogenous Change Record evidence kind (D0001) with a typed body `{ repo_id, identity, content_hash, foreign_ledger_seq, seal_domain, as_of }`, admitted into the local graph by the observation pass, capturing one foreign accepted head. The content-addressed evidence a cross-repository pin's freshness resolves against on the gate path (D0014.C2). Not a new artifact kind.\\n- **Cross-Repository Compilation** — linked per-repository compilations exchanging repo-qualified pins (D0009 design), each admitting into its own repository's graph under its own repository's policy. Not a cross-repository graph.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers {#el:rationale-pointers}\\n\\nRFC 0001 design (one graph per repository; cross-graph references as repo-qualified pins; the Exogenous Change Record). RFC 0009 design and D0009.C1/C2/C5/C8/C10 — the `### Cross-graph pins` section (registry resolution; linked per-repository compilations; `Get(pin)` vs `ResolveHead(identity)`; the pin grammar's optional `repo_id`); the observation pass as the admission path for world-authored change. Advancing `striatum-next` toward `multi-repository-compilation-ready@1`.\\n\\n## Problem {#el:problem}\\n\\nThe compiler compiles one repository — its own. Every accepted decision already anticipates more than one. RFC 0001 states it flatly: \\\"One artifact graph exists per target repository; the compiler's own repository is itself a target repository. Cross-graph references are ordinary pins qualified by repository identity.\\\" D0009 fixed the substrate to match: `repo_id` bound at genesis, per-repository Graph Stores under `graphs/\\u003crepo_id\\u003e/`, a workstation registry of registered graphs, a pin grammar in which `repo_id` is an optional field (`artifact_pin := {repo_id?, identity, version_seq?, content_hash}`; absent ⇒ local), and the rule that \\\"eager marking is graph-local; cross-graph freshness is lazy at plan/gate time\\\" (D0009.C8). Every piece of substrate for this exists and is idle: repo-qualified pins have no resolver, the registry has no cross-graph reader on the compilation path, and the \\\"linked per-repository compilations exchanging repo-qualified pins\\\" model named in D0009 design has no realization.\\n\\nLeaving the flow undecided invites the freshness reconciliation to be answered by accident in code — a live cross-graph read slipped onto the gate path in the name of the D0009 prose, silently breaking C11 and the guard that holds it. principal halbritt. Advancing `striatum-next` toward `fleet-knowledge-is-compiled`. Follows the proposal; enacts Discovery 0020 with one new subject, one new pass, and Evidence exactly as it is.\\n\\n## Scope and Position {#el:scope-and-position}\\n\\nThis design fixes *what should exist* for the fleet to hold its own knowledge under the compiler's guarantees. Content produced by the compiler is a **Product Artifact**. The claim model already computes exactly the dynamics the desired state names — pointed now at a Product element instead of a code head.\\n\\n3. **The fleet's evidence reaches the subject through the wire that already carries foreign state.** The Foreign Head Attestation (D0014) freezes a foreign head as local, immutable evidence; the knowledge pass consumes those attestations. No new kind, no new wire, no live cross-graph read.\\n\\nWhat remains genuinely new is one transformation — distilling admitted evidence into a maintained Product — and that is one pass.\\n\\n## Knowledge is the fleet-knowledge subject's element-structured Product {#el:knowledge-is-product}\\n\\nThe `fleet-knowledge` subject owns one artifact graph (Discovery 0017); it is a new *subject*, not a new ontology noun. Its Product Artifact is **element-structured** — the element grain decision records already carry for element-grain linking (RFC 0001) — and each element is one **knowledge element**: a scoped, falsifiable statement (the lesson), the set of evidence bindings that support it, and the applicability scope that says where it holds (a backend, a language, a pass class, a deployment shape). The Product is durable, versioned, provenance-bearing, and has exactly one producing pass run per version (P1); it is never hand-authored. A knowledge element is therefore neither the product nor the instance *of the subject that taught it* — it is the Product of a distinct subject, which is precisely the third category Discovery 0020 names.\\n\\n## The knowledge-promotion pass {#el:knowledge-promotion-pass}\\n\\nOne new pass, `knowledge-promotion`, maintains the Product. It **consumes** the fleet's admitted evidence — Review Ledgers, Verification Reports, and Exogenous Change Records — resolved from foreign subjects as Foreign Head Attestations, together with the current knowledge Product head. It **produces** the next version of the `fleet-knowledge` Product Artifact, element by element: proposing new elements, binding freshly corroborating evidence to existing ones, and letting superseded bindings lapse. Its distillation — reading many attestations and stating a lesson — is a **nondeterministic capability carried by a lane** (the compiler's thesis: compile the outputs of nondeterministic providers into gated truth); the Driver plans, gates, and admits the resulting Product exactly as it admits any artifact, acquiring no judgment. The pass is the only new durable concept this RFC introduces, and it is a new instance of an existing P2 category (compiler pass), entering the language through the N8 amendment below.\\n\\n## Sufficiency and independence are the claim model {#el:sufficiency-independence}\\n\\nA knowledge element binds the content hashes of the Foreign Head Attestations that support it, and its trustworthiness is `claim(element@v)` — computed, never stored (W8). The lattice reads directly onto the desired state:\\n\\n- **Designed** — the element is a proposed candidate: stated by the pass, well-formed, but not yet corroborated by admitted evidence.\\n- **Asserted** — supported by admitted evidence that is *not* independent: one subject's own runs, or co-blind lanes sharing provenance ancestry. A lesson believed on a single anecdote stops here, by construction.\\n- **Verified** — supported by binding closure over evidence that is **execution-independent** (RFC 0005: \\\"minting evidence must share no provenance ancestry — lane, backend session, synthesis lineage\\\"). A lesson corroborated by two independent subjects — praxis and engram, distinct models even — is Verified; the same lesson from one subject repeated is not.\\n\\nPromotion to Verified is minted by a **Review gate** (independent judgment closing on \\\"the corroboration is real and independent\\\") — an existing gate class, not a new one. \\\"Sufficient and independent\\\" is not a new threshold to invent; it is the promotion rule the compiler already enforces for every claim.\\n\\n## Decay is supersession {#el:decay-is-supersession}\\n\\nKnowledge decays with no actor demoting anything (P6): when a bound Foreign Head Attestation's content hash moves — because the source subject's evidence changed, the failure was fixed, the pattern was superseded — the binding no longer matches and the computed level falls, `Verified → Asserted → Designed`. A lesson about a bug outlives the bug only until the fixing evidence lands; then it decays. Evidence is never invalidated; its force lapses (RFC 0003/0005). Stale knowledge retires itself.\\n\\n## Cross-fleet sourcing rides the existing wire {#el:cross-fleet-sourcing}\\n\\nThe pass reads foreign evidence exactly as any cross-repository compilation reads foreign state: it observes the foreign subject's evidence head at planning, off the gate path, and freezes it as a local Exogenous Change Record — the Foreign Head Attestation (D0014) — before consuming it. No cross-repository graph, no shared mutable store, no new evidence kind, and no live cross-graph read on the gate or admission path: execution-free, content-addressed admission holds across graphs (D0010.C11), and the standing guard extends unchanged. Cross-fleet sourcing is a new *use* of the wire, never a new wire.\\n\\n## Bootstrapping rides the same wire {#el:bootstrapping}\\n\\nA new subject or a new pass begins from the fleet's knowledge by observing the `fleet-knowledge` subject's head — the same Foreign Head Attestation every cross-fleet read already uses — and reading the knowledge elements whose scope it matches, at the level they currently compute. Knowledge is consumed where head state is already consumed; nothing new carries it into a subject.\\n\\n## Serving is a derived projection {#el:serving}\\n\\nAny model-readable retrieval surface over the knowledge Product — a search index, an embedding store — is a derived, rebuildable projection under the Derived-State Doctrine (D0002.C2): computed from the Product plus the ledger, discardable and reconstructible, never a second system of record. The truth is the gated, computed Product; the index is a cache. This is the seam through which an external capability (an engram-shaped retrieval service) may serve knowledge without ever owning it.\\n\\n## Alternatives Considered {#el:alternatives-considered}\\n\\n- **A new distilled-observation evidence kind (a thirteenth artifact kind).** Rejected: knowledge is Product, not Evidence; its inputs are already-existing evidence. A new kind pays the Cost of a Noun (Discovery 0018) for a home the Product role already provides.\\n- **Knowledge as a Claim.** Rejected: a Claim is a contentless computed level over one artifact version (W8); knowledge is content over many. Knowledge *has* a claim; it is not one.\\n- **Knowledge as Decision Records.** Rejected: a Decision Record is the generated interface of exactly one RFC identity (RFC 0001); fleet knowledge spans backends, deployments, and conventions that are not RFC-level architecture. Architectural knowledge still graduates into RFCs by the existing path; this subject holds the rest.\\n- **An independent knowledge project owning the truth (e.g., an embedding store).** Rejected: it is the \\\"accumulated as notes or prompt cargo\\\" the desired state replaces, and a second system of record the Derived-State Doctrine forbids. An external *retrieval* capability is admissible only as a derived projection.\\n- **A new cross-graph wire for findings.** Rejected: the Foreign Head Attestation already transports foreign evidence content-addressed and off the gate path; findings are foreign evidence, observed.\\n- **Storing the computed level on the element.** Rejected: W8 — claims are computed, never stored; any persisted level is a derived cache, not truth.\\n- **A new promotion gate class.** Rejected: promotion to Verified is independent judgment closing a verdict — a Review gate, already defined.\\n\\n## Decision (clauses) {#el:decision-clauses}\\n\\n- **C1 — The fleet-knowledge subject.** A `fleet-knowledge` subject owns one artifact graph (Discovery 0017). It is a subject, not a new ontology noun; no P2 category is added by it.\\n- **C2 — Knowledge is that subject's element-structured Product Artifact.** Each element is a scoped falsifiable statement with its supporting evidence bindings and applicability scope; the Product is durable, versioned, provenance-bearing, one producing pass run per version (P1), never hand-authored.\\n- **C3 — The knowledge-promotion pass.** A single new pass consumes admitted evidence (Foreign Head Attestations of foreign Review Ledgers, Verification Reports, and Exogenous Change Records) plus the current knowledge head, and produces the next Product version. Its distillation is a lane; its admission is Driver-gated. It is the sole new durable concept (N8).\\n- **C4 — Evidence is unchanged.** The four evidence kinds stand exactly; the pass mints no new evidence and reinterprets none. Cross-fleet inputs are existing evidence observed as Foreign Head Attestations (D0014).\\n- **C5 — Trust is the computed claim over the element (W8).** A knowledge element binds its supporting attestations' content hashes; `claim(element@v)` is computed from those bindings, never stored. Any persisted level is a derived cache.\\n- **C6 — Promotion is binding closure plus independence (RFC 0005).** Designed = proposed; Asserted = non-independent support; Verified = binding closure over execution-independent corroboration, minted by a Review gate. No new gate class, no new threshold.\\n- **C7 — Decay is bound-hash movement (P6).** When a supporting attestation's hash moves, the element's level falls with no actor demoting it; superseded knowledge retires itself. Evidence force lapses; evidence is never invalidated.\\n- **C8 — Sourcing and bootstrapping ride the Foreign Head Attestation (D0014, D0010.C11).** The pass reads foreign evidence, and downstream subjects read the knowledge subject's head, only through frozen local attestations off the gate path; no cross-repository graph, no shared store, no live cross-graph read.\\n- **C9 — Serving is a derived projection (D0002.C2).** Any retrieval index over the Product is rebuildable and discardable; it is never a source of truth. An external retrieval capability may serve it, never own it.\\n- **C10 — The Driver stays deterministic.** Distillation is a lane; the Driver plans, gates, and admits the knowledge Product execution-free and content-addressed, acquiring no judgment.\\n- **C11 — The existence proof.** `fleet-knowledge-is-compiled` is satisfied when this decision is generated, the promotion pass is delivered and dual-signal verified, and the fleet-knowledge subject holds at least one knowledge element that computes to Verified from execution-independent cross-fleet evidence.\\n\\n## Consequences {#el:consequences}\\n\\nThe fleet stops forgetting: a lesson learned once is held under gated truth, corroborated across subjects, and retired when superseded, rather than surviving only in a context window or a human's memory. New subjects and passes begin from what the fleet knows. The cost is one pass and one subject; Evidence, the claim model, the gate classes, the invalidation algebra, the ledger registry, and the scheduler are untouched. The standing risk this forecloses is a side memory grown beside the graph — an embedding cargo that no gate tested and no decay retired; the Derived-State Doctrine and the claim model keep knowledge compiled, not accumulated.\\n\\n## Constrains {#el:constrains}\\n\\n- **P1** — every knowledge Product version has exactly one producing pass run; the raw material enters as evidence through existing passes; nothing is hand-authored.\\n- **P2 / N8 / N11 / Discovery 0018** — exactly one new noun (the pass), shadowing no existing home; the subject and the knowledge-as-Product are instances of existing concepts.\\n- **W8 / P6 (RFC 0005)** — claims computed never stored; Verified requires binding closure and provenance independence; decay is arithmetic on bound-hash movement.\\n- **D0002.C2** — the knowledge graph and any serving index are derived, rebuildable projections; neither is a system of record.\\n- **D0010.C11 / D0014** — execution-free, content-addressed admission across graphs; cross-fleet evidence frozen as Foreign Head Attestations before consumption; no live cross-graph read.\\n- **W4** — world-authored fact still enters only through the observation pass; the knowledge pass consumes admitted evidence, not an unbounded world read.\\n\\n## Language Amendments (N8) {#el:language-amendments}\\n\\n- **`knowledge-promotion` pass** — a compiler pass that reads the fleet's admitted evidence and produces or updates the fleet-knowledge subject's Product Artifact, one knowledge element at a time, under a Review promotion gate. It shadows no existing home: not `observation` (admits world-authored fact as evidence; never distills across it), not `decision-generation` (distills one RFC identity into a Decision Record), not a `review`/`verification` posture (attests one artifact; never generalizes across the fleet). No other term is new: \\\"fleet-knowledge subject\\\" instances *subject*, \\\"knowledge\\\" instances *Product Artifact*, and sourcing, trust, and decay instance Foreign Head Attestation, Claim, and decay already defined.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers {#el:rationale-pointers}\\n\\nDiscovery 0020 (knowledge is neither product nor instance); Discovery 0017 (one graph per subject; the non-repository generalization it left floating); Discovery 0019 (the instance/product cut and the missing promotion path); Discovery 0018 (the Cost of a Noun); RFC 0001 (artifact roles, P1, P2, element grain); RFC 0003 (the four evidence kinds); RFC 0005 / W8 / P6 (claims computed not stored, binding closure, independence, arithmetic decay); D0014 / RFC 0014 (Foreign Head Attestation); D0010.C11 (execution-free admission); D0002.C2 (Derived-State Doctrine).\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0015-fleet-knowledge/proposal.md\": \"# RFC 0015 Proposal: Fleet Knowledge {#el:rfc-0015-proposal-fleet-knowledge}\\n\\n## Status {#el:status}\\n\\nProposed for RQ-8043 (`striatum-next/passes/fleet-knowledge`); principal halbritt. Advancing `striatum-next` toward `fleet-knowledge-is-compiled`. Names Discovery 0020 (Knowledge Is Neither Product Nor Instance) and enacts it under the Principal's cost constraint: one new subject, one new compiler pass, Evidence exactly as it is.\\n\\n## Problem {#el:problem}\\n\\nThe compiler is accumulating knowledge it has no home for. Every real subject teaches it something — a backend failure mode, a verification pattern, a reusable architectural theorem, a deployment lesson, a handoff convention, a discovered invariant, a simplification of the language — and that knowledge is neither the product nor the instance (Discovery 0020). It is not the product: the product \\\"defines the compiler — language, decisions, runtime, schemas, policies, explanations, declarations — and ships\\\" (Discovery 0019), and a lesson is none of those. It is not the instance: an instance \\\"describes one execution… and belongs to the instance\\\" (Discovery 0019), and a lesson is true across many executions, owned by none.\\n\\nToday that third thing survives only where a context window or a human still holds it — scattered across plan logs, discoveries, reviews, and prompt cargo, decaying the moment the window closes. The compiler that computes truth for everyone else forgets what it learns, and rediscovers it subject after subject.\\n\\nThe ontology has left exactly this gap open, twice by name. Discovery 0017 generalized the compiler to subjects but recorded that \\\"the generalization to non-repository subjects still floats.\\\" Discovery 0019 placed *all* observations on the instance side — \\\"plan logs, handoffs, pass narratives, deep reviews, satisfied one-shot target states, observations… belongs to the instance\\\" — with **no promotion path** from that instance evidence to reusable, product-level, model-readable knowledge. And the cross-graph wire that exists carries only head state: the Foreign Head Attestation \\\"freezes what it saw into a local, immutable piece of evidence… capturing the foreign `{repo_id, identity, content_hash, seal_domain, as_of}`\\\" (D0014) — a pin, not a finding. Nothing distills the fleet's evidence into knowledge, nothing holds that knowledge durably, and nothing lets a new subject begin from it.\\n\\n## Motivation {#el:motivation}\\n\\nSelf-hosting and the fleet are in force: praxis (a Python product) and engram (a knowledge-graph project) have each earned Verified through the same funnel, and a second, independent model reproduced the pattern down to its specific choices. The fleet is real, and a real fleet learns. The next reach is that the fleet's learning be held under the same guarantees as everything else it produces — derived from evidence, gated on sufficiency and independence, decaying when superseded, provenance-total — rather than accumulated as notes that no gate ever tested and no decay ever retired.\\n\\nLeaving this undecided invites the wrong architecture by default: a side database of embeddings or a prompt-cargo memory grown alongside the graph — which is precisely the \\\"accumulated as notes or prompt cargo\\\" the desired state exists to replace, and a second source of truth the Derived-State Doctrine forbids. Deciding once, and deciding it *inside* the compiler, keeps knowledge *compiled* — its truth gated, its confidence computed, its staleness arithmetic — and keeps the whole capability a strengthening of the accepted ontology rather than a new mechanism beside it.\\n\\n## Target State {#el:target-state}\\n\\nA recorded decision that enacts Discovery 0020 as a strengthening of the accepted ontology, stated so that its cost is exactly one new subject and one new pass:\\n\\n- **Knowledge is the fleet-knowledge subject's Product Artifact — not a new noun.** A dedicated `fleet-knowledge` subject owns one graph (Discovery 0017; a subject is not a new ontology noun). Knowledge is therefore *neither product nor instance of the subject that taught it* — it becomes the Product of a distinct subject whose whole purpose is knowledge.\\n\\n- **One new pass distills it.** A `knowledge-promotion` pass (analysis/transform class) reads the fleet's existing evidence and produces or updates the knowledge Product. Its candidate distillation is a nondeterministic capability carried by a lane (Striatum's thesis: compile the outputs of nondeterministic providers); its promotion is gated by existing gate classes. This pass is the *only* genuinely new noun, and it is a new instance of an existing P2 category (compiler pass), not a new category.\\n\\n- **Evidence is sourced across the fleet with no new kind.** The pass's inputs are the fleet's existing evidence — Review Ledgers, Verification Reports, and Exogenous Change Records of failures — observed from foreign subjects through the *existing* Foreign Head Attestation (D0014, the observation pass's Exogenous Change Record). A new *use* of the wire, not a new evidence kind. Evidence keeps its four kinds exactly.\\n\\n- **Trust and decay are the claim model, unchanged.** A knowledge element's trustworthiness is `claim(element@v)` — computed, never stored (W8). \\\"Promoted only when supported by sufficient evidence\\\" is **binding closure**; \\\"and independent\\\" is the existing **Verified independence rule** (a lesson resting on one instance's self-report is aliased and cannot reach Verified); \\\"stale or superseded knowledge naturally decays\\\" is **arithmetic decay on bound-hash movement** — supersession *is* decay (RFC 0005, P6). The truth is the gated Product; the index is a cache.\\n\\nIf instead the capability requires re-deciding an accepted clause or minting a second new noun, the amendment is explicit and the owning decision regenerated. The expectation, tested by the design, is that it does not: the subject, the Product Artifact role, the claim model, the four evidence kinds, and the Foreign Head Attestation suffice, and one pass completes them.\\n\\n## Non-Goals {#el:non-goals}\\n\\n- **No new evidence kind.** Evidence keeps its four kinds (Review Ledger, Receipt, Verification Report, Exogenous Change Record) exactly. Knowledge is Product, not Evidence; its inputs are existing evidence observed cross-fleet.\\n- **No new artifact role and no Claim contortion.** Knowledge is a Product Artifact; it is not a Claim (a claim is a contentless computed level over one artifact version, W8) and does not become one.\\n- **No new claim mechanism, gate class, invalidation algebra, ledger record type, verb, or lease.** Promotion is binding closure + independence; decay is bound-hash movement; both stand as decided.\\n- **No independent knowledge project as source of truth.** An external store with its own truth is the \\\"accumulation\\\" the desired state replaces and a second system of record the Derived-State Doctrine forbids. The `fleet-knowledge` subject is a new subject, not a new noun.\\n- **Every knowledge element has exactly one producing pass run (P1); nothing is hand-authored.** The knowledge Product is produced by the promotion pass; the raw material enters as evidence through existing passes.\\n- **Claims stay computed, never stored (W8 / P6).** A knowledge element's level is computed from its evidence bindings; any persisted level is a derived cache. Verified requires binding closure and provenance independence; it decays when bound hashes move.\\n- **The Derived-State Doctrine holds (D0002.C2).** The knowledge graph and any serving index are derived, rebuildable projections over evidence + ledger; neither is a new system of record.\\n- **Execution-free, content-addressed admission holds across graphs (D0010.C11).** No live cross-graph read on the gate/admission path; cross-fleet evidence is frozen locally as Foreign Head Attestations before the pass consumes it.\\n- **The Driver stays deterministic.** The nondeterministic distillation lives in a lane; the Driver plans, gates, and admits the knowledge Product as it does any artifact — it acquires no judgment.\\n\\n## Language Amendment (N8) {#el:language-amendment}\\n\\nOne term enters the ubiquitous language:\\n\\n- **`knowledge-promotion` pass** — a compiler pass (analysis/transform class) that reads the fleet's admitted evidence and produces or updates the fleet-knowledge subject's Product Artifact, one knowledge element at a time, under a promotion gate. Advancing `striatum-next` toward `acceptance-follows-review`. Follows the proposal; enacts the grant RFC 0006 named, with zero new nouns.\\n\\n## Scope and Position {#el:scope-and-position}\\n\\nThis design fixes *what should exist* for routine acceptance to stop waiting on a human hand without any authority moving. It sits on the delegation model (RFC 0006 §Delegation — data in `policy/gates.yaml`, two enforcement rules, machine-checked), on the gate trichotomy (D0005.C4 — the acceptance predicates already read \\\"the Principal, or policy the Principal has explicitly delegated\\\"), and on the review machinery (independent judgment, closed verdicts, independence enforced by placement). It adds no gate class, no record type, no verb semantics, and no term: only the explicit grant that has been contemplated and never made, plus the declared conditions and guardrails that make the grant safe to hold.\\n\\n## The Decision Structure {#el:decision-structure}\\n\\nThree observations collapse the capability onto existing machinery:\\n\\n1. **Acceptance conflates two things: judgment and authority.** By the time a candidate reaches an IR acceptance gate, the judgment has been rendered — review gates closed on independent verdicts. What the acceptance act adds is authority: the deployment's decision that this work matters enough, or is uncertain enough, to bear a human's name. For most ladder positions on most subjects, it adds nothing else.\\n\\n2. **Where the judgment is unanimous and the subject is quiet, the authority act is a deterministic function of ledger records.** \\\"Unanimous clean review, fresh inputs, no open escalation, nothing significant\\\" is a predicate the Driver can compute — the same computational class as every check gate. Computing it is not judgment; it is reading the judgment already recorded.\\n\\n3. **The delegation model already carries the grant shape.** Scope, conditions, expiry, `authorized_by`, mechanical refusal, exercised-delegation recording: all delivered and proven by the harvest-issuance grant. Graduated acceptance is a second entry in an existing table, not a second mechanism.\\n\\nWhat remains genuinely new is one decision: *which* acceptances may follow review mechanically, under *what* conditions, with *what* escape hatches — and that is this RFC.\\n\\n## The grant and its scope {#el:grant-scope}\\n\\nThe grant covers exactly the three IR acceptance gates: `proposal-acceptance`, `design-acceptance`, `implementation-plan-acceptance`. Nothing else is acceptance-delegable under it:\\n\\n- **Decision-record acceptance is never in scope.** D0005.C4/C7 stand; this RFC does not grant it; the Driver's existing machine-check (an acceptance-scope delegation reaching decision-role artifacts refuses without a pinning decision record from an RFC that grants *that*) holds against this grant by construction, because D0016 grants only the three IR gates.\\n- **Rejection is never in scope.** Policy may accept or wait; only the Principal rejects. Rejection steers revision — that is judgment, and it stays personal.\\n- **Escalation resolution and gate override are never in scope.** They are dispositions of open questions, owned by the standing rule: no pre-scripted resolutions, ever.\\n\\n## Significance: fail-open below RFC grain {#el:significance}\\n\\nThe Principal's ruling, fixed in-session: the default is delegable, and significance is the exception the Principal declares — not the reverse. Curating an allowlist of routine work recreates the noticing burden this RFC exists to remove; curating the short list of what deserves personal eyes does not.\\n\\nMechanically, a candidate's acceptance is delegable unless any of these holds, each failing toward the human:\\n\\n- the subject is an **RFC identity** (`rfcs/*`): architecture is always personal, at every rung of its ladder;\\n- the subject or target matches a **declared exclusion pattern** on the policy entry (Principal-curated, like the backlog: read-only to the Driver);\\n- the compilation request carries a **significance mark** set at issuance — one flag, pinning everything under that request personal;\\n- **any exclusion evaluation fails or cannot be computed** — ambiguity is significance.\\n\\n## The condition set {#el:conditions}\\n\\nAt gate evaluation, the Driver closes a delegable IR acceptance gate mechanically iff *all* of the following hold, each a predicate over ledger records, each failure leaving the gate waiting for the Principal exactly as today:\\n\\n1. **The delegation stands**: the `graduated-acceptance` entry is present, `enabled`, unexpired, and its scope covers this gate and subject (RFC 0006's mechanical refusal, unchanged).\\n2. **The judgment is unanimous**: every review gate required at this ladder position closed with accept verdicts — no rejecting or mixed verdict — over the *exact candidate version* (evidence bound by content hash; the independence rules are the review placement's, already enforced, not re-litigated here).\\n3. **The subject is quiet**: no open escalation names the subject or the request.\\n4. **Nothing is stale**: no gate passes over a stale input — standing law, restated as a condition so the delegated path carries it explicitly.\\n5. **No personal pin**: the Principal has not previously rejected a candidate at this (identity, position).\\n\\n## Personal-rejection pinning {#el:rejection-pinning}\\n\\nA Principal rejection at a ladder position is a signal that the Principal has entered that loop deliberately. From that rejection on, the position is personal for that identity — across revisions, regardless of how clean the revised candidate's reviews are. The revision machinery is unchanged (the rejection reason steers the fresh revision, as delivered); what changes is only that policy never closes a loop the Principal opened. The pin is per (identity, position), computed from the ledger's acceptance-class `gate_result` history — no new record.\\n\\n## Attribution and the retrospective queue {#el:attribution-queue}\\n\\nA delegated acceptance is an ordinary acceptance-class `gate_result` whose authority is the `delegation_ref`, carrying an `authority_proof` that pins the condition evidence: the review-ledger content hashes, the escalation-scan bound, the freshness bound, the exclusion evaluation. Nothing ever claims the Principal's identity; every exercised delegation is recorded on the record it licensed (RFC 0006 rule two, verbatim).\\n\\nEvery delegated acceptance enters the **retrospective queue**: a computed, ledger-derived projection (never stored truth) of delegation-authority acceptances not yet acknowledged by the Principal, surfaced by `status`. Acknowledgment rides the existing status-store queue fold — the `defer` pattern: ledger-visible triage without a new record type. The queue converts pre-hoc gating into post-hoc audit; it is the guarantee that delegation removes the Principal from the loop's *latency*, never from its *visibility*. The entry MAY declare `max_unacknowledged`: when the queue exceeds it, the class suspends until the Principal catches up — declared backpressure, defaulting to absent (the Principal declined a rate cap; this bound is the principled version, opt-in).\\n\\n## Kill switch, expiry, and the revocation asymmetry {#el:kill-switch}\\n\\n- **The kill switch is immediate and RFC-free**: `enabled: false`, or removing the entry, suspends the class at the next gate evaluation. Narrowing — shrinking scope, adding exclusions, shortening expiry — is always a plain policy edit. Only *granting* acceptance delegation required an RFC; stopping it never does.\\n- **Expiry is mandatory**: an acceptance-scope entry without `expires` is malformed and refused. Renewal is a deliberate Principal act, the same shape as the harvest-issuance grant.\\n- **The grant pins its decision**: any acceptance-scope delegation entry must carry `authorized_by` pinning the accepted, fresh D0016. Revoking D0016 fails the entire class closed — the RFC-grant discipline, machine-checked, extended from the decision-role case to all acceptance scope.\\n\\n## Capacity: the ceiling, raised as named {#el:capacity}\\n\\nRFC 0006 stated the v1 Principal ceiling out loud and named its one lawful exit; this is it. Delegated closures bypass the `principal_attention` capacity pool — the pool continues to price exactly what still needs the human: significant work, RFC ladders, rejections, escalations, decision records, the retrospective queue. The conditions never read capacity, and capacity pressure never touches this or any gate (standing law): graduated acceptance raises throughput by removing re-judgment, never by cheapening judgment.\\n\\n## Alternatives Considered {#el:alternatives-considered}\\n\\n- **An agent principal holding acceptance (an LLM judge).** Rejected: it reintroduces nondeterministic judgment at the authority seam — the compiler's thesis run backwards — and lands adjacent to the pre-scripted-resolution failure mode the standing rule exists to kill. The delegate is deterministic policy or nothing.\\n- **Fail-closed allowlist significance.** Rejected by the Principal's ruling: allowlist curation recreates the noticing burden. The constitution is held instead by the categorical exclusions (RFC grain, decision records, rejection) plus declared opt-out.\\n- **Skipping the acceptance gate when review is clean.** Rejected: that erases the authority layer instead of delegating it — the gate trichotomy keeps acceptance a distinct class, and the delegated `gate_result` is what carries attribution, the queue, and the kill switch. An absent gate carries nothing.\\n- **Batch-acceptance ergonomics as the fix.** Rejected as sufficient: `accept --batch` (designed, unshipped) optimizes the *spending* of attention; the ceiling is the *need* for it. Both can exist; only this one raises the ceiling.\\n- **A new auto-acceptance record type.** Rejected: the acceptance-class `gate_result` with delegation authority already carries the fact (P2 — strengthen the existing home).\\n- **A per-drive rate cap.** Declined by the Principal. The blast-radius bounds are the kill switch, expiry, exclusions, personal-rejection pinning, and the opt-in `max_unacknowledged` backpressure — each tied to visibility or authority, where a rate cap is tied to neither: it converts throughput back into queue latency without adding a guarantee the retrospective queue does not already give.\\n\\n## Decision (clauses) {#el:decision-clauses}\\n\\n- **C1 — The grant.** Graduated acceptance is a delegation class over exactly `proposal-acceptance`, `design-acceptance`, and `implementation-plan-acceptance`. Decision-record acceptance, rejection, escalation resolution, and gate override are never in its scope (D0005.C4/C7 stand).\\n- **C2 — The delegate is deterministic policy.** The Driver evaluates the declared conditions at gate evaluation and appends the closing `gate_result` itself; no agent principal may hold acceptance scope. Where the conditions do not decide, the gate waits for the Principal. The Driver acquires no judgment.\\n- **C3 — Significance is fail-open below RFC grain.** Delegable by default; RFC-identity subjects (`rfcs/*`) always personal; policy exclusion patterns and a request-level significance mark opt back to personal; any exclusion-evaluation failure is significance.\\n- **C4 — The condition set is conjunctive and mechanical.** Delegation standing (present, enabled, unexpired, in scope); unanimous accept verdicts on all required review gates over the exact candidate version; no open escalation naming subject or request; no stale input; no personal pin. Each is a predicate over ledger records; each failure leaves the gate personal.\\n- **C5 — Personal-rejection pinning.** A Principal rejection at (identity, position) pins that position personal thereafter, across revisions, computed from acceptance-class `gate_result` history.\\n- **C6 — Attribution is honest and total.** The delegated `gate_result` carries the `delegation_ref` and an `authority_proof` pinning the condition evidence; it never carries the Principal's identity; every exercised delegation is recorded on the record it licensed.\\n- **C7 — The retrospective queue.** Every delegated acceptance is surfaced by `status` until the Principal acknowledges it; the queue is a computed projection (no new record type; acknowledgment rides the status-store queue fold). An entry MAY declare `max_unacknowledged`, suspending the class when exceeded; absent means unbounded.\\n- **C8 — Kill switch, expiry, decision pin.** `enabled: false` or entry removal suspends immediately; `expires` is mandatory and renewal deliberate; every acceptance-scope entry must pin the accepted, fresh D0016 via `authorized_by`, so revoking D0016 fails the class closed. Narrowing is always a policy edit; only granting required this RFC.\\n- **C9 — The constitution is untouched.** Escalations queue, refused gates wait, decision records and naming stay personal, and the no-pre-scripted-resolutions rule is intact: a delegated acceptance is neither an escalation resolution nor an override — it closes only never-refused gates after independent judgment has been rendered, and says so in its attribution.\\n- **C10 — Capacity is bypassed, never consulted.** Delegated closures do not draw on the `principal_attention` pool; the conditions never read capacity; capacity pressure never touches the gate.\\n- **C11 — Claims are unchanged.** A delegated acceptance moves accepted heads identically to a personal one; it mints no evidence and touches no claim computation or level.\\n- **C12 — The existence proof.** `acceptance-follows-review@1` is satisfied when this decision is generated, the evaluation is delivered through the funnel with its standing guards executing inside verification (accepts iff all conditions; refuses on each single-condition failure; never a decision-role gate; pinning; kill-switch immediacy), and at least one real IR acceptance has closed under the full condition set, ledger-attributed and retrospectively surfaced.\\n\\n## Consequences {#el:consequences}\\n\\nThe Principal's attention becomes what the constitution says it is: authority, spent on significance, rejection, escalation, and decision records — not a mechanical restatement of unanimous reviews. The keystone's autonomous issuance stops piling acceptances against a fixed budget; a full IR ladder on a routine pass subject runs review-gated end to end and queues for the human zero times, while every rung it closed remains visible in the retrospective queue and reversible by the kill switch. The cost is zero new nouns and one new policy entry. The standing risk — authority quietly eroding into automation — is held by the categorical exclusions (C1), the honest attribution (C6), the queue (C7), the decision pin (C8), and the fact that every ambiguity resolves toward the human (C3, C4).\\n\\n## Constrains {#el:constrains}\\n\\n- **D0005.C4/C7** — decision-role acceptance stays personal; this grant's scope is machine-checked against it.\\n- **P4** — passes produce; gates permit; the Driver transitions. The delegated closure is the Driver appending an authority fact under declared policy, then transitioning.\\n- **RFC 0006 §Delegation** — both enforcement rules extend verbatim to this entry; the v1 ceiling paragraph is delivered by this RFC, not amended.\\n- **The Driver stays deterministic** — the conditions are the check-gate computational class; underspecified means wait.\\n- **W7 / RFC 0005** — gate results keep their semantics; no new verdict values, no gate class added.\\n- **P10** — no hidden lifecycle state: the pin, the queue, and the exercised grants are all computed from ledger records.\\n\\n## Language Amendments (N8) {#el:language-amendments}\\n\\nNone. **Graduated acceptance** is the proper name of the delegation this RFC grants — an instance of RFC 0006's delegation model exercised by the Driver under declared policy — not a new P2 category, gate class, verdict, or record type. RFC 0006 reserved the name; D0016 fills it.\\n\\n## Rationale Pointers {#el:rationale-pointers}\\n\\nRFC 0006 (§Delegation, the acceptance verbs, the v1 Principal ceiling and its named exit; agent-principal boundaries); D0005.C4/C7 (gate trichotomy; decision-role delegation prices an RFC); RFC 0005 / W7 (gate-result semantics; no gate passes over a stale input); RFC 0008 (the `principal_attention` pool; capacity never touches gates); `planner-auto-schedules-the-backlog@1` (the keystone that made this urgent); `progress-needs-no-principal@1` (the carve this RFC enacts at the acceptance layer); the standing Principal rule of 2026-07-06 (no pre-scripted resolutions — C9's boundary); the Principal's directive of 2026-07-07, verbatim in the deferrals registry and RQ-9089's note.\\n\",\n    \"rfcs/0016-graduated-acceptance/implementation.md\": \"# RFC 0016 Implementation Plan: Graduated Acceptance {#el:rfc-0016-implementation-plan}\\n\\n## Status {#el:status}\\n\\nImplementation plan for RQ-9089 (`striatum-next/passes/graduated-acceptance`); principal halbritt.
